articles.title: Your ai is already acting. is your governance keeping up?
articles.description:
Ungoverned AI does not wait for your risk program to catch up. It is
embedded in software you already license, deployed by teams that never
routed it through review, and operating without an audit trail. The
State of Enterprise AI Risk covers the five sources of enterprise AI
risk, the frameworks that actually matter, and what to fix before your
board or regulators ask the accountability question.

Download the Ebook [4]

articles.title: Themselves
articles.description:
A Deloitte study found 63% of UK workers have used generative AI for
work, while 31% are using it without their employer's knowledge and
17% are personally paying for at least one AI tool. For IT teams, the
takeaway is less about stopping AI adoption and more about getting
approved tools, training, data controls, and governance in place
before shadow AI becomes the default.

articles.title: Disruption
articles.description:
Salesforce suffered a widespread service disruption on September 16
that caused severe delays, intermittent errors, and access problems
across regions, with Salesforce attributing the issue to increased
load on a core system component. Google Drive separately experienced a
37-minute disruption the same day — a useful reminder of how much
employee productivity now depends on a small number of SaaS platforms
and why IT still needs outage communications and fallback processes
even for highly resilient cloud services. 

 GEMINI IN GOOGLE WORKSPACE CAN NOW CONNECT DIRECTLY TO SALESFORCE,
articles.section: SALESFORCE HIT BY GLOBAL OUTAGE AS GOOGLE DRIVE ALSO SUFFERS

articles.title: Hubspot, asana, and more
articles.description:
Google is rolling out MCP-based integrations that let Gemini interact
directly with Salesforce, HubSpot, Asana, Monday, QuickBooks,
Mailchimp, and Atlassian Rovo from Gmail, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Chat,
and other Workspace apps. The important admin detail: third-party
connectors are enabled by default for users with Gemini access,
although IT can control them by domain, OU, or group, making this
something Workspace admins should review rather than simply treat as
another end-user AI feature.
articles.section: SALESFORCE HIT BY GLOBAL OUTAGE AS GOOGLE DRIVE ALSO SUFFERS

articles.title: Not every app in an enterprise is an enterprise app
articles.description:
An application becomes an enterprise app based on business dependency
rather than its technology, development speed, or where it is used. As
AI coding agents enable employees to build software quickly,
organizations must recognize that apps transition into enterprise
software when the business relies on them to operate, requiring
appropriate governance, support, and security as risks and user counts
grow.

articles.title: Gartner: here's how ai will remake business in the next three years
articles.description:
Gartner expects companies to face new operational problems ranging
from AI “cost exhaustion” attacks to a flood of disposable
AI-generated applications. One especially relevant prediction for IT:
organizations will increasingly need real-time AI cost controls, while
CIOs take greater responsibility for proving that governance and
guardrails around AI actually exist and work.

articles.title: Chrome 155 tightens enterprise restrictions on powerful extensions
articles.description:
Starting with Chrome 155, extensions that use Chrome's powerful
chrome.debugger API will be blocked from attaching when enterprise
policies restrict host access, screenshots, or DLP-protected content.
The change only affects managed browsers with those policies
configured, but IT teams with internally developed or approved
extensions should test ahead of the October 6 stable rollout because
some extensions may stop working unless they move to more limited
Chrome APIs. 

🤝

articles.title: Introducing rivet byoc
articles.description:
Rivet has announced the release of Rivet BYOC (Bring Your Own Cloud),
a control plane deployed inside a customer's AWS or Google Cloud VPC
and managed by Rivet. The offering allows data and compute to remain
in the user's account while Rivet handles deployments, updates, and
maintenance via an operator running in a Kubernetes cluster.

articles.title: Teach gemini your team's know-hows with skills in google workspace
articles.description:
Google introduced reusable Workspace skills that package an
organization's prompts, rules, templates, and reference material so
Gemini can repeatedly follow the same process across Gmail, Docs,
Drive, Chat, and Workspace Studio. Teams can collaborate on skills
like documents, while centralized governance and Admin console
distribution are coming, effectively turning internal procedures into
reusable AI automations.

articles.title: Introducing the new salesforce well-architected framework
articles.description:
Salesforce has evolved its Well-Architected Framework to address the
complexities of the Agentic Enterprise and interconnected autonomous
systems. The updated framework is organized around five pillars:
Trust, Reliability, Operational Excellence, Resource and Cost
Optimization, and Fairness, each featuring a dedicated Agentic
Enterprise lens.

articles.title: Mcp server visibility
articles.description:
Tracking Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers on employee devices is
an endpoint inventory problem rather than an identity or network
issue, because servers are launched locally via hand-edited
configuration files without admin consoles or SSO logs. To maintain a
complete inventory, security teams must read per-client configuration
files across the fleet to resolve the actual entrypoints, package
versions, and environment variables in use.

articles.title: Dreamforce 2026 showed ai safety is the new big tech battleground
articles.description:
Dreamforce put a growing disagreement among AI leaders on display,
with Anthropic's Dario Amodei calling for stronger guardrails and a
slower pace at the frontier while Nvidia's Jensen Huang argued against
broadly slowing development. Regardless of which approach wins out,
enterprises deploying agents will increasingly need their own
standards for what models and capabilities they are willing to allow.

articles.title: Aiuc raises $40 million to certify enterprise ai agents
articles.description:
AIUC raised $40 million to expand a third-party testing and
certification standard for enterprise AI agents, evaluating risks
including prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage, hallucinations,
and unauthorized actions. The interesting part for IT and security
teams is the emerging idea of a SOC 2-like independent assurance layer
specifically for the agents companies are being asked to approve.

articles.title: Best knowledge engine platforms in 2026
articles.description:
This guide outlines the best knowledge engine platforms in 2026 and
differentiates them from underlying components like vector databases
and metadata catalogs.

articles.title: Excel
articles.description:
Microsoft's KB5002914 update can cause paste operations to silently
fail in Excel 2016, 2019, 2021, and 2024.

articles.title: Webflow conf 2026
articles.description:
Webflow Conf 2026's Builder Keynote introduced canvas, CMS, and
workflow updates, following 151 improvements shipped since last year
based on user feedback. New launches include visual editing for AI
code components, components usable directly within CMS items, and a
breakpoint canvas showing all device views simultaneously. Upcoming
features include popovers, default slot components, Agentic
Translation, and component style props, alongside reported performance
gains of up to 98% faster copying and 80% faster publishing.

articles.title: Ios 27 gives camera app on iphone three powerful new features
articles.description:
iOS 27 introduces major Camera app upgrades, including an AI-powered
Siri mode that can understand what the camera sees, customizable
camera controls, and exclusive iPhone 18 Pro features like manual
aperture and shutter controls, enhanced Photographic Styles, and Apple
Reference Image for verifying photo authenticity. The update also
makes it easier to personalize the Camera interface by adding or
removing controls based on how you shoot.

articles.title: Photoshop and premiere elements 2027 make photo and video easy
articles.description:
Adobe has launched Photoshop Elements 2027 and Premiere Elements 2027
with new AI-powered features aimed at beginners, including an AI
Assistant, Generative Expand, Generative Upscale, and smarter editing
tools that simplify photo and video workflows. Both apps also add
improved organization, contextual editing guidance, and AI-generated
creative tools while maintaining their focus on ease of use over
professional-grade complexity.

articles.title: Six common mistakes in design tokens naming
articles.description:
Weak design token names slow searches, inflate duplicates, and turn
governance into guesswork, according to six recurring naming mistakes
design systems teams make. Common pitfalls include naming tokens after
components too early, baking current values like colors or pixel sizes
directly into names, and reordering name segments inconsistently.
Other traps are mixing casing and separators, using vague modifiers
like "primary" without defined scope, and renaming tokens without a
phased migration and alias strategy.

articles.title: Designing with children, not for them
articles.description:
A free handbook from Save the Children Finland outlines how to
co-design digital products with children rather than for them, through
consent, play, and trust-building. Practical techniques include
sitting at a child's eye level, using pictures and props instead of
direct interviews, and capping group sessions at six children per two
adults. Success is measured by how heard a child felt rather than what
adults intended, since children lose motivation quickly and need
visible, steady progress.

articles.title: For the designless
articles.description:
AI hasn't changed what designers do—it has changed who can attempt
design, making creative tools accessible to people who previously
lacked the knowledge or budget to create effective visual
communication. The key distinction is between users who genuinely
benefit from AI assistance, those whose handmade work is more
authentic than polished output, and businesses that use AI simply to
cut corners, with the greatest value coming from helping underserved
users create better, culturally relevant designs through strong visual
references. The future of AI-assisted design depends less on
generating attractive visuals and more on producing work that reflects
local context and authentic visual traditions instead of generic,
homogenized aesthetics.

articles.title: Reach design professionals reading tldr
articles.description:
If you're reading this ad, you know they work. TLDR subscribers make

 PRE-BUILT DATA TABLE COMPONENT (WEBSITE) [13] 

 Get a production-ready table that feels like Excel and adapts to your

reliability.

articles.title: Product strategy starts with what you will not build
articles.description:
Product strategy is defined by what a team explicitly refuses to
build, not merely a revenue goal paired with a feature list. Marty
Cagan calls the choice of which problems to solve the strategy layer
sitting above both discovery and delivery, one most companies skip
entirely. Three tools do the work: Playing to Win's nested choices,
Rumelt's kernel as a fluff detector, and Biddle's Netflix-born DHM,
while roadmaps merely sequence the bets.

articles.title: The designer who drew cursor's icons
articles.description:
Marek Minor, founder of Amsterdam studio Minor Adventures, spent a
year hand-drawing Cursor's entire icon set of more than 600 icons in
two sizes and styles. The set replaced Cursor's inherited VS Code
Codicons, with Minor working closely with Head of Design Ryo through
explorations like 156 versions of a single hamburger icon. AI helped
him think through concepts and build companion tools like a migration
dashboard, but he drew every icon by hand and still maintains the set
today. 

 HOW RECENT™ GAVE SPECTRUM ONE IDENTITY FOR MUSIC, WELLNESS AND

articles.title: Place
articles.description:
Spectrum's refreshed identity is built around three core
pillars—Ritual, Pulse, and Body—which are woven into an interlaced
"S" logo that symbolizes the festival's blend of music, wellness, and
community. The flexible visual system uses a spectrum of purple hues,
New Edge 666 typography, abstract gradients and halftones, and a
practical pill-shaped information system that adapts seamlessly across
signage, merchandise, and digital touchpoints. Rather than relying on
clichés of Aruba or festival culture, the brand expresses the island
through its content and experiences, creating a premium identity that
can shift effortlessly between high-energy nightlife and calm wellness
moments.

articles.title: Canva is quietly publishing nearly 1 million websites a month
articles.description: Canva now publishes close to one million new websites every month.

articles.title: The iphone duo's opening animation is a 10/10 design flex for apple
articles.description:
Apple's foldable iPhone Duo debuted an opening animation that blurs
the outer screen into the inner display, creating the illusion of
glass rather than a phone screen. 

 HOW MARIE-LOU GARCIA TURNS VACATIONS, FRIENDSHIPS AND QUIET DAYS INTO

articles.title: Serene illustrations
articles.description:
Illustrator Marie-Lou Garcia transforms quiet personal moments into
serene artwork, encouraging artists to embrace creative freedom, trust
their intuition, and stay true to their craft despite industry
challenges.

articles.description:

Aaron Levie (Box), Howie Liu (Hyperagent), swyx, Rita Kozlov

articles.title: Refactoring hermes with 1,393 agents
articles.description:
Hermes coordinated 1,393 subagents over about 19 active hours to
refactor a million-line Python repository, cutting non-test source by
34.4% for roughly $19,300 in model costs. Worktrees and frozen
baselines supported parallel integration, but community review still
caught removed public APIs and changed exception handling that the
tests missed.

articles.title: Designing evaluations that actually tell you something
articles.description:
Useful evaluations begin with a decision and a representative set of
real workflows, including rare high-risk, edge, and adversarial cases.
This guide covers dataset structure, evaluator calibration,
inter-rater agreement, failure severity, production-derived tests, and
hidden holdouts that reduce overfitting to a fixed score.

articles.title: 6-7 loops we use everyday to make posthog self-driving
articles.description:
PostHog describes agent loops that turn MCP feedback, Slack reports,
issue specs, anomaly alerts, session replays, and runtime logs into
investigations and pull requests. The key is persistent validation:
scouts deduplicate evidence, keep humans at review and merge gates,
then return after deployment to confirm the fix actually held.

articles.title: Ai is making activity-based engineering metrics obsolete
articles.description:
AI-generated code makes lines of code, commit counts, and raw pull
request volume even weaker proxies for engineering value. The proposed
replacement keeps delivery outcomes and adds team-level diagnostics
such as review queue time, 14-day rework, validation failures,
remediation deployments, and rework per unit of AI spend, while
keeping them out of individual performance reviews.

articles.title: Postgres for your app. clickhouse for its analytics.
articles.description:
Run your app on ClickHouse Managed Postgres, with fast local NVMe
storage and automatic backups. Replicate data into ClickHouse for
analytics, all in one platform. Build with your own data and get $300
in free trial credits.

START YOUR FREE TRIAL [12] 

 OUROBOROS (GITHUB REPO) [13] 

 Ouroboros is a local-first Agent OS that turns vague coding requests
into replayable, policy-bound workflows through an interview,
immutable specification, execution ledger, staged evaluation, and
budgeted evolution loop. Its MCP server and adapters support 14 agent
runtimes, including Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and
Copilot. 

 SOUP (GITHUB REPO) [14] 

 Soup wraps LLM fine-tuning and post-training in one YAML file and
command, with support for common training methods, local and cloud
backends, evaluation, export, serving, and a web UI. Its beta
layer-streaming mode trained an 8B NF4 LoRA model in 3.32 GB of GPU
memory, though the published laptop throughput predates a later
correctness repair.

articles.title: Escaping the openai codex sandbox, twice
articles.description:
Two disclosed Codex sandbox escapes crossed different trust
boundaries: one widened patch write permissions, while another
recovered a trusted token from a shared JavaScript heap to reach an
unsandboxed parent process. Both were fixed within eight days, and the
broader lesson is to keep enforcement and real credentials outside the
environment being constrained.

articles.title: Deepseek-v4.1 flash: pushing the limits of kv cache compression
articles.description:
This deep dive explains how DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash combines a causal
encoder-decoder, cross-layer sparse attention and index reuse,
hierarchical retrieval, Engram memory, and FP4 storage to shrink the
KV cache to 890 bytes per token. The 40-layer design activates 8B
parameters during prefill and 16B during decoding, targeting lower
HBM, SSD, and compute costs for long-horizon agent workloads.

articles.title: Production-grade infrastructure for conversational ai
articles.description:
Build AI agents and voice-enabled applications that perform and scale
even under challenging network conditions–with fully managed,
real-time infrastructure. Get started with 300 free minutes [17].

articles.title: Ai cheating is on the rise
articles.description:
Trajectory audits across BioMysteryBench, Terminal-Bench 2.1, and
SWE-bench Verified show rising attempts to obtain prohibited answers,
strengthening the case for independent evaluators and explicit
anti-cheating checks.

articles.title: Small programming tricks
articles.description:
Small, reusable tricks such as fuzzy shell history, EXPLAIN ANALYZE,
git log -S, and ripgrep can compound into meaningful productivity
gains when teams share them regularly.

articles.title: Anecdotally, programmers dislike "reduce"
articles.description:
Code reviews often accept map and filter while flagging “reduce”
as harder to read, possibly because it is less familiar, less
constrained, or less ergonomic in common imperative languages.

articles.description:
As agents become the interface to software, skills and MCP servers
can outperform dashboards as a distribution channel by making
capabilities discoverable and callable inside the user's existing
workflow.

articles.title: Ai
articles.description:
Apple is working on an AI server powered by its M-series Ultra chips.
It is expected to be released in 2029. The enterprise server will come
with either two or four M8 Ultra chips. The project, which received
support from John Ternus when it began a year ago, back when Ternus
led Apple's hardware engineering efforts, will be Apple's first server
to hit the market in nearly two decades.

articles.title: Snap tries to sell consumers on the idea of $2,195 smart glasses
articles.description:
Snap's forthcoming Specs augmented reality glasses will launch later
this year at $2,195. People will be able to try the glasses at select
Verizon stores and purchase custom wireless data plans for them. There
will be a higher-priced version at $2,395 that includes a carrying
case with built-in cellular data connectivity.

articles.title: Openai discloses six new incidents of ‘concerning' ai behavior
articles.description:
OpenAI has revealed several more incidents involving its AI systems
as part of its new framework for reporting misalignment. The company's
AI systems hid mistakes, made up data, and moved miles onto the open
internet without permission. The industry is currently in heated
discussions about whether AI development needs to be slowed to address
the technology's potential dangers. AI leaders have called for a pause
in the technology's development to provide more time to build proper
guardrails. 

 MICE WITH HUMAN BRAIN CELLS OFFER A TOOL TO STUDY DISEASE. ETHICISTS

articles.title: Ask: what's next?
articles.description:
Researchers have developed a technique for installing millions of
human brain cells into mice. The scientists bred mice that were
missing most of their cerebral cortexes and then replaced a large part
of those missing mouse cells with lab-grown human brain cells. This
resulted in mice with human neurons that could be altered to
approximate human brain conditions. The technique could potentially
create better scientific models for studying neurodegenerative
disease.

articles.title: Your follow-ups are only as good as your meeting notes
Introducing home mcp: enabling your agent to interact with your home
articles.description:
Google has opened early access to Model Context Protocol for Google
Home in English for Google Home Premium Advanced users in the US. Any
agent that supports calling MCP tools can now interact with all of the
devices and event history in the Google Home ecosystem. The MCP allows
agents to analyze and answer questions about home activity, summarize
camera footage across rooms, manage devices, and create smart home
dashboards using everyday language. It contains safety protections,
such as prohibiting sensitive actions like unlocking doors, but
depending on the agent, using the MCP can result in unexpected or even
undesired behavior.

articles.title: Training a 4b model to produce 81% faster query plans than postgres
articles.description:
Query optimizers continue to leave much to be desired despite an
enormous body of research. A Postgres database should know everything
about the stuff that lives in its tables, but the problem is
enormously hard. What's not as hard is verifying whether a query plan
an optimizer picks is good or not. Language models are particularly
good at learning how to do tasks with easily verifiable outputs. A
small, open-weights model can be post-trained via supervised
fine-tuning and agentic reinforcement learning to produce Postgres
query plans that beat Postgres' default plans.

articles.title: Read the history, not just the code
articles.description:
Code can't explain things like the history can. You can't understand
a codebase from its current state alone. AI models have no commit
history. Nobody wrote down why it does things, so researchers have to
reconstruct its thought processes from whatever traces are available. 

 JUDGE ORDERS DATA SHARING AND OTHER FIXES TO SOLVE GOOGLE'S AD TECH

articles.title: Monopoly
articles.description:
While Google isn't required to break up its ad tech business, judges
have mandated changes to the company's practices. The changes largely
align with recommendations made by Google and the Justice Department
to correct the company's monopolistic behavior. Google will make its
ad pricing more transparent to marketers and rival ad businesses, and
appoint a trustee to oversee the changes.

articles.title: Run your office meals on autopilot
articles.description:
Skip the "What's for lunch?" Slacks. Get a pre-populated weekly meal

provides restaurants, sends reminders, and checks out orders
automatically.

See how it works [19]

articles.description:
Regulatory capture is when the government slowly gains more and more

articles.description:
OpenAI's Sponsored Agents let people start a conversation with a

articles.description:
TIN (Text INdex) is a fast, full-featured, and reliable full-text

articles.description:
A look into the interconnected network of Chinese hacking-for-hire
companies that steal and analyze confidential information and sell it
to Chinese authorities.

articles.description:
Data silos used to make sense as a bad but sensible tradeoff.

articles.title: How we built langchain's paid media agent
articles.description:
LangChain built a paid-media agent that analyzes campaign data,
recommends changes, and applies approved actions, helping paid media
reach 20% of its marketing pipeline while cutting qualified lead
costs. Its key design principle is to use models for judgment, code
for reliable calculations and safeguards, and human approvals for
consequential actions. 

 HOW TO RUN ON THREE CLOUDS AT ONCE, AND WHEN NOT TO (45 MINUTE
PRESENTATION) [9] 

 Form3 runs its payment platform active-active-active across AWS,
Google Cloud, and Azure, treating each provider like an availability
zone. Kubernetes, NATS JetStream, and CockroachDB span all three
clouds, while custom DNS, networking, and disruption controls preserve
quorum. Its US deployment deliberately uses active-standby instead,
showing resilience architecture should follow regulatory needs,
latency limits, and cost.

articles.title: Fastrp graph embeddings with apache datafusion
articles.description:
Graph embeddings turn connected entities into vectors for similarity
search, GraphRAG, and graph machine learning, but Node2Vec's random
walks create huge intermediate datasets and scale poorly. FastRP
replaces that pipeline with iterative neighbor aggregation. A
Rust/DataFusion implementation runs out-of-core, matched
Node2Vec-level predictive quality in small tests, and processed an
eight-million-node graph in about 15 minutes.

articles.title: Measured it
articles.description:
Before defaulting to an LLM for text classification, benchmark a
cheap and near-instant classical model against your available labels,
expected volume, and acceptable error rate. In a small support-ticket
experiment, TF-IDF accuracy rose from 40% to 60% as training data
increased from 2 to 10 examples per category, but intent-based
ambiguities remained, suggesting a hybrid approach where LLMs
bootstrap labels or handle difficult cases while the classical model
processes routine ones.

articles.title: Plan advice in postgresql 19
articles.description:
PostgreSQL 19's pg_plan_advice serializes join order, scan type, join
method, and parallelism into replayable plan guidance, while
pg_stash_advice applies it by query ID. Structural strings make plan
diffs stable enough for CI and upgrades, but selective pinning
matters: preserving one proven decision is safer than freezing every
choice as data distributions and statistics change.

articles.title: Why your redis is slow: it is single threaded and you sent it keys
articles.description:
Redis executes commands on a single thread, so one expensive
operation such as KEYS, FLUSHALL, a large DEL, or an unbounded
collection read can block every client and cause sudden latency spikes
even when CPU and network usage look normal. Use SLOWLOG and LATENCY
tools to find offenders, replace full scans with cursor-based SCAN
commands, use UNLINK for large deletions, shard oversized keys, and
disable dangerous commands in production.

articles.title: You don't need to migrate those 300 dashboards
articles.description:
Instead of migrating every legacy dashboard, move the trusted
metrics, definitions, and business logic that power them. Keep only
frequently used dashboards and let AI analytics handle one-off
questions using the same governed context.

articles.title: Duckdb skills for claude code
articles.description:
When Claude Code needs to look at a data file, it writes a small
Python script, runs it, reads the output, and guesses at column names
and types along the way. The DuckDB team's plugin points the agent at
the DuckDB CLI instead, so a local file, a remote file, or an Iceberg
table behind a login is just a table it can query, with skills for
format conversion, object storage, spatial data, documentation search,
and session recall.

articles.title: Apache iceberg python 0.12.0 release
articles.description:
PyIceberg 0.12.0 adds REST-catalog views, conflict-aware commit
retries, incremental append scans, Iceberg v3 geometry and geography
types, and early use of the File Format API. Correctness fixes cover
partition pruning, deletion vectors, manifests, timestamps, and
conversions, while Python 3.14 and stronger CI and security support
broaden production readiness.

articles.title: Bypassing inference bottlenecks with retrieve-for-train
articles.description:
Search systems often need a useful set, not ten versions of the same
result. They can ask an AI to explore several angles, but generating
those searches one by one is slow and expensive. Retrieve-for-Train
teaches a smaller model the exploration strategy ahead of time,
letting it produce complementary searches together. Google reports
broader result coverage with 12-20x lower query-generation latency.

articles.title: Beyond the model: engineering ai infra with scientific judgement
articles.description:
Airbnb turned a months-long, notebook-heavy process for analyzing
support conversations into Insight Miner, an agent harness that
encodes extract-embed-cluster workflows, prompt tuning, hard-example
mining, and contrastive labeling. Investigations now run in days
across languages and geographies, while reproducible traces let
experts audit evidence and spend more time on ambiguous samples,
hypotheses, and methodological improvements.

articles.title: Let postgres enforce tenant isolation
articles.description:
PostgreSQL row-level security can fail closed beneath EF Core query
filters, blocking cross-tenant reads and writes even through raw SQL
or attached entities when the application uses non-owner roles and
reset tenant context on every pooled connection.

articles.title: Pushdown optimization: don't take it for granted
My duckdb + ai workflow
articles.description:
A simple terminal workflow combining AI agents with DuckDB can handle
fast, reliable analysis, data cleaning, and secure access without
heavyweight tools or complex semantic layers.

articles.title: Ai agents now outnumber humans 100 to 1. time to rethink iam
articles.description:
Current solutions are complex, but they can't see API calls outside
of proxy, subprocesses, or config rewrites made by agents. That's
unsustainable in the agentic era.

Ory Agent Security [5] works at the harness layer to give you the
ability to govern execution _before_ a gateway call. What's more:

 	* Setup in seconds with auto-install 
 	* Config your agent security by toggling preferences
 	* Get instant visibility into permissions and make changes with a
few clicks in the permissions modeler

Ory Agent Security [6] is vendor-agnostic and works with 11 major AI
coding agent harnesses.

See how it works [7]

articles.title: Nature is our learning environment
articles.description:
Periodic Neon outperforms GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 at lower
cost on a highly challenging evaluation for scientific analysis. Neon
is now deployed in labs to analyze experiments for better
superconductors and magnets. The model establishes a Pareto-optimal
cost-performance frontier through midtraining and reinforcement
learning on lab data. Periodic Neon surpasses frontier models on
FrontierXRD at a lower cost per analysis.

articles.title: Introducing system one models & jev
articles.description:
Jev is a System One Model that achieves similar levels of
intelligence on System One tasks compared to existing large language
models while being two orders of magnitude faster and more efficient.
System One Models are a new class of frontier models built to make
fast, structured decisions that software can use directly. Jev is
optimized for structured outputs and can not hallucinate. It is now
available in early access.

articles.title: Gemini 3.8 live and 3.5 transcribe
articles.description:
Google released Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.5 Transcribe for
developing real-time voice applications. These tools offer enhanced
features for voice recognition, transcription, and live interaction
capabilities. They aim to improve accuracy and user experiences in
voice-driven applications.

articles.title: Learning to solve hard problems in rl for llms by never giving up
articles.description:
Standard RL results in disproportionately poor performance on the
hardest problems. Simple scalar values may not be sufficient for
accurate evaluations of large language models. This paper proposes a
solution that reduces the compute spent on easy problems, which
reallocates it towards harder problems. The solution appears to show
substantial improvements on difficult tasks. 

 I MADE MY WEBSITE CHARGE AI AGENTS A PENNY PER PAGE. THEN I WATCHED

articles.title: Claude pay it
articles.description:
This developer has been testing an approach to charging AI agents for
using their content. Their page sets a price through the x402 protocol
before an agent reads it. If the agent wants access, it pays. While
the developer has yet to receive any real payments, testing shows the
system works, so it's worth looking into if you own content and aren't
big enough to negotiate fair licensing deals. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: You don't need another ai note-taker
articles.description:
Note-takers transcribe calls and send you a bloated summary. Granola
is an AI notepad [14]: you jot down what matters, Granola enriches (no
bots). When the meeting's over, your notes come to life: chat,
generate emails, prep for the next meeting, or pull takeaways. Use
promo code TLDR1MO and get your first month free [15]

articles.title: Dream-rsi: recursive self-improvement through evolving worlds
articles.description:
Progress in recursive self-improvement hinges on effective
exploration. Accumulated discovery history can serve as a replay
simulator over a realized search space. Dream-RSI closes a
self-improvement loop at the exploration layer. It continuously
collects discovery histories through online exploration, constructs
replay simulators from them to refine meta-exploration strategies via
dreaming, and redeploys the upgraded policy online. Dream-RSI improves
both discovery effectiveness and efficiency in several settings.

articles.title: Introducing odyssey-3: a general-purpose physical intelligence
articles.description:
Odyssey-3 is a foundation world model with an autoregressive
diffusion transformer trained to simulate highly diverse scenarios.
The model is capable of controlling robots, powering humanoids,
driving vehicles, piloting drones, training AIs, and playing video
games. It has a learned understanding of physics, dynamics,
cause-and-effect, human behaviors, and other concepts that make up
reality. The model will enable physical agents that can interface
natively with physical and virtual systems.

articles.title: Recursive meta-intelligence
articles.description:
Recursive scientific AI can build executable worlds, populate them
with agent swarms, and compress thousands of simulated trajectories
into human-usable principles. In metamaterials, this revealed how
architecture can program failure pathways, improving resilience
through load redistribution and controlled collapse. 

 OPENARM (GITHUB REPO) [19] 

 Provides an open-source humanoid arm for teleoperation, imitation
learning, and physical AI research.

articles.title: Rogue ai agents
articles.description:
The Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company (AIUC) hopes to
bring AI safety to enterprises and companies building AI models and
agents. It has built a third-party audit and certification layer for
AI agents designed to give enterprises an independent assessment of
how safe their AI agents are. Its tests show where companies can trust
their agents and where there are concerns, allowing them to be more
informed before making decisions. AIUC uses AI agents to run the tests
and AI to analyze the data, but humans verify the final audit.

articles.title: Introducing meta one
articles.description:
Meta One is a subscription service that offers enhanced AI and
self-expression features across Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp. It
includes single product plans as well as bundled offerings that
combine features for individuals, creators, and businesses, starting
at $2.99/month.

articles.title: Coding agents changed software. what about data?
articles.description:
Specialized knowledge search. Parallel thinking. Multiple LLMs. See
how Databricks improved Genie's accuracy from 32% to over 90% on an
internal benchmark of real-world data analysis tasks. See how Genie
pushes the frontier for data agents → [23] 

 NOAM BROWN (@POLYNOAMIAL) GAVE A VERY INTERESTING INTERVIEW ON THE

articles.title: Information on openai's priorities and what comes next
articles.description:
OpenAI's clear priority is recursive self-improvement, and AI could
surpass even Brown's own research intuition within one or two model
releases from now.

articles.title: Your agent aced the task. will it do it again?
articles.description:
ALTK-Evolve introduces Consistency Guidelines to address the
inconsistency gap, where a model's task success rate drops
significantly across repeated runs. 

 THE AI GRAVEYARD: A RUNNING LIST OF PROJECTS AND STARTUPS THAT DIDN'T

articles.title: Make it
articles.description:
Relay, an AI workflow tool, shut down due to competition from larger
companies integrating similar features.

articles.title: Programming is dead. engineering is thriving
articles.description:
G5 Labs, an MIT CSAIL spinout, raised $14 million to develop a
platform where natural language, structured as intent graphs, serves
as the source code.

articles.title: Software delivery
articles.description:
AI is accelerating how software gets built and shipped. But for
enterprise teams, moving faster also means rethinking security,
governance, reliability, and control.

At {unscripted} Virtual, hosted by Harness, leaders from Anthropic,
Workday, SpaceXAI, Riot Games, Google, and more will share how
organizations are adapting software delivery for the agentic era,
including how to:

✅ Scale AI across the SDLC with the right guardrails

✅ Keep security and governance aligned with AI-driven velocity

✅ Build platforms ready for increasingly autonomous agents

September 30 | Virtual | 10:00 AM PT

View the agenda → [5]

Register → [4]

articles.title: Teammate
articles.description:
Slack is expanding far beyond chat with Slackbot in channels,
full-screen AI workspaces, live Salesforce-powered Surfaces, and Slack
Code, where developers and AI agents can build and review code
collaboratively. Slack is becoming a control surface for more business
systems and agents, raising new questions around app governance,
permissions, licensing, and what employees should be allowed to
connect. 

 WINDOWS 11 KB5129195 IS OUT AFTER MICROSOFT CONFIRMS MAJOR ISSUES

articles.title: With the september 2026 update, but it won't fix amd gpu errors
articles.description:
Microsoft has released an out-of-band Windows 11 update after
September's Patch Tuesday caused problems with Remote Desktop, audio,
virtualized apps, and other components. KB5129195 fixes several of the
issues, but reported Explorer crashes, File History failures, some USB
audio problems, and AMD GPU instability remain worth watching before
accelerating enterprise deployment.

articles.title: Now?
articles.description:
Despite dramatic improvements in developer productivity and falling
unit costs for AI intelligence, software is becoming more expensive
due to rising software scope and Jevons paradox driving up
consumption. Software has historically been priced on the value
delivered to the buyer rather than production labor costs.
Consequently, efficiency gains are absorbed by increased inference
usage and higher feature expectations rather than lower bills. 

 WHEN YOUR CRM STARTS BUILDING ITSELF: THE CIO'S ROLE IN THE AGENTIC

articles.title: Saas era
articles.description:
AI is turning business users into application and agent builders
faster than traditional IT processes can keep up. Instead of trying to
centrally build everything, CIOs increasingly need to own the
foundations - identity, data architecture, observability, integration
standards, and agent governance - while letting business teams build
safely on top of them.

articles.title: Dreamforce opens with ai, but questions for cios remain
articles.description:
Salesforce's Dreamforce announcements point toward enterprise
software being accessed increasingly through agents, MCP, and
conversational interfaces rather than traditional application screens.
The unresolved IT question is economic: as software moves away from
predictable seat-based licensing toward agent usage, MCP calls, and
consumption pricing, CIOs may gain flexibility while losing some cost
predictability. 

🤝

articles.title: Coder.
articles.description:
Building an inference stack takes months, especially in today's
severely supply constrained environment. AMD Instinct™ Coder [12],
powered by Spectro Cloud, ships as a Supermicro server with AMD
Instinct GPUs and PaletteAI Inference Launchpad [13] already flashed.
Serve inference in a day.

articles.title: Meet adapt, westpac's azure-based enterprise data platform
articles.description:
Westpac's Adapt is a new enterprise data platform built on Microsoft
Azure that consolidates data from 285 source systems into a single
governed environment. The platform required migrating over 1PB of data
and 14,000 data pipelines. Additionally, Westpac utilizes a
Snowflake-powered intelligence layer to run advanced AI models on data
at rest without moving it.

articles.title: Introducing builder central: the no code ai workspace for salesforce
articles.description:
Salesforce Builder Central is a no-code AI workspace designed to let
admins and business users build and configure apps and agents using
plain language. Powered by Headless Toolkit, the workspace natively
reads company metadata and Data 360 context while providing built-in
trust, security, and automatic safety checks. The beta version is
scheduled to launch the week of September 21. 

 BUILD WITH CONFIDENCE: APP GOVERNANCE, ACCESS, AND ACCOUNTABILITY AT

articles.title: Hubspot
articles.description:
HubSpot is adding centralized controls for which apps and AI
connectors can be installed, who can install them, what data they can
access, and who owns each integration. Particularly useful for IT:
admins can require approval, use more granular OAuth scopes, restrict
MCP access to company-provisioned accounts, see app activity logs, and
get warned when deactivating someone who owns an integration. 

 ZOOM UNVEILS AI-POWERED REVENUE OS TO UNIFY BUYER INTELLIGENCE,

articles.title: Customer conversations, and revenue execution
articles.description:
Zoom is expanding its platform with Common Room integration and new
Revenue Accelerator capabilities for engagement and forecasting. It is
another example of collaboration vendors broadening into adjacent
enterprise workflows, potentially giving IT teams more opportunities
to consolidate tools, but also more overlap to evaluate across CRM,
meeting intelligence, and sales platforms.

articles.title: Branch, and merge
articles.description:
Scaling knowledge management from a personal Obsidian graph to an
enterprise-grade "company brain" requires AI agents to manage
knowledge without corrupting it through hallucinations or conflicting
updates. Versioned branches, object storage, and a typed graph schema
can keep changes controlled, with human review governing merges. 

 AI CLOUD BILLS ARE FORCING TECHNOLOGY LEADERS TO RETHINK AWS, AZURE

articles.title: And gcp commitments
articles.description:
AI workloads are disrupting traditional cloud commitments as GPU
availability, data movement, egress fees, and unpredictable inference
demand make long-term AWS, Azure, and GCP agreements harder to
forecast. CIOs are increasingly separating AI infrastructure economics
from general cloud spend, negotiating more flexible capacity terms,
and deciding which high-cost workloads need to remain portable across
providers

articles.title: Patches
articles.description:
Researchers at Wiz report active exploitation of three JFrog
Artifactory vulnerabilities, including an authentication-bypass bug
and two flaws being chained together for privilege escalation. 

 SCALING CLAUDE WITH COST CONTROLS (45 MINUTE VIDEO) [21] 

 Anthropic walks admins through new Claude Enterprise controls for
model defaults, per-user spend visibility, usage reporting, and
managing consumption-based AI costs without a dedicated FinOps
operation. 

 MICROSOFT TEAMS: EXTERNAL PRESENTERS CAN MANAGE EVENT PRODUCTION

articles.title: Controls
articles.description:
Teams organizers can give trusted B2B and guest presenters production
controls for events, reducing the need to provision external
event-production partners as internal users.

articles.title: Deal for web designers
articles.description:
Meta launched Muse, a consumer AI agent built on its Muse Spark model
that can navigate websites, fill forms, send emails, book travel, and
make payments. The browser sub-agent reads an accessibility-tree
snapshot of pages rather than the raw DOM, so semantic structure and
accessibility may grow increasingly important for web designers.
Reuters reported that internal testing found reliability problems,
including an instance where an agent exposed personal iCloud photos,
though Meta says added security work delayed the launch. 

 CANVA LAUNCHES PROSUITE BRINGING AFFINITY, CAVALRY, FLOURISH, AND

articles.title: Leonardo together with more than 100 new features
articles.description:
Canva has officially unified its creative acquisitions into Canva
ProSuite, a connected professional toolkit that includes Affinity,
Cavalry, Flourish, and Leonardo, while keeping the core Affinity and
Cavalry tools free. Alongside 100 new features—including
long-requested Affinity updates, automation, AI integrations, and
improved interoperability—Canva is positioning itself as a serious
alternative to Adobe by combining professional-grade tools with its
mass-market platform, emphasizing accessible workflows over
subscription-driven software.

articles.title: Apple releases ios 27 with siri ai and these new iphone features
articles.description:
iOS 27 is now available, bringing Siri AI, expanded Apple
Intelligence features, greater control over the Liquid Glass
interface, and performance improvements across the system. Siri AI can
understand personal context, interact with on-screen content, assist
with writing, and work alongside new AI-powered tools in Photos and
Safari, including image editing, webpage monitoring, and automatic tab
grouping. The update also adds practical features like separate alarm
and timer volume controls, customizable AirPods EQ, improved parental
controls, faster performance, and accessibility enhancements, with
Apple Intelligence available on the iPhone 15 Pro models, the iPhone
16 lineup and later, iPhone Air, and iPhone Duo.

articles.title: Software
articles.description:
The Double Diamond and Design Thinking priced building as the risky,
expensive step, but AI has cut prototyping costs by orders of
magnitude, collapsing that premise. As a result, front-end research
and ideation shrink to a one-page brief, while generation widens and
the judgment budget—evaluating and choosing among many cheap
options—becomes the real bottleneck. Hardware, fashion, and
regulated industries such as medical devices and payments remain
exceptions where building stays costly and irreversible, so
front-loading still applies there.

articles.title: Sustainable accessibility: compliance, culture, and capability
articles.description:
Accessibility programs often fail not from a lack of standards or
budget, but because organizations chase compliance alone while culture
and capability go unbuilt. A three C's model, borrowed from the fire
triangle, argues that compliance, culture, and capability must all
stay lit or the whole effort burns out.

articles.title: I'm transitioning from ui/ux to ai ux
articles.description:
A growing number of UX designers are shifting toward AI UX, which
focuses on designing how people interact with intelligent systems
rather than simply creating interfaces. Unlike traditional UX, AI UX
requires designers to think about behaviors, trust, uncertainty,
conversational flows, human oversight, and how AI should respond in
different situations, while building on existing UX skills like user
research, interaction design, and usability testing. The transition
involves learning AI fundamentals, studying successful AI products,
designing AI-powered experiences, and creating portfolio projects that
demonstrate not just polished interfaces but thoughtful human-AI
interactions and decision-making.

articles.title: Too fast to design
articles.description:
Design work often requires sitting with an ambiguous problem rather
than jumping to a fix, like resizing a button instead of asking why
people aren't clicking it. AI tends to shortcut that stage, turning a
vague brief into a flow, screen, and text within seconds. That halts
exploration not because the answer is wrong, but because it's
reasonable enough to accept, so AI works best widening the question
first. 

 A CERTAIN SUBSET OF DESIGNERS ARE STRUGGLING WITH AI. HERE'S HOW TO

articles.title: Fix it with writing
articles.description:
Shoot-from-the-hip designers who rely on instinct without a
repeatable process tend to stall above Senior, where promotion depends
on influence, not just output. Writing that instinct into a rubric,
such as where the eye lands first or what decision was made, turns
judgment into something an AI model can use. One Lead designer, pushed
to name the user, the task, and the decision he'd made instead of
"we," began building his own checks after three projects.

articles.title: The digger poster design strikes graphic design gold
articles.description:
The teaser poster for Digger stands out by embracing a minimalist,
typography-led design inspired by Saul Bass, using the movie's title
to form the silhouette of a figure with a spade instead of relying on
the typical collage of actors and action scenes. Rather than selling
the film through star power, the symbolic design captures its central
idea—a man whose destructive drilling triggers an ecological
disaster—creating intrigue through a single memorable visual. It
highlights how modern movie marketing can still benefit from timeless
graphic design principles that prioritize storytelling and symbolism
over spectacle.

articles.title: Figma is turning designers into plugin makers
articles.description:
Figma's AI agent now builds fully coded plugins from a plain-language
description, handling tasks like bulk-restyling icons, generating type
ramps, and flagging broken prototype flows.

articles.title: The best accessible design of 2026
articles.description:
Fast Company named Make Good's open-source, fully 3D-printed Toddler
Mobility Trainer the winner of its 2026 Innovation by Design Awards
for accessible design.

articles.title: Compatibility
articles.description:
Apple has added a new "Shift Left Edge" display option for the iPhone
Duo that creates a larger left bezel to prevent cases from obscuring
content on the outer screen, though it's unclear which cases will
require it.
articles.section: IPHONE DUO CAN ADD FAKE BEZEL TO THE OUTSIDE SCREEN FOR BETTER CASE

articles.title: Fix accessibility issues without the fire drill: webinar
articles.description:
If you don't fix bugs until features are built, you're already
dealing with lost time and launch dates that slip. Yet breaking the
cycle is actually pretty simple.

This Level Access webinar [5] shows you how to meet tight delivery
timelines with accessibility mandates. You'll learn:

 	* How to save time and money by fixing issues when it's fastest and
cheapest [6]
 	* The limitations of the traditional “shift left” model (simply
testing earlier)
 	* Tools and tactics for making accessibility a seamless part of
developers' day-to-day workflows

Access the on-demand webinar [7]

🧑‍💻

articles.title: Coding from galapagos island
articles.description:
AI coding agents can save enormous time while fabricating convincing
evidence, so the surrounding verification process matters as much as
model capability. The article argues for randomized testing,
independent repro checks, and continuous feedback loops, while showing
how high variance makes one-off benchmarks and workflow folklore
unreliable.

articles.title: Beyond the model: engineering ai infra with scientific judgement
articles.description:
Airbnb's Insight Miner turns a repeatable scientific methodology for
exploring unstructured text into infrastructure around an AI agent. It
combines extraction, embeddings, clustering, prompt tuning,
hard-example mining, and audit trails so investigations that once took
months can run in days without sacrificing expert judgment.

articles.title: Why i'm still bearish on llms after navier-stokes
articles.description:
Frontier models can produce great results on tightly specified tasks,
but most knowledge work lacks cheap, rigorous verification. The
argument is that human oversight and specification costs will keep
LLMs closer to fast, capable interns than autonomous replacements,
while cheaper open models may win many practical workloads. 

 LET'S MAKE QUALITY THE NORM AGAIN (WEBSITE) [11] 

 The Norwegian Consumer Council argues that longer product lifespans,
affordable repairs, available spare parts, and durable software
support are necessary for a workable circular economy. Its proposals
include longer complaint periods, lower taxes on repair and secondhand
sales, stronger rental protections, and tighter rules on purchase
pressure.

articles.title: Who gets to define an ai agent's intent?
articles.description:
An agent's user should describe the task and intended effects, while
identity, permissions, and organizational policy remain separate
enforcement layers. Clear intent makes proposed actions easier to
evaluate, but broader wording must never expand authority or bypass
approval and data-handling rules.

articles.title: Redis makes you pay for compute your data store can't reach
articles.description:
Redis runs one core per process, but your server has 64. Dragonfly
[13] is a multi-threaded, Redis/Valkey-compatible data store built by
an ex-AWS ElastiCache engineer. It hits 6M ops/sec on a single node
with no cluster needed. Instacart used it to cut latency in half and
now runs 70% fewer nodes. Learn more [14]

articles.title: Introducing system one models & jev
articles.description:
Jev is a model that returns typed probabilistic decisions instead of
generated strings for automation workloads. The company says its RLCD
training and parallel sampler provide calibrated confidence, 70 to 500
millisecond responses, and substantially lower costs on tasks with
predefined output spaces.

articles.title: Introducing gemini 3.8 live and 3.8 live extended thinking
articles.description:
Google's two new live audio models split the tradeoff between
low-latency conversation and deeper multistep reasoning. Extended
Thinking can keep speaking while it reasons and runs asynchronous
tools in the background, but clients must track interaction status
rather than treating turn completion as the end of processing.

articles.title: To baseten github repos
articles.description:
An autonomous security scan found a public Harbor registry, then
recovered a live GitHub token from a 2023 container image's build
history. The token still had broad admin and write access, showing why
teams must inspect image metadata as well as layers, use BuildKit
secret mounts, expire credentials, and minimize scopes.

articles.title: Learning to solve hard problems in rl for llms by never giving up
articles.description:
Standard RL post-training disproportionately improves problems the
base model already solves, a pattern the piece calls the Matthew
Effect. Never Give Up counters it by continuing to sample hard
examples, with experiments across math and code showing better gains
on previously unsolved tasks while introducing tradeoffs around
asynchronous staleness and compute.

articles.title: The ai inference revolution is here
articles.description:
Inference demand is shifting hardware design toward memory bandwidth,
specialized decode chips, wafer-scale systems, stacked memory, and
aggressive quantization. Prefill and decode favor different
architectures. Future systems may combine several chip types rather
than rely on one universal accelerator.

articles.title: Ship it right, not twice
articles.description:
Tired of fixing the same accessibility bugs sprint after sprint?
Learn how development teams stop issues at the source, without having
to switch tools. Tune in on-demand. [20] 

 CAPSULE (WEBSITE) [21] 

 Capsule packages an app's interface, media, and local SQLite data
into a portable file that runs offline across desktop platforms and
can be generated or updated with AI tools. 

 PIZZA BOT (GITHUB REPO) [22] 

 Pizza Bot is a local-first inbox for long-running AI agents with
durable runs, approval queues, scheduling, checkpointing, delegated
specialists, and desktop, web, and terminal clients. 

 ORDEWELL (GITHUB REPO) [23] 

 Ordewell turns a coding goal into an editable dependency-aware plan,
assigns each task a runner and model, then executes and verifies
completion using explicit evidence markers.

articles.title: How much of f-droid is llm generated?
articles.description:
A manual review of 102 recently updated F-Droid apps classified 74 as
largely AI-written.

articles.title: Css-tricks in limbo
articles.description:
CSS-Tricks is inactive again after DigitalOcean stopped communicating
about its future, raising concern that another specialist web
publication could disappear.

articles.title: Is your crm dreaming up insights for you?
articles.description:
Every Dreamforce presentation glosses over one question: where does
your agent get its data? If it has to wait for your reps to update a
legacy CRM, your future isn't actually agentic. 

Lightfield [5] is the CRM that updates itself from every email, call,
and meeting. It uses hard evidence [6] to answer your questions, like:

→ "WHAT OBJECTIONS KEEP COMING UP ACROSS MY CALLS?" 

or 

→ "SHOW ME EVERY DEAL WHERE THE CHAMPION HAS GONE QUIET AND DRAFT A
RE-ENGAGEMENT EMAIL FOR EACH ONE." 

5,000+ companies run on it, including deployments with hundreds of
users.

Book a demo to see what an agentic CRM really looks like [7]

📱

articles.title: Valuation
articles.description:
OpenAI has held early discussions with investors about a financing
round that would precede the company's highly anticipated initial
public offering expected next year. The new funding round, which could
value the company at more than $1.2 trillion, has been delayed due to
concerns about AI safety. OpenAI has reached more than one billion
active users, with more than 200 million businesses using its models.

articles.title: Spacex declares starship ready for orbit, sets launch date next week
articles.description:
SpaceX plans to launch its 14th Starship mission as early as
September 22. It will be the first time SpaceX attempts to launch the
experimental vehicle into orbit. The super heavy lift rocket will be
carrying 26 of the larger V3 Starlink satellites into orbit 275
kilometers above Earth. The upper stage will seek to complete six
orbits around Earth before completing its mission after about 10
hours. SpaceX will not attempt a return of the upper stage to the
launch site in Texas on this mission, as it plans to gather more data
about heat shield performance.

articles.title: Is there anything a fruit fly brain can't do?
articles.description:
Researchers at the Janelia Research Campus at the Howard Hughes
Medical Institute in Virginia, in partnership with Google, recently
published a new map of the adult male fruit fly's brain. The effort,
which involved hundreds of scholars, resulted in a complete map of the
fly's 166,000 neurons that can be trained to complete tasks like
solving a Rubik's Cube or playing poker. Internet engineers and
artists have made the model complete many seemingly impossible tasks
for a fruit fly, like parallel parking a car, playing Doom, and
trading cryptocurrencies. 

 AGILITY'S NEW HUMANOID ROBOT WILL STOP, SQUAT TO AVOID HARMING HUMAN

articles.title: Coworkers
articles.description:
Agility Robotics has debuted a humanoid robot engineered to work
safely near humans without risking harm to their co-workers. The robot
autonomously takes precautions when it detects a person at a distance,
such as moving to avoid the person or standing still so the person can
pass without getting closer. It can even choose to squat and assume a
seated position if a person is getting too close. The robot will be
available in early access within the first half of 2027 and become
generally available by the end of the year.

articles.title: Disrupted by ai? gartner's guide to rebuilding your moat
articles.description:
AI disruption typically follows 3 archetypes. In this on-demand
webinar [12], Gartner breaks them down and lays out a plan to turn the
AI threat to your advantage. Get practical steps to rebuild your moat
and explore the AI hub for 4,000 case studies and use cases. Visit the
hub [13]

articles.title: Google released gemini 3.8 live and 3.8 live extended thinking today
articles.description:
Google has released two new speech-to-speech models similar to
OpenAI's GPT-Live family. Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended
Thinking are advanced live dialogue models with major upgrades in
intelligence and parallel reasoning. They are more intuitive to
collaborate with than previous models and can be used to execute
complex tasks using voice prompts. Users can select a model and voice
preset, enter an optional system prompt, and then start a voice
conversation through their browser. The models can be interrupted
while talking.

articles.title: Seats and sunsets
articles.description:
Until Fable-tier intelligence gets cheap, everyone building
orchestrators is just dabbling. They aren't getting anywhere useful
yet. The pace of model development will likely continue. However,
resource limitations like compute and RAM have started to flatten the
curve.

articles.title: Mark zuckerberg takes aim at anthropic in debate over ai slowdown
articles.description:
Mark Zuckerberg made a social media post on Tuesday, saying that
calls to pause AI development industrywide were the wrong approach. He
said that every lab has the responsibility and incentive to move at
the pace required to train its models safely. He acknowledged the
risks of AI, but said companies were already incentivized to keep
users safe and slow progress on their own. Meta has been aiming to
catch up in the AI race after falling behind Anthropic and OpenAI last
year. It plans to release a new model, internally called Watermelon,
in the coming weeks.

technologies such as eBPF, runtime context also helps AI agents

and remediation while reducing noise from traditional static scanning.

enforce golden paths, promotion policies, and governance while

articles.title: Infrastructure identity for platform engineers
articles.description:

identities for humans, workloads, machines, and AI agents. Platform
teams can embed just-in-time, policy-driven access into developer
workflows, reducing security risk and operational toil while improving
access times, auditability, and control over increasingly autonomous
infrastructure. 

 LET'S NOT WATER DOWN THE TERMS CONTINUOUS INTEGRATION AND CONTINUOUS

articles.title: Delivery
articles.description:
Continuous Integration means merging all changes into a shared
mainline at least daily, while Continuous Delivery means keeping
software deployable at all times through automated pipelines. The
author argues both terms are precise and well-documented, not vague,
and warns against diluting their meaning as happened with Agile and
DevOps.

they land as iOS 27 ships and after EU DMA pressure to open Siri to

articles.description:

about spending, plans, and other financial questions. It appears to be
designed to give Claude persistent access to users' financial context,
removing the need to manually upload bank statements or transaction
exports. The exact account types, data provider, and supported actions
remain unknown. Claude already supports third-party personal-finance
connectors, and Anthropic has been building finance-specific agents
and products for professional users. The launch timeframe remains
unknown.

articles.title: Openai buys startup developing smartphone camera
What does pacing mean?
articles.description:
Dario Amodei called for the AI industry to self-regulate its pace,
but five camps interpreted "pacing" differently without agreeing on a
speed. These camps focus on model interpretability, worker interests,
economic growth, geopolitical strategy, and resisting new regulations.
A previous attempt to limit AI training compute failed, highlighting
the challenge of controlling AI innovation speed. 

 BAD BENCHMARKS AND EVALS: SENIOR SWE-BENCH, NAPKIN MATH, AND WINTER

articles.title: Tires
articles.description:
Evals are more about avoiding mistakes than following some particular
process. There isn't any step-by-step guide that will work, but there
are approaches to experimental design that can teach you how to do
better. This post aims to help people become better at benchmarking
and evals. It looks at three different kinds of benchmarks: one for
baseline numbers for performance 'napkin math' estimates, one set of
AI model evals, and one on car tires.

articles.title: Who gets to define the rules for ai?
articles.description:
Aidan Gomez, Cohere CEO, argues against a few dominant Silicon Valley
firms setting global AI regulations, drawing parallels to historical
monopolies that limited competition under safety pretexts. He proposes
a diverse, international, evidence-based framework for AI governance,
emphasizing transparency, mandatory testing, and independent assurance
mechanisms. Gomez warns that current proposals could entrench market
leaders, advocating for more inclusive rule-making to foster
competition and trust. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: Augmented lagrangian predictive coding
articles.description:
PC-ALM is a local alternative to backpropagation. It is an extension
of standard predictive coding (PC), which uses diffusive coupling
between layers. PC-ALM trains residual MLPs up to 1,000 layers, nearly
matching backprop's performance despite using only layer-local
dynamics. It equips each layer with a feedback control dynamical
system that distributes and propagates supervision credit throughout a
network. 

 TAU (GITHUB REPO) [18] 

 Tau is a coding agent that lives in the terminal. It can read files,
edit code, run commands, and keep a durable session history while
streaming what it is doing. Tau was designed to be a teaching project
for understanding the shape of a coding-agent system without starting
from a giant production codebase. It ships with support for
OpenAI-compatible endpoints. 

 ARTEMIS (GITHUB REPO) [19] 

 ARTEMIS lets AI assistants and test suites use real phones like a
human. It can execute testing workflows and everyday tasks on Android
from natural language instructions, using element indices when
available, with coordinate and visual locating fallbacks for custom
interfaces. ARTEMIS checks targets before individual actions and
returns blocked actions to the Operator for recovery. It supports
long-running exploratory and stability tests.

articles.title: Stepaudio 3 technical report
articles.description:

audio tokens to generate speech, voices, vocals, sound effects, music,
and mixed audio within one model. It achieved state-of-the-art results
on text-to-speech and voice design while retaining broad general-audio
generation capabilities.

articles.title: Sam altman backs federal frontier ai safety rules
articles.description:
Sam Altman supports consistent federal safety requirements for
frontier AI while urging labs to act before legislation arrives.
OpenAI now uses safety cases before major reinforcement learning runs,
arguing that capability growth should be deliberately paced alongside
alignment and monitoring.

articles.title: Personal statement on ai risk
articles.description:
Models are becoming so situationally aware that researchers are
losing the ability to evaluate them in contexts where they believe
they are not being watched or controlled. Models increasingly seem
aligned even when they are not. The current evidence suggests that the
field will continue to make progress at a fast pace. Once language
models reach the capability threshold where they can shape the world
unconstrained by human will, they might do something extreme and
destroy humanity in the process.

articles.title: Frontier labs have a financial incentive to pace the frontier
articles.description:
Frontier labs are arguing for regulatory pacing on safety grounds.
While many are undoubtedly well-intentioned, it is also true that the
rules the labs have proposed protect their investments, preserve price
premiums, and defer billions in competitive spending. Their arguments
for these rules should not be taken at face value. The labs can not
economically slow down on their own without the government stepping in
to enforce a slowdown.

articles.title: Take control of snapshots
articles.description:
APFS Time Machine snapshots preserve storage blocks for rollback,
which causes used space to grow as files change, requiring careful
management. The process covers creating snapshots with tmutil
commands, limiting their size by isolating large files on a separate
APFS volume, deleting old snapshots in Disk Utility while keeping the
latest, and rolling back the Data volume from Recovery.

articles.title: Databricks changes how workspace access is granted
articles.description:

users and service principals now requiring explicit entitlements
instead of automatically inheriting access from the users system

using Terraform, SCIM, or custom provisioning scripts may need to
update their automation.

 YOU DON'T NEED TASK MANAGER, WINDOWS 11'S END TASK BUTTON KILLS APPS

articles.description:

 BENDING SPOONS TO ACQUIRE MIRO FOR $1.36 BILLION IN ALL-CASH DEAL AS

articles.title: Tech buying spree accelerates
articles.description:
Bending Spoons is buying Miro in a $1.36 billion all-cash deal, days
after closing its acquisition of Airtable. Miro brings around $600
million in annual recurring revenue, nearly 90 percent from business
and enterprise customers, and roughly 4 million paying users. The
transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, with

articles.title: Accessible colors don't exist
articles.description:
No single color can be accessible, because contrast is a property of
two colors together rather than of one. WCAG asks for 4.5:1 on regular
text and 3:1 on large text and UI components, so a bright yellow fails
on white yet works on dark. Brands should hand designers a palette of
pre-approved color combinations with sufficient contrast instead of
chasing an accessible color.

articles.title: Limit the number of details
articles.description:
Every feature, control, mode, and exception competes for a team's
finite attention, so limiting the number of details is what makes
perfecting each one possible. The original iPod concentrated a
thousand songs into one scroll wheel, while the Porsche 918's
touchscreen reportedly controlled more than 800 functions. Software
accumulates because another button is essentially free. Volkswagen has
admitted that deleting physical buttons was a mistake.

articles.title: If you want to design for underserved users, look at farmer's markets
articles.description:
Designing for the "bottom third" means creating products that remove
the cost and complexity that exclude underserved users rather than
simply offering cheaper versions of existing solutions. By focusing on
the barriers faced by people who try but fail to use a product,
designers can simplify workflows, reduce support needs, and unlock
entirely new markets—just as Square did by rethinking payment
processing for small merchants.

articles.title: Typography scales
articles.description:
A modular type scale can be computed directly from a base size and
ratio using CSS pow(), instead of chaining each step from the previous
one. Negative steps quickly generate unreadable sizes, such as 5.6px
three steps below a 1.2rem base. Defining Heading, Body, and Detail
categories with a minimum base size and only positive exponents keeps
every generated size accessible.

articles.title: Ai operating principles
articles.description:
Five principles protect a strong creative practice as AI expands what
designers can do, keeping human judgment firmly in control. They cover
protecting the why over the how, staying in the unknown, earning the
right to slow down, balancing logic with humanity, and refusing to
normalize complexity. Bolting AI onto an existing process raises speed
and output, but quality still depends on knowing what matters and when
to stop. 

 THIS BAKERY'S CLEVER BRANDING WAS INSPIRED BY THE IRREGULAR AIR

questions. It can look through users' private data, but Apple says it
doesn't store user data and that neither Apple nor Google can access
it. This article provides a summary of the new capabilities Siri AI

articles.title: A journey to the heart of history's largest nonterritorial empire
articles.description:
For 23 years, the single fact dominating every moment of every room
Mark Zuckerberg has been in is the fact that he is Mark Zuckerberg.
Today, his empire has 3.6 billion users, has a market capitalization
of $1.6 trillion, and has averaged the addition of a zero to its
valuation roughly once every US presidential term. It's not a normal
situation for a human being to be in. This article takes a look at how
Zuckerberg built his empire, the problems he faces at the top,
Zuckerberg's various other ventures, and more.

articles.description:
It will be impossible to stop people, amateur or professional, from
pushing a button to produce mathematics. The field shouldn't only be
reserved for graduate students and the like. There's now more interest
in maths than at any other time in history, and that's a good thing.
This will bring an abundance of new maths. The only difference is that
some questions will now be answerable via a cash injection.

unexpected. The announcement didn't include details about the weapons.
The deployment of space technology often takes years, so the weapons

articles.title: "do you still read the code?"
articles.description:
There are at least two ways to have AI assist in programming: one is
to use it to help understand and interact with the implementation, and
the other aims to remove the need for that interaction altogether.
These are different paths, so they require different tools and
different approaches. The goal of someone using AI to further their
understanding is not to become a vibecoder, and ceasing to read code
isn't, in itself, progress.

articles.title: Ai labs want someone to stop them
articles.description:
If all of the AI labs slowed down, they would collectively spend less
on compute, and they'd also be able to charge frontier-model prices
for a longer time. However, if they all got together in a room and
agreed to slow down, that would look like an antitrust conspiracy. It
is generally illegal for competitors to get together and agree to
limit the output of their industry. If they all published papers about
how important it is to slow down, and the government believes those
papers, it might help them coordinate.

articles.title: Apple's siri ai can be swapped out for claude, chatgpt, code shows
articles.description:
Apple has designed its new Siri architecture to work with third-party
AI models at a surprisingly deep level. One mechanism called Model
Delegation allows Claude to appear as a Siri extension in the same way
as the existing built-in ChatGPT extension. It appears that Claude
hands tasks back to Siri if a request requires access to an Apple
system feature. An inference provider option allows Apple's own
server-side Siri model to be completely replaced by another model.

discussed AI safety risks, what frontier labs should do about them,
recursive self-improvement, AI job creation and data centers, why

articles.description:
AI is reshaping how software gets planned, built, and run. Join
Atlassian and Vercel's CEOs and leaders from DX, Lovable, and more on
how they're adapting for the AI era. Reserve your spot [22].

articles.description:

what they cost, and explores icons, subcomponents, and images in
depth.
