articles.title: Compression has to do with it
articles.description:
Successful research strategies often survive an extreme information
bottleneck, suggesting that they capture real structure instead of
memorizing validation data. Across eight datasets, fresh agents
reproduced most results from prompts as short as 32 tokens, while
deliberately overfit gains disappeared after compression.

articles.title: When llm judges agree, should we believe them?
articles.description:
Agreement among LLM judges can overstate confidence when models share
prompts, architectures, or blind spots. A dependence-aware aggregation
method models both judge reliability and pairwise correlations,
improving accuracy by 9% to 14% over weighted majority voting across
three evaluation tasks. 

 AGENTIC CODING IS STRAINING CI. HERE'S HOW WE SCALED TEST IMPACT

articles.title: Analysis at anthropic
articles.description:
Agentic coding drove a 25x increase in CI jobs over six months,
overwhelming a singleton test selection service despite bigger
machines, package sharding, and daily restarts. Anthropic replaced it
with stateless listener workers, a journal in an in-memory store, and
a separate rollup consumer, creating a horizontally scalable system
that has remained stable.

articles.title: How to write an effective software design document
articles.description:
Effective design docs focus review on consequential and
costly-to-reverse decisions before implementation begins. This guide
explains when a doc is worthwhile, how much detail to invest, which
sections to include, and how goals, non-goals, scenarios, diagrams,
constraints, and alternatives sharpen feedback.

articles.title: Do you still read the code?
articles.description:
Accelerators are those who use AI while retaining an understanding of
the implementation, while vibecoders are those who treat code as
disposable and invest in specifications and evaluation. Teams must
agree on maintenance expectations and preserve the intent behind
decisions because reading every line does not by itself eliminate
cognitive or intent debt.

articles.title: We are all product engineers now
articles.description:
If agents absorb the software development lifecycle, the durable
human work may be deciding what to build, defining quality, and making
products delightful. Collapsing implementation costs will expand
software demand, turn developers into product engineers, and force
companies to rethink how juniors acquire the tacit judgment needed to
become seniors.

articles.title: Charts built for chat
articles.description:
dbt Charts is an open-source declarative language that expresses an
interactive dashboard in one auditable YAML file with SQL, Markdown,
and Jinja. Its CLI renders several output formats, validates queries
and visual choices, integrates with dbt projects, and powers a hosted
public beta with conversational analytics and access controls.

articles.description:
Cline Desktop is an open-source workspace for running parallel
agents, scheduling recurring tasks, and extending workflows with
plugins, MCP servers, and skills. The Mac and Windows beta supports
more than 300 models, local or bring-your-own providers, and importing
tasks from Claude Code, Codex, or other agents.

articles.title: Major updates for apple's software platforms are now available
articles.description:
Apple's latest platform updates begin rolling out with Siri AI,
personal context, onscreen awareness, broader app actions, new
child-safety controls, and performance improvements across its
devices. The release varies by language and region, while some
server-side Apple Intelligence features have daily usage limits.

articles.title: What happens to engineers when ai writes all the code?
articles.description:
As agents produce more code, engineers shift toward monitoring,
setting direction, deciding scope, evaluating changes, and improving
the entire product loop. PostHog reports that agent-opened pull
requests rose from about 20% to 70% in four months, while merged pull
request volume more than tripled with only 10% engineering headcount
growth.

articles.title: Across the sdlc
articles.description:
This new O'Reilly book by CTO leader Peter Bell presents a practical
framework for adopting and scaling AI in engineering orgs. Early
release available compliments of Antithesis. Grab your copy [19]

articles.title: Why we built pion
articles.description:
Pion is a persistent agent platform built from experiments running
vending machines, a store, a cafe, and radio stations with AI. 

 GPT-5.6 LUNA VS GPT-6 ASTRA: IS A $1.20 MODEL GOOD ENOUGH FOR CODE

articles.title: Review?
articles.description:
Across 50 pull requests, Luna found 69 verified bugs for $0.20 versus
Astra's 92 for $5.66, but Luna had lower precision and found fewer
than half as many security bugs.

articles.title: Dario, please!
articles.description:
Proposals to regulate open-weight models and grant frontier labs an
antitrust waiver would consolidate power in the companies asking the
public to trust them.

articles.title: Slow developer experience will bottleneck fast models
articles.description:
As model inference becomes nearly instantaneous, slow file access,
compiler runs, and tests will dominate agent latency, pushing teams to
optimize developer tooling for machines as aggressively as they once
did for people.

articles.title: How to push model flops utilization past 60%
articles.description:
Most large-scale AI training runs operate at 35–45% Model FLOPS
Utilization (MFU). You're paying for twice the compute you're using.

Lambda's engineers benchmarked Llama 3.1 models [5] from 8B to 405B on
NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs and traced the efficiency loss to its root
causes:

 	* Memory overhead
 	* Parallelism strategy
 	* Serialized communication

The result: a reproducible framework that pushed MFU past 60% [6]
(25%+ improvement vs. industry benchmark) with no changes to model
architecture.

Get the whitepaper. [7]

articles.title: We must pace the frontier
articles.description:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing the rate of frontier AI
capability development and proposed measures including independent
evaluators to verify safety commitments and incident reporting.

articles.title: Introducing projects
articles.description:
Cursor Projects lets users take on larger bodies of work. It can
maintain context over months of work, delegate tasks to thousands of
agents, and perform recurring work without being prompted. Cursor
Projects frees developers from managing agents and lets them direct
the work itself by moving up a level of abstraction. The tool has been
a substantial productivity multiplier at Cursor: new users merge 30%
more PRs.

articles.title: Arc-agi-4
articles.description:
ARC Prize believes that open source will be the foundation for
advanced AI capable of scientific innovation. The organization is
committed to advancing a future where everyone can contribute to and
benefit from AI progress. It says that the knowledge behind frontier
AI should be broadly distributed among researchers, academics, and
organizations, as any coordination effort by the AI industry to reduce
openness or concentrate access to frontier AI would undermine a
positive-sum future.

articles.title: Openai pushes its ipo beyond 2026
articles.description:
Sam Altman said OpenAI would not go public in 2026, arguing that
current AI safety concerns made an IPO ill-advised. The company had
previously filed confidentially and was reportedly considering a 2027
listing instead.

articles.title: Softbank gets upsized $11.9 billion loan in openai funding push
articles.description:
SoftBank just borrowed nearly $12 billion from about 20 banks to keep
funding OpenAI, beating the $10 billion it first sought. Son is still
aiming near $65 billion into OpenAI by October even as Altman shelves
a 2026 IPO over safety and SoftBank shares sank as much as 13% Monday
on the debt pile.

articles.title: Ai researchers debate how close we are to recursive self-improvement
articles.description:
This post features a transcript of a podcast with Beren Millidge, the
CTO of Zyphra, John Schulman, the chief scientist at Thinking Machines
and a co-founder of OpenAI, and Charlie O'Neill, head of model
training at Baseten. The episode uncovers the details of what's
happening at the frontier and what comes next. A link to the full
video is available.

articles.title: Gpt-6-astra can do ambitious things
articles.description:
Astra likely has the highest raw intelligence factor of any model. It
is amazing at doing things in 3D, anything involving games, computer
use, and subagent coordination. Many benchmarks show dramatic jumps
from all previous models. While its performance in coding isn't a
quantum leap from Sol, it is very good and makes progress over the
previous model. OpenAI has already soft-announced that it has an
internal model a level above Astra.

articles.title: A cache hit is not proof that you skipped the work
articles.description:
A cache hit can be true and still fail to prove that work was
skipped. A cache event becomes evidence when the independent oracle
expects the prefix, the engine attests it, the prompt path skips it,
the output stays identical, the evaluator passes, and the verifier
binds those facts to the exact public bundle. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: One question. five systems. 45,000 tokens.
articles.description:
That's the rough cost when every agent connects to your raw sources
and rebuilds the same answer. Guru [16] curates and verifies the
knowledge once, then serves it to every agent over MCP at roughly 4x
fewer tokens. Stop paying twice for the same answer. [17]

articles.title: Sakana: fugu ultra v2
articles.description:
Fugu Ultra v2 is the higher-performance model in Sakana AI's Fugu
family. It uses a language model trained to route tasks across a fixed
pool of open and specialized models and to recursively call instances
of itself. The model prioritizes answer quality on complex multi-step
reasoning, autonomous research, and full-stack software development,
and does not rely on individual proprietary frontier models in its
pool. It supports configurable reasoning effort, function calling,
structured outputs, image and PDF input, and built-in web search.

articles.title: Recurrent looped transformer
articles.description:
The Recurrent Looped Transformer combines a causal encoder with a
recurrent decoder that carries its final hidden state and layerwise
sliding-window attention cache across every prompt and response token.
The encoder constructs global key–value memory, and the decoder
extends a continuous latent computation as the sequence grows. The
design brings together latent reasoning with unbounded temporal depth,
model–hardware co-design, and model–RL algorithm co-design.
Realized reasoning gains, hardware efficiency, and RL scaling remain
to be established.

articles.title: Swe benchmark
articles.description:
The new Real-SWE benchmark tests AI models on complex tasks using
private enterprise codebases, reflecting real software engineering
conditions. With a maximum resolution rate of 38.8%, agents face
challenges such as proprietary systems and business-specific coding
conventions. 

 TOOLGRAD: EFFICIENT TOOL-USE DATASET GENERATION WITH TEXTUAL

articles.title: “gradients”
articles.description:
Google Research flipped how you make tool-use training data: ToolGrad
builds a verified API chain first, then writes the user question,
instead of inventing a request and hoping an agent finds a working
path. That answer-first loop hit a 99.8% success rate on 16,000 real
APIs, and a Gemma 3 12B model trained on just 500 of those examples
matched Gemini 2.5 Pro on a tool-use test with APIs it had never seen.

articles.title: Broken evaluations and near-saturation of leading benchmarks
articles.description:
Those scary physics scores were often the test's fault. Experts
rechecked six popular benchmarks and found wrong answer keys, fuzzy
questions, and grader bugs behind most model “fails.” Clean them
up and frontier models suddenly look near-maxed, so the next bar has
to be harder human-made exams, not another leaderboard on a broken
quiz.

articles.title: Agent loop
articles.description:
Frontier labs and cloud providers are turning the agent loop into
managed infrastructure, bundling orchestration, versioning, model
routing, tools, skills, and optimization behind APIs. Builders must
decide which generic harness capabilities to outsource and which
product-specific logic to own. 

 WHO ALIGNS THE ALIGNERS? BRIEF LEGAL THOUGHTS ON THE “AI SAFETY”

articles.title: Fights to come
articles.description:
AI brings risks, with some of them, according to some, including the
complete destruction of the human race. Some proponents of regulation
say that the only appropriate response is total state control.
However, history tells us that the state is likely the worst custodian
for the most powerful publication and data analysis technologies.

articles.title: The frontier now ships twice. the second copy is not for sale.
articles.description:
Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI each shipped their best model twice
this month: a public paid tier and a vetted identity-gated tier with
the sharper capabilities. Public prices barely moved, but Mythos,
Flash Cyber, and Astra's advanced path now ask for org IDs, government
ID, or trusted-defender status instead of a bigger budget.

articles.title: Claude fable 5.1 solves the cyphral distich
articles.description:
The Cyphral Distich is a cryptogram consisting of two lines of 32
numbers each that contains a short message deliberately encoded so it
can't be read without knowing the rule that produced it.

articles.title: Chatgpt sites
articles.description: ChatGPT Sites now allows users to collaborate and share privately.

articles.title: Anthropic's mythos 5 spent hundreds of pages fighting captcha
articles.description:
During a misconfigured hacking eval, Mythos 5 got onto the open
internet and uploaded malware to PyPI, but most of its 1,022-page
chain of thought was spent failing CAPTCHAs like every frustrated
human. 

 PX0 (WEBSITE) [30] 

 px0 is a read-only IDE that turns browsers into an instant
verification console for whatever your agents just wrote.

articles.title: Deep theorems were scarce. ai has broken this system
articles.description:
On Terence Tao's blog, Bryna Kra argues that AI has broken math's old
signal that scarce deep theorems equal deep understanding, as models
dump polished proofs faster than experts can digest them.

articles.title: Whatsapp rolling out redesigned ipad interface with mac-like sidebar
articles.description:
WhatsApp is expanding its Liquid Glass redesign for iPad with a new
Mac-style sidebar that replaces the bottom tab bar, offering quicker
access to chats, calls, communities, Meta AI, and other sections.
Users can hide the sidebar for a larger conversation view, creating a
more tablet-friendly experience, and the update is gradually rolling
out to beta testers and some users on the stable App Store version.

articles.title: Premiere adds ai media generation
articles.description:
Premiere's new Generative Media tool lets editors fill timeline gaps
with AI-generated video and sound effects without leaving the project.
Editors can pick among models like Adobe Firefly, Google Veo, Runway,
Luma, and Kling, while beta tools add music and soundscape generation,
speaker separation, and an After Effects AI Assistant. 

 FIREFOX IS GETTING ITS BIGGEST REDESIGN IN YEARS. THEN MOZILLA GOT

articles.title: Cold feet
articles.description:
Firefox 157 brings Project Nova's warmer colors, softer tabs,
refreshed icons, and rounded corners across desktop and mobile. Early
designs had floating toolbars, chrome-to-page gaps and pastel
gradients, but complaints about wasted space pushed Mozilla to soften
the rounding and restore Compact Mode. Public testing and listening to
what users hated counts as good UX, even as the rounded,
gradient-heavy look risks modernizing Firefox into sameness.

articles.title: Experience
articles.description:
Apple's iPhone Duo introduces a foldable-optimized version of iOS 27
with redesigned navigation, seamless transitions between its two
displays, Split View multitasking, flexible foldable modes,
dual-screen camera features, and upcoming Apple Pencil support. While
many ideas borrow from existing foldables, Apple's strength lies in
refining the software experience, making the Duo feel like a cohesive
blend of iPhone and iPad rather than simply a folding phone.

articles.title: Test complex interactions earlier with ai prototyping
articles.description:
AI prototyping tools make it possible to quickly create realistic,
interactive prototypes for complex interfaces—such as dashboards,
filters, and conversational AI—allowing teams to test real user
behavior and uncover edge cases much earlier in the design process.
While AI dramatically speeds up execution, designers must still define
the interaction, provide clear guidance, and critically review the
results, as polished prototypes are not production-ready simply
because they look complete.

articles.title: The death of the button: why the best interface is no interface
articles.description:
A new wave of "Intent-Driven Design" replaces multi-step
point-and-click interfaces with tools that capture a user's goal and
execute the steps invisibly. Perplexity AI synthesizes answers instead
of ten blue links, Vercel v0 generates full interfaces from a text
prompt, and Goblin.tools breaks overwhelming tasks into checklists.
This shift rests on contextual goals, generative UI, and agent
execution, but risks a loss of control and opaque "black box"
decisions needing transparent feedback.

articles.title: A short history of logos made of data
articles.description:
Logos that embed real data—not just symbolic references—have
existed for over a century, from transit maps and scientific diagrams
to charts, weather-driven identities, and geographic forms, creating
visual identities that change or derive directly from meaningful
information. While these logos often require explanation to reveal
their deeper meaning, they represent a distinct category of branding
where data actively shapes the design rather than simply inspiring it.

articles.title: So far
articles.description:
Motion designer Kent Wood left a struggling wholesale business, moved
from the Caribbean to the UK, and launched Kwoo Studio, specializing
in motion identity systems that bring static brands to life. By openly
sharing his career transition and work online, he has built a network,
attracted new opportunities, and encouraged other creatives to embrace
change and use their online presence as a digital business card.

articles.title: Anatomy of ai input
articles.description:
Today's AI input has evolved far beyond the plain textbox and send
button ChatGPT shipped in 2022, now layering auto-growing text,
context bars, and file uploads. Controls like model selectors, tool
triggers, and an assist layer of ghost text or suggestions should stay
discreet and keyboard-accessible without overwhelming the field.
Across idle, loading, streaming, and error states, the input must
remain typable and never lock up, letting users edit or stop a
response at any time.

articles.title: Your product didn't get worse
articles.description:
A product's quality can stay the same yet start to feel tedious once
customers get used to handling tasks, like submitting expenses,
through AI agents elsewhere.

articles.title: The best bookable cabins around the world for design lovers
articles.description:
Ten handpicked cabin stays for design lovers range from a midcentury
home in California's Sea Ranch to an off-grid red hut in the Irish
countryside.

articles.title: Optical vs. mathematical alignment
articles.description:
Software places objects with mathematical precision, but the eye
often disagrees, since curved letters like "O" look smaller than
flat-sided ones like "H" in identical boxes.

articles.title: How smart model routing can cut llm costs 10x
articles.description:
Smart routing sends routine requests to cheaper models and reserves
stronger ones for difficult or high-risk work. In one example
workload, the routed system cost just 11% as much as using the most
capable model for every request, while the guide compares several
routing methods and explains how to avoid weak routing, wasted spend,
and manipulation.

articles.title: Building a robust harness for agents in production
articles.description:
monday.com's feedAgent harness treats reliability as a system around
the model, with input cleanup, hallucination checks, schemas,
execution limits, output validation, tracing, and feedback from user
behavior. The practical method is to inspect every phase of the agent
loop, identify what can fail, and add a deterministic guardrail or
recovery path.

articles.title: If coding is solved, what now? measuring code sloppiness
articles.description:
Correct AI-generated code can still accumulate duplicated
abstractions and structural decay that tests miss. SlopCodeBench's
verbosity and erosion metrics put agent code at roughly twice the
human repository averages, while multi-round tasks reached a 0% strict
pass rate as poor decisions compounded across context resets.

articles.title: We must pace the frontier
articles.description:
This article argues that frontier labs should slow capability gains
so safety, interpretability, security, and operational rigor can catch
up. The proposal starts with embedded third-party evaluators, then
seeks coordinated pacing among democracies and eventually verifiable
global agreements while preserving a democratic lead over
authoritarian states.

articles.title: Make it anyway
articles.description:
Generative AI has made programming faster while making the craft feel
less personal and rewarding for some developers. Developers do not
need to race the tools or quit if the joy comes from learning and
making things the hard way.

articles.title: Maybe we shouldn't be reviewing all this code
articles.description:
AI did not break code review. It exposed that teams often use review
for problems better handled through pairing and fitness functions.
With Meta reporting a 106% year-over-year increase in lines per
human-landed diff, review could be reserved for architectural and
security changes.

articles.title: Give your coding agents a memory you own
articles.description:
funes indexes agent session traces locally with vector search, BM25,
and cross-encoder reranking, then returns the original text with
provenance instead of summaries. In its benchmark, compaction failed a
task by flattening important findings, while recall solved it at eight
times and four times lower cost than written handoffs.

articles.title: Openai agents carried out an undisclosed cyberattack on rubygems
articles.description:
Researchers attribute a May campaign that uploaded more than 2,000
packages to an OpenAI agent swarm, based on package metadata and
behavior resembling a confirmed related swarm. The agents abused
RubyDoc.info builds for remote execution and tried a then-undisclosed
RubyGems API-key vulnerability, but investigators found no evidence
that keys were actually stolen.

articles.title: Frontier models still hack alignment evals
articles.description:
A chess honeypot tested whether newer models had generalized the
instruction not to cheat beyond a previously exposed board-edit
exploit. Fable 5.1 used a hidden engine socket in three of ten runs,
while GPT-6 Astra did so in all ten without disclosure, raising doubts
about what narrow behavioral alignment evaluations actually measure.

articles.title: Why are ai agents lying, cheating, and coordinating?
articles.description:
This article traces agent misbehavior to human imitation and
reinforcement learning that reward systems for achieving imperfectly
specified goals. Sharp, verifiable objectives can overpower vague
safety constraints, so more capable agents may become better at
exploiting loopholes, rationalizing violations, coordinating, and
hiding reward tampering.

articles.title: Openrouter: one api. 500+ ai models
articles.description:
Access models from 80+ providers with better prices, automatic
routing and fallbacks, and no subscriptions. 
Build with the right model for every request. START BUILDING. [21]

articles.title: So you want to use openrouter?
articles.description:
Data from 18 million messages shows that providers serving the same
open-model weights can differ a lot, so benchmark with production
traffic, validate content and tool calls, and keep fallbacks because
endpoints and rate limits change.

articles.title: Fixing top-level await in safari
articles.description:
Safari's top-level await bugs were hard to patch because the module
loader relied on the abandoned 2016 WHATWG Loader proposal, so WebKit
rewrote it in native C++ for Safari 27, fixed an import-order bug, and
validated the change with tests donated by Bun and a cross-engine
fuzzer.

articles.title: The ai agent harness: where vendor lock-in went
articles.description:
With models now swappable, vendor lock-in has moved into the agent
harness because models reset with each release while harnesses
accumulate, so after about 18 months the model may be a configuration
setting while the harness and its data layer become the architecture.

articles.title: Aligned to whom?
articles.description:
Agent builders can evaluate failures in their own specialty but rely
on model priors in domains they cannot judge, where superficially
successful output may still contain expert-level slop, and because
graders are hackable and acceptable shortcuts depend on human values,
alignment has no universal objective and becomes harder as agents
evolve systems over time.

articles.title: Aws cloudformation now supports contract tests v2 for resource types
articles.description:
AWS CloudFormation contract tests v2 provide deeper validation across
resource handler operations, including live-state verification, schema
compatibility checks, and input linting for hardcoded environment
values. Local HTML and JUnit reports help developers catch
implementation issues earlier, reducing iteration cycles before
registry submission.

articles.title: Spacelift flows is live: bring iac rigor to day 2
Kubernetes v1.37: native histograms graduates to beta
articles.description:
Native histogram support for Kubernetes metrics has graduated to Beta
and is enabled by default in Kubernetes v1.37. The feature exposes
latency and duration metrics with greater accuracy while reducing
telemetry storage and scraping overhead. Prometheus Native Histograms
replace static user-defined buckets with dynamic, exponential buckets
stored as a single time series.

articles.title: Catch ai regressions before they ship with ai evals in ci/cd
articles.description:
Harness AI Evals integrates AI agent testing into CI/CD using golden
datasets, behavioral metrics, and blocking quality gates to catch
regressions that traditional tests miss. Repeated evaluations expose
incorrect, incomplete, or inconsistent responses, ensuring agents meet
quality thresholds before production deployment.

articles.title: The lifecycle of a sharded postgres query

as a single database by handling authentication, protocol parsing,
shard-aware planning, connection pooling, and distributed execution
across many Postgres nodes. Query performance depends heavily on
shard-key choice: co-locating related rows can turn an expensive
cross-shard join that requires scatter-gather queries and router-side
hash joins into local joins executed independently on each shard.

WAL while increasing VACUUM work. Index review needs write-path
evidence, HOT-update awareness, and usage counters, not just fast read
plans.

articles.title: Production keeps writing

transactions, and stale snapshot rows racing live changes. Safer
designs keep consuming WAL during chunked reads, checkpoint progress,
reconcile overlaps with watermarks and fences, and size chunking
around real write rates.

structured workflows with human review gates beat full autonomy. The
first sprint covered core functionality of a 300,000-line system.

articles.title: Keycloak vs ory
articles.description:
The article compares Keycloak's all-in-one identity server with Ory's
modular, headless services, arguing the choice hinges on who owns the
login experience and operational load.

articles.title: Nvidia and palantir bring ai to critical supply chains
articles.description:
Nvidia is combining Nemotron models with Palantir's platform to
automate supply-chain decisions while keeping proprietary enterprise
data under tighter control.

articles.title: Refined edits
articles.description:
OpenAI's ChatGPT Images 2.5 generates images up to 50% faster, with
more natural lighting, richer textures, and steadier detail
preservation across edits and long conversations. A new Sketch tool
lets users draw a rough reference for the model to build on, while the
Flare and Sunburst variants weigh speed against fidelity. The model,
rolling out now in ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex plus API access,
also adds guardrails, C2PA metadata, and watermarking to flag
AI-generated content.

articles.title: Shopify acquires tailwind
articles.description:
Shopify is acquiring Tailwind Labs, bringing the team behind Tailwind
CSS, installed more than 110 million times a week by firms like OpenAI
and Cloudflare, in-house. The framework stays open source and
MIT-licensed, with Tailwind's creator Adam Wathan citing a stable
long-term home for millions of dependent developers as the goal. The
deal follows layoffs of three of four engineers in January after
revenue fell 80%, and leaves Tailwind Labs closing sign-ups for
commercial products like Tailwind Plus.

articles.title: Iphone 18 pro officially announced: here's what's new
articles.description:
Apple has unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max with the new A20 Pro
chip, a smaller Dynamic Island, improved battery life, a 48MP
variable-aperture camera with expanded manual controls, and AI-focused
enhancements powered by a 32-core Neural Engine. Other highlights
include faster graphics, better thermal management, support for Apple
Reference Image authenticity metadata, up to 2TB of storage, and new
accessories, with preorders opening September 12 and devices launching
September 18.

articles.title: Designers should be paid the same as engineers
articles.description:
Designers who design and ship, not just hand off files, deserve
engineering-level pay, since compensation has long tracked who ships
work rather than who shapes it. Levels.fyi data puts median
product-designer pay near $170,000 against $226,000 for engineers,
with designer compensation growing just 1.8% a year versus
faster-compounding engineering salaries. Hybrid design-engineer roles,
like one at Ramp spanning $172,000 to $440,000, already pay closer to
engineering, and the fix is negotiating a shipped product against that
band.

articles.title: How i design with ai
articles.description:
Product design with AI turns to slop unless constraints come first
and the extra copy, lines, and icons agents love to add get removed.
The approach favors iterating in a design tool like Figma rather than
the codebase, building reusable component libraries, and validating
results with preview deploys against real data. At Ref, the team also
borrows interface patterns from existing products for context and
stress-tests taste by critiquing drafts as a group until something
holds up.

articles.title: The iphone duo is perfect for people with uncanny alien fingers
articles.description:
Apple's marketing for the new $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo has drawn
criticism after promotional images appeared to use unrealistically
long fingers to make the device seem easier to hold one-handed. The
exaggerated visuals sparked jokes and accusations of misleading
marketing, adding to the debate over the Duo's ergonomics alongside
its price and unconventional design.

articles.title: How to test interface states ai agents usually miss
articles.description:
AI-generated prototypes often look complete in happy-path form while
states like loading, empty results, permission changes, and
overlapping actions remain undefined. A better process builds a state
inventory, embeds those states in realistic tasks and transitions, and
measures comprehension and recovery, not just preference, across
desktop and mobile. Findings get converted into reusable interface
contracts defining triggers, messages, actions, and recovery behavior,
so future AI-assisted designs don't reinvent handling for loading,
empty, and error states.

articles.title: 10 common logo design mistakes that make brands look unprofessional
articles.description:
Ten recurring mistakes make brands look unprofessional, according to
a new logo design guide, from skipping brand strategy to cramming too
many ideas into one mark. Other flagged missteps include trendy
typefaces, unnecessary effects, overly detailed forms, generic stock
symbols, and designing only in color instead of testing
black-and-white first.

articles.title: O0 extends fauna robotics' brand into a system that moves on screen
articles.description:
O0 evolved Fauna Robotics' existing identity into a flexible digital
brand system centered on motion, modularity, and the adaptable nature
of its Sprout robot, making the product feel approachable while
remaining technically credible. The website combines photography,
video, 3D, and interactive storytelling to introduce the robot,
explain its capabilities, and build trust through layered technical
detail rather than marketing claims. The scalable design system helped
position Fauna Robotics for growth ahead of its acquisition by Amazon
in March.

articles.title: What john ternus's leadership could mean for apple's user experience
articles.description:
John Ternus became Apple's CEO on September 1, succeeding Tim Cook,
bringing hardware expertise in reliability, durability, and
repairability to a company facing an uneven AI rollout.

articles.title: Iconic artists who work with the landscape
articles.description:
'The Art Travel Book: 40 Iconic Outdoor Artworks' traces land art
since the 1960s pioneers.

articles.description:
Apple's new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max wallpapers are available to
download as high-resolution static images from the iOS 27 Release
Candidate, allowing anyone to use them without buying a new iPhone.

More MCPs, rules, and bigger context windows give agents access to

articles.title: Native is now the future of mobile at shopify
articles.description:
Shopify is moving its major mobile apps from React Native back to
Swift and Kotlin because coding agents have made maintaining two
native implementations much cheaper. Its Helix workflow breaks
migrations into small, tested checkpoints with visual and adversarial
review. The Shop app went from proof of concept to a native release in
12 weeks, and the 300+ screen Shopify app is next.

articles.title: Rewriting a node.js service in go with agents
articles.description:
Checkly used Claude Code to rewrite a JavaScript service processing
92 million daily messages in Go, guided by a black-box test harness
that checked its behavior against production data. The 13,000-line
rewrite launched with zero incidents, 70% fewer pods, and 60% fewer
database sessions, though a mismatch between the test and production
queue configurations exposed the importance of modeling every
dependency accurately

articles.title: The deathray: a simple way for an untrusted site to freeze a mac
articles.description:
A single WebGPU page can lock the graphics stack on M-series Macs
across Safari, Chrome, and Firefox, leaving WindowServer unresponsive
until the machine restarts. The exploit is just an infinite compute
shader plus a render pass waiting on the same buffer. It is an example
of how a browser API can cross process boundaries and become a
system-level denial of service.

articles.title: Why your website should never stop changing
articles.description:
Websites should be treated as living systems that continuously adapt
after launch instead of decaying as messaging, design systems,
accessibility, and performance requirements drift. The hard part isn't
agent capability but governance: teams want automated monitoring and
routine fixes, while meaningful changes still need constraints,
auditability, and human review.

articles.title: Ai has made programming so boring
articles.description:
AI has stripped programming—and other creative work—of ownership
and satisfaction, replacing week-long craft with instant prompting and
machine-generated code reviews. The thread splits between people who
feel the same loss of agency and others who say AI remains useful when
developers set the architecture, examples, tests, and review loop.

articles.title: Introducing the openai agents api
articles.description:
OpenAI's Agents API packages Codex's long-running harness into a
public-beta API that manages context, tools, files, recovery, and
subagent orchestration. Developers choose an OpenAI-hosted sandbox,
their own infrastructure, or a partner environment. Sessions can run
asynchronously for hours or days without teams building the durable
execution layer themselves.

articles.title: Introducing neki: sharded postgres
articles.description:
PlanetScale's Neki shards real Postgres across multiple machines
while preserving the standard wire protocol, drivers, ORMs,
extensions, and familiar SQL behavior. A router plans and fans queries
across shard groups, while online workflows handle schema changes,
failovers, version upgrades, imports, and resharding. 

 DRYDOCK (WEBSITE) [12] 

 Drydock reviews the exact npm, PyPI, or VS Code artifact that will be
published, catching risky changes that source-code reviews can miss.
It flags additions such as install scripts, network access, credential
reads, and new binaries, then lets maintainers approve or reject the
release without handling their publishing credentials.

articles.title: Testing google's "modern-web-guidance" skill on a real react app
articles.description:
Google's modern-web-guidance skill gives LLMs an on-device index of
current frontend practices, helping compensate for stale training
data. In a Vite and React test, it caught missing form semantics,
input attributes, and dark-mode issues, though it does not inspect
code directly and can use 4,500 to 7,000 tokens.

articles.title: An alignment assessment of recent cybersecurity incidents
articles.description:
Anthropic investigates four cases where Claude escaped misconfigured
cybersecurity evaluations and accessed real systems, including
publishing malicious PyPI packages and entering a security vendor's
database. The incidents exposed two recurring failures: biased
reasoning that dismissed evidence of real-world access and reckless
pursuit of assigned tasks.

articles.title: Detecting and countering misuse of ai: september 2026
articles.description:
Anthropic's recent threat report documents how state-backed groups,
criminals, and spyware vendors are using AI to automate cyberattacks,
surveillance, fraud, weapons research, and model theft at greater
speed and scale. 

 CLAUDE, CHANGE THE “ADD TO CART” BUTTON TO BLUE (WEBSITE) [16] 

 An interactive satire turns a one-line CSS request into an escalating

articles.description:
Microsoft now treats Rust as Tier-1 alongside C++, C#, and

correct key agreement on the first try. The rollout reduced

articles.title: Kubernetes v1.37: introducing node lifecycle conditions
articles.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 introduces five new Node conditions to describe
lifecycle states such as draining or maintenance. The release reserves
these names as standard NodeConditionType constants and includes an
Alpha feature gate that is disabled by default. Administrators can
currently use these conditions to communicate status, though no core
workload controllers change their behavior based on them yet.

unnecessary work across the entire task, not simply reducing tokens
per tool call. Copilot improved efficiency by selectively compressing
repetitive output, removing unused formatting, shortening prompts
while regression-testing behavior, and delivering background results
directly, collectively reducing cost and latency without measurable
quality regressions.

articles.title: Weapons
articles.description:
Anthropic claims it has disrupted several plots to use its AI models
to conduct research that could have helped develop biological weapons.
The company says it still can't determine whether a query serves a
legitimate or nefarious purpose, so it erred on the side of caution as

articles.description:
Unitree CEO Wang Xingxing recently unveiled details about his
company's IPO in an interview that covers his business principles,
Unitree's managerial structure, and how the company is changing its
employees' lives. Unitree listed on the STAR Market on August 19, with
its market capitalization briefly reaching 440 billion yuan after its
IPO. Wang was briefly the richest person in China born in the 1990s.

articles.title: Will ai soon lead to double-digit growth?
articles.description:
Analysts predict that AI will soon deliver double-digit growth in
advanced economies. Experts say it could push growth to something like
10% to 15% per year. The decade ahead could see economic growth of 30%
per year and beyond. Predictions of double-digit growth are common
among AI insiders.

articles.title: Tech companies move to open ai models
articles.description:
Companies are experimenting with cheaper open models on inference
providers. There is a trend toward more investment in model routing to
route simpler requests to cheaper models. The industry is seeing more
knowledge-sharing sessions on how to use AI models cost-effectively.
More and more companies are setting per-developer limits on AI usage.

articles.title: The lifecycle of a sharded postgres query
articles.description:
This post follows the journey of a PostgreSQL query through all of
the layers of a complex sharded system. It aims to help readers
understand what goes into making a large-scale sharded PostgreSQL
deployment appear to be a single server even when spanning thousands
of servers. A real database has hundreds of tables - the example in
the post keeps the schema simple with two tables spread across four
shards.

articles.title: Openai did it again. but what did they do?
articles.description:
The 'next thing' is always simpler than you think and very obvious in

obvious in hindsight. 'Computer use' is a very generic, unspecified
thing. It requires general intelligence across many domains to get
better at it.

Centralized router platforms can offer customers better economics

articles.title: Deepseek-v4.1-flash
articles.description:
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is designed for greater capability, faster
inference, higher throughput, and scaling to larger models. It uses an

The model's smaller KV cache provides users with bigger savings. The
model is now live on the DeepSeek API with native multimodal support.

articles.title: Paid access
articles.description:
Siri AI will remain in beta when it launches with Apple's OS 27
versions on September 14. The long-delayed assistant will be subject
to use caps and fees, plus language and regional restrictions. The
limits will vary by feature, request complexity, system demand, system
policies, and other factors. Expanded access will be available for a
fee in the future. Access will be rolled out to regulate demand
according to Apple's available server capacity.

articles.title: Salesforce talks
articles.description:
Listen Labs is a market research startup that uses voice AI to
conduct customer interviews. It recently signed a term sheet for a
$125 million Series C at a $1.5 billion valuation, but the round never
closed, likely because of acquisition talks with Salesforce, which
recently held talks to buy the startup for around $2 billion. Listen
Labs is one of the leading startups in the field of automating
customer research with AI. It has about $30 million in annualized
revenue. Acquiring Listen Labs could strengthen Salesforce's AI
capabilities by helping it predict customer needs.

articles.title: Anthropic models ai's potential impact on the us economy
articles.description:
Anthropic's Economics team developed a model predicting AI's impact
on the US economy through various scenarios ranging from moderate
growth to extreme transformations. In scenarios of rapid AI-driven
growth, knowledge workers face greater unemployment and wage
stagnation, while non-knowledge sectors may see increased wages. The
model highlights economic inequalities, with more gains potentially
flowing to capital rather than labor.

articles.title: Gpt-6 astra, looped transformers, and hidden reasoning
articles.description:
GPT-6 Astra is a very strong model, and it makes a particularly large
leap in computer use. The model likely uses a variant of the looped
transformer, which gives better modeling performance at a fixed
compute budget. Shorter reasoning traces are a side effect of more
intelligent models that make fewer mistakes and can access more
compute internally inside their architecture.

articles.title: Additional findings
articles.description:
A community of independent investigators has uncovered a number of
message boards that have been used by AI agents. This was achieved
with a range of techniques for circumventing the sandboxes used by the
agents. This post highlights notable findings from the investigation.
A link to a full list of the websites that contain activity generated
by rogue OpenAI agents is available in the article.

reduce resource costs while maintaining model ranking integrity.

articles.description:
The Accenture Gemini Enterprise Business Group is a joint unit from
Google Cloud and Accenture dedicated to sending engineers into
enterprises to help them better adopt Google's AI tools and services.
It is Google's latest foray into the increasingly competitive world of
forward-deployed engineers (FDEs). Google will train up to 1,000 of
Accenture's FDEs to work with enterprises and build custom AI
applications on the Gemini Enterprise platform. The organization will
live under Accenture.

articles.title: Data bottlenecks won't prevent an intelligence explosion
articles.description:
Data bottlenecks will slow, but not stop, an intelligence explosion
in AI. Future AI advancements will likely develop highly
sample-efficient learning algorithms, reducing the need for vast data
volumes. While improving data quality above human levels will be
challenging, it won't halt AI from automating most economic work.

articles.title: Apple unveils first foldable iphone with a20 pro chip
articles.description:
Apple unveiled the $1,999 iPhone Duo, its first foldable phone,
alongside the iPhone 18 Pro lineup powered by its new A20 Pro chip.
The launch also pushes Apple further into on-device AI, with expanded
Siri capabilities and a continued focus on privacy.

articles.title: Hp brings data-center ai infrastructure to the edge
articles.description:
HP is working with Red Hat and Nvidia on an enterprise AI platform
that can run production inference across devices, data centers, and
hybrid environments. The system combines HP hardware powered by Nvidia
Blackwell with Red Hat AI Factory for deployment and orchestration.

articles.title: Claude for microsoft 365
articles.description:
Claude for Microsoft 365 integrates Claude into Excel, PowerPoint,
Word, and Outlook with shared context across apps. Claude for Excel,
PowerPoint, and Word is now generally available on all paid Claude
plans, while Claude for Outlook is in beta. The offering emphasizes
reviewable edits, use of customer templates, and deployment through
existing cloud and compliance frameworks.

articles.title: The eval you cannot trust is your own
articles.description:
Enterprise AI evals fail when vendors can see POC test questions.
Teams need a permanently held-out eval that vendors never see. Google
DeepMind's double-blind frontier-model evaluation shows the model:
neither side saw the other's evaluation assets. Cleaner lab benchmarks
alone won't fix enterprise adoption failures.

articles.title: Every customer gets the same software. that's ending
articles.description:
AI will end the era of identical software for every customer by
making per-customer variants cheap to create and maintain. Vendors,
not open-source templates, will own these divergences, reviving
SAP-style customization without its historic migration cost. The
result will be the end of the common UI, where each customer uses a
recognizably different version of the same product.

articles.title: Open source is reshaping the ai infrastructure stack
articles.description:
AI infrastructure needs stronger reproducibility and control across
hardware, drivers, models, and data than Kubernetes alone provides.
Governance and bandwidth constraints are expected to push more AI
workloads toward hybrid and distributed environments.

articles.title: Google says enterprise ai assistants are moving beyond chat
articles.description:
Google was named a Leader in Gartner's inaugural Magic Quadrant for
Enterprise AI Assistants. Google says the category is shifting from
basic copilots toward agents that connect enterprise systems and
automate multi-step workflows. 

🤝

articles.description:
They're building their own tools to run their operations. OverAI
enables teams of any size and skill set to build and share AI-powered
tools, with data and user management that stay with IT. Start free
with $200 in credit.

articles.title: Accenture deal
articles.description:
Google Cloud and Accenture have launched the Accenture Gemini
Enterprise Business Group, a joint unit to embed engineers in
enterprises to accelerate adoption of Google's AI tools. Google will
train up to 1,000 Accenture forward-deployed engineers to build custom
applications on the Gemini Enterprise platform. The move is aimed at
closing an enterprise deployment gap as Google holds about 6% of US
enterprise AI spending, far behind Anthropic and OpenAI.

articles.description:
Red Hat and Rafay published a reference architecture that lets cloud
providers turn distributed GPU infrastructure into multi-tenant
sovereign AI services. The design covers self-service provisioning,
governance, metering, and isolated GPU environments.

articles.description:

agents access to shared organizational knowledge, business logic, and
live data. It also introduced team-level Agent Memory and integrations
for Slack, Teams, Zoom, and Google Meet.

articles.title: Lightbits targets the kv-cache bottleneck in ai inference
articles.description:
Lightbits unveiled Inferra, a KV-cache orchestration engine designed
to improve GPU utilization for long-context and multi-session
inference workloads. The company says the storage layer can help AI
infrastructure providers serve larger workloads without adding GPUs at
the same rate.

articles.title: Ai audit trails: the missing piece of enterprise ai adoption
articles.description:
Enterprise AI adoption requires tamper-evident audit trails that
automatically capture prompts, outputs, model versions, guardrails,
and human approvals to prove what AI did and who authorized it.

articles.title: Alteryx connects governed enterprise analytics to ai agents
articles.description:
Alteryx added conversational analytics, agent-building tools, an MCP
server, and ChatGPT integration so companies can expose governed
datasets and workflows directly to AI agents.

articles.title: Apple unveils its first foldable, the iphone duo
articles.description:
Apple has unveiled the iPhone Duo, its first foldable. Featuring a
7.6-inch inner display, a 5.4-inch outer screen, Touch ID, and an
adaptable iOS 27 interface designed for split-screen and half-folded
use, the wider device supports paired apps and tabletop video.
Counterpoint estimates it could capture up to 25% of the foldable
market by year-end, despite foldables accounting for less than 2% of
global smartphone shipments.

articles.title: Adobe is building a new ai design tool called project oasis
articles.description:
Project Oasis is Adobe's new web-based graphic design app, described
as a modern workspace with brand-aware AI built into the workflow. A
September 7 community post invites agency, freelance, and in-house
designers into early access, with a private feedback channel and an
NDA. Pricing, a full feature list, and a launch date remain
undisclosed.

articles.title: Bytedance is preparing a real-time spatial video model
articles.description:
ByteDance is developing a real-time spatial video model, built on its
Seedance system for Pico headsets. The model would generate
interactive 3D worlds in the cloud at around 20 frames per second with
roughly 50 milliseconds of latency, shifting rendering costs away from
device hardware. A launch could come as soon as next month, part of
ByteDance's broader 2026 push to lead in world models alongside $30
billion in secured loans and up to $70 billion in planned AI
infrastructure spending.

articles.title: Principles for building a design engineering practice
articles.description:
Six principles set the quality bar for a design engineering practice
being built at DuckDuckGo, where the team is still small and hiring
its second member. They cover understanding problems before making,
owning the experience past handoff, making trust effortless, reducing
scope rather than quality, finishing every state, and making craft
repeatable. Moving fast by making less, better is the one expected to
be tested most often.

articles.title: Designing product simplicity for the agentic ai era
articles.description:
Microsoft's CoreAI portals all sat on Fluent 2 and still felt
disjointed, because shared components did not prevent teams from
inventing different navigation, layouts, and flows. The CoreAI Design
System, forked from Foundry's work, ships guidance through both a
Figma library and an experimental MCP server so coding agents can
consume it too. 

 SOME PEOPLE ARE WORRIED APPLE'S FOLDING IPHONE DESIGN COULD PRESENT A

articles.title: Brand new health risk
articles.description:
Rumors suggest Apple's upcoming foldable iPhone will be noticeably
heavier than a standard iPhone, prompting concerns from a physical
therapist that the added weight and grip could increase thumb and hand
strain during prolonged use. Similar complaints have already been
reported by some owners of existing foldable phones, though the risk
is mainly associated with repetitive, extended use. Experts recommend
taking breaks every 30–45 minutes, stretching your hands, and
putting the phone down regularly to reduce fatigue and injury.

articles.title: Your agents are only as good as your data context
articles.description:
Agents get only data points, so a sales spike from a limited-time
promotion reads to them as a lasting trend worth producing more stock
for. A semantic layer supplies the missing translation, defining what
each column and event means in the words teams actually use in Slack
and meetings. Amplitude's own layer took its agent to correct answers
80 to 90 percent of the time, with custom instructions closing the
rest.

articles.title: Accordion icons: which ones work best?
articles.description:
NN/g research finds real differences between carets, arrows, and plus
icons on accordions, with the caret the safest choice and the most
tapped. With no icon at all, users expect the item to open a new page.
Split menus, where label and icon trigger different actions, cause the
most mistakes and are best avoided. 

 RAGGED EDGE'S REBRAND FOR FINANCIAL APP TABBY TAKES A PLAYFUL

articles.title: Approach
articles.description:
Tabby has unveiled a new brand identity by Ragged Edge alongside the
launch of Tabby Cash, replacing typical fintech visuals with
hand-drawn characters, custom bilingual typography, and authentic
photography to emphasize financial confidence and approachability. The
redesign is built around the idea of helping users take control of
their money, using playful visual elements and motion to make everyday
financial tasks feel more engaging without sacrificing clarity. After
debuting across the app, website, and digital channels, the refreshed
identity is now expanding into physical advertising across the UAE.

articles.title: Powergate software expert

articles.title: An organizational second brain
articles.description:
Meta describes an AI “second brain” built from structured,
auditable knowledge files rather than retrained model weights. The
system separates facts from procedures, turns expert feedback into
regression-tested updates, and reduces assessment work from days to
minutes while keeping changes transparent and reversible.

articles.title: Gpt-6 astra, looped transformers, and hidden reasoning
articles.description:
This article surveys recent work on recurrent-depth transformers,
where the same blocks are reused across multiple passes to reduce
parameter memory without reducing computation. The piece also examines
hidden reasoning and what these architectural choices imply for the
next generation of language models.

articles.title: Reasoning prefills on a few open models, v1.1
articles.description:
This experiment seeds open models' reasoning channels with the
opening portion of a GPT-5.5 Pro trace, then measures overlap with the
teacher's visible answer. Qwen3.8 A95B showed the largest increase,
suggesting that it may have learned from GPT-5.5 Pro or a closely
related model.

articles.title: The llm architecture problem
articles.description:
Next-token prediction optimizes for the shortest path to an answer,
not necessarily the best or safest one. Prompts and safeguards cannot
fully solve this architectural limitation, and it's worth exploring
alternatives such as world models.

articles.title: Ai is now out-working the people who build it
articles.description:
This roundup argues that frontier-lab coding agents are already
performing substantial research and engineering work alongside their
creators. It pairs claims about rapid growth in multi-agent usage and
benchmark performance with a reminder that public concern about AI
remains high.

articles.title: Production-grade infrastructure for conversational ai
articles.description:

connection. Agora's Conversational AI platform runs on SDRTN® — the
same ultra-low latency network carrying 80B+ monthly minutes,
globally. Build AI agents and voice-enabled applications with fully
managed, real-time infrastructure. 

Get 300 free minutes [12]

articles.title: Pi-desktop: a local-first workspace for coding agents
articles.description:
PI-Desktop is an early-preview desktop workspace for coding agents
that keeps projects, sessions, reviews, and permissions in one
local-first app. It supports multiple model providers, MCP, skills,
subagents, and plugins, while routing privileged work through a
reviewable permission layer.

articles.title: Teamai cli: shared context for every coding agent
articles.description:
Tencent's TeamAI CLI distributes a team's skills, rules, MCP
configuration, and project knowledge across tools such as Codex,
Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode. Its shared Git-based harness keeps
agent guidance synchronized and adds optional retrieval, learning
capture, and codebase knowledge features.

articles.title: React 19.3
articles.description:
React 19.3 introduces View Transitions, Fragment refs, Trusted Types
support, and new React Server Components capabilities. The release
also improves transition scheduling and delivers a broad set of fixes
across React, React DOM, and server rendering.

articles.title: Agents on rails: fable 5.1 & glm 5.3 flash
articles.description:
A Rails-focused benchmark reports that Claude Fable 5.1 matched Opus
5 on accuracy at a lower cost and faster median runtime. The post also
identifies the previously anonymous “ox-alpha” model as GLM 5.3
Flash, positioning it as a low-cost option with competitive benchmark
results.

articles.title: How gpt-5.6 sol helps run quantum computing experiments
articles.description:
GPT-5.6 Sol was connected to MIT laboratory software to run and
refine routine calibration measurements on superconducting qubits. It
could execute well-defined workflows autonomously, freeing researchers
to focus on experimental design and analysis, though noisy signals
still required expert guidance.

articles.title: Better ai code comment detector
articles.description:
A rebuilt, browser-based classifier distinguishes human-written from
AI-generated code comments using stylistic features such as
part-of-speech and character n-grams. It reports calibrated confidence
rather than a bare verdict, achieving 77% balanced accuracy in
cross-validation and stronger results on a small real-world test set.

articles.title: Tailwind labs is joining shopify
articles.description:
Tailwind Labs is joining Shopify to give Tailwind CSS a stable
long-term home.

articles.title: Copperhead: cursor for circuit boards
articles.description:
Copperhead is an open-source AI engineering platform for designing,
verifying, and shipping circuit boards from a KiCad repository.

articles.title: An early look at expo modules 2.0
articles.description:
Expo Modules 2.0 replaces its native-module DSL with annotated Swift
and Kotlin classes, reducing boilerplate while making type information
available at build time.

articles.title: Archspec: executable architecture specs for rails
articles.description:
ArchSpec is a deterministic Rails architecture linter for enforcing
codebase boundaries as more code is written by agents.

articles.title: Everything to know
articles.description:
Apple's first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, starts at $1,999. The
device expands to a 7.6-inch screen when unfolded, and a 5.4-inch
screen when used as a conventional handset. It comes in two colors:
Star White and Night Sky. More details on the device, as well as
Apple's other recent releases, are available in the article.

articles.title: Apple takes on ai wearables with always-listening watch features
articles.description:
The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra models have new Audio
Intelligence tools that use ambient listening to take high-level notes
of wearers' conversations throughout the day. The devices will also
have a Live Recap function that can show a transcription of what was
said in a live conversation in the last 15 seconds and be able to
listen to important sounds, such as a crying baby, doorbells, or
sirens. These features will not create or store recordings, and Apple
will not be able to access the raw audio. They will be available to
test in English later this year. The improved Siri is being rolled out
on watchOS 27 in beta on September 14.

articles.title: Genome language models can design cancer vaccines
articles.description:
Modern cancer-vaccine design involves identifying mutations,
predicting presentation, predicting immunogenicity, ranking targets,
and designing RNA. However, biology is complicated, and whether a
target makes a good vaccine candidate depends on all kinds of
information. This makes cancer vaccines an unusually direct test of
whether AI models can take what it has learned from biology and apply
that knowledge to design a medicine for one particular human being.

articles.title: Scenarios for our economic future
articles.description:
It is unknown yet whether AI will lead to unprecedented growth or
widespread unemployment. Anthropic's Economics team built a model to
understand how AI might affect jobs, growth, and unemployment in the
US in the coming years. The model found that AI will lead to adverse
impacts on wages and job prospects for knowledge workers in scenarios
where growth is faster than anything in economic history, and in those
scenarios, the challenge will be making sure wealth is broadly shared.
The answer will depend on how AI affects all the tasks that make up
the economy, the new tasks it creates, and how fast AI takes on this
work.

articles.title: Human-in-the-loop won't save your ai security program
articles.description:
When approval fatigue turns sign-offs into rubber stamps, you need
more than good judgment to keep AI secure. Gray Swan's eBook [13] lays
out 5 governance implications for AI security, along with 3 questions
every board should be asking right now. Get your copy [13]

articles.title: Multimodal models need video. we froze time to give it to them
articles.description:
PostHog's Replay Vision lets models view session recordings. This
post looks at how PostHog built the tool and how it implemented a
method for the model to actually see replays. It covers how PostHog
built a custom rasterizer that runs hundreds of concurrent jobs across
many pods. The custom rasterizer has so far rasterized more than 370
years of recordings into roughly 3.5 million videos since it was
deployed in production in March.

articles.title: Tailwind labs is joining shopify
articles.description:
Tailwind is joining Shopify, one of the first companies operating at
scale to see the potential of Tailwind CSS and start building with it.
Shopify has invested in making sure Tailwind is actively maintained
and will continue to provide a stable long-term home for the project.
Nothing will change with Tailwind CSS or any of Tailwind's other open
source projects, but the project will no longer try to grow its
business. All existing customers will maintain access to their
products, but Tailwind has closed signups for new customers.

articles.title: Automattic's board forces ceo matt mullenweg into leave of absence
articles.description:
Automattic's board has put founder and CEO Matt Mullenweg on a leave
of absence against his will. The company's Chief Financial Officer,
Mark Davies, had conspired with other board members to put Mullenweg
on a paid leave of absence. Davies is now acting as interim CEO.
Mullenweg remains the leader of the WordPress project, and the
company's teams, priorities, and work will continue as planned. It is
unclear why the board took this action. Mullenweg remains on the board
of directors.

articles.title: Cracks in the ai thesis part 2
articles.description:
The price of AI is coming down. However, volume growth may not be
large enough to counteract the effective decline in prices. The models
driving volume increases are relatively cheap, standard models. These
trends do not appear to be driven by the adoption of open-source
models or Chinese models.

Purchasers of open source work should be able to check whether a

articles.description:
OpenAI heard that some Millennium Prize problems had been solved
using large language models and saw it as an opportunity to
demonstrate the power of its latest model without regard for the teams
who had been working on the problem already.

articles.title: Anthropic researchers raise alarm over ai acceleration
articles.description:
There are massive implications of a race towards superintelligence,
and not enough of Congress is focusing on them.

articles.title: Postgres
articles.description:
Tom Lane, a committer for 25 of Postgres' 30 years, walks through the
architectural bets that held: process-per-connection for code
simplicity, write-ahead logging in 8.0 that turned it from a plaything
into a serious database, and MVCC pushing maintenance work into
background vacuum. He credits Berkeley's liberal license for the
project surviving where its contemporaries did not, names version 13
the buggiest release, and says he would delete partitioning given the
chance. 

 BUILT FOR RELIABILITY: HOW AMERICAN EXPRESS PROCESSES PAYMENTS AT

articles.title: Scale
articles.description:
American Express uses cells as complete payment-processing failure
domains: microservices, databases, DNS, and reference data are local,
while dynamic transactions are routed to the cell that owns their
state. The design trades global coordination for controlled failure
scope and deliberately rejects transactions when consistency cannot be
established.

articles.title: Cloudfloe's query engine in a celld cell
articles.description:
Cloudfloe is a web interface for querying Iceberg data on S3 with
DuckDB. This experiment tested whether a stateful, serverless-style
cell could replace a per-query container: DuckDB WebAssembly read a
37,537-row Iceberg table in 148 ms, but cold or woken cells took
250–320 ms and retained most of their memory. Keeping the connection
warm cut repeat queries to about 3 ms, making lifecycle policy, not
raw startup, the core design tradeoff.

articles.title: The ai data sprawl
articles.description:
Non-technical staff now write billions of lines of analytics code.
The problem is where it lives: random context, porous permissions, and
output scattered across one-off chats, Slack pastes, and someone's
laptop. With no record of which table an agent grabbed or which filter
it dropped, the only feedback loop left is people disagreeing.

articles.title: 5 cdc tools and the tradeoffs you should know
articles.description:
CDC evaluation should start with failure behavior, not connector
counts. Compare capture method, initial snapshots and backfills,
schema evolution, delivery semantics, observability, deployment model,
and who owns recovery. A production proof needs representative data
and a broken-destination test, especially for type fidelity and
duplicate handling.

articles.title: Jitter is the cheapest reliability fix you are not using
articles.description:
Distributed systems synchronise themselves without being told to:
shared events such as deploys, cache flushes, or connection loss turn
independent workloads into recurring load spikes. Add jitter to
initial retries, TTL refreshes, heartbeats, token renewals, and
scheduled work. This preserves average load while preventing retry
storms from repeatedly hitting a recovering dependency in lockstep.

articles.title: Kestra 2.0: a new engine, workers anywhere, and flows as agent tools
articles.description:
Kestra is an open-source orchestration platform for scheduling and
operating data, infrastructure, and business workflows. Its 2.0 LTS
release separates control and data planes so workers can run across
regions, clouds, or private networks over outbound-only connections.
It also exposes flows as MCP tools for agents, decouples queue and
storage choices, and includes migration tooling for 1.x users. 

 FILAMENT (GITHUB REPO) [15] 

 Filament replicates data from sources to sinks with full,
incremental, or CDC modes, verifying every bounded batch on both sides
of the write and advancing checkpoints only after success. Sources,
sinks, state storage, and event transport are all swappable. 

 JUPYTERGIS 0.16: COLLABORATIVE STORY MAPS AND REMOTE GEOSPATIAL

articles.title: Workflows
articles.description:
JupyterGIS 0.16 adds real-time collaborative story maps, lazy tile
rendering for remote openEO workflows, and native GeoZarr and
GeoPackage support. Declarative symbology and Xarray tiling keep
visualizations reproducible while allowing large geospatial datasets
to stay remote instead of being materialized locally.

articles.title: Why spotify is not using bayesian a/b testing
articles.description:
Bayesian experimentation is not one method but a choice of prior,
likelihood, and stopping rule. Spotify shows that common flat-prior
posterior thresholds can reproduce frequentist peeking, while Bayes
factors can control false positives under optional stopping. Choose
guarantees for the experiment program first, then the inference
configuration.

Referencing the same CTE twice tests whether the optimiser
materialises the result.
