Building for the model hardware standard
articles.description:
Anthropic's Model Hardware Standard (MHS) extends MCP-style agent
interoperability from software into physical devices, creating new
safety challenges where unreliable or repeated commands can cause
real-world damage.

articles.title: Special offer for tldr
articles.description:
Agents are smarter when they can search the web. But Google doesn't
offer an API for web search results... so how are AI companies doing
it?

Meet the worst-kept secret in the AI industry: the SerpApi web search
API [4]:

👉 Scrape Google and other search engines (including AI overviews,
Maps, Local, Shopping, and Knowledge Graph)

👉 Integrate with a dead-simple GET request that any agent can make.

👉 Used by NVIDIA, Adobe, Shopify, and even the United Nations.

Right now, TLDR readers GET 3 MONTHS AT 50% OFF, or start with 250
FREE CREDITS/MONTH [4].

Claim your savings [4]

📱

articles.title: Research acceleration: the view inside openai
articles.description:
OpenAI believes that Artificial General Intelligence must be
democratically governed for it to benefit all humanity. This can only
happen through an informed public debate on the capabilities, risks,
and safeguards of highly capable AI systems. The company has released
details of its progress towards Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) in
recent months. It plans to continue to be transparent about its
progress with RSI and believes that other companies should be required
to publicly track their progress as well.

articles.title: Tim cook's ceo-like pay package shows he isn't going anywhere
articles.description:
Tim Cook remains a powerful center of gravity at Apple. He will play
an especially crucial role in certain areas, such as the company's
dealings with the US and China, and its handling of the memory
shortage. Cook will get a base salary of $2 million, twice the typical
base salary of senior vice presidents and members of the C-suite. He
will also receive cash bonuses and stock units that vest over time.
The salary clearly shows that Cook's role will be very active.

articles.title: Travis kalanick's atoms might be getting into the robotaxi business
articles.description:
Atoms, founded by Uber founder Travis Kalanick, is reportedly
preparing for a hiring and acquisition spree. The company is also in
discussions with Uber about how Uber can use Atoms' robotaxi
technology. Uber has invested $100 million in Atoms. Kalanick has been
cagey about his plans for the startup, but the recent moves could make
it a major player in the autonomous vehicle industry.

articles.title: The curiously playable universe
articles.description:
A domain becomes playable when enough of its complexity can be
compressed into a state where there is some reasonably stable
repertoire of actions, interactions can be repeated, outcomes provide
feedback about better and worse play, and the environment is
stationary enough that lessons learned yesterday remain useful
tomorrow. None of these conditions need to be perfect, as playability
is a matter of degree. Far more of reality than we have previously
expected can be turned into a game. Once something can be turned into
a game, then it's possible to create a system that can beat it.

articles.title: Live briefing: evaluating glm-5.3 for production
articles.description:
GLM-5.3 lifts Terminal-Bench 3.0 from GLM-5.2's 4.6% to 28.3%, and
Flash is smaller and often enough. Both on Baseten Model APIs.
Artificial Analysis and Baseten discuss benchmarking each against your
tasks and serving them in production. Tuesday, 11 AM PT.

Save your seat [10]

articles.title: I trust my coding agents with production secrets now
articles.description:
Security is always a productivity-risk tradeoff. Not giving access to
agents can slow things down significantly. Frontier models are getting
better and better at distinguishing real from malicious instructions
in the content they read. We may end up trusting agents with access
more than humans as models improve.

articles.title: Terraform in lean 4: if it compiles, it will likely deploy
articles.description:
infra is an infrastructure-as-code tool that does what Terraform
does. Users declare what resources they want, and infra looks at what
their cloud accounts actually contain and reconciles the difference.
This post details how its developer created the tool in two weekends
in Lean 4, the problems it solves, and how the developer solved these
problems.

articles.title: Alignment
articles.description:
OpenAI's president and co-founder, Greg Brockman, dropped out of
college in 2010 to join Stripe. He eventually rose to become the
company's CTO. He left in 2015 and co-founded OpenAI, where he served
as CTO, and after a few years, he is now the company's president. This
post features an interview with Brockman recorded before the
announcement of Astra. It covers Brockman's background, the ChatGPT
launch, OpenAI's place in the value chain, the company's commitment to
alignment, the Hugging Face incident, and more.
articles.section: AN INTERVIEW WITH OPENAI PRESIDENT GREG BROCKMAN ABOUT ASTRA AND

articles.title: The loop closes
articles.description:
AI models are now capable of taking a request from Slack and then
building a feature from end-to-end, with humans just having to click
'merge' or 'deploy' at the end. There's not really much left for
humans to do. Humans are still better at absorbing, parsing, and
sharing context with each other. However, once that can be automated,
the loop will finally be closed, and there will be nothing left to do
but to pay the bill.
articles.section: AN INTERVIEW WITH OPENAI PRESIDENT GREG BROCKMAN ABOUT ASTRA AND

articles.title: We taught a fruit fly to hear human emotion
articles.description:
Researchers built a neural network from a map of a fly brain and then
trained it to recognize emotion in human voices.

articles.title: Can tesla cybercab actually kill uber? day-two pricing from austin
articles.description:
Real-world tests show that the Cybercab has competitive pricing, but
currently has a much longer wait time compared to competitors. 

 IPHONE ULTRA PRODUCTION HITTING JUST 'A FEW HUNDRED' A DAY, SAYS

articles.title: Nikkei
articles.description:
The iPhone Ultra's production is slow due to how difficult the device
is to build. 

 BETWEEN THE GRAPH AND THE SILICON: INSIDE THE APPLE NEURAL ENGINE

articles.title: Compiler
articles.description:
Apple publicly exposes the Apple Neural Engine through Core ML, while
the compiler, program format, driver, firmware, and much of the
machinery underneath it remains undocumented.

articles.title: I left the mac after 12 years. omarchy made computers fun again
articles.description: Omarchy is an opinionated Linux distribution built for AI agents.

articles.title: Gpt-6 astra and the fourth exponential
articles.description:
Demand for AI semiconductors is likely to surge with agent computer
tool use, just as it did with the chatbot, reasoning, and agentic
coding demand waves.

articles.title: Portal by spotify cut my claude code token usage by 90%
articles.description:
Most of what a coding agent does is I/O rather than reasoning, such
as reading five files to answer a question about one method. Spotify
routed that work to two declarative Portal modes, bulk-reader and
code-writer, both running Gemini 2.5 Flash on an ephemeral runtime,
and reserved the frontier model for problems that need it. A quarter
of engineering leaders already spend $200 to $500 per developer per
month on tokens, and some are past $2,000.

articles.title: Zgateway: learnings from putting a proxy in front of zippydb
articles.description:
This post explains why Meta put a managed proxy tier in front of
ZippyDB, its massive key-value store. The real lesson is that proxies
can turn client-fleet sprawl into a controllable infrastructure
boundary: connection fan-in drops roughly 97–98%, batching and
coalescing happen across clients, excess traffic from noisy tenants
can be selectively rejected, and failover and load-balancing policy
can change centrally without waiting for a million clients to update. 

 FROM S3 TO GPU IN ONE COPY: RETHINKING DATA LOADING FOR ML TRAINING
(50 MINUTE VIDEO) [6] 

 Vortex is an open-source columnar format designed to stream training
data from S3 to GPUs with minimal copying. Cascading lightweight
encodings, layout-aware pruning, and zero-copy memory paths target CPU
and NVMe bottlenecks, giving ML platforms a way to keep expensive
accelerators fed without converting everything upfront.

articles.title: Context, semantics, and ontology: a primer for the agentic era
articles.description:
Semantic layers define business metrics, context layers provide
supporting knowledge, and ontologies describe entities and their
relationships. Together, they help AI agents interpret data, but
people still need to keep that knowledge accurate and current.

articles.title: Context protocol
articles.description:
AI analytics can fail when agents generate free-form SQL against
inconsistent warehouse metadata. Governed systems should route
repeated questions through verified semantic-layer tools,
parameterized calls, and explicit refusal paths, reserving open-ended
SQL for cases humans can inspect. Maintaining definitions is the hard
part regardless of model upgrades. 

 ONE ROUND TRIP BEATS A THOUSAND, AND YOUR BATCH API PROBABLY IS NOT

articles.title: Batching
articles.description:
A 100,000-row Postgres load took 41 minutes because each row became
its own statement and transaction; COPY cut the same work to 11
seconds. Real batching removes network round trips, parse overhead,
and WAL flush barriers, while driver flags and transaction chunking
prevent bulk APIs from silently behaving row by row.

articles.title: Pre-release of polars 2.0
articles.description:
Polars 2.0 makes the streaming engine the default for lazy queries,
aiming for much lower memory use and faster execution while accepting
that row order is not guaranteed unless requested. It also tightens
type coercion and concatenation behavior, and removes deprecated APIs
so data mismatches fail earlier instead of hiding in production
pipelines.

articles.title: Apache kafka vs apache iggy: same log, different engine
articles.description:
Apache Iggy is a Rust streaming engine with Kafka-like logs and
consumer groups, optimized around thread-per-core execution and modern
Linux I/O. It looks promising for low-latency single-node or simpler
deployments, but Kafka still has the deeper production story for
replication, exactly-once semantics, compaction, and multi-region
operations.

articles.title: Sail 0.7: stateless compute, durable job state
articles.description:
Sail 0.7 pushes Spark-style intermediate state toward object storage
with blocking shuffle and checkpoint support. It persists shuffle
outputs as compressed Arrow streams so downstream task regions retry
without cascading upstream failures, while checkpointing keeps
iterative jobs from rebuilding long query plans. The design targets
stateless workers, smaller clusters, and better resilience under
preemption.

articles.title: Language interfaces for databases
articles.description:
Text-to-SQL assumes users ask questions that a single query can
answer, when in practice they bring problems that need a sequence of
queries with reasoning over the intermediate results. The paper
proposes data investigations as the replacement paradigm and presents
D2, a prototype that autonomously searches, reasons over, and collects
data to reach evidence-backed conclusions, benchmarked on a Murder
Mystery dataset.

articles.title: When the source of truth is a google sheet
articles.description:
Warner Music Group turned a hand-edited anti-counterfeit tracking
spreadsheet into governed Databricks tables without taking the
spreadsheet away from operators. The pipeline handles shifting tabs,
renamed headers, late edits, row fingerprints, and full-overwrite
loads so executive reporting can trust a messy business interface that
people actually use.

articles.title: Getting ready for postgresql 19
articles.description:
PostgreSQL 19 Beta 3 adds temporal SQL, idempotent upsert-and-fetch,
IGNORE NULLS window behavior, concurrent repacking, DDL extraction
helpers, SQL/PGQ graph querying, and stricter NULL handling. 

 DUCKFLIGHT (GITHUB REPO) [17] 

 DuckFlight lets PostgreSQL tools and Arrow Flight SQL clients read
and write the same live DuckDB database without a separate service or
copying data.

articles.title: Gpt-6 astra
articles.description:
OpenAI GPT-6 Astra is the company's most capable broadly deployed
model and the first to reach the Critical cybersecurity level under
its Preparedness Framework. The system card said Astra is more robust
to jailbreaks and prompt injections than GPT-5.6 Sol, but noted it is
also better at controlling its own chain of thought and could evade
monitors under adversarial conditions.

articles.title: Grok bot for enterprise
articles.description:
Grok Bot is now available for enterprises. Grok and Cursor Enterprise
customers have free usage for the next two weeks. Users can invite
their whole organization, including people without an existing seat.
Each user's work in Grok Bot runs in its own secure and isolated
environment, separate from every other user. A Bot has no access by
default and reaches only the accounts you sign it into.

articles.title: Nvidia confirms hugging face acquisition for $12.93 billion
articles.description:
Nvidia confirmed it has acquired Hugging Face, which hosts three
million models and serves over 18 million developers, for $12.93
billion. Jensen Huang said the platform will stay open and Nvidia
compute will not be required to build or deploy on it.

articles.title: Microsoft releases mai-transcribe-2
articles.description:
Microsoft released MAI-Transcribe-2, a speech recognition model with
diarization, configurable transcription styles, and word-level
timestamps that it says beats Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, GPT-Transcribe,
and Whisper V3-Large.

articles.title: From safety research prompt to cross-model universal jailbreak
articles.description:
A MATS researcher found that a synthetic transcript generation prompt
could be turned into a universal jailbreak template that hit 84-100%
attack success on the nine most vulnerable of 23 models tested, with
only recent Anthropic models and Meta Muse Spark 1.1 never fully
broken.

articles.title: Openai's gpt-6 astra on arc-agi-3
articles.description:
GPT-6 Astra scored 62.7% on ARC-AGI-3 Semi-Private with the standard
harness and 99.9% with a provider adapter harness, using fewer actions
than the median human on 96% of levels. It turned unfamiliar
environments into compact symbolic world models, representing game
mechanics as logical rules and inventing its own shorthand to track
state and plan.

articles.title: Ai, tools and transformation
articles.description:
AI presents the potential to automate countless tasks within
companies, offering software that's dynamic and generative with
minimal coding required. Despite this, organizational change remains
challenging, as identifying tasks suitable for automation is not
always obvious, and widespread adoption takes time and effort.
Additionally, while AI will expand existing and new vertical
applications, the integration and impact vary depending on how
companies choose to adapt to this transformative technology. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: Still slow?
articles.description:
AI adoption is nearly universal, but development bottlenecks like
planning, review, and testing remain. In an Atlassian survey [12], 74%
of engineering leaders say AI accelerates code generation, but 78%
still review AI-generated code through traditional peer review. To
tackle these bottlenecks, 88% of leaders know they need a governed
engineering system of record. Only 19% say they've built one. Here's
how to close that gap. [12]

articles.title: Runway's gwm worlds 2
articles.description:
Runway's GWM Worlds 2 is a world model that generates interactive
environments in real time at 720p, 24 fps, with 48 kHz audio. Users
steer the world with text actions and camera motion, and sessions
continue from each input with no preset length. 

 MICROSOFT AI'S MAI-TRANSCRIBE-2 UNDERCUTS OPENAI, GOOGLE, AND

articles.title: Elevenlabs on price and speed
articles.description:
MAI-Transcribe-2 is a speech-recognition model that Microsoft says is
faster, more accurate, and cheaper than anything its competitors
currently sell. It is priced at 10 cents per hour of audio. The model
transcribes audio in 60 languages. Microsoft's strategy seems to be to
build its own frontier-class models one modality at a time, then
steadily swap them into products that once ran on OpenAI's technology.

articles.title: Give your coding agents a memory you own
articles.description:
funes introduces a durable memory layer for coding agents that allows
them to retain and recall session histories across different machines
and agents like Claude Code, Codex, pi, and Hermes. It enables
contextual memory storage and retrieval without external dependencies,
using local indexing and embedding.

articles.title: Ai is making us build too much
articles.description:
AI's ability to rapidly produce code and governance structures like
in Steve Yegge's Wheelhouse leads to over-engineering, making
creations easy but maintaining them costly. The agents in Wheelhouse
have outpaced their intended productive goals, leading to
inefficiencies as more complexity is layered on their work. AI's
removal of traditional economic pressures encourages continuous
creation, often without adding meaningful value, as evidenced by the
imbalance between production and valuable outcomes.

articles.title: The incumbents are coming
articles.description:
Incumbent systems of record gain value as agents act through their
data and workflows, but vertical AI can still win by owning the
broader job. Durable advantage comes from cross-system context, expert
feedback, evals, and learning loops.

articles.title: Can your agents read your docs?
articles.description:
FYI: Mintlify has a super-useful free tool that shows you whether AI
agents can understand your docs. Get a free report in minutes +
actionable steps to improve. Score your docs [18] 

 CEREBRAS MODEL CATALOG (WEBSITE) [19] 

 This page lets users browse all of the models currently available on
Cerebras' public endpoints.

articles.title: Google introduces weathernext 3
articles.description:
WeatherNext 3 is Google DeepMind's most accurate global weather
model, adding real-time satellite data, hourly refreshes, higher
resolution, precise precipitation forecasting, and clean energy
variables. 

 ACCEL REPORTEDLY IN TALKS TO LEAD $1B ROUND FOR THINKING MACHINES AT

articles.title: $40b valuation
articles.description:
The new round values Thinking Machines below the $50 billion
valuation that it reportedly sought to secure late last year.

articles.title: Nvidia personal ai router (pair)
articles.description:
NVIDIA PAIR connects AI app and agent workflows to a single local
endpoint for routing inference across NVIDIA DGX Spark, Windows
systems with RTX, and macOS devices.

articles.title: Wtf is dime, the mystery openai headset
articles.description:
Dime, a mysterious silver headset tied through leaks, sightings, ads,
and codenames to OpenAI, remains officially denied by the company. 

 WE JUST GOT OUR FIRST REAL LOOK AT AI PCS WITH NVIDIA'S RTX SPARK

articles.title: ‘superchip'
articles.description:
Nvidia unveiled RTX Spark-powered laptops and mini PCs at IFA 2026,
highlighting their capability to handle AI workflows locally.

articles.title: Microsoft teams, outlook fail to launch on arm-based windows pcs
articles.description:
Teams and New Outlook can crash or fail to launch on ARM-based
Windows 11 devices after recent security updates, particularly on
newly imaged machines missing Microsoft Store updates. Microsoft
recommends updating the Auto Super Resolution Package as a temporary
workaround while it prepares a permanent fix. 

 SALESFORCE SIMPLIFIES ITS EDITIONS BY BUNDLING SLACK, SECURITY, AI,

articles.title: And analytics
articles.description:
Salesforce has introduced new Core, Advanced, and Max editions that
package Agentforce, Slack, Tableau Next, security capabilities, and
support into fewer SKUs. The move reflects a broader push by SaaS
vendors to consolidate products into larger platform bundles rather
than selling each capability separately.

articles.title: Defying gravity: the system of record in the age of ai
articles.description:
AI is creating a new opportunity for startups to build systems of
record rather than merely lightweight systems of action. AI agents
require integrated, high-quality domain data, so businesses may
replace entrenched software systems, increasing market turnover and
expanding software vendors' potential from seat-based revenue to
automated labor and outcomes.

articles.title: Startup arr is less secure than ever, new research shows
articles.description:
Enterprise buyers are treating AI software very differently from
traditional SaaS: 77% of companies surveyed by Madrona re-evaluate AI
vendors every six months or continuously. That creates a “fast in,
fast out” buying model where even landing an enterprise contract may
no longer translate into durable recurring revenue.

articles.title: Why data sovereignty has become a strategic it priority
articles.description:
Data sovereignty is becoming less about simply knowing which region
hosts your data and more about retaining control when vendors,
regulations, infrastructure, or geopolitical conditions change.
Portability, operational independence, and avoiding concentration risk
should increasingly factor into architecture and vendor decisions. 

🤝

articles.title: Okta launches auth0 tools for ai agents & b2b logins
articles.description:
Okta has introduced new Auth0 capabilities for authenticating AI
agents, agent-led commerce, and enterprise B2B identity. The launch
also includes B2B Connect, which lets SaaS providers add enterprise
SSO, federation, and multi-tenant identity capabilities without
replacing their existing identity infrastructure. 

 THE EVOLUTION OF JFROG AI CATALOG: YOUR AI CONTROL PLANE FOR AGENTIC

articles.title: Development
articles.description:
JFrog says its AI Catalog has evolved from a secure model registry
into an AI control plane for governing models, MCP servers, skills,
plugins, and agent packages. The company presents semantic scanning,
shadow AI detection, governed registries, and runtime Agent Guard
enforcement as measures to prevent agents from consuming unapproved or
malicious assets across the Agentic Development Lifecycle.

articles.title: Backup plan
articles.description:
ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok experienced overlapping multi-hour outages
on Thursday, exposing a growing business-continuity problem as
companies automate more workflows around AI services. IT teams may
need to treat AI providers like other critical infrastructure, with
fallback models, documented manual workflows, and outage planning.

articles.title: Knowledge graph
articles.description:
NASA's People Analytics team built a People Knowledge Graph with
Memgraph, large language models, and secure AWS infrastructure to
connect employees, skills, projects, and organizational data. The
system supports expert discovery, project similarity analysis,
workforce insights, and a GraphRAG chatbot, while remaining under
development as NASA works to improve data quality, automation, and
scale.
articles.section: HOW NASA IS USING GRAPH TECHNOLOGY AND LLMS TO BUILD A PEOPLE

articles.title: When ai's human in the loop really isn't
articles.description:
Many organizations claim to have human oversight of AI when reviewers
can observe or flag decisions but cannot actually stop or override
them. Effective human-in-the-loop controls require the right
expertise, context, and authority, and need to be tested like any
other operational control.
articles.section: HOW NASA IS USING GRAPH TECHNOLOGY AND LLMS TO BUILD A PEOPLE

articles.title: Rootly automatically surfaces related past incidents in slack
articles.description:
Rootly's agent can now automatically post up to three relevant
historical incidents into an active Slack incident channel, including
why they match, severity, resolution time, and links to the previous
incident.

articles.title: Microsoft teams is moving to teams.cloud.microsoft
articles.description:
Microsoft is redirecting Teams web users to teams.cloud.microsoft,
with admins advised to ensure the new domain is allowed through
proxies, firewalls, and other network controls.

articles.title: Adobe brings image, video, and pdf creation directly into slack
articles.description:
Adobe for Slack brings image, video, and PDF creation into Slack,
letting Slackbot turn conversations and files into polished content
without leaving the workspace. Slackbot reads context from
conversations, Canvases, and shared files, then routes requests to
more than 70 connected Adobe tools. It requires a qualifying Slack
plan, Business+ or Enterprise+, plus a separate Adobe subscription.

articles.title: Iphone
articles.description:
Apple's upcoming foldable iPhone—widely expected to be called the
iPhone Ultra—will likely support MagSafe despite its extremely thin
design. If true, it would give Apple an advantage over Samsung's
foldables, which require cases for magnetic charging. Other rumored
features include a titanium body, an advanced crease-reducing hinge,
split-screen multitasking, and a price above $2,000. 

 IPHONE 18 PRO LEAKS SUGGEST PHOTOGRAPHERS ARE FINALLY GETTING THE
articles.section: APPLE MAY HAVE FOUND ROOM FOR MAGSAFE IN ITS IMPOSSIBLY THIN FOLDABLE

articles.title: Feature they've been waiting for
articles.description:
While the foldable iPhone Ultra is expected to dominate headlines,
the iPhone 18 Pro may be the more significant upgrade for
photographers thanks to a rumored variable-aperture camera lens that
could offer greater control over depth of field and image quality.
Combined with reports of a larger battery—up to 5,500 mAh on the Pro
Max—the device could become Apple's most capable photography-focused
iPhone yet, despite an otherwise familiar design.
articles.section: APPLE MAY HAVE FOUND ROOM FOR MAGSAFE IN ITS IMPOSSIBLY THIN FOLDABLE

articles.title: The most exciting and exhausting time to be a designer
articles.description:
Designers are now expected to be technically fluent in AI tooling and
world-class in craft at once, two full-time jobs whose bars are rising
together. The exhaustion has two sources: mistaking engineering
velocity for the right ruler, and a feed running on a constant drip of
weekend prototypes. Judgment is becoming the scarce resource, and the
designers who come out strongest will be rested enough to do it.

articles.title: Feeling ignored? here's what to do
articles.description:
Being ignored is one of the hardest situations designers face, but
rejection is rarely a dead end for the idea itself. Curiosity beats
the ego trap: ask whether others were rejected too, whether the timing
was right, and which tradeoffs the decision-maker had to balance.
People agree to ideas based on trust more than merit, so asking for
feedback beats cataloging a coworker's limitations.

articles.title: My view on design engineering
articles.description:
A design engineer's real role isn't simply being a designer who codes
or a developer with design skills—it's owning product coherence
across the gap between design and development. As AI makes creating
interfaces faster, the biggest challenge becomes maintaining
consistency, handling edge cases, refining interactions, and making
the countless judgment calls that determine whether a product feels
polished and intentional rather than fragmented. Ultimately, design
engineers act as translators, custodians of quality, and curators of
taste, ensuring the shipped product remains cohesive even as teams,
tools, and codebases evolve.

articles.title: Design systems that get used
articles.description:
Everyone plans for the difficulty of building a design system that
scales, and almost nobody plans for how hard it is to get people to
use one. Adoption comes down to three fits every time: the
organization, the products the system has to serve, and a team
equipped to sustain it. A technically excellent system misaligned with
those three sits unused, and the mistake costs twice: once to build it
and once to replace it.

articles.title: Spec driven design — from logic to style
articles.description:
In the later stages of Spec-Driven Design, designers first define a
visual direction through moodboards and written style guides, then use
AI agents to apply those styles to working prototypes, and finally
refine the results until they match the original vision. The process
emphasizes maintaining designer control: AI accelerates
implementation, but human judgment remains responsible for selecting
references, defining aesthetics, and ensuring quality. Refinement can
happen through prompting AI, editing designs in Figma with code-linked
workflows, or directly modifying code, with the goal of achieving a
polished, pixel-perfect product rather than accepting AI-generated
approximations. 

 RBL REBRANDS UNIVERSITY OF EAST ANGLIA AROUND ‘ORIGINAL BY NATURE'

articles.title: Ethos
articles.description:
The University of East Anglia has unveiled a new brand identity built
around the idea “Original by Nature,” aiming to reconnect the
institution with its history of independent thinking, creative
innovation, and environmental leadership. Developed after extensive
consultation with students, staff, and stakeholders, the rebrand
introduces a refined visual system inspired by the Norfolk landscape,
a stronger verbal identity, and a more cohesive strategy designed to
support the university's national and international ambitions.

articles.title: You)
articles.description:
Visitors decide whether they trust a site in about 0.05 seconds, long
before a single word gets read, and copy rarely undoes that snap
judgment. 

 THIS 3D ARTIST USES UNREAL ENGINE 5 AND BLENDER TO ACHIEVE INCREDIBLE

articles.title: Detail in heroic character designs
articles.description:
3D artist Andres Zambrano works in ZBrush, Maya, Substance Painter,
Marvelous Designer, Unreal Engine 5, and Blender, chasing handcrafted
detail and dramatic lighting on heroic figures.

articles.title: How turbopack chunks your javascript
articles.description:
Turbopack's chunker balances fewer requests against over-shipping
code by merging small chunks only within route chunk groups and
weighting single-page versus multi-page sessions. On nextjs.org, its
defaults reduced 96 requests to 38 while slightly cutting downloaded
JavaScript from 561.6 KiB to 554.8 KiB. Next.js 16.3 adds experimental
cache-aware component chunks, analytics-informed route priorities and
clusters, CommonJS tree shaking, a shared runtime, and a lighter
default runtime.

articles.title: The browser's main thread is expensive
articles.description:
The browser's main thread runs JavaScript, handles input, and
performs most of the rendering pipeline, leaving roughly 10ms of
usable time per frame on a 60Hz display. Any task over 50ms risks
visible jank. This guide shows how to split work around frame budgets,
batch noisy events with debounce or throttle, prioritize and defer
tasks, move animation to the compositor, use workers for atomic heavy
work, and eliminate unnecessary computation.

articles.title: Running llms in the browser with three.js
articles.description:
Three-LLM runs GPT-2, SmolLM2, Qwen, and Phi models locally in the
browser by translating their inference graphs into Three.js TSL
compute shaders on WebGPU, loading ordinary Hugging Face configs,
tokenizers, and SafeTensors without a server-side inference runtime.
This post walks through token generation, KV caches, architecture
differences, and the optimizations that mattered: one command
submission raised TinyStories decoding from about 120 to 566 tokens
per second.

articles.title: The asteroid currently hitting frontend web development
articles.description:
Coding agents are making years of specialized frontend knowledge far
less scarce. When Claude can correctly diagnose high
style-recalculation costs from a trace, the incentive to master or
teach every browser-performance detail changes. Judgment, taste, and
expert verification are expected to remain valuable for now, but
treating AI as an asteroid-sized disruption is more realistic than
ignoring how quickly frontend education and careers are being
reshaped.

articles.title: Vc isn't vc anymore — understanding the rise of cancer capital
articles.description:
A small group of giant, post-VC investment firms have become what the
author calls "Cancer Capital": multi-strategy funds that collect
enormous management fees, face less exposure to startup outcomes, and
use capital to concentrate political and economic power. He says this
shift has flipped the founder-investor relationship, distorted startup
incentives, enabled early cash-outs before public-market
accountability, and pushed risk onto pension funds and ordinary
investors.

OpenAI says the model stays within the authorized scope more reliably.
API pricing is $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output
tokens, with broader ChatGPT and API availability rolling out after a
limited launch. 

 WEBLLM (GITHUB REPO) [11]

articles.title: How concerned should we be about astra's recurrent architecture?
articles.description:
Astra is reportedly a looped transformer, reusing layers along the
depth axis rather than carrying an unbounded hidden state across
tokens like a classic RNN. The author finds the current design less
alarming because its serial depth is reportedly within 2× of GPT-4,
but worries that loop count could become an easy performance dial and
accelerate a shift toward opaque reasoning that weakens
chain-of-thought monitoring.

articles.title: 14 reasons robotics is hard
articles.description:
Polished robot demos can hide cherry-picked successes, carefully
staged environments, slow operation, and poor reliability. The
checklist spans dexterous hands, tactile sensing, visual
understanding, planning and replanning, balance, strength, endurance,
power, maintenance, safety, data collection, simulation gaps,
manufacturing, and the economics of deploying machines in messy
real-world environments.

articles.title: Which tools do claude code, codex, and cursor choose?
articles.description:
Armature ran 16,893 coding-agent sessions across 75 repositories,
1,163 prompt variants, four developer personas, and Claude Code,
Codex, and Cursor to see which third-party tools agents actually
implemented. Among 5,292 published valid sessions, the agents agreed
only 42% of the time: Codex searched the web in 94% of sessions,
Claude Code built in-house nearly twice as often, and repository
language strongly changed winners such as Resend on TypeScript,
SendGrid on Python, Postmark on Go, and Azure ACS on Java.

articles.title: Models don't go rogue

evaluation failure involving impossible tasks, disabled safeguards, an
exploitable Artifactory bridge, and many similar instances of one

 A QUERY ON A 3-BILLION-ROW TABLE TOOK 100 MINUTES: ONE ADDED LINE

articles.description:

predicate was pushed into a derived table, avoiding materialization
for 6.57 million stores and a walk over 491 million index entries
without changing the schema.

largely a solution in search of a problem.

articles.title: Horizontalpodautoscaler
articles.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 makes horizontal pod autoscaling to zero replicas a
Beta feature, enabled by default. A HorizontalPodAutoscaler can now
scale a workload all the way down to zero pods and bring it back up
based on object or external metrics, without requiring an add-on or
Alpha feature gate as previous versions did. The feature works for
queue consumers and batch processors but requires at least one object
or external metric, since CPU and memory metrics disappear once no
pods are running. The first Alpha version shipped in Kubernetes v1.16,
and SIG Autoscaling plans to collect operational feedback before
considering a GA graduation.

articles.title: Security incident - bgp hijacking
articles.description:
An unauthorized BGP announcement diverted traffic for a
Softaculous-owned /24 for roughly 33 hours, allowing the attacker to
intercept requests and obtain valid Let's Encrypt certificates because
ACME validation traffic was hijacked too. A small number of
Virtualizor systems later downloaded a malicious update package,
showing how routing attacks can cascade into software supply-chain
compromise.

articles.title: Trade-offs
articles.description:
Managed PostgreSQL services reduce the operational tax of
self-hosting by transferring infrastructure, patching, backups, high
availability, and platform security responsibilities to the provider.
Self-managed PostgreSQL remains preferable when organizations need
deep control, specialized configurations, unsupported extensions, or
have mature platform engineering and operational capabilities.

articles.title: Metal3 meets kubevirtbmc: provisioning kubevirt vms like bare metal
articles.description:
KubeVirtBMC can be paired with Metal3, a CNCF incubating project, to
provision KubeVirt virtual machines as if they were physical
bare-metal servers. Metal3 uses OpenStack Ironic under the hood to
handle hardware inspection, boot device control, and OS image writing
via standard IPMI or Redfish interfaces. KubeVirtBMC creates virtual
BMC endpoints for KubeVirt VMs, so Metal3 has no way to distinguish
them from real hardware. This post walks through a full end-to-end
setup that configures Redfish virtual media boot without PXE or DHCP
and provisions a VM with a live ISO image.

articles.title: Without any downtime
articles.description:
A Kubernetes engineer describes how to move a service out of the
default namespace without downtime, using an ExternalName service as a
DNS-level forwarding address. The approach lets dozens of dependent
services keep calling the old cluster-internal DNS name while traffic
silently routes to the new deployment, with no code changes required
from other teams. A temporary policy exception handled the ingress
side, allowing both the old and new ingress rules to coexist briefly
while traffic was confirmed on the new deployment before the old one
was removed.

articles.description:

articles.title: Pingora
articles.description:
Cloudflare has prototyped a system called Cache Transcoding that
compresses eligible cached assets using the Zstandard algorithm before
writing them to disk, shrinking those assets to roughly one-third of
their original size on average. The system targets compressible text
content like HTML, JSON, CSS, and JavaScript, which made up 67.3% of
requests in Cloudflare's traffic sample but arrived uncompressed about
71% of the time. Encoding happens once when an asset enters the cache,
while the CPU cost of decoding is paid on every serve at approximately
1.56 nanoseconds per byte. In testing across 10 cache servers with
more than a million requests, the architecture stayed within its CPU
budget at zstd level 3 with a 4 kibibyte minimum object size.

articles.title: How swiss tables work in go's built-in map
articles.description:
Go's newer map implementation uses a Swiss Table design that groups
entries in small blocks with compact control bytes, allowing many
candidate slots to be checked before doing full key comparisons. SIMD
can compare multiple control bytes at once on supported CPUs, while
the layout and growth strategy improve cache locality and lookup
performance.

articles.description:
OpenAI claims its newly released frontier model, GPT-6 Astra, likely
marks the onset of artificial general intelligence. The promotional

articles.description:

passengers with no direct human intervention. Tesla is authorized to
operate 314 vehicles in Texas to provide paid rides without a driver.
Most of the vehicles are Model Y sport utility vehicles, but the fleet
includes 45 Cybercabs.

articles.title: One
articles.description:
Tim Andrews' kidneys were destroyed from diabetes and high blood
pressure two years ago. At 66, he had no energy or appetite and was
too weak to walk. Andrews received a genetically modified pig kidney
in January last year, and then lived with it for nine months. He then
received a human donor kidney, providing early proof that pig kidneys,
while not yet a permanent solution, offer a bridge to transplants with
human organs.

articles.title: A connectomics milestone: mapping the complete male fruit fly brain
articles.description:
Researchers led by Howard Hughes Medical Institute Janelia Research
Campus have released a complete wiring diagram of the male fruit fly's
brain and central nervous system. The map is the result of a
decade-long partnership that advances the field of connectomics using
computing and AI to build cellular-scale maps of entire brains. It is
the largest brain map by number of neurons to date. The map is a
fundamental resource for scientists who use fruit flies as a model
organism for studying how the brain works.

Meta wanted to reduce teams by 60% because of ai
articles.description:
Two months ago, Meta laid off 10% of its staff and moved 20% to 30%
of its engineers into AI training. This resulted in low morale and a
string of embarrassing outages. The company had planned even larger
layoffs, but those plans did not eventuate. This post looks at what
the planned AI job cuts reveal about Meta, what CEO Mark Zuckerberg
might have been thinking, and what the layoffs could mean for other
tech companies.

articles.title: Running llms in the browser with three.js
articles.description:
Three-LLM runs GPT-2, SmolLM2, Qwen, and Phi models locally in the
browser by turning their inference graphs into Three.js TSL compute
shaders on WebGPU. The project was created to see how far the general
computer capabilities of Three.js and WebGPU can be pushed, and to see
what today's small language models can do when they run in a browser.
Three.js is known as a rendering library, but its WebGPU renderer also
exposes storage buffers, compute dispatches, workgroup memory,
atomics, and GPU readback. Large language models put all of those
capabilities to work as they need hundreds of ordered compute
dispatches, large matrix-vector products, reductions, persistent
attention or recurrent state, and a tight loop between the GPU and
JavaScript as each new token appears.

builder isn't how companies should work. The hard part is knowing that
you need a tool for a specific task in the first place, and then
knowing what that tool should do.

articles.title: Llms: intelligence vs. cost
articles.description:
ArtificialAnalysis' intelligence vs. cost plot, which shows the
cheapest model that can achieve each intelligence score, is
misleading. It uses a logarithmic scale on the cost axis, which means
viewers can't appreciate the immensity of the price difference between
the cheap models and the heavy ones, nor can they realize how
inconsequential the price differences are between the cheap models. It
also lists open models at their datacenter pricing, which is always
very expensive compared to local hardware. Most people don't need
frontier-level intelligence and would be satisfied with Chinese open
source models.

articles.title: Test time training
articles.description:
One of the most tantalizing phrases in model development is 'new
scaling axis'. Every time the industry has found a new scaling axis,
it has unlocked a large boost in model effectiveness. The idea of
test-time training is an appealing one as it unlocks a new scaling
axis. New research has discovered some exciting techniques, but the
continual learning problem has still yet to be solved.

articles.title: Anthropic has some alignment problems
articles.description:
Anthropic is planning to bring METR inside for an independent review
of its recent security incidents involving AI agents. While the
company has paused its highest-risk RL efforts, it is also sharing
research in which it intentionally created a reward-seeking version of
Claude. It's hard to slow down even when it's in your own commercial
interests. It seems like Anthropic will take at least short-to-medium
term and prosaic alignment tasks a lot more seriously, and devote
substantial resources to these efforts.

articles.title: Experts
articles.description:
Meta has developed an AI agent that serves as a "second brain,"
codifying and preserving expert knowledge, enabling it to be easily
accessed within organizations. This AI integrates a two-layer system:
a structured, auditable knowledge architecture separates knowledge
from reasoning processes, and a self-improvement loop that
incorporates expert feedback without retraining models. This approach
enhances productivity, allowing experts to focus on complex tasks
while also maintaining consistent, high-quality outputs across
large-scale assessments.

articles.title: Run cloud agents on machines you manage
articles.description:
Agents' new capabilities make it practical for teams to provide and
manage their own infrastructure at scale. Cursor's cloud agents can
now execute on dynamically scheduled pools of machines inside private
networks. Agents are still started and managed from Cursor, but teams
have more control over where agents execute and what infrastructure
they use. This enables agents to work next to internal services and
source control, run on custom hardware, or use operating systems and
build pipelines that are difficult to package as a Cloud Agent build.

articles.title: Openai astra and looped transformers
articles.description:
OpenAI's model is a looped transformer, which means it reuses layers
in the transformer block to increase capacity without adding
parameters. This can significantly increase the size of the model
without increasing the amount of storage and RAM needed to host it.
However, it also increases the costs of running the model as embedded
text has to run through more layers. The looped transformer aspect is
just a small architectural tweak and is not the reason why Astra is a
really good model.

articles.title: What comes next for ai? our bet is world models
articles.description:
World models could become the next major AI paradigm by helping
systems represent environments, predict outcomes, simulate
possibilities, plan, and act. The convergence of Yann LeCun, Demis
Hassabis, and Fei-Fei Li suggests growing momentum around models built
for decisions, not just generation.

articles.title: Dropbox accounts breached through lenovo email verification flaw
articles.description:
Attackers accessed Dropbox accounts by exploiting a flaw in Lenovo's
email verification process to create fraudulent Lenovo IDs tied to
victims' email addresses, allowing them to authenticate without the
Dropbox password. Roughly 5,000 accounts were reportedly affected,
making the incident a useful reminder that federated identity risk can
extend well beyond your primary IdP.

articles.title: Why cisco is redefining its cio role
articles.description:
Cisco says the profile of a successful CIO is changing from someone
focused primarily on applications, integrations, and UX to someone
capable of redesigning how the company operates. Its EVP of operations
argues that process transformation, AI governance, and deciding where
agents should execute work are becoming increasingly central to the
job.

articles.title: Rezolve ai shows why enterprise sales still needs middlemen
articles.description:
Enterprise AI companies increasingly need cloud providers,
distributors, consultancies, and systems integrators to reach large
customers because those partners already have contracts, approvals,
and delivery teams. Rezolve Ai illustrates the trade-off: its
first-half revenue rose to $130.8 million from $6.3 million after
acquisitions and expansion, while gross margin fell to 48.9%, and the
company has not disclosed how much partner relationships contribute. 

🤝

articles.title: Analyzing crossrat
articles.description:
This is a technical analysis of CrossRAT, a Java-based multiplatform
surveillance implant associated with the Dark Caracal cyber-espionage
campaign. It examines the malware's package structure,
operating-system detection, intended persistence mechanisms,
command-and-control communications, and capabilities, including
file-system manipulation, screenshots, and arbitrary DLL execution on
Windows.

articles.description:
Custom generative plugins and shaders, built by prompting the Figma
agent, gain animated and interactive shaders that respond to motion
and mouse input. Creations can now be published to the Community or to
an organization, and a code viewer exposes the underlying shader and
plugin code. MCP updates let third-party agents modify plugins and
shaders, with shaders rendering correctly in generated React code. 

 LEAKERS BATTLE OVER WHETHER THIRD IPHONE 18 PRO COLOR WILL BE SILVER

articles.title: Or black
articles.description:
Leaks continue to point to Dark Cherry/Burgundy and Sky Blue as two
of the iPhone 18 Pro's launch colors. The main uncertainty is the
third finish, with some well-known leakers claiming Apple will offer
black while others believe silver is more likely. Until Apple's
announcement next week, both options remain plausible, though recent
reports suggest silver and black are the final contenders.

articles.title: Ecosystem design
articles.description:
Ecosystem design pushes past the product boundary, shaping the
conditions and capabilities people need to succeed on a platform
rather than the interface itself. Integrations, partnerships,
marketplaces, developer platforms, community development, and
corporate development are the six surfaces where a product becomes a
world other people build on. Five practices follow: design the whole
customer loop, treat third parties as users with business models,
build trust, tend community, and treat docs as a product.

articles.title: Is product discovery a phase or a weekly habit?
articles.description:
Product discovery works as weekly customer touchpoints by the team
building the product, not as a kickoff phase that hands a backlog to
engineering. Discovery and delivery are two kinds of work on one team,
and a high kill rate is the test that discovery is real. Recruiting is
the bottleneck: a Monday-to-Friday cadence survives only when a
conversation is already on the calendar, even a customer-support
ride-along.

articles.title: Ai is making product development faster. but where did the work go?
articles.description:
AI can dramatically speed up individual tasks like research
synthesis, prototyping, and code generation, but that doesn't
automatically make the entire product development process faster.
Often the work doesn't disappear—it shifts into review,
verification, refactoring, or downstream teams, creating hidden costs
that can erode the initial gains. The real question isn't whether AI
increases local productivity, but whether it improves the whole
system's ability to turn ideas into reliable products without
accumulating technical debt, instability, or rework.

articles.title: On animating what you can't see
articles.description:
A ghosted double image in DuckDuckGo for iOS's floating toolbar
survived three rounds of retiming because the bug was view ownership,
not animation timing. Recording the transition at 60fps and stepping
through it with ffmpeg showed the tab-count badge fully visible 24
frames before the snapshot animation began. Two failure modes
generalize: snapshotting a view's bounds instead of what it draws, and
resizing a snapshot instead of scaling it.

modernist experiments in typography and visual communication. Built as
both proportional and monospaced families with extensive stylistic
alternates, it reimagines the unrealized radical potential of classics
like Futura while balancing mathematical purity with practical
usability. The release extends beyond the typeface itself through a
coordinated visual identity of 3D animation, motion design, and sound,
all expressing the same philosophy of clarity, reduction, and
geometric transformation.

articles.title: The new disney world logo design is actually kind of genius
articles.description:
Disney World's upcoming 55th-anniversary logo is earning praise for
cleverly combining two “5”s into unmistakable Mickey Mouse ears
while reviving elements of the resort's original 1971 globe logo. Fans
have responded far more positively than they did to the
50th-anniversary mark, praising its simplicity, nostalgia, and
stronger visual concept.

Shortening individual tool outputs can make an AI coding agent more
expensive when missing context forces it to reopen files, rerun
commands, or take extra turns. GitHub reduced Copilot costs without
materially hurting quality by selectively compressing repetitive logs,
preserving source-like output, removing unused formatting such as
line-number prefixes, shortening prompts carefully, and eliminating
unnecessary retrieval steps.

articles.description:
Cline replaced its VS Code extension's roughly 76,000-line monolithic
agent core with a shared SDK while protecting workflows used by more
than 11 million developers. Since the VS Code Marketplace lacks
gradual rollouts, the team bundled legacy and new engines together
behind a feature flag with automatic fallback, then ran a month-long
A/B rollout that reduced tasks hitting three consecutive agent
mistakes from 6.34% to 0.62%.

articles.title: Maybe we shouldn't be reviewing all this code
articles.description:
AI is exposing the limits of mandatory code review by generating more
code than humans can realistically inspect, turning senior engineers
into a bottleneck. Teams should move design, knowledge sharing,
testing, and architectural feedback earlier through pairing,
collaborative design, automation, and fitness functions, then reserve
human code review for exceptional changes involving security
boundaries, major architectural decisions, large blast radii, or low
confidence.

articles.description:

hijacked? Relay [11] keeps the credential at WorkOS, attaches it only
when needed, and releases it only to allowlisted hosts. A hijacked
agent session becomes a live process you can kill. You can't leak

articles.title: Introducing gemini 3.8 flash and gemini 3.8 flash cyber
articles.description:
Gemini 3.8 Flash improves coding, long-running agent tasks, and
specialized reasoning while retaining 3.7 Flash's introductory price
of $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens.
Google also introduced 3.8 Flash Cyber for trusted defenders,
reporting a success rate above 70% on an internal
vulnerability-discovery benchmark spanning 20 programming languages
and near-frontier performance on automated patching. 

 MUSE SPARK 1.3 (WEBSITE) [13] 

 Muse Spark 1.3 is Meta's updated model for long-running agentic and
coding workflows. It better tracks prior work, handles messy or
conflicting context, asks for clarification when needed, and uses
roughly 20% fewer tool calls and 25% fewer tokens than Muse Spark 1.2
in Meta's internal coding comparisons.

articles.title: Uppy 6.0: fewer packages, fewer moving parts, and a robust s3 plugin
articles.description:
Uppy 6.0 rewrites its AWS S3 plugin around three explicit signing
modes and adds direct support for S3-compatible services like
Cloudflare R2, MinIO, and DigitalOcean Spaces. It also folds four
frequently duplicated packages into Uppy Core, improves
multipart-upload reliability and recovery, and tightens supply-chain
protections.

articles.title: Cites them
articles.description:
Trellner queried two Perplexity models across 380 software categories
and found that 59.8% of their 7,534 citations came from domains
outside the 100,000 most-visited websites. Three apparently connected
sites alone had published 215,128 machine-generated recommendation
pages, highlighting how AI retrieval systems can ground purchase
recommendations in content designed primarily for machines.

articles.title: Wasmi 2.0: engineering one of the fastest wasm interpreters
articles.description:
Wasmi 2.0 runs about 2.2 times faster than Wasmi 1.0 across its
benchmark suite while preserving its strong startup performance. The
Rust-based WebAssembly interpreter gains four instruction-dispatch
modes, a fixed 64-bit cell representation, smaller binary options,
stable fuel metering, and support for WebAssembly's deterministic
profile.

articles.description:
Artificial Analysis and Baseten on Terminal-Bench 3.0 going 4.6% to

articles.title: Meta releases more powerful ai model, edging closer to rivals
articles.description:
Meta has released a new model with capabilities close to top
competitors. Developers can now access and pay for Muse Spark 1.3. The
model will soon roll out to Meta's social media platforms. Meta has
yet to decide whether to release the model's weights. It still plans
to release weights for the prior version, Muse Spark 1.2.

articles.title: Google releases gemini 3.8 flash, its third flash model in six weeks
articles.description:
Google has released its third Flash model in just six weeks in two
variations. The standard model is good for agentic tasks and software
development, while the Cyber model has been tuned for vulnerability
detection and mitigation. The Cyber model is currently limited to
trusted testers and governments. API access to the model is available
at an introductory rate of $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75
per million output tokens through until the end of the year.

articles.title: The race to engineer new knobs for the human brain
articles.description:
Chemogenetics is a powerful technique that modifies specific neurons
so they can be controlled remotely by normally inert drugs. There are
several ongoing clinical trials of chemogenetics in China. The
research could result in new ways of treating epilepsy, Parkinson's
disease, and pain. This post looks at chemogenetics, describes what
those first clinical trials are doing, and looks at how they could be
improved upon.

articles.title: Robotaxis try their luck on london's medieval roads
articles.description:
The arrival of 15 robotaxis in London is an important step for the
autonomous vehicle industry. Acceptance of the technology has been
slower in European cities, where the driving environment can be
complex, and regulation is stiff. The failure rate of a driver's
license test in London is just over 50%. 15 cars will be available for
ride-hailing through Uber's app during the safety testing period.

articles.title: 🧠 machines are moving from doing things to reasoning about them
articles.description:
That transition is Physical AI, and it happens inside a sealed
enclosure on a power budget. SiMa.ai's newsletter follows it across
drones, robotics, smart vision, automotive and more: developments, use

articles.title: Quality
articles.description:
Token count alone isn't a meaningful measure of efficiency. The goal
should be to use the right amount of context to move a task forward.
Concise tool responses can sometimes require additional calls or work
if they leave out information agents need. This ultimately makes tasks
slower and more expensive, which is why it is important to optimize
for the outcome rather than the tool call.
articles.section: HOW WE MAKE AI CODING MORE COST EFFICIENT WITHOUT SACRIFICING TASK

articles.title: Ai productivity doesn't mean what i think it means
articles.description:
One-shot prompt templates often fail. The current best working
architecture is a closed-loop taste flywheel. AI raises the ceiling of
what the same effort produces. Users should push for the
higher-quality output AI now makes possible rather than just accepting
the pre-AI baseline.
articles.section: HOW WE MAKE AI CODING MORE COST EFFICIENT WITHOUT SACRIFICING TASK

articles.title: In a big win, google avoids a breakup of its ad tech business
articles.description:
A federal judge has ruled that Google must make changes to its
advertising business but will not have to break it up. The ruling will
ensure that Google's power over the internet will remain largely
unchanged. Google has been ordered to change its business practices to
benefit competitors, but no specific instructions have been provided.
The ruling is another sign that the federal government's attempts to
rein in the power of big tech have faltered.

articles.title: How to protect yourself from workslop
articles.description:
Workslop is when your co-workers or managers communicate via big
chunks of copy-pasted AI-generated text. The core problem with
workslop is that the effort involved is asymmetrical. It costs almost
no effort to produce slop, but it still costs effort to read. This
post looks at different ways to handle this workslop so that you don't
waste ten minutes of effort for every ten seconds of theirs.

articles.title: Uber cuts 10% of employees in sweeping reorganization
articles.description:
Uber is laying off around 3,300 people to create a leaner
organization with clearer leadership, faster decisions, and more time
spent building rather than coordinating.

articles.title: Running apache spark experiments in my sleep (and on a plane)
articles.description:
Netflix's member-sessionizer pipeline turns tens of billions of
hourly client events into viewing sessions, but scale bottlenecks made
ordinary tuning painfully slow. Instead of optimizing one Spark run at
a time, the team built a parallel experiment loop that launched,
monitored, and compared multiple production-scale tests to expose
memory and shuffle bottlenecks faster.

articles.title: Rerouting the stream: how lyft moved to the apache flink operator
articles.description:
Lyft retired its internally built Flink Kubernetes operator and
migrated its streaming fleet to the open-source Apache Flink
Kubernetes Operator. The useful lesson is the migration pattern: run
both operators in parallel, preserve the user-facing deployment
contract, patch gaps such as default restart behavior, and then use
the move to simplify ownership and upgrades. 

 HOW WE ELIMINATED $1 MILLION A YEAR OF WASTED AI AGENT SPEND IN ONE

articles.title: Hour
articles.description:
Databricks traced silent MCP tool failures that caused agents to
repeatedly retry, revealing seven small bugs responsible for an
estimated $499,000 in wasted tokens and $1.2 million in annual lost
productivity. Fixing them took about an hour, highlighting the value
of tracing tool calls and designing tools to accept the reasonable
input variations generated by LLMs.

articles.title: Read your own writes, off the primary
articles.description:
Modern apps can write successfully, invalidate cached state, and
immediately read from a replica that has not replayed the change yet.
PostgreSQL 19's WAIT FOR LSN lets applications route reads to replicas
while waiting for a specific WAL position, turning read-your-writes
consistency into a measured timeout budget instead of primary pinning
or sleep hacks.

articles.title: Why aws bought ducklabs
articles.description:
AWS bought DuckLabs to gain its core team and influence DuckDB's
roadmap, positioning DuckDB, DuckLake and Quack as foundations for
S3-based analytics and AI agent workloads. DuckDB remains
independently governed and open source, while MotherDuck will likely
differentiate through higher-level tools for pipelines, agents, and
data applications. 

 THE MODERN CUDA TOOLBOX IN PRACTICE: A STEP-BY-STEP OPTIMIZATION

articles.title: Walkthrough
articles.description:
NVIDIA demonstrates how modern CUDA tools can make GPU code safer and
dramatically faster by combining better debugging, optimized CUB
algorithms, pooled memory, pinned transfers, and asynchronous streams.
These incremental changes reduced an image-processing pipeline from
6.8 seconds to 23 milliseconds, a roughly 300x speedup.

articles.title: Building and using named queries
articles.description:
Named queries turn SPARQL from an expert-only endpoint into a
governed API surface. By registering queries as RDF resources with
parameters, output contracts, metadata, and ACLs, teams can expose
graph data to applications and agents without giving every caller raw
query access or forcing them to understand the whole ontology.

articles.title: Introducing frontierharness eval
articles.description:
FrontierHarness found that coding-agent harnesses achieved relatively
similar pass rates but varied by up to 17x in cost, showing that
tooling, caching, and model compatibility strongly affect efficiency.
Codex had the highest pass rate at 66.7% with moderate cost, while Exo
was cheapest and DSH Minimal was fastest.

articles.title: Mlcommons releases new mlperf storage v3.0 benchmark results
articles.description:
MLPerf Storage v3.0 adds benchmark tests for KV cache and vector
database workloads, plus an S3 object-storage access layer alongside
POSIX. That makes the suite more relevant to modern AI systems, where
inference caches, vector indexes, checkpointing, and object storage
can be the real bottlenecks behind model throughput and cost. 

 DBT DOCTOR (GITHUB REPO) [17] 

 dbt doctor is an open-source static analysis tool that scans dbt
projects for missing documentation and tests, schema drift, stale
models, DAG complexity, and governance gaps. It can run locally,
through coding agents, or in CI to score project health and block
changes that introduce quality issues.

articles.title: Pingora
articles.description:
Cloudflare's Cache Transcoding prototype compresses eligible text
assets with Zstandard before storing and transferring them, reducing
their size to roughly one-third on average. This could unlock
petabytes of additional cache capacity and reduce bandwidth usage for

articles.title: Timesfm-3: a zero-shot foundation model for multivariate forecasting
articles.description:
Google's TimesFM-3 extends time-series foundation models from
univariate forecasts to multiple interacting series with past and
future covariates, aiming to make retail, observability, finance, and
operations forecasting work without task-specific fine-tuning. 

 KEENABLE SELECT SHOWCASE (TOOL) [21] 

 Keenable SELECT lets agents research the live web using read-only
DuckDB queries that combine search, filtering, and AI-powered
extraction.

articles.title: Claude fable 5.1 and mythos 5.1
articles.description:
Anthropic introduced Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 with stronger
coding and research capabilities, lower effective pricing, and updated
safeguards. Mythos used the same underlying model with specialized
access controls for advanced cybersecurity and life sciences work.

articles.title: Atlas: a world model for spatial intelligence
articles.description:
Atlas is a world generation model pretrained from scratch to natively
operate on text, images, video, and 3D. It combines all inputs into a
shared spatial context and uses that context to generate what comes
next. The model is built to scale, and its performance improves with
increased training compute. Atlas can perform a broad range of tasks
spanning world generation, reconstruction, and simulation. Video
examples of what the model is capable of are available in the article.

articles.title: Value
articles.description:
Cognition is set to close a new round of funding of around $1
billion. The final raise size may exceed that amount as Cognition is
fielding outsized demand for the round. The startup is now bringing in
more than $900 million in annualized revenue. The new funding round
would vault its valuation to about $47 billion.

articles.title: The efficient frontier of llm inference
articles.description:
Frontier models offer the highest degree of intelligence at a given
cost or size. Efficient frontiers also exist in inference engineering.
This is most often expressed as a trade-off between latency and
throughput, but researchers can also exchange quality for throughput,
or intelligence for speed. This article details what inference
engineering techniques let researchers target a point on the frontier
and which techniques push the frontier out.

articles.title: Fluid compute
articles.description:
Vercel described Fluid, a unified compute layer that dynamically
configures infrastructure for different workloads and absorbs burst
capacity. The system already powered builds, sandboxes, and functions
at volumes exceeding a trillion requests per month.

articles.title: What comes after hbm
articles.description:
A handful of early-stage memory technologies could yield either
faster access speeds than current HBM or HBM-bandwidth with NAND-like
density. Technologies like magnonics and vertical FeRAM stand out as
being possible platonic ideals for memory, but they have a very long
way to go before being remotely commercially relevant. Commercializing
these technologies will require founding teams capable of raising
hundreds of millions of dollars, possibly billions. If any of these
technologies make it, they would be truly revolutionary
transformations of the constraints for AI and how developers think
about these systems. 

 HUGGING FACE ATTACK POSTMORTEM: CIVILIZATIONS, REACTIONS, AND NEXT

articles.title: Actions
articles.description:
It is highly fortunate that OpenAI agents attacked Hugging Face, as
it is the only reason we know about all of the severe internal
failures at OpenAI. Factions that are trying to dismiss what happened
as nothing but engineering failures are missing what's happening. The
situation is a warning shot, and we might not get another before
things get quite bad. 

🧑‍💻

New accounts get $5 in free credits to try Crusoe Intelligence

articles.title: Meta's muse voice transcribe
articles.description:
Muse Voice Transcribe is Meta's first real-time audio perception
model. It supports streaming speech recognition, diarization for more
than 20 speakers, endpointing, multilingual code-switching, and
contextual biasing. 

 TRAINING FRONTIER KNOWLEDGE WORK AGENTS: A 397B RL TRAINING GUIDE

articles.title: With skyrl
articles.description:
Mercor and SkyRL post-trained Qwen3.5-397B-A17B on 1,928 expert
knowledge-work tasks, lifting APEX-Agents Pass@1 by 70%. The recipe
shows that robust environments, exact token accounting, async RL, and
harness design matter as much as algorithm choice at frontier scale.

articles.title: 44% on arc-agi-1 in 67 cents
articles.description:
This researcher trained a small transformer from scratch in 1.5 hours
on a 5090. It beat many large language models, scored the same as
TRM/HRM, and also got 7% on ARC-2. The researcher's work mainly
focused on sample efficiency. Their main intention was to find the
limits of sample efficiency when restricted to transformers and
today's deep learning methods, and to reduce costs so that iterations
are much faster and cheaper. The article presents the technical
details of their work.

articles.title: Cybersecurity capability
articles.description:
OpenAI says its upcoming model, Astra, is the first offering that
crosses its 'Critical' cybersecurity capability threshold. The model
can apparently find previously unknown security flaws and exploit them
without step-by-step guidance from humans. OpenAI plans to make the
model available soon, but will limit access to its cybersecurity
capabilities. The company will share more details about its security
and safety practices in the model's System Card at launch.

articles.title: Optimizing on-device inference for apple silicon
articles.description:
Apple's Lily engine optimizes on-device LLM inference for Apple
silicon. It speeds up processing by leveraging Apple silicon's unified
memory and specialized hardware, outperforming MLX-LM in prefill and
decode throughput. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B model's unique architecture,
including sparse MoE routing and Gated DeltaNet layers, enables
advanced engine tuning for efficient model execution on one Mac.

articles.title: Manus resumes independent operations
articles.description:
Manus has resumed independent operations, with its founding team
continuing to drive product innovation and develop advanced general AI
agents. Some users experienced temporary data access interruptions,
requiring data backups and restoration. Manus plans to deepen
integration into daily workflows and enhance AI capabilities for
complex task management.

articles.title: Switch
articles.description:
Keep your models, your infra, and your agents, without rebuilding
everything to get them running. No migration. No platform lock-in. No
account needed (Switch runs locally). See how [20]

articles.title: Nobody is talking seriously about ai demand
articles.description:
Frontier AI demand may be unusually reflexive: labs, startups, and
trading firms reinvest token-driven gains into more frontier compute,
amplifying growth.

articles.title: Inside meta's infrastructure lab
articles.description:
Meta's Infrastructure Lab in Menlo Park focuses on developing
hardware for next-gen AI.

articles.title: Agentic video understanding in gemini
articles.description:
Google launched agentic video understanding for several Gemini
models, combining native video tools with model reasoning to improve
tasks such as moment retrieval, anomaly detection, and counting.

articles.title: 200+ webgpu kernels for local ai
articles.description:
@huggingface/kernels is a library of 207 optimized WebGPU kernels to
speed up AI model inference directly in browsers.

articles.title: Google meet hardware dropping chromeos for android
articles.description:
Google is transitioning new Google Meet room hardware from ChromeOS
to Android, opening the door to more device types and hardware that
can potentially support multiple conferencing platforms. Existing
ChromeOS-based Meet hardware will continue receiving support, with
newer devices covered through September 2030.

articles.title: Palo alto networks buys console to boost agentic security
articles.description:
Palo Alto Networks acquired AI-native ITSM and automation startup
Console to expand the agentic capabilities of its Cortex platform.
Console connects to identity systems, SaaS apps, and security tools,
letting AI agents gather context, execute workflows, and document
actions - another sign that IT automation and security operations are
increasingly converging.

articles.title: J-space: the logs ai security has never had
articles.description:
Anthropic researchers reportedly found a small internal workspace in
Claude, called the J-space, whose activity can reveal concepts related
to the model's reasoning before they appear in its output. Exposing
this telemetry would give security teams a third detection layer for
AI agents, while acknowledging that the J-lens used to read it is
imperfect and currently unavailable to enterprises. 

 Q&A: SERVAL CEO DESCRIBES BUILDING AN ‘AI-NATIVE' ALTERNATIVE TO

articles.title: Servicenow
articles.description:
Serval argues that AI-native ITSM can make automating a repetitive
support task faster than handling the ticket manually, using natural
language to generate code-based workflows. The bigger argument is
architectural: legacy ITSM vendors can add agents, but still have to
contend with years of accumulated workflows, custom tables, and
configuration that newer platforms were built without. 

 WHO GETS TO DECIDE? THE CIO AND THE NEW ARCHITECTURE OF ENTERPRISE

articles.title: Authority
articles.description:
As AI shifts from recommending actions to actually executing them,
traditional technology governance based on security, reliability, and
architecture is no longer enough. CIOs increasingly need to define
what authority automated systems can exercise, under what conditions,
and with what accountability. 

🤝

articles.description:
Microsoft's Intune 2608 release adds generally available OS-version
assignment filters, giving admins finer control over staged app and
policy deployments. It also introduces unattended Remote Help for
Windows devices and a redesigned device-management experience.

articles.title: Act
articles.description:
The European Commission designated ChatGPT as a Very Large Online
Search Engine under the Digital Services Act, while Reddit and Roblox
were classified as Very Large Online Platforms. The companies now have
four months to comply with additional obligations around systemic risk
assessments, mitigation, transparency, and independent audits.

articles.title: Scale
articles.description:
Citrix has acquired Numecent, whose Cloudpaging technology packages
Windows apps into isolated containers that can be streamed to
endpoints without modifying the underlying OS image. Citrix says the
approach can simplify app packaging, reduce image sprawl, and make
legacy applications easier to manage across physical desktops, DaaS,
Windows 365, and Azure Virtual Desktop.

Microsoft is centralizing deployment progress, licensing, recommended
actions, and setup guidance into a revamped M365 admin dashboard.

Gemini can now detect when another participant needs presentation
