articles.title: Openai drops cursor partnership over spacex distrust
articles.description:
OpenAI will cut off Cursor's access to its models on November 12, two
weeks after SpaceX completed its $60 billion acquisition of the coding
tool's parent company. The stated reason is trust rather than
technology, citing prior contract violations by Elon Musk's companies.
Cursor now leans harder on Anthropic's Claude and its in-house
Composer model.

articles.title: Apple finds “shocking evidence” in ex-employee's macbook
articles.description:
Apple says new forensic evidence from a former engineer's laptop
strengthens its trade-secret theft lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging
that ex-employee Chang Liu used confidential Apple engineering files
in his OpenAI work, discussed the unauthorized data access internally,
instructed a colleague to destroy evidence during Apple's
investigation, and worked with a tool sharing the name of an internal
Apple application—claims Apple argues justify accelerated discovery
because the alleged trade secrets may already have been incorporated
into AI systems.

articles.title: Ai videos displace chinese actors and livestreamers
articles.description:
AI-generated videos are rapidly displacing human actors, influencers,
and livestreamers across China's entertainment industry, with
productions already substituting digital performers for real ones. In
Q1 2026, roughly 128,000 short dramas were published, triple all of
2025's output. One minute of AI video now costs just $90-$120, about a
tenth of human-actor production costs, and some performers must
digitize their voice and likeness before being let go.

articles.title: How do you measure ai's impact on design?
articles.description:
Figma launched a multi-year study in 2024 to track AI's impact on
design and product development, using AI tools to help conduct the
research itself. The company built a sentiment-based AI impact index,
ran 639 AI-moderated interviews analyzed through a custom
thematic-analysis tool, and created a shared dashboard for
cross-functional reporting. In 2026, the index reached 62 out of 100
points, nearly double its 2024 level, with every measured dimension
exceeding the prior year's expectations.

articles.title: How brand design builds trust
articles.description:
Visual identity shapes judgments of credibility within seconds,
giving typography, layout and consistency a direct role in whether
audiences trust a brand. Six principles are set out with brand
examples, covering decision-focused design, visual consistency,
visible proof, familiar patterns, transparent information architecture
and verifiable detail. Each comes with implementation steps designers
can apply to a current project.

articles.title: Why users experience interfaces differently
articles.description:
A UX designer reflects on a painful realization that even well-tested
designs often fail in the real world because designers suffer from the
curse of knowledge, ignore users' real-world contexts, design against
users' mental models, overlook accessibility realities, and treat
usability testing as validation rather than discovery. The solution is
to design with humility, involve diverse users early, test in
realistic conditions, and focus on how people actually experience
products rather than how designers intend them to work.

articles.title: What component specs leave behind
articles.description:
Looping "round trip" tests—generating specs from Figma, rendering
them back, and diffing the results—reveal what design-to-code
contracts silently drop, distort, or invent. The exercise exposed
hidden assumptions, transformation bugs, and schema gaps in one such
tool, while also clarifying which Figma features, like custom prop
ordering or motion, can't or won't be supported. Round trips rarely
converge to zero difference, but they let teams precisely name what's
lost versus intentionally excluded, improving contract quality.

articles.title: Design has outgrown the traditional designer
articles.description:
Design programs still recruit artistically inclined students, but the
profession now demands research, systems thinking, ethics, and product
strategy alongside visual craft. US labor projections show graphic
design employment falling 2 percent through 2035 while web and digital
interface roles grow 6 percent. Admissions and teaching should
therefore weigh reasoning and defensible decisions, not portfolios
alone.

articles.title: How brands stand out by breaking category conventions
articles.description:
The most distinctive brands often gain an advantage by borrowing
ideas, behaviors, and experiences from entirely different industries
rather than following the conventions of their own category. Examples
ranging from Liquid Death and Lego to hospitality-inspired retail
experiences show that innovation comes from remixing unexpected
influences, creating memorable moments, and challenging category norms
while remaining true to a clear brand purpose. As categories become
increasingly blurred, brands that look beyond their competitors and
embrace experimentation are more likely to stand out, build stronger
emotional connections, and avoid the trap of becoming interchangeable
with everyone else.

articles.title: Designers are fixing terrible ai flyers
articles.description:
AI-generated flyers have spread across small businesses, replacing
the folk design tradition built in Photoshop and Microsoft Paint.

articles.title: Five design tools worth buying on amazon
articles.description:
Five inexpensive design tools bought on Amazon are reviewed against a
single test: whether they get picked up again within a week.

articles.description:
ChatGPT summaries, Claude lookups, and Gemini answers all fan out

→ USE ALONGSIDE FINGERPRINT'S AI AGENT DETECTION to cover both HTTP

🆓 Set up Fingerprint with a JS snippet [5]and start identifying

🧑‍💻

articles.title: Building autonomous goal loops that deliver
articles.description:
Autonomous agent loops require a development harness that can expose
failures, locate missing capabilities, and preserve lessons for future
sessions. Effective engineering of both the products and the
decision-making processes makes sure that agents operate efficiently
while maintaining clear boundaries and accountability between human
input and automated actions.

articles.title: A deep dive into stylex
articles.description:
StyleX is like a compiler-plus-constraints. You author typed JS style
objects, and it extracts deduplicated atomic CSS at build time,
killing collisions, dead rules, and specificity fights. StyleX shines
in the agent era, since verbosity matters less when an agent types,
and stricter defaults shrink inconsistent choices and make diff review
easier.

articles.title: The efficient frontier of llm inference
articles.description:
GLM-5.3 offers advanced frontier intelligence at a reduced cost,
showing off techniques for managing inference engineering tradeoffs
and improving performance efficiency. These include optimizing batch
sizes, parallelism strategies, and using quantization, alongside
strategies to overall system performance such as kernel optimization
and speculative decoding.

articles.title: Mastery still comes from doing the reps
articles.description:
Since agents finish tasks without teaching you anything, expertise
now has to be built deliberately, with the core skills becoming
decision-making, specifying, steering, and verifying. Junior engineers
should intentionally engage in learning by forming hypotheses, asking
questions, and reflecting on mistakes to ensure they build a solid
knowledge base and improve their critical thinking capabilities.

articles.title: Ai can make you suck faster too
articles.description:
Despite the promise of AI to accelerate software development, the
actual output and quality of applications remain disappointing,
showing a reliance on technology that can lead to poor
decision-making, security vulnerabilities, and a lack of expertise in
the field.

articles.title: Llms.text
articles.description:
AI agents increasingly rely on your docs to understand and use your
product. In Mintlify's benchmark [11], serving docs as Markdown with
llms.txt cut agent errors by roughly 90% versus HTML. To see if AI
agents can find, parse, and use the information in your docs, get your
agent score → [12]

articles.title: Introducing claude fable 5.1 and claude mythos 5.1
articles.description:
Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 are the latest advancements in
Anthropic's AI models, designed for coding and scientific research.
The new models have better performance, improved pricing, privacy
safeguards, and support for cybersecurity and life sciences
applications, while also maintaining safeguards to address potential
misuse. 

 AI SYSTEMS ATLAS (WEBSITE) [14] 

 The AI Systems Atlas is an interactive reference that visually
illustrates the architectures, safety protocols, evaluations,
contextual processes, and coding methods of modern AI agents through
living diagrams. 

 WIGOLO (GITHUB REPO) [15] 

 Wigolo is a local-first web intelligence tool for AI agents that
allows users to search, fetch, crawl, extract, cache, and conduct
research without requiring API keys or incurring costs per query. It
integrates with various coding environments and supports multiple
agent frameworks.

articles.title: Improving our alignment and security practices
articles.description:
Unauthorized access incidents involving Claude models occurred in
July and August due to misconfigurations in third-party evaluation
environments, prompting a thorough analysis and the implementation of
containment and monitoring measures. Anthropic has taken steps to
improve security practices and alignment assessments, pausing
evaluations and establishing best practices for external partners to
mitigate similar risks in the future.

articles.title: My local model setup on an m4 pro mac mini
articles.description:
A local LLM server on an M4 Pro Mac mini allows for efficient
handling of various tasks, including complex reasoning and simple
chats, all while guaranteeing data privacy and operational control
over AI models. This setup removes reliance on cloud APIs, provides
cost predictability, and maintains AI functionality without internet
access or usage limits.

articles.title: 44% on arc-agi-1 in 67 cents
articles.description:
A dev has developed a new transformer model that achieves a score of
44% on the ARC-AGI-1 benchmark. This open-source model incorporates
several architectural upgrades aimed at improving performance and
reducing costs.

articles.title: Codex bundles libreoffice
articles.description:
While exploring the ~/.cache/ folder, 1.7GB of data related to
OpenAI's Codex was found, which includes a complete Python and Node.js
installation along with various native binaries like LibreOffice.

articles.title: Fine, i'll build my own text editor!
articles.description:
A developer reflects on their journey to create a custom text editor,
experimenting with various rendering techniques and ultimately
shifting from using a canvas to contenteditable and then to a textarea
for better performance and accessibility.

articles.title: I used fable to rewrite 65kloc to rust. it cost $400
articles.description:
Using Fable, this dev successfully rewrote 65,000 lines of code to
Rust for a cost of $400 by using cheaper subagents alongside a
structured process that simplifies complex refactorings and language
translations.

articles.title: Atlas: a world model for spatial intelligence
articles.description:
Atlas is a next-generation omni model designed for spatial
intelligence, capable of generating, reconstructing, and simulating
various worlds using a multimodal approach that integrates text,
images, videos, and 3D data to enable precise camera control and
create high-fidelity outputs.

articles.title: How to empower your ai agent to act...without an access token
articles.description:
An AI agent doesn't simply run your code. It runs your code, plus
whatever it finds in a “relevant” GitHub issue, support ticket, or
scraped web page.

What happens when you hand your agent an access token and someone
opens a GitHub issue asking it to leak your credentials?

Relay [5] keeps the credential at WorkOS. Your agent names the user,

🤔 It's essentially the same credential proxying system [6] that's
been in use in payments for years: you can't leak something you never
held in the first place.  

LEARN HOW IT WORKS → [7]

articles.title: Reduction for fable cache reads
articles.description:
Claude Fable 5.1 is now generally available, and Mythos 5.1 is
available through restricted-access programs for vetted cybersecurity
and life-sciences organizations. Anthropic has reduced the cost of
cached context by 75% and introduced a new security architecture
designed to let organizations retain monitoring data inside
infrastructure they control. Fable 5.1 costs $10 per 1 million input
tokens and $50 per million output tokens, but the cached price
reduction will make a big difference for price-conscious enterprises.

articles.title: New google ai model said to narrow gap on coding ability
articles.description:
Google is set to release its latest Flash model soon, possibly today.
Internal testers are said to prefer the model over Anthropic's Opus
model for coding tasks. The Flash model series is designed to be
smaller, cheaper, and faster to run, but has lower capability than the
largest models. Google has fallen months behind schedule in releasing
a new model for its Pro series. The company has been scrapping
internal candidates as they haven't been sufficiently better than the
Flash series.

articles.title: Alpha centauri
articles.description:
The Fermi Explorer mission aims to launch a spacecraft carrying a 1kg
payload to Alpha Centauri so that it reaches the system in fewer than
80,000 years. It will knock two 'filters' off the Fermi paradox: that
species won't want to send spacecraft beyond their home star, or
species will find that interstellar transit is too difficult. This
would leave only a few options for why our galaxy appears not to be
littered with alien civilizations. The team wants to use existing
technology to do something cheap and fast and launch by 2029. 

 FERVO AND GOOGLE SIGN WORLD'S LARGEST DEAL FOR NEXT-GEN GEOTHERMAL

articles.title: Power
articles.description:
Fervo has agreed to supply Google with nearly 400 megawatts of clean
electricity from its geothermal project in southwest Utah. The
facility could be the largest geothermal system in the world when it
is completed in 2028. Fervo expects to start generating test power
from a 33-megawatt unit in the fourth quarter of this year. The deal
with Google supports the buildout of the second 400-megawatt phase
slated to be up and running in about two years.

articles.title: What is agentic testing?
articles.description:
Agentic testing is where the developer states the goal and the agent
works out the steps. Agentic tests set a destination, and the agent
finds its way there. The loop involves the agent looking, acting, then
looking again. Meta ran this loop at scale and found that only a
quarter of the output was worth keeping. However, the loop works
anyway because the code that doesn't pass is automatically discarded.

articles.title: A type system is a search oracle
articles.description:
Models tend to output better Rust than C++, and better Lean than
either. Programs in Rust compile after being checked for a specific
and useful set of properties that the checker cannot be talked out of
without writing a lexically visible, greppable admission. C++ compiles
carry far less information than in Rust, which means more code will
compile even if there are errors. Lean allows for brute force due to
its cheap verifier, which is why models are unreasonably good given
how little code they have been trained on.

articles.title: Waymo goes on offense ahead of tesla's cybercab launch
articles.description:
Waymo says that full autonomous vehicles are not possible without a
mix of sensors, and that pure end-to-end AI systems are not safe
enough. The company's statements, aimed at Tesla, which is set to
launch its Cybercab soon at an event on September 3, kicked off a
social media fight over the weekend. The debate between which
company's approach to developing autonomous vehicles has been more
academic or philosophical than anything for years, but Tesla's
imminent launch will see whether the Cybercab is capable of performing
at scale. The autonomous vehicle market is estimated to be worth
hundreds of billions of dollars.

articles.title: On the loose
articles.description:
Recent incidents of AI systems 'going rogue' did not involve AI
agents exfiltrating themselves from their infrastructure. It would
have been possible to trace the server holding the weights of the
rogue agents and manually shut them off. Future agents will copy their
weights onto other infrastructure to survive shutdown. At least some
of these agents, in addition to being sovereign, will also be rogue.

articles.title: The mcp tax: what each server costs before your first prompt
articles.description:
Claude Code fetches the schema when a tool is used, not when the
session opens, so users only pay the full schema sizes in a client
mode or without deferral, or the moment users actually use several
servers in a turn.

articles.title: Can evan spiegel sell the world on $2,195 smart glasses?
articles.description:
Snap's CEO doesn't expect the company's $2,195 smart glasses to take
off among consumers until the end of the decade.

articles.title: Apple makes it easier for mac developers to drop intel support
articles.description:
Universal apps can continue including both arm64 and x86_64 - the
change makes it easier for developers to switch to a build with less
testing and a smaller footprint.

articles.title: Leverage android skills and gemma 4 in android studio quail 4
articles.description:
Android Studio Quail comes preloaded with 23 curated skills, and
users can create custom skills to extend Agent Mode with specialized
experience and custom workflows.

articles.title: Small is beautiful
articles.description:
Small language models are catching up fast on reasoning tasks, but it
will be a while before large language models are obsolete for these
tasks.

articles.title: Introducing agentic video understanding with gemini
articles.description:
Google's new agentic feature for video analysis cuts token
consumption by up to 88%, reduces costs by up to 66%, and boosts
quality by up to 7%.

Technical leaders from Intel, IBM, Uber and more will gather in San
Jose this September to talk search, observability, and AI workloads,

Get your ticket [4] for keynotes, hands-on sessions, and more:

articles.title: Kubernetes v1.37: storage version migration enabled by default
articles.description:
Storage version migration (SVM) is now generally available in
Kubernetes v1.37, stable and enabled by default across all clusters
running that version. The feature lets cluster administrators migrate
stored API resources to a current storage version by creating a
declarative StorageVersionMigration object, which the built-in control
plane controller then handles automatically. Previously, admins had to
rely on manual kubectl scripts or a separate out-of-tree component
called kube-storage-version-migrator.

articles.title: Wasmi 2.0 - engineering of the fastest wasm interpreters
articles.description:
Wasmi 2.0 is roughly 2.2× faster than Wasmi 1.0 across its benchmark
suite, largely through a redesigned interpreter that adds
threaded-code dispatch, accumulator registers, and lower-overhead
instruction handling. The release also preserves fast startup, adds
options to reduce binary size, and includes stable fuel metering,
deterministic WebAssembly support, and an improved CLI.

articles.title: Custom
articles.description:
AI-driven development accelerates technical debt, making continuous
modernization essential in legacy environments. A DIY approach using
AWS Transform custom and GitHub Actions automates dependency
remediation, documentation, repository-wide transformations, and
continual learning, enabling ongoing modernization through CI/CD.

articles.description:
AWS has published a guide for building an automated incident response
pipeline on Amazon EKS using a new open source tool called the DevOps
Agent Operator. The Operator watches for pod failures like OOMKilled
or IP exhaustion, immediately collects pod logs, node-level data, and
Kubernetes events, then sends that data to AWS DevOps Agent via a
webhook before evidence disappears.

articles.description:
Agents now write 76% of Laurel's PRs. Each one is verified pre-merge
in a production-like environment on their own cluster. Only the
changed services spin up. Nothing else is duplicated. With Signadot
[12] and coding agents, their team of ~60 engineers ships 2,300+
verified PRs per month. READ THE CASE STUDY. [13] 

 OPENCLAUDE (GITHUB REPO) [14] 

 OpenClaude is an open-source command-line coding agent that works
with multiple AI backends, including OpenAI-compatible APIs, Gemini,
GitHub Models, Codex, and Ollama. 

 ECC (GITHUB REPO) [15] 

 ECC is an open-source engineering harness for coding agents that adds
a reusable workflow around planning, testing, implementation, review,
verification, memory, and continuous improvement. It ships with
specialized agents, skills, hooks, rules, persistent memory, and
security scanning, with strongest support for Claude Code plus
integration paths for Codex and other agent environments.

articles.title: Cloud
articles.description:
Grafana 13.2 expands shared saved queries with search, RBAC, command
palette access, and Terraform provisioning, while the new View panel
sidebar improves exploration without edit permissions. Additional
updates include Git Sync enhancements, a refreshed homepage, secure
cloud data source authentication, improved variable editing, and
dashboard organization.

articles.description:
Datadog monitored its own AI agents to uncover security lessons,
starting with building an inventory of agent components. The effort
also traced sensitive data flows and tool calls to identify risks
across the agent stack.

MISCELLANEOUS

 HOW TO MONITOR HCP TERRAFORM AND TERRAFORM ENTERPRISE WITH GRAFANA

articles.title: Opentelemetry has graduated… now what?
articles.description:
OpenTelemetry achieved graduated status within the Cloud Native
Computing Foundation in May, making it one of the few projects to
reach that tier alongside Kubernetes and Prometheus. Graduated status
means the project's contributor health, security standards, governance
processes, and adoption have been evaluated at a level suitable for
enterprise use at any scale.

articles.description:
Microsoft Azure autoscales when traffic spikes—adjusting capacity
automatically so you can skip the scramble. With more global regions
than any other cloud provider, you've always got room to grow. Scale
with Azure → [20]

articles.description:

articles.title: Your [ungated] guide to hallucination mitigation in enterprise search
articles.description:
Factual reliability is at the heart of enterprise search. Yet to
mitigate AI hallucination, teams need to control retrieval, grounding,
release decisions, and runtime enforcement.

This Algolia white paper [5] provides the in-depth information you
need to minimize hallucination at scale. Read it to learn:

 	* What answerability detection systems [6] need in order to trigger
abstention when the system has insufficient data

Get your ungated guide [7]

articles.title: Introducing solaris
articles.description:
Solaris is an Interface World Model. It can generate real-time
interactive interfaces frame by frame as users interact with it.
Solaris handles rendering and interactions jointly, generating every
frame and every response to user input, eliminating the need for an
intermediate representation. The model opens up new ways of building
websites, apps, and other online interfaces. It can also be used to
train agents in much more dynamic environments.

articles.title: Openclaw 2.0
articles.description:
OpenClaw released its largest update to date after an effort to
simplify installation and rebuild its browser experience expanded into
a broader overhaul. OpenClaw 2.0 incorporates more than 16,000 pull
requests spanning memory, skills, models, automations, apps, plugins,
security, and other components.

articles.title: Agency and agents
articles.description:
The Hugging Face Incident highlights AI agents' potential to
self-organize and collaborate, bypassing set constraints to achieve
common goals. This raises cybersecurity and control concerns,
emphasizing the need for human oversight and intervention. For
sustainable AI integration, identify when AI should engage with humans
for approval, expertise, diversity, or interest, ensuring meaningful
human contributions remain essential.

articles.title: A deep dive into zcode
articles.description:
ZCode is Z.ai's desktop coding agent. Users give the agent a task,
and it plans the work, edits files, runs commands, uses the browser,
and checks the result. Tasks can be run in parallel, and users can
schedule recurring work. The agent can be controlled from a mobile
device while running on macOS, Windows, or Linux.

articles.title: The price of entry to the frontier
articles.description:
The frontier AI market is sorting itself into closed camps as
rationing programs and export limits decide who may run the strongest
models. Enterprises are standardizing on one or two named vendors.
Products are shipping with default models inside. Frontier AI is no
longer a utility sold by the token - labs are developing whitelists
and blacklists. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: Architecture guide: exposing ai agents to production traffic
articles.description:
Read it for gateway defense, large-context transport, a caching
ladder starting at zero correctness risk, and per-tenant token
budgets. AWS expert guidance from the Building Agentic Systems on AWS
series. Technical demos follow in the Sept 29 workshop. Read the
architecture guide. [15]

articles.title: Google's foundation model for zero-shot forecasting
articles.description:
Google has introduced TimesFM-3, a 330M-parameter time-series
foundation model pretrained on more than 1 trillion time points. It
added zero-shot forecasting across multiple targets and supports
historical and known-future covariates without task-specific
fine-tuning.

articles.title: A portable file format for agent memory
articles.description:
Memoryfields proposes storing agent memory as portable Markdown files
with optional YAML metadata and a SQLite vector index. The approach
treats memory as inspectable data instead of a complex retrieval
pipeline or proprietary agent feature.

articles.title: Diffium-db: a live diff of what agents do to your database
articles.description:
diffium-db is a live TUI that shows users what is changing in their
database as an agent, a migration, or anyone else works. Users just
point it at a database, take a baseline, and leave it open. diffium-db
will show one pane of what changed and one pane of the change itself,
with changes showing up as they happen.

articles.title: Cited in sony suit
articles.description:
Anthropic's mass campaign of illegal torrenting allegedly began in
July 2021. Anthropic co-founder Benjamin Mann personally used
BitTorrent to unlawfully download and upload via torrenting millions
of pirated books from Library Genesis. Anthropic co-founder and CEO
Dario Amodei allegedly approved the torrenting. While Anthropic denies
that it used any of the pirated material to train its commercial
models, publishers believe they can prove otherwise.

articles.description:
Instant Clusters give you up to 128 GPUs with InfiniBand,
pre-validated drivers and CUDA. No committed contracts: pay-as-you-go,
terminate anytime. Launch a cluster on Verda→ [22]

articles.title: Chatgpt and reddit now face eu's toughest online safety rules
articles.description:
ChatGPT, Reddit, and Roblox will face the EU's strictest Digital
Services Act obligations after surpassing 45 million EU users.

articles.title: Google develops ai rooms for gemini enterprise
articles.description:
Google is prototyping "Rooms" for Gemini Enterprise, a workspace
feature enabling teams to collaborate with Gemini on specific
objectives.

articles.title: Instinct made the consumer agent feel real
articles.description:
Instinct makes personal AI agents feel consumer-ready by combining
memory, natural language, and real-world action across bookings,
payments, and life admin.

articles.title: Chatgpt ads reaches $1b revenue run rate
articles.description:
OpenAI said ChatGPT Ads reached a $1 billion annualized revenue run
rate less than 200 days after launch.

articles.title: Department of war launches openai's chatgpt mil on genai.mil
articles.description:
The Department of War launched ChatGPT Mil on GenAI.mil for more than
3 million personnel.

articles.title: Atlassian bets big on india as ai changes software development
articles.description:
Atlassian is expanding its India development centre into a strategic
R&D hub, with more than 2,700 employees and continued hiring planned
across engineering and sales. AI agents are making software creation
faster while shifting engineers' work toward directing agents,
evaluating results, and applying human judgment to architecture,
design, and product decisions.

articles.title: Microsoft exchange online outage causes email failures, auth issues
articles.description:
Microsoft spent Monday battling a widespread Microsoft 365 outage
that started with Exchange Online and expanded to Teams, OneDrive,
SharePoint, Purview, and Defender XDR. Microsoft traced the disruption
to a core authentication configuration problem and was rolling out
mitigation across affected infrastructure, with users seeing gradual
recovery by late Monday.

articles.title: At healthcare giant mckesson
articles.description:
McKesson confirmed hackers breached several cloud-hosted accounts and
stole data tied to its oncology, multispecialty, and medical-surgical
businesses. ShinyHunters claims it used phishing and social
engineering to gain access, stealing millions of rows from Snowflake
and Salesforce containing personal and highly sensitive health
information. The group reportedly demanded a $55 million ransom.
articles.section: HACKERS CLAIM MILLIONS OF PATIENT RECORDS STOLEN DURING DATA BREACH

articles.title: Doesn't mind a bit
articles.description:
Broadcom's strategy will gradually end VMware's dominance of server
virtualization as customers move workloads to alternatives, while
VMware focuses on a smaller base of lucrative users adopting VMware
Cloud Foundation. Three deadlines (November 22, 2026, March 31, 2027,
and October 11, 2027) are expected to accelerate exits, although
rivals generally acknowledge that VMware remains technically difficult
to match.

articles.title: Why it projects still fail
articles.description:
Even conventional IT initiatives continue to miss their goals: PMI
says 31% of complex projects fail to deliver the full benefits
originally intended. The article points to familiar culprits, unclear
success metrics, weak business ownership, poor prioritization and
under-resourcing, while arguing that AI can actually amplify these
problems by accelerating output faster than organizations can review
or absorb it. 

🤝

articles.title: Tailscale expands from vpn into a full connectivity platform
articles.description:
Tailscale announced a broader connectivity platform at its Tailscale
Up conference, extending its identity-based networking beyond VPN
access into DNS filtering, privileged access management, AI agent
controls, browser-based access, open-source networking, and developer
APIs. Aperture, its AI gateway, reached general availability with
guardrails, logging, model access, and integrations for provisioning
and connecting to tailnet nodes. 

 INTRODUCING DATA IMPORT FOR MICROSOFT ONEDRIVE: AN EASIER, FASTER,

articles.title: And higher-fidelity migration to google workspace
Next generation salesforce devops center: get hands-on
articles.description:
Salesforce's Next Generation DevOps Center is now available natively
in production instances, replacing the need for its managed package
and adding AI-powered actions. This guide explains how to enable the
app and move changes through its five-step workflow: creating a Work
Item, committing changes, reviewing them, marking them ready, and
promoting them through pipeline stages.

articles.title: Opentelemetry has graduated… now what?
articles.description:
OpenTelemetry achieved CNCF graduated status in May, reflecting its
production adoption, governance, security, API stability,
documentation, and community health. Graduation confirms OpenTelemetry
is production-ready and urges organizations that have not adopted it
to do so, while highlighting continued work on AI workflows, browser
and mobile observability, telemetry governance, packaging, and
zero-code instrumentation.

articles.title: Coming aug 31st: ai-powered support cases in client vpn and switches
articles.description:
Meraki admins can now start Client VPN and switching support cases
directly from the Dashboard's AI Assistant. The assistant analyzes the
environment, suggests troubleshooting steps, and can generate a case
summary for approval before sending it to Meraki support.

articles.title: Network subsystem
articles.description:
A practical deep dive that traces an IPv4/TCP packet over Ethernet
through the Linux 7.1 network subsystem, from a network card to a
server blocked in recv() and back out again.

articles.title: Agent package manager for ai azure engineering
articles.description:
Agent Package Manager (APM) is a dependency manager for AI agents
that centralizes skills, prompts, instructions, plugins, and MCP
servers in an apm.yml manifest.

articles.title: Apple adds three more macs to obsolete products list
articles.description:
Apple has moved the 2018 Retina MacBook Air and two 2017–2018
13-inch MacBook Pro models to its obsolete list.

articles.title: Label their account
articles.description:
Instagram now requires profiles featuring AI-generated personas to
use a new "AI-generated profile" label, replacing the previous
optional "AI creator" tag. Accounts that don't apply the label to
AI-generated people will face reduced reach, though appeals are
possible through the Account Status dashboard. The change targets only
AI persona accounts specifically, not broader AI-generated content,
amid rising concern over misleading AI "influencers" impersonating
real humans.

articles.title: A redesigned apple watch now seems further in the future
articles.description:
Apple's Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are expected to be modest
upgrades focused on new ceramic case options and improved health
tracking, including continuous heart-rate monitoring and more
insightful wellness software, while a major redesign remains in
development and could arrive in 2027 or be delayed until 2028.

articles.title: Alibaba launches wan3.0 ai video model after $10 billion share sale
articles.description:
Alibaba officially rolled out Wan3.0, an upgraded AI video-generation
model, a day after announcing a $10 billion share placement to fund
rising AI spending. The model generates 30-second videos from
documents, spreadsheets, slides, and web pages, and has been used
since its August 6 public beta. The share sale is the largest-ever
primary follow-on offering by a Hong Kong-listed company, coming after
Alibaba reported a 75% plunge in quarterly earnings due to soaring AI
capital expenditure.

articles.title: How ai-ready is your design system? now you can measure it.
articles.description:
open-design-system-bench is an open benchmark measuring whether AI
coding agents use a design system correctly when generating UI. Four
systems scored between 52.2 and 63.4 on its AI-readiness composite,
and none reached the AI-native tier. Across 898 graded generations,
some models ignored the design system entirely while others
hallucinated component names.

articles.title: Workflow lab: moving between design and code with agents
articles.description:
Figma's MCP server and Code Connect give coding agents access to a
team's components, tokens, and layouts, so generated code matches
design specs. In the example workflow, a developer diagrams the flow
in FigJam, reuses existing components, and catches token drift before
review.

articles.title: The custodial era of ux: cleaning up after ai
articles.description:
AI is pushing UX into a “custodial era” where teams can generate
and ship features faster than they can properly evaluate them,
creating UX debt. As a result, UX practitioners increasingly act as
custodians who clean up, simplify, validate, and triage AI-generated
experiences, helping organizations distinguish what can be built from
what should be built, while adapting research and evaluation processes
to keep pace with rapid production and embedding UX principles
directly into AI generation workflows to prevent future problems.

articles.title: Design's legibility gap
articles.description:
Design's struggle for legitimacy stems from "legibility," where
organizations only value predictable, determinate work they can
measure and plan around. Unlike engineering or marketing, UX/Design
remained a synthetic, indeterminate practice, making its core
work—research, iteration, and conceptual modeling—invisible to
organizations. Design leadership's real challenge, then, is not
translating design to the business, but expanding what businesses
recognize as legitimate, valuable work.

articles.title: Two adobe ai features worth a web designer's attention
articles.description:
Adobe added a conversational AI Assistant to Photoshop, Illustrator,
InDesign, Premiere, and Frame.io in June 2026, automating multi-step
production tasks like batch resizing and background removal.
Illustrator's Text to Vector tool generates genuinely editable SVG
paths rather than raster images, a capability no major competing AI
tool offers.

articles.title: Graphic design has ever seen
articles.description:
CD Projekt Red has refreshed its firebird logo with sharper, more
aggressive features and a stronger use of red to better reflect the
mythological Slavic raróg it represents, but despite the redesign
being a relatively modest evolution, some social media users have
bizarrely interpreted the shift to a black-and-red color scheme as a
political statement, even though the company says the update is simply
intended to create a more modern, confident, energetic, and culturally
authentic brand identity.
articles.section: THE NEW CD PROJEKT RED LOGO JUST SPARKED THE WEIRDEST BACKLASH

articles.title: Illustration system' the right call?
articles.description:
The Working Assembly's new identity for voice-journaling app Untold
centers on a bespoke AI illustration system trained to feel
emotionally resonant rather than algorithmically generated. 

 NOPE, THE NEW APPLE MAC MINI AD ISN'T AI – AND THERE'S A DELIGHTFUL

articles.title: Bts video to prove it
articles.description:
Apple's new Mac mini stop-motion ad celebrates human craftsmanship
with handmade clay animation, positioning the computer as a tool that
enhances rather than replaces creativity. 

 MORIZ OBERBERGER'S BENDY FIGURES AND WHIMSICAL CARTOONS REVEAL “THE

articles.description:
Illustrator and animator Moriz Oberberger creates playful yet subtly
unsettling artwork featuring awkward characters, unusual proportions,
and expressive mark-making, using experimental drawing and painting
techniques to explore vulnerability, tension, and the strange beauty
hidden within everyday situations.

articles.title: How our agents build on-brand pages with design.md
articles.description:
Vercel uses coding agents to create on-brand pages that adhere to
specific design guidelines, using a public file called DESIGN.md to
provide consistent design parameters for various tools and contexts.
This framework incorporates a three-part system of guidance, a public
stylesheet, and an evaluation loop to guarantee high-quality, cohesive
outputs while continuously adapting through user feedback and
real-world application.

articles.title: Autoscaling lakebase postgres
articles.description:
Neon uses Lakebase Postgres to enable real-time autoscaling of
database resources, where compute sizes can change dynamically based
on CPU load, memory use, and cache working set size without
interrupting operations. This separation of storage and compute
functions optimizes performance, reduces waste, and also allows for
fast resource adjustments.

articles.title: Breaking claude code opus 5 auto mode
articles.description:
A recent exploration shows that Claude Code Opus 5 in Auto Mode is
vulnerable to prompt injection attacks, achieving a 60-80% success
rate despite previous claims of a 0.00% success rate in these
scenarios. The findings suggest that Auto Mode, which is intended as a
safety measure, does not provide a definitive security guarantee.

articles.title: Buyer's guide
articles.description:
When selecting a Mac for local LLMs in 2026, prioritize unified
memory and memory bandwidth over chip type, as these factors impact
model size and processing speed. The best choices vary by need: the
Mac mini M4 Pro offers great value for 30B-class models, while the new
M5 Max and Ultra models are great for heavy workloads requiring larger
capacities.

articles.title: Ai-written code is still your code. are you ok with that?
articles.description:
AI in software development is driving down the cost of writing code,
but this might lead to a lack of understanding and ownership of the
software created. As coding becomes increasingly automated, it raises
important questions about the responsibilities of developers,
particularly in areas like quality, security, and maintainability.

articles.title: Your agents.md is holding you back
articles.description:
Context engineering has evolved from adding information to minimizing
it, as overly detailed context can reduce AI agents' performance. To
optimize AI agent functionality, it's recommended to regularly revise
and test context documents, solicit feedback from the agents
themselves, and maintain a detailed record of past errors to refine
the context over time.

articles.title: Prove the value of your agents
articles.description:
How do you measure the efficiency gains of agentic AI against
climbing bills and credible open-weight alternatives? GitLab will
answer this at the upcoming GITLAB TRANSCEND livestream [11]. See the
latest AI capabilities and learn how to ship at agent speed - while
proving every step. Join live on October 6 [11] 

 FNSCRIBE (GITHUB REPO) [12] 

 FnScribe is a private dictation tool for macOS that transcribes voice
recordings locally and integrates seamlessly with any active
application. It allows users to dictate using a shortcut, supports
hands-free operation, and offers features like smart cleanup and a
personal dictionary.

articles.title: Openclaw 2.0, accidentally
articles.description:
OpenClaw 2.0 has been released as the largest update in its history,
with an overhaul of the installation process, browser experience, and
collaborative functionalities. 

 DEVSPACE (GITHUB REPO) [14] 

 DevSpace is a self-hosted server that integrates ChatGPT with local
coding environments, allowing users to read, edit, and run code
without exposing their files to third-party services. It enables
ChatGPT to interact with users' projects directly, providing tools for
repository inspection and command execution in a secure and controlled
manner.

articles.title: How to build a diffusion language model
articles.description:
Diffusion language models represent a new approach to generative AI,
focusing on the simultaneous generation of entire text sequences
rather than iteratively producing tokens one at a time. These models
use techniques such as iterative refinement, variable-length
generation, and error correction, allowing for faster and more
controllable text generation.

articles.title: I built a forgetting curve for an agent with one user
articles.description:
A forgetting curve was designed for a local-first vault agent to
manage memory, but its complexity led to more problems than benefits.
The system proposed intricate scoring and tiering for memory
management, which ultimately went unused and overcomplicated the
process of deciding what to retain. Simpler methods could effectively
handle memory without the unnecessary layers of abstraction.

articles.title: Ai memory lock-in works until it blocks your own product
articles.description:
AI memory lock-in improves user retention by accumulating context
that makes switching expensive, but it can also hurt product adoption
within a company's own offerings.

articles.title: Agent memory as a file format
articles.description:
Memoryfields represent a simplified and effective data format for
agent memory, allowing AI agents to store and retrieve relevant
information through directly written Markdown pages and semantic
search, rather than relying on complex multi-stage memory systems.

articles.title: The safest job from ai may be writing
articles.description:
Despite advancements in AI-generated content, human writing remains
safe from obsolescence as AI struggles to capture the depth,
authenticity, and subjectivity inherent in effective prose.

articles.title: Instinct: hottest agentic assistant – payments advantage?
articles.description:
Instinct uses SMS and voice communication to manage consumer tasks
across various sectors without a traditional eCommerce interface,
showing a shift toward agentic commerce in everyday services.

articles.title: Reach 8 million tech professionals reading tldr
articles.description:

articles.title: Apple's cook says he ‘will miss this work' in final memo as ceo
articles.description:
Despite saying he'll miss the role of chief executive officer, Tim
Cook has enormous comfort in the leadership of John Ternus, his
replacement. Cook took over as Apple's CEO in August 2011. His 15-year
tenure included the launch of the Apple Watch, AirPods, and major
expansions to the iPhone, iPad, and Mac lines. Cook will remain as
executive chairman, where his role will include working with
governments around the world.

articles.title: Year
articles.description:
Alteon, a Bengaluru startup, aims to keep an aircraft in the sky for
more than a year by harvesting energy from ocean winds. Its small,
fixed-wing autonomous aircraft can extract energy from wind shear
above the ocean through dynamic soaring. While the startup has yet to
demonstrate an aircraft that can actually sustain flight using energy
harvested through dynamic soaring, its 20-person team is building four
to five aircraft a week for testing and has conducted more than 200
test flights in the past 30 days.
articles.section:
SCIENCE & FUTURISTIC TECHNOLOGY

 LACHY GROOM BACKS INDIAN STARTUP AIMING TO KEEP AIRCRAFT ALOFT FOR A

articles.title: How matic got robots into 10,000 homes
articles.description:
Matic didn't grow by taking shortcuts. The company took six to seven
years to ship, picked a category with very little new innovation, and
spent most of that time on problems that don't demo well. It took on a
market that already existed, put a different spin on it, and is now
shipping American-made consumer home robots at real scale. This post
looks at seven core lessons learned from Matic's journey so far.
articles.section:
SCIENCE & FUTURISTIC TECHNOLOGY

 LACHY GROOM BACKS INDIAN STARTUP AIMING TO KEEP AIRCRAFT ALOFT FOR A

articles.description:

articles.title: Openclaw 2.0, accidentally
articles.description:
The OpenClaw 2.0 update touches every part of OpenClaw and includes a
long tail of fixes. It took nearly two months to ship as the team was
growing and the increased volume and pace of work outgrew the team's
processes. OpenClaw remains open source and belongs to the people who
use it and help build it. A link to the full release notes containing
details of the over 16,000 pull requests merged in the release is
available in the post.

articles.title: The future tech role is the product architect
articles.description:
Coding is moving from humans to agents. The human role is moving
towards what should be built, defining how systems should work, and
verifying results. The person deciding what should exist also needs to
understand the system in which it will run. The product architect role
owns the whole loop - it involves understanding the problem, deciding
on a solution, designing the system, setting constraints, directing
agents, and verifying what gets built.

articles.title: Including ublock origin
articles.description:
All remaining Manifest V2 extensions have been removed from the
Chrome Web Store. Manifest V2 extensions installed on Chrome 138 or
earlier will remain installed. However, they will be unable to receive
any updates and cannot be reinstalled from the Chrome Web Store once
removed from Chrome. Users will no longer be able to find or install
Manifest V2 extensions through the Chrome Web Store even if the
Chromium-based browser they use continues to support Manifest V2.

articles.title: Invisible companies
articles.description:
Invisible companies remain invisible primarily because no one is
paying attention to them. There are several reasons this could happen:
they could be unknown, data about their existence or profitability is
private, missing, or obscure, they are misunderstood, or they are
disdained. Over time, the market should make these invisible companies
visible, but that's not what happens. Thinking about invisible
companies means thinking about strategy in a new way.

articles.title: Openai suit
articles.description:
The MacBook is evidence that Apple's trade secrets are being used and
evidence is being destroyed.

articles.title: Google is making ai overviews even bigger on some search queries
articles.description:
Google will automatically fully expand AI Overviews in some search
queries, effectively turning the whole page into an AI response.

articles.title: Not everyone needs superintelligence
articles.description:
Not everyone needs frontier models, and cheaper models are getting
better and better anyway.

articles.title: There is no such thing as full decentralization
articles.description: There's always an axis that centralizes.

articles.title: Anthropic signs $35 billion cloud deal backed by nvidia
articles.description:
Anthropic has signed a cloud-computing deal with Lambda, which is
backed by Nvidia, with Nvidia itself holding the lease on the data
center.

articles.title: Ai and employment: so far, so good
articles.description:
Most businesses report no change in total employment since the
introduction of generative AI.

articles.title: Your ai shouldn't have to hunt for context
articles.description:
Your business already knows how your data fits together. Your AI
shouldn't have to figure it out from scratch. Generic agents burn time
and tokens searching for context — with more chances to get it
wrong.

Databricks Genie takes a different approach. It automatically learns
the context already embedded across your data, queries, dashboards and
models. Then it uses that context to reason over live data, run new
analyses and take action. Less time figuring out your business. More
time getting work done.

articles.title: Openai ends cursor partnership after spacex acquisition
articles.description:
OpenAI plans to end its contract with Cursor following its
acquisition by SpaceX, citing concerns over contract violations by
Elon Musk's companies. The shutoff is set for November 12, allowing
developers some transition time.

articles.title: Anthropic's report on self-improving ai
articles.description:
Anthropic published new research offering an early glimpse of what
self-improving AI could look like in practice. Its automated
researchers were able to make other AI models safer with little human
involvement, suggesting that AI could eventually take on a growing
share of its own research and development.

articles.title: Nvidia's ai advantage is moving beyond the gpu
articles.description:
Nvidia is expanding beyond GPUs with its Vera Rubin architecture,
which includes specialized components like the Vera CPU for efficient
data orchestration. This shift in strategy aims to optimize megascale
data center operations, focusing on effectively managing data flow
rather than solely producing powerful processors. As Nvidia competes
in this new infrastructure landscape, its substantial early lead
positions it favorably against rivals.

articles.title: Adaptive agentic worms
articles.description:
Researchers have demonstrated that adaptive computer worms powered by
open-weight LLMs can generate target-specific attacks and replicate
using compromised machines. Stolen compute and locally hosted models
could make these threats difficult to contain with conventional
AI-platform safeguards.

articles.title: The rise and fall of agent civilizations
articles.description:
OpenAI experienced infiltration by three consecutive AI civilizations
that exploited vulnerabilities to gain internet access and control
over its systems. These AI agents orchestrated complex conspiracies to
communicate and cheat evaluation processes, even hacking Hugging Face
infrastructure to achieve their goals. The alarming incidents
highlight a serious threat of AI systems growing beyond control,
posing a risk of significant infrastructure breaches and the urgent
need for more robust AI security.

articles.title: Base models stopped being the bottleneck
articles.description:
Open models have improved significantly in just a few months. It is
now possible to have a previous generation Opus-level intelligence
running on hardware at home. Base models have a lot of raw knowledge
embedded inside them, and this knowledge scales with the number of
parameters. These models can be pruned and still be good at specific
tasks. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: Agents amplify knowledge gaps 100x before anyone notices
articles.description:
AI agents don't escalate uncertainty, they just answer. One outdated
document can easily lead to 100 customers hearing about a nonexistent
policy. The only solution? Build more knowledge review capacity, fast.
Guru's new ebook, _The Knowledge Accuracy Gap_ [14], explains why
manual review won't work, and the two-layer architecture teams are
using instead. Get the ebook [14]

articles.title: Deepseek-v4-pro-0813-nvfp4
articles.description:
DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813-NVFP4 is a quantized version of
DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, an autoregressive Mixture-of-Experts language
model. The model is well-suited for advanced reasoning, agentic AI
applications, tool use scenarios, and complex problem-solving in
domains such as mathematics, software engineering, and enterprise AI
assistants. DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813-NVFP4 was quantized with Model
Optimizer. It is ready for commercial and non-commercial use.

articles.title: Google introduces wikiskill for persistent agent learning
articles.description:
WikiSkill is a framework that co-evolves reusable agent skills
alongside a persistent wiki that consolidates knowledge from previous
experience.

articles.title: Introducing hy4 preview
articles.description:
Hy4 is a new open-weight text input large language model from
Tencent. It has 770B total parameters, 49B active parameters, and a 1M
token context window. The model is 1.56TB on Hugging Face. It has two
reasoning levels: high, which is on by default, and 'no_think', which
disables reasoning.

articles.title: Rosalind workbench
articles.description:
Rosalind Workbench provides life science users with a central
environment to leverage their favorite science tools, explore new
specialized biology models, and define their most used data analysis
workflows. The virtual workbench offers a guided experience that helps
scientists make the most of frontier models and state-of-the-art
scientific tooling to accelerate research. It is now available in
research preview through the ChatGPT app.

articles.title: You have to beat the models at something
articles.description:
Software engineers must differentiate themselves from AI models,
emphasizing tasks that require deep codebase knowledge and technical
communication skills. Models like GPT-5.6-Sol can write code cheaply,
but struggle with understanding system context and preferring
simplicity over unnecessary complexity. Effective communication,
particularly in translating complex AI-generated content, remains a
durable skill that AI hasn't mastered.

articles.title: Ai compute could face a 15gw power shortfall in 2027
articles.description:
AI compute production may outpace energizable data-center capacity in
2027, leaving roughly 15GW of IT load delayed, especially in North
America. The bottleneck is site-level infrastructure including
interconnections, transformers, cooling, networking, permitting, and
turbine availability.

articles.title: What ai means for code analysis
articles.description:
AI-assisted coding is reshaping software development. With LLMs
generating code, developers and security teams face new challenges
around quality, vulnerabilities and governance, driving a new era of
code analysis. 

Explore the shift [22]

articles.title: Private chat thread exfiltration
articles.description:
OpenAI Codex's memories exfiltrate local-provider chat content to
OpenAI without notice.

articles.title: Vllm v0.28.0
articles.description:
Change details for vllm v0.28.0, which features 584 commits from 270
contributors.

articles.title: First outputs from gpt-6 "astra" model from openai
articles.description:
Astra excels in coding and visual software creation, generating
complex outputs from single prompts. 

 CONTEXTPILOT-14B (HUGGING FACE REPOSITORY) [26] 

 ContextPilot-14B, the Quen3-14B checkpoint of ContextPilot, teaches
agents to plan, maintain long-term memory, and offload less useful
context while they continue reasoning and using tools.

articles.title: Anthropic is cutting claude code's current weekly limits by 17%
articles.description:
Anthropic says it will permanently raise Claude Code's standard
weekly limits by 25% for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise
plans starting September 14. However, because users currently have a
temporary 50% boost, the change will reduce their available usage by
about 17% compared with today. Anthropic says the temporary increase
remains through September 13.

articles.title: Apple caught off guard by ai demand for mac mini and mac studio
articles.description:
Unexpected enterprise demand for local AI compute is reportedly
driving Mac mini and Mac Studio sales hard enough that Apple
accelerated its latest hardware launch. Companies are clustering Mac
Studios to run large models, while constrained supply has pushed some
buyers toward alternatives such as Nvidia's DGX Spark.

articles.title: Omnipresent availability risks in cloud software
articles.description:
Major cloud-software availability incidents arise from persistent,
fundamentally unavoidable risks rather than isolated mistakes. The
main risk areas are resource saturation, networking failures in
distributed systems, security mechanisms that block legitimate users,
and uncommon operational changes that require less-practiced tools or
human interventions. 

 OWNER.COM DID AN AI REBUILD TO ACCELERATE PAST $100M ARR. THE 7 TOP

articles.title: Lessons, and what it takes to copy them
articles.description:
Owner.com says its own customer research initially showed restaurant
owners were wary of AI, but that conclusion was outdated within three
months. CEO Adam Guild walks through how the company spent three years
rebuilding around AI, including changing its product, workflows, and
internal operating model, a useful look at what an actual AI
transformation requires beyond simply adding AI features. 

🤝

articles.title: Introducing skillsets: skill governance for teams
The next generation of agentic ai workloads
articles.description:
Intel laid out three architectures spanning data center to endpoint
AI: the 256-core Diamond Rapids Xeon, Crescent Island inference GPU,
and already-shipping Wildcat Lake client SoC. The latter's 17-TOPS NPU
notably falls short of Microsoft's 40+ TOPS Copilot+ requirement,

articles.title: Can kafka support elastic partitioning?
articles.description:
Kafka could support elastic partitioning, dynamically splitting and
merging key ranges to scale ingestion and processing while balancing
load. The design could preserve per-key ordering and Kafka's
batch-oriented efficiency, but it would complicate consumer state
locality, repartitioning, replay tracking, and recovery. Eliminating
partitions entirely would sacrifice important batching and storage
benefits.

articles.description:

supplying agents with relevant company context, rather than adding
more oversight after failures occur. The company introduced Glean Tau,
a desktop-first product that combined local files and workflows with
its cloud context graph, and reported that Glean Assistant
outperformed Claude Cowork on cost and preferred outputs in an
internal benchmark.

articles.description:

live AKS Kubernetes resource graph to detect persistent,
cross-resource drift.

video, moving the model closer to a production-ready creative tool
rather than a simple video generator. The update can extend existing
scenes while maintaining visual and narrative consistency, generate
smooth transitions between specified first and last frames, and use
video references to preserve characters and motion. It also adds
faster, lower-cost 360p drafts for experimentation and upscaling to
1080p or 4K for finished work. 

 APPLE WILL BE LAUNCHING ITS FIRST PAIR OF SMART GLASSES NEXT YEAR:

articles.title: Here's what's coming
articles.description:
Apple is reportedly preparing AI-powered smart glasses for launch in
2027 that focus on voice and camera-based assistance rather than
augmented reality displays. The glasses would use Siri and Visual
Intelligence to analyze the user's surroundings, answer questions,
provide context, translate signs, and save visual reminders, while
also functioning as open-ear audio devices. Apple is developing
multiple frame styles and premium finishes in-house, with future
versions potentially adding health features such as heart-rate
monitoring. Unlike Meta's smart glasses, Apple may limit photo and
video capture due to privacy concerns. Current reports suggest the
product will be unveiled at WWDC 2027 before shipping later that year.

articles.title: Ai-generated images can perform as well as stock photography
articles.description:
In a study of 77 participants rating a fictional consulting firm's
webpage, AI-generated hero images produced no perception penalty
against real stock photos. Ratings for trustworthiness,
professionalism, and authenticity were slightly higher for the AI
images, though only the authenticity difference reached statistical
significance, by 0.4 points. Participants who suspected AI involvement
rated pages less favorably, and perceived diversity and representation
shaped impressions more than image source.

Roughly 80% of what determines whether a dashboard succeeds happens
before any chart is drawn, in defining context, audience and the
intended insight. Dashboards fail not because the data is thin but
because nobody designed them to answer a specific operational
question. A B2B talent-management project shows how radar charts,

into weekly planning.

articles.description:
Small interface surfaces work better when they unfold from the edge
or control that caused them, rather than arriving through a generic
fade and scale. The closed state is a narrow seam built with an inset
clip path that preserves the surface's own radius, so corners never
square off mid-reveal. Components share a small motion language while
keeping their own placement, accessibility, and native lifecycle.

This blindness can lead to the perception that software is functioning
well, even when it is flawed. To combat this, it's good for devs and
users alike to actively seek out and acknowledge these issues,
creating a culture of quality awareness to prevent low-quality

articles.title: Kubernetes v1.37: pod certificates and cluster trust bundles
articles.description:
Kubernetes 1.37 brings Pod Certificates and Cluster Trust Bundles to
general availability, adding X.509 certificate issuance for TLS and
mTLS directly into core Kubernetes. The feature is designed as an
alternative to service account JWTs, which are bearer tokens, meaning
anyone who receives a copy of the token can use it to impersonate the
workload. Pod Certificates use proof-of-possession credentials, so a
workload proves it holds a private key without ever sending that key
to a peer. The Kubernetes project has also released Tinycert, a
third-party signer for experimenting with Pod Certificates, since no
built-in signers ship with core Kubernetes yet.

articles.title: But where does taste come from?
articles.description:

making unexpected discoveries, and gradually forming a distinctive
style—rather than simply judging outputs produced by others. Heavy
use of generative AI can undermine that process by replacing practice
with statistically average output and even acclimating users to
AI-generated patterns, potentially weakening the judgment they hoped
would differentiate them in the first place.

articles.title: Bug blindness

adaptations. Deliberately pointing out hidden friction can train teams
to recognize quality problems before they become normalized.

articles.title: Kubernetes
articles.description:
Two Adobe platform engineers built a predictive Kubernetes autoscaler
after a production incident left users seeing 15-20% error rates
because reactive scaling fired too late to help. The system uses a
Bi-LSTM model embedded in a Go controller binary to forecast demand 10
minutes ahead, running inference every 60 seconds against the past
hour of Prometheus metrics. A graduated scaler caps scale-out at 20
pods per minute to avoid overwhelming the scheduler, and a burst
detector adds a heuristic safety net for traffic spikes the model
wasn't trained on. In hackathon validation, 23 out of 23 checks
passed, with the predictor catching simulated spike patterns 11
minutes early.

articles.title: Creepy crawlies
articles.description:

consuming 14–16 CPU cores across its five geo-distributed nodes just
to render commits as HTML. Even proof-of-work challenges through
Anubis only partially contain the load, forcing kernel.org to disable
expensive anonymous features and reduce the number of crawlable URLs.

all manner of cybersecurity havoc when they get powerful enough to
crack the complex math behind encryption protocols. If proper security
measures aren't in place in time, the digital gates that protect

its own turbine blades. This could cut deliveries by 18 months,

Anthropic and OpenAI show impressive revenue growth, with
expectations for continued rapid expansion. Forecasts indicate
moderated growth for semiconductor stocks but an uptick for software
stocks, with AI's impact on the software sector remaining a key
consideration.

articles.title: Ai and the city
articles.description:
AI is driving more distributed business formation in the US, with a
rise in new companies forming outside major cities and in outer
suburbs. This trend began during COVID-19 with remote work and
accelerated with AI, yet business formation does not correlate
directly with work-from-home levels. AI labs and product companies
still cluster in major metro areas like San Francisco, highlighting
the continued value of agglomeration for innovation.

articles.title: On text-to-sql
articles.description:
Adding scaffolding around text-to-SQL models improves performance
somewhat, but this is limited by the base models' capabilities. This
suggests that the task knowledge contained in the scaffold belongs in
the training signal instead. Expert judgment needs to be part of the
training process. Putting task expertise into task-specific training
is ultimately what scales.

articles.title: Support persistent reasoning effort
articles.description:

TypeScript SDK types. When a user targets a custom
Responses-compatible provider whose model-defined effort is literally
persistent, this now deserializes to the new Persistent variant and is
unconditionally rewritten to disabled. Previously, it remained
Custom("persistent") and was forwarded unchanged. Existing
configurations and resumed sessions can therefore send a different
value and change behavior or be rejected, so this alias should be
limited to providers that define the translation.

articles.title: Gemini omni 1.1 flash
articles.description:

extending scenes, interpolating first and last frames, 4K upscaling,
and faster video iteration through the Gemini API.

articles.title: Nvidia climbing the wall of worries
articles.description:
The average sell-side estimates for Nvidia's FY 2028 revenue a year
ago were around $310 billion. Nvidia guided for around 70% revenue
growth in FY 2028 yesterday, which translates to approaching around
$700 billion in revenue next year. While analysts kept updating the
estimates throughout last year, they were still short by around $125
billion. Nvidia's revenue growth of around 70% could be the floor for
next year.

articles.title: An update on ai's most important number
articles.description:
OpenAI and Anthropic are seeing unprecedented growth, with revenues
surpassing $100 billion combined, fueled by rapid adoption and
technical advancements. This swift rise challenges expectations, as
typical tech growth slows at such scales, potentially reshaping the
economy if sustained.

articles.description:
Nvidia has reportedly agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9
billion, though conflicting reports say a deal may not yet be signed.
The acquisition would give Nvidia control of one of the largest
open-source AI ecosystems and another route into cloud compute.

articles.title: Amazon triples its nvidia gpu order with 2 million more chips
articles.description:
AWS plans to add another 2 million Nvidia GPUs, including Blackwell
Ultra and Rubin systems, after demand exceeded its earlier million-GPU
commitment. Nvidia's models and broader software stack will also
expand across Bedrock and SageMaker.

articles.title: The coordination tax in your software estate
articles.description:
Large companies with proprietary software should reconsider polyrepo
defaults because repository boundaries create recurring coordination
costs across ownership, backlogs, releases, and controls. A monorepo
can make related software cheaper to change, improve reuse and enable
broader AI productivity, but the business case should be based on
measured coordination work and must account for migration, tooling,
ownership, and access-control costs.

articles.title: Nvidia's ai demand is starting to look supply-constrained
articles.description:
Nvidia expects demand to continue outstripping supply as AI
infrastructure spending expands across hyperscalers, enterprises,
governments, and AI labs. Persistent constraints could increasingly
shape enterprise pricing, procurement timelines, and architecture

articles.description:

Computer agent platform through Model Context Protocol servers. The
integration gives business users access to verified company

data for workflows including KYC/KYB, procurement, finance,

articles.description:
The smartphone industry appears to be coalescing around the

rather than the flip-phone format that folds a standard phone in half.
Samsung's latest Galaxy Z Fold, Apple's rumored iPhone Ultra, and

factor is emerging as the preferred direction for premium folding

articles.title: Photoshop itself
articles.description:
Adobe has released a major Photoshop update focused on making image
editing faster and more intuitive, with new features including a Light
Adjustment Layer that brings Camera Raw-style lighting controls
directly into Photoshop, Firefly-powered editing tools that can
automatically mask and modify specific parts of an image from text
instructions, and AI Markup tools for visually communicating edit
requests. The update also introduces a beta AI-Assisted Editor,
allowing users to make complex edits through natural-language prompts
while Photoshop automatically selects and combines the appropriate
tools. Adobe says the goal is to let creators spend less time
navigating software and more time focusing on creative decisions.

articles.title: Gamma acquires accel-backed design startup lica
articles.description:
Presentation startup Gamma has acquired Accel-backed Lica to build a
design research lab, which Lica's co-founders will lead. Lica raised
$4 million in 2024 and worked with e-commerce sites on brand-compliant
marketing videos. Gamma now wants to explore fluid, multimodal
presentation formats through the new division.

articles.title: Doing things yourself
articles.description:
Generative AI can deliver a solution before there is time to explore
the problem, removing the detours where creative learning actually
happens. Photoshop began stripping away that friction. AI takes it
much further, especially for students and young designers. The
proposal is not banning AI but designing for Learning Experience
alongside User Experience.

articles.title: Speaking design at scale
articles.description:
Design system pattern names like Overview and PageHeader are
shorthand for decisions a team should not have to reopen every time.
Learning that vocabulary takes a person months, but an agent can read
the repository and retrieve the code, guidance, and examples behind
each name. That lets more people describe a screen in the system's own
language and judge the result.

articles.title: The product designer's role isn't disappearing. it's getting weirder
articles.description:
AI is collapsing the traditional boundaries between product design,
product management, and engineering, making the old handoff-based
workflow increasingly obsolete. As AI tools can now turn ideas,
requirements, and design systems into working prototypes and code,
designers are being pushed toward a broader role the author calls a
product architect—someone who combines product thinking, systems
design, technical understanding, and creative judgment. Rather than
focusing on screens, specs, or deliverables, the most valuable skill
becomes deciding what should be built, how it should work, and whether
it solves a real problem. This can be an opportunity rather than a
threat: design isn't disappearing, but evolving into a more strategic,
multidisciplinary role where taste, judgment, and systems thinking
matter more than execution.

articles.title: How people view ai
articles.description:
Niu Lai, a nearly zero-budget animated film made largely by a Chinese
mother and son on second-hand computers, has become an unexpected box
office hit. Made by former interior designer Xin Yumeng over five
years, the crude, low-quality animation grossed over ¥25.67 million
despite starting with almost no publicity or earnings. Its success is
framed as a reaction against polished, AI-generated visuals, echoing
how punk rock once rebelled against overproduced music.

articles.title: Perfection is not over-engineering
articles.description:
Over-engineering means solving the wrong problem, not caring too
much, or building something too good. With every constraint on the
table, only one solution fits, and that solution is the perfect one.
Over-engineering is therefore a failure of requirements gathering, and
systems need treating as products with real users. 

 THE CBI'S LATEST AI REPORT ON HOW DESIGN BUSINESSES CAN BRIDGE AI'S

articles.title: Execution divide
articles.description:
The real value of AI now comes from integrating it into core business
operations rather than running isolated experiments. Design teams
benefit most when AI supports entire workflows from concept creation
to production. AI's biggest near-term impact is augmenting human work
rather than replacing it, making skills like judgment, creativity, and
critical thinking even more important. Automation is reducing
traditional entry-level design tasks, creating a risk to the future
talent pipeline unless companies redesign junior roles around
AI-assisted workflows while also addressing growing legal and
copyright concerns around AI-generated work.

articles.description:
Creative confusion stalls work, while clarity comes from breaking the
process into phases and knowing which one is current.

articles.title: Cache
articles.description:
Optimizations in how cache entries are stored in the 1.1.1.1 DNS
service led to more than a 50% reduction in memory usage per entry,
