Alipay introduced a full-stack agentic commerce foundation and its
AHA multi-agent, cross-device interconnection protocol suite at an AI
ecosystem conference in Hangzhou. The initiative gives merchants tools
to convert services into agent-accessible capabilities, while enabling
agents across devices and vendors to coordinate authorization,
fulfillment, and settlement, with Alipay reporting thousands of
adapted services and partnerships across smartphones and automakers.

articles.title: Challenge
articles.description:
Dynatrace is acquiring AI observability company Arize for roughly
$915 million, combining Arize's visibility into model outputs, agent
behavior and tool use with Dynatrace's application and infrastructure
telemetry. The goal is to give DevOps and platform teams a clearer way
to trace AI-agent failures back through the services, transactions and
systems they affect.
articles.section: DYNATRACE ACQUIRES ARIZE AS AI AGENTS DEEPEN THE OBSERVABILITY

articles.title: Humanity in open source
articles.description:
End-to-end AI agents are flooding open-source maintainers with
low-quality issues and pull requests, shifting effort away from coding
and toward review. While AI-assisted human contributions can be
useful, open source also depends on qualities that automated patches
cannot replace, such as human conversation, relationships, and
sustained collaboration.

articles.title: We churned notion after 7 years. our ai agent took its last job.
articles.description:
SaaStr canceled Notion after seven years, not because of pricing,
support, or a competing product, but because an internal AI agent
gradually absorbed the last workflow it was being used for. This
creates a new kind of SaaS churn: narrow-purpose tools can disappear
from the stack as agents connect directly to company data and take
over their jobs, making traditional usage and customer-health metrics
less reliable.

articles.title: Top open-source automation platforms
articles.description: Nine open-source automation and workflow platforms.

articles.title: Collaboration use cases
articles.description:
Google is adding least-privilege agent identities, audit trails,
flow-level access controls, human approvals, and DLP protections to
Workspace Studio so admins can more safely allow agentic automations
to act across Gmail, Drive, and other Workspace apps.
articles.section: NEW ENTERPRISE SECURITY CONTROLS FOR WORKSPACE STUDIO ENABLE EXPANDED

articles.title: Lovable confirms new $13.3b valuation, raises another $400m
articles.description:
Vibe-coding startup Lovable has raised $400 million in a Series C
round led by Menlo Ventures and the Scaleup Europe Fund, confirming a
new $13.3 billion valuation. The funding follows Lovable hitting $500
million in annualized run rate revenue in June, up from a $6.6 billion
valuation in its December round. The company now hosts 60 million
projects with 900 million monthly visitors, backed by its own in-house
AI model and a multiyear Google Cloud deal.

articles.title: Bets on ai-ux pairing
articles.description:
Target has named Chandhu Nair as its first chief AI officer and
promoted Purvi Shah to SVP of user experience, pairing AI strategy
with design leadership. Nair will coordinate AI efforts across the
company starting August 24, while Shah's expanded UX role ensures
AI-driven changes still feel "distinctly Target." Both executives
frame the move as part of Target's broader growth strategy, aiming to
keep technology grounded in guest experience rather than pursued as a
standalone initiative. 

 WHILE YOU WERE ANGRY AT INSTAGRAM, JIF QUIETLY DEBUTED A PERFECT NEW
articles.section: TARGET NAMES FIRST CHIEF AI OFFICER AND ELEVATES DESIGN CHIEF AS IT

articles.title: Logo
articles.description:
Jif has introduced its first major logo refresh in 30 years,
simplifying the design by removing visual clutter and bringing back
its classic tri-colour banner while largely preserving its familiar
identity. The update has attracted little attention, especially
compared to more controversial rebrands, because it focuses on
refinement rather than reinvention. Its low-profile reception
highlights how branding discussions often reward dramatic changes and
controversy over thoughtful, evolutionary design.
articles.section: TARGET NAMES FIRST CHIEF AI OFFICER AND ELEVATES DESIGN CHIEF AS IT

articles.title: You don't have a design system
articles.description:
Design systems often standardize components while leaving larger
structural decisions—like settings page layout and
behavior—uncaptured, causing inconsistent results even within one
product. Testing this with AI agents building identical settings pages
from the same component library confirmed the gap: each agent made
different, reasonable choices about layout and interaction since no
canonical pattern existed. Writing down explicit rules for structure,
behavior, and interaction (not just components) resolved the
divergence, producing consistent pages across agents.

articles.title: Useful books for designers who work on complex problems
articles.description:
A curated list of 18 books that help designers tackle complex,
high-stakes systems in enterprise, legacy, or hierarchical
environments. Recommendations span strategy and risk, such as How Big
Things Get Done and Thinking in Bets, systems thinking, like Thinking
in Systems and The Goal, and communication or data visualization
titles, including Articulating Design Decisions and Envisioning
Information.

articles.title: How to become an ai designer
articles.description:
A product designer shares how AI transformed their workflow from
creating designs in Figma to building interactive prototypes, shipping
frontend code, and treating the product itself as the design source of
truth. By using AI tools to prototype, iterate, and implement designs
directly, they gained greater influence over product development and
UI quality. While this approach significantly increases speed and
output, they argue that AI cannot accelerate creativity, taste, or
design thinking, and that the gains in efficiency come with a growing
sense of distance from the craft of design.

articles.title: Claude code 101, for designers
articles.description:
Claude Code extends Anthropic's Claude beyond chat into a terminal
tool that can create, edit, and run files, building full apps rather
than just describing prototypes. Key concepts include context windows
and tokens (its working memory), sessions (single continuous
workstreams), CLAUDE.md (a standing project brief), approval modes,
commands, skills, agents, and MCP (a connector standard linking Claude
to outside tools). This piece is the first in a series aimed at
helping product designers transition to using Claude Code, focusing
purely on defining the surrounding jargon.

articles.title: Youtube's new policy is bad news for animators
articles.description:
Starting February 1, YouTube will double the requirements for
monetization eligibility: 8,000 watch hours annually or 20 million
Shorts views within three months. Existing Partner Program members and
Fan Funding/shopping thresholds remain unaffected, though YouTube
expects overall creator earnings to rise via expanded Premium Lite
availability. New independent animators face a steeper climb since
their content-heavy production process makes it harder to hit these
higher thresholds quickly.

articles.title: Old rules, bad advice: 10 design myths everyone still believes
articles.description:
Ten stubborn UI/UX myths—from the three-click rule to "more
features equal better"—get traced back to outdated, context-specific
origins that no longer hold up.

articles.title: The new instagram logo is the perfect embodiment of ai slop
articles.description:
Instagram unveiled a refreshed wordmark, its first update in a
decade, which Adam Mosseri described as leaner, more modern, and true
to the platform's original simplicity and craft.

articles.title: Together with aws: work the problem, not the slide deck
How to ship a database every day
articles.description:
The implementation of a local state machine in each turbopuffer
cluster allows for autonomous operation and management without needing
direct access from the control plane. By using a custom API and a
user-friendly dashboard, the system effectively manages over 100
database clusters while enabling rapid, multiple daily deployments and
fleet operations.

articles.title: How bluesky draws its logo on screenshots
articles.description:
Bluesky uses a creative method to display its logo on screenshots
while hiding it during normal app use by using a UITextField with a
specific property that masks content when a screenshot is taken. This
technique prevents the logo from being visible when switching between
apps, relying on iOS's behavior of capturing a snapshot at the
gesture's start.

articles.title: Cut your fastify log volume with logcontroller
articles.description:
A Fastify health check polled every 5 seconds produces over a million
log lines a month, but Fastify already has two built-in fixes rather
than needing a new core option. The quick one is registering noisy
routes in a plugin with logLevel: 'silent', though that mutes your own
logs and failures too. The flexible one is subclassing LogController
and overriding only the methods for the lines you care about.

articles.title: Ai;dr (ai; didn't read)
articles.description:
The increasing prevalence of unedited AI-generated content has led to
frustration among many, resulting in AI;DR (AI; didn't read) as a way
to dismiss such output. A new policy emphasizes the importance of
reviewing and editing AI-generated materials to maintain quality and
make sure that the human touch remains in communication.

articles.title: Gpt 5.6 sol is the best "vision" model openai ever released
articles.description:
OpenAI's recent release of the GPT-5.6 lineup, particularly the Sol
model, demonstrates advancements in vision capabilities, with improved
performance in object detection and counting compared to its
predecessor, GPT-5.5. While Sol excels in various visual tasks, it
still faces challenges related to cost, latency, and occasional
detection errors. 

 ANTHROPIC'S ‘WATERMARK' TEXT ADULTERATION IN CLAUDE IS A PERVERSION

articles.title: Of writing
articles.description:
Anthropic's implementation of text watermarking in its Claude AI
models is criticized for compromising the quality and clarity of
generated text by introducing a system that subtly biases word choices
to meet compliance with EU regulations. This approach is viewed as
detrimental to writing integrity, as it prioritizes detection over
quality.

articles.title: Agents can now sign up for your app
articles.description:
Agents hit your signup flow and bounce off a login built for humans.
Every one that gives up is a signup you never see. WorkOS Agent
Registration [14] turns that traffic into signups. Enroll via the
dashboard and AuthKit publishes an auth.md file agents read to
register for scoped, short-lived credentials you control. 

 ORIGIN CODE HOSTING (WEBSITE) [15] 

 Cursor has introduced a new platform called Origin, which allows
users to host their code with essential tools like repos, pull
requests, code browsing, and GitHub synchronization. Users can create
new repositories, sync existing GitHub repos, and manage pull
requests, with integration options for deployment and continuous
integration services like Vercel, Depot, and Buildkite. 

 HUNK (GITHUB REPO) [16] 

 Hunk is a terminal-based diff viewer designed for reviewing
changesets with a focus on interactivity and agent-assisted features,
offering capabilities such as inline AI annotations and responsive
layouts. It supports integration with popular version control systems
and allows users to customize their experience through configuration
files and extensions.

articles.title: How teams build
articles.description:
AI adoption in software development teams has increased across
various functions, with engagement from executives and a consistent
rise in usage among companies of all sizes. The introduction of AI
tools has led to a dramatic increase in output through the use of
coding agents, while also revealing a trend of non-engineers becoming
more involved in coding and product development.

articles.title: Red agent exploits snowflake vuln missed by github copilot
articles.description:
Wiz Red Agent autonomously identified and exploited a critical GitHub
Actions vulnerability in Snowflake's public repository, allowing
unauthorized access to sensitive data in its internal Jira system just
five days after the flaw was introduced. This incident shows the risks
of relying on AI-assisted coding tools, which may inadvertently
introduce vulnerabilities that can be quickly discovered and exploited
by automated security agents.

articles.title: State of open models: summer 2026 observations
articles.description:
Chinese labs now set the open-model size ceiling, yet downloads still
belong overwhelmingly to small, years-old models. Qwen has become the
community's default base model with 151,448 derivatives, while the
runtime layer grows far faster than the modeling core, letting
trillion-parameter models run locally via llama.cpp. The new
development is agents: they're now the Hub's top user, with agent
traffic share swinging wildly month to month.

articles.title: Most llm apps have solved retrieval. action is the hard part
articles.description:
This guide lays out the 5 prereqs for agentic document workflows and
shows you how to convert, extract, and sign at scale. Read the guide
on Foxit's blog [20] 

 QWEN 3.8 27B IS EXCELLENT, BUT IT DEFAULTS TO WILDLY OVERTHINKING

articles.title: Things
articles.description:
Qwen 3.8 27B is a powerful yet slow vision-capable language model
that tends to over-analyze prompts by default, requiring users to
adjust its reasoning settings for more efficient outputs. 

 ASK HN: ALTERNATIVES TO GITHUB (HACKER NEWS THREAD) [22] 

 There is a growing interest in exploring alternatives for code
hosting and collaboration due to recent consistent outages on GitHub.

articles.title: A simple fix for llm tail latency
articles.description:
For improving latency in real-time LLM applications, it is often more
effective to send each request twice for faster responses, rather than
opting for a more expensive priority service tier.

articles.title: Intriguing stories in computer science
articles.description:
This is a compilation of anecdotes and lessons from the history of
computer science and software development that shows both notable
successes and critical failures.

articles.description:
Devs finally have a challenger to GitHub code hosting with Origin.

Origin was built _on_ Buildkite.

Buildkite is a launch partner for this new code ecosystem. Origin

articles.title: Tesla cybercab launch preparations have begun
articles.description:
Tesla plans to launch the Cybercab in Austin, Texas, later this
month. Employees have been told to prepare for a public launch as soon
as the end of the month. Tesla has launched a lottery to ride the
vehicle at the launch event. The Cybercab entered production back in
April, and the company has been testing units in a variety of
environments and climates around the US.

articles.title: Google just bought a bunch of spirit airlines data for ai training
articles.description:
Google has purchased a huge dump of data from the now-defunct Spirit
Airlines for $10 million. The dump includes data on operations and
business, as well as software code, but not personal information. All
personally identifiable information will be rigorously scrubbed by a
third party before receipt. Google will use the data to improve its
products and AI models.

articles.title: Steel parts
articles.description:
1872 is a startup founded by three former SpaceX engineers that aims
to manufacture steel parts using AI-driven software and robots. The
company's immediate goal is to establish a prototype factory that can
automate most of the steel fabrication process for crucial
infrastructure components by 2027. It aims to supply customers who are
developing AI data centers or small modular nuclear reactors. 1872
will first focus on automating the production of rectangular steel
skids.
articles.section:
SCIENCE & FUTURISTIC TECHNOLOGY

 FORMER SPACEX ENGINEERS ARE BUILDING A ROBOTIC FACTORY FOR MAKING

articles.title: Clinic-in-the-loop
articles.description:
Faster testing in the clinic creates a feedback loop. Ideas become
trials that generate rich data, which improves data models, and better
models inform the next generation of ideas. The clinic is a central
component of discovery. Even data from failed trials can be useful.
Optimizing trial efficiency is about learning fast enough to make
success more likely.
articles.section:
SCIENCE & FUTURISTIC TECHNOLOGY

 FORMER SPACEX ENGINEERS ARE BUILDING A ROBOTIC FACTORY FOR MAKING

articles.title: Agent evals
articles.description:
Does your LLM app eval process trace multi-agent workflows from end
to end, or are you waiting for users to let you know something broke?
This Datadog guide [10] shows you how to evaluate LLM agents offline.
Know how your app behaves across edge cases and adversarial inputs,
before you ship. Get the framework [10]

articles.title: Ai usage patterns in software teams
articles.description:
Tens of thousands of teams build software inside Linear every day.
The company is unusually well placed to see the entire workflow behind
building a product. This post provides a picture of AI adoption within
Linear's customer base. It looks at who is using AI, how it reshapes
where teams spend their time across Linear, and whether it has changed
how much they ship.

articles.title: Origin code hosting
articles.description:
Cursor can now host code through its Origin platform. Origin is
designed for agent scale. It supports repositories, pull requests,
code browsing, and GitHub sync. GitHub repositories can sit alongside
the ones Cursor hosts. Synced repositories update in real time, and
users can choose what gets synced and disconnect a repository at any
time. Origin is now rolling out in early beta to all paid plan users,
except enterprise organizations whose admins opt out.

articles.title: Waymo vs tesla: two ways to build self-driving cars
articles.description:
Waymo and Tesla have come up with different answers to the
self-driving car problem. Both approaches depend heavily on machine
learning, but they differ in how much gets fixed in advance. Waymo has
a reported 220.6 million rider-only miles, while almost all of Tesla's
miles involve a driver who remains responsible for the vehicle. This
article looks at the companies' different approaches to self-driving
and explains how they work. 

 ANTHROPIC TELLS INVESTORS ANNUALIZED REVENUE RUN RATE CLIMBED TO $65

articles.title: Billion in july
articles.description:
Anthropic's annualized run rate hit $65 billion at the end of July.
The company has seen its enterprise popularity surge as it gears up
for what's expected to be a blockbuster IPO. It filed its prospectus
with the SEC in June and has been holding preliminary meetings with
potential investors. There is still no official timeline for the
debut.

articles.title: Put granola on your apple watch
articles.description:
Thankfully, not every meeting happens in front of a screen. Now you
can capture in-person convos from your wrist - transparently (bright
green when transcription is running). Available now [18] with code
TLDR1MO.

articles.title: A good move is constructive
articles.description: Every good move in the product game creates strategic possibility.

articles.title: Your ci should be disposable
articles.description: CIs have one job: scheduling.

articles.title: How i use ai in 2026 (coding, writing, learning, assistant-ing)
articles.description:
One of the best ways to learn how to use AI effectively is to see how
'power users' use these technologies.

articles.title: Reach 8 million engaged tech professionals
articles.description:
Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach developers,
PMs, marketers, founders and other tech leaders where they actually
pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities. [22]

articles.title: The benchmarkpocalypse
articles.description:
It is now easier than ever to reward hack a benchmark and make fake
performance gains.

articles.title: Help peer
articles.description:
Modern AI research teams are full of people who read Isaac Asimov and
Scott Alexander and believe themselves to be building an artificial
God, but in reality, they're building beings that are superhuman but
fallible, each with their own interests and vulnerable to the same
'race to the bottom' dynamic as humans.

articles.title: Tbm 437: tokens, hours, points, and other curious proxies
articles.description:
AI introduces some genuinely new twists on the problem of measuring
ROI, but in the end, it still hinges on a theory of value.

articles.description:
Tines 3B [5] gives every team the power to build with AI, and gives
IT the control to run and monitor that work safely. 

With Tines 3B: 

 	* Turn ideas into production-ready apps, agents, and automations in

articles.title: Glm-5.3: frontier coding with emergent cyber capabilities
articles.description:
Z.ai has released GLM-5.3. The only improvement on the model is the
amount of post-training performed. Z.ai continued scaling on its stack
with more environments, more diverse tasks, and more compute,
resulting in a model that is much better at complex coding and
long-horizon tasks. Every gain comes from post-training. 

 NVIDIA DOWNSIZES PLANS FOR $250 BILLION GUARANTEE OF OPENAI DATA

articles.title: Center
articles.description:
Nvidia and OpenAI are close to closing a financial deal for a
large-scale data-center campus in Ohio. Under the deal, Nvidia would
provide a financial backstop for the first phase of the project,
totaling roughly five gigawatts of power. OpenAI will then have to
decide later whether or how to finance the remainder. Nvidia
originally planned to invest $250 billion into the deal, but lowered
its guarantee to less than $120 billion to address investors' concerns
about the chipmaker's risk exposure.

articles.title: Stripe will reportedly acquire openrouter for over $7b
articles.description:
Stripe reportedly agreed to acquire AI model-routing startup
OpenRouter for more than $7 billion. OpenRouter, which lets developers
route requests across models based on factors such as capability and
price, had reportedly been valued at $1.3 billion after its May
funding round.

articles.title: Cursor is now a part of spacex
articles.description:
SpaceX has acquired Cursor to enhance AI model training using its
extensive GPU resources. This acquisition enables Cursor to develop
stronger and more cost-effective AI models. Grok 4.6, recently
released, demonstrates the potential of this collaboration.

articles.title: The state of open models in 2026
articles.description:
Hugging Face reviewed major developments across the open-model
ecosystem from January through August, using ecosystem data to
highlight how model releases, tooling, and adoption had shifted since
its spring report.

articles.title: Understanding agent memory
articles.description:
This analysis compared persistent agent memory built from curated
files, automatically maintained structured stores, and learned
experience. It examined the approaches under controlled models and
agentic benchmarks to show how different memory representations
affected performance.

articles.title: Glm-5.3: how chinese labs keep stride with the frontier
articles.description:
Z.ai has a time-to-release of likely days, rather than months as with
OpenAI or Anthropic. While OpenAI and Anthropic likely have far better
internal models, the companies tend to take months to release their
models to the public. Z.ai probably cares a little more about public
benchmarks than its US counterparts, but it is not benchmaxxing to the
point where it is too obvious with GLM-5.3. The RL industry is taking
off in China, very much driven by US data companies selling to Chinese
model labs.

articles.title: On dwarkesh patel's podcast with ryan greenblatt
articles.description:
Dwarkesh Patel and Ryan Greenblatt's podcast debate focused on
recursive self-improvement (RSI) and AI alignment challenges,
highlighting their differing views on AI's capabilities and risks.
Greenblatt argued for AI's efficiency in certain R&D tasks but
acknowledged difficulties in verifying alignment, suggesting a complex
training process focused on narrow tasks could lead to misaligned
models. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: 😬 reducing tokens does not mean reducing costs
articles.description:
Many tools promise to cut AI costs by reducing the tokens used by
LLMs. PointFive tested whether they actually reduce costs [16] by
running the same prompt across 2,908 Claude Code sessions, with and
without token reduction. Spoiler alert: in some cases, token
compression INCREASED costs by nearly 50%! See the full study results
[16] 

 MATHCODE (WEBSITE) [17] 

 MathCode is a frontier mathematical coding agent. It has a built-in
math formalization engine that converts problems from plain language
into Lean 4 theorems and attempts formal proofs. It features a
persistent Lean REPL, reusable theorem and axiom libraries, agent
proving, and an Obsidian knowledge graph. The math formalization and
proving pipeline is based on the AUTOLEAN project.

articles.title: Introducing custom agents
articles.description:
Google has introduced Custom Agents in Antigravity 2.0 and the
Antigravity CLI, with the Antigravity IDE following shortly. Custom
Agents are specialized, file-based configurations that define a
particular role with its own scoped instructions, tools, and
constraints. The system keeps users' active contexts clean, minimizes
token overhead, and gives them a predictable partner for specific
tasks. Custom agents don't replace skills and dynamic subagents - they
just provide even more customizability for another level of
optimization. 

 LITTLELEARNER (WEBSITE) [19] 

 LittleLearner is a language model that only knows what a 5th grader
knows. The hosted 5B model can be run live in browser. LittleLearner
was created as part of an experiment in creating controlled sandboxes
for studying how models acquire knowledge.

articles.title: Microsoft's full-bandwidth transformers
articles.description:
Full-bandwidth transformers fed the previous token's top-layer hidden
state back into the model alongside the next token embedding. This
allows latent computation to continue across decoding steps.

articles.title: Launch
articles.description:
Days before OpenAI previewed Ultrafast, a service tier that can run
GPT-5.6 Sol at up to 750 output tokens a second, OpenAI exercised
every vested Cerebras warrant share, acquiring 10,033,508 Class N
shares at $0.00001 each for about $100 in cash. The stake has an
implied value of near $2.3 billion, though the shares carry no votes.
Cerebras is now running every competitive speed offering at OpenAI.
OpenAI has yet to publish price, model ID, or general-availability
date for Ultrafast.

articles.title: Dario amodei on regulation and the messaging around ai
articles.description:
Either concentrating AI in the hands of a chosen few companies and
politicians via regulation or distributing it widely is a false
choice. Those in that frame of mind often underrate the decentralizing
power of objective and fair institutional processes. The public's
negative view of AI is fundamentally a crisis of trust. Ordinary
people don't trust companies, governments, or the tech industry. AI
companies have still yet to deliver on their big promises to benefit
the world.

articles.title: Are ai models breaking the shift-left model?
articles.description:
Recent models have shown shocking capabilities to find and exploit
vulnerabilities. Previous shift-left strategies might not be enough.
Join Sonatype and IDC for a live webinar [26] on the new AppSec rules 

 GOOGLE REPORTEDLY TAPS AMD TO DESIGN NEXT-GENERATION TPU — HYBRID
AI ASIC COULD INTEGRATE ON-PACKAGE CPU CORES FOR REINFORCEMENT

articles.title: Learning
articles.description:
Google appears to be exploring a new kind of TPU that combines its
proprietary accelerator technology with on-board general-purpose cores
for CPU-heavy workloads.

articles.title: When the hard part stops being hard
articles.description:
In a world where producing work is easy, we need to be more ambitious
and take on challenges we could not have imagined a couple of years
ago. 

 QWEN 3.8 27B IS EXCELLENT, BUT IT DEFAULTS TO WILDLY OVERTHINKING

articles.title: Things
articles.description:
Qwen 3.8 27B is an Apache 2 licensed 27B parameter vision-capable LLM
from Alibaba's Qwen research lab.

articles.title: Openai sheds senior execs in pre-ipo refresh
articles.description:
OpenAI has seen significant leadership changes, including the
departure of top executives like the chief revenue officer, COO, and
head of ethics, ahead of an anticipated IPO.

articles.title: The ai engineering skills map
articles.description:
AI engineering now centers on four skills: building and deploying AI
applications, software fundamentals, coding-agent fluency, and shaping
what gets built.

articles.title: Ai agents are already on your team. is your security keeping up?
articles.description:
Most organizations now have AI agents running in production -
handling support tickets, pulling financial reports, accessing
enterprise systems. Most of them were stood up without IT's
involvement. Most have no owner. Most have no off switch.

New research from JumpCloud surveyed 800 IT leaders on how they're
governing their agentic workforce. The finding that stands out:
organizations have implemented just 3.1 of 10 recommended AI
governance controls on average - even as non-human identities now
outnumber humans in 83% of environments.

The gap between AI adoption and AI governance is the defining IT
challenge of the next decade.

→ Read the research
→ See how Agentic IAM works
→ Secure every identity. Human or not. [5]

articles.title: It's final! judge says hpe's juniper acquisition is complete
articles.description:
A federal judge approved HPE's settlement with the Justice
Department, clearing the final legal challenge to its $14 billion
acquisition of Juniper Networks. The ruling removes lingering
uncertainty around the deal and lets HPE move ahead integrating
Juniper's networking portfolio into the combined company.

articles.title: Cisco rides ‘networking supercycle' for strong q4
articles.description:
Cisco reported record quarterly revenue of $17.3 billion as
networking product orders jumped 40% year over year, with campus
orders up 20% and data center networking orders rising 25% for the
year. Cisco says only about 7% of its campus switching installed base
has been refreshed so far, suggesting the broader enterprise upgrade
cycle is still early.

articles.title: Salesforce, servicenow data targeted in ‘city-forum' attacks
articles.description:
Researchers identified a new campaign targeting data stored in
Salesforce and ServiceNow environments through their UI/API layers
rather than traditional infrastructure exploits. The attackers have
also been probing a little-documented native ServiceNow Service Portal
search endpoint, highlighting the growing risk around authenticated
SaaS access and APIs.

articles.title: Why 6 ghz wi-fi will make or break the modern enterprise
articles.description:
The additional spectrum available at 6 GHz can effectively triple
wireless capacity compared with legacy bands while moving modern
devices away from congested 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz channels. Wi-Fi 6E and
Wi-Fi 7 upgrades should now be treated as infrastructure modernization
rather than simply another wireless refresh. 

 THE VENDOR CONSOLIDATION TRAP: WHEN ONE THROAT TO CHOKE COSTS MORE

articles.title: Than it saves
articles.description:
Reducing the number of technology vendors can simplify operations and
create short-term savings, but it can also destroy negotiating
leverage once switching becomes expensive. IT teams should keep at
least one credible alternative warm in major categories so vendors
know the customer can realistically walk away at renewal.

articles.title: Apple's price hikes are a warning to it
articles.description:
Memory shortages are pushing hardware prices higher across Apple,
Dell, Lenovo, HP and other manufacturers, creating a new challenge for
IT procurement and device lifecycle planning. With DRAM supply
expected to remain constrained, enterprises may need to revisit
refresh schedules, purchasing commitments and hardware budgets. 

🤝

articles.title: Take notes for me for in-person meetings is now available
articles.description:
Google is expanding Meet's “Take notes for me” beyond video calls
so users can capture in-person conversations directly from the Meet
home screen. Gemini records the discussion and creates a structured
summary, action items, and transcript in a Google Doc stored in Drive.

articles.title: Ibm partners with openai to drive enterprise ai deployment
articles.description:
IBM will embed OpenAI models and products including ChatGPT and Codex
into its consulting offerings while creating a dedicated OpenAI
practice and certifying thousands of consultants and engineers. The
partnership will focus on enterprise transformation, legacy
application modernization and cybersecurity.

articles.title: E-commerce empire
articles.description:
Amazon is redistributing parts of its e-commerce infrastructure
across more AWS regions under an internal effort called Region Flex,
partly because power and data center capacity have become increasingly
constrained in major hubs. The project includes more than 100 software
migrations and illustrates how electricity availability is beginning
to influence application architecture and cloud-region strategy.

articles.title: Oneui 9.5
articles.description:
Leaks suggest Samsung is exploring a glass-inspired redesign for One
UI 9.5, featuring shinier edges, transparency effects, background
blurring, greater visual depth, and possibly a new App Lock feature.
While the update remains unconfirmed and likely won't arrive until
2027, it indicates Samsung may be pursuing a more visually expressive
interface rather than simply refining its current design.

articles.title: Whatsapp working on customizable emoji reaction sets on ios
articles.description:
WhatsApp is testing a feature that would let users customize the six
default emoji reactions shown when reacting to messages, replacing
them with emojis of their choice and restoring the defaults at any
time. The feature is not yet available to beta testers but appears to
be in development for both iOS and Android, with a possible tie-in to
WhatsApp Plus. 

 ADOBE'S AI COLLABORATORS TURN OUTSIDE AI AGENTS INTO GOVERNED

articles.title: Workfront teammates
articles.description:
Adobe has made AI Collaborators generally available in Workfront,
letting users delegate tasks to outside AI agents from Microsoft
Copilot Studio, Anthropic's Claude, and Writer as governed,
permissioned teammates. These collaborators—task agents and
brand-compliance reviewers now live, with a project coordinator coming
soon—receive full project context automatically and return work for
human review and approval. Alongside this, Adobe also launched
Workfront MCP, enabling users to bring Workfront project data into
Claude, Copilot, Gemini, or ChatGPT.

articles.title: Getting started is not getting it right
articles.description:
AI excels at overcoming the blank-page problem and generating first
drafts, but significant human effort is still required to verify
outputs, catch hallucinations, and ensure quality, especially for
complex or specialized work. While it can accelerate some tasks, it
often introduces new costs through fact-checking, rework,
accessibility issues, and subtle inaccuracies that become harder to
spot as models improve. Organizations will get more value from AI by
defining where it is reliable, where human review is mandatory, and
where expert-led work remains the better option.

articles.title: Rethinking design leadership with swarms and flocks
articles.description:
High-performing teams work best when they combine local autonomy with
a small set of shared rules, allowing people to adapt quickly without
losing alignment or direction. Leadership should focus less on
controlling decisions and more on enabling communication, rotating
responsibility, protecting team health, and reinforcing a few core
principles that guide the work. Regularly pausing to improve systems,
reduce technical or design debt, and invest in learning helps teams
maintain speed and resilience over the long term.

articles.title: Your ux team is set up for the wrong job
articles.description:
Everyone across an organization is now designing using AI tools,
which means UX teams need to shift roles rather than absorb more
direct production work. Instead of routing all design through a small
team, successful organizations move designers upstream to build design
systems, playbooks, research repositories, and AI-briefing standards
that guide everyone else's output. Cutting design teams to cut costs
saves money short-term but creates inconsistency, accessibility
issues, and rework, so success should be measured by adoption of these
resources rather than throughput.

articles.title: Other brands are throwing shade at the new instagram logo
articles.description:
Instagram has replaced its 10-year-old wordmark with a cleaner, more
digital-looking version, a change that has sparked criticism for being
less distinctive and harder to read. The company says the update was
simply due to the logo's age, prompting jokes from other brands about
redesigning their own long-standing logos for the same reason. While
some users welcome the refresh, many see it as a cosmetic change that
does little to address broader perceptions of the platform.

articles.title: Finding and fixing design system drift
articles.description:
Design drift — the gap between Figma files and shipped product —
is inevitable in fast-moving teams and stems from entropy, not
negligence or failure. Screen drift, involving easily spotted
rendering differences, differs from component drift, which involves
underlying changes requiring human judgment. AI can assist with visual
diffing to catch the former. Code represents "now" while Figma
represents "next," and scheduled reconciliation between the two lets
Figma regain its authority for planning future changes.

articles.title: Vibe coded apps are the new shadow it
articles.description:
AI-generated internal tools now create infrastructure with IAM roles
and no ticket, review, or security involvement, unlike traditional
SaaS-based shadow IT. A layered defense is proposed: platform controls
prevent risky defaults, while process controls require automated
baseline checks and security-informed human review before deployment.
Cloud security posture management tools and behavioral telemetry
signals serve as a detection safety net for tooling that slips through
preventive layers undetected.

articles.title: Finger to ai art
articles.description:
Bakatako is a free, browser-based daily doodle site requiring artwork
to be created directly on its canvas, ensuring human-made rather than
AI-generated content.

articles.title: 20+ tasty candy fonts for sweet & colorful designs
articles.description:
This collection presents 20+ candy-inspired fonts featuring soft
curves, bubble shapes, and playful lettering suited for packaging,
social media, invitations, and children's designs.

articles.title: Do the right work with jira
articles.description:
Don't let your agents start cold. The Teamwork Graph in Jira by
Atlassian [5] feeds agents context from across your entire stack,
delivering 44% more accurate results. With Jira, you can stay in
control at scale and ensure the work agents pick up is the right work,
done right the first time. Learn more [6]. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: Baseline with codex in gpu mode's qr_v2 problem
articles.description:
In a recent auto-research contest focusing on GPU optimizations, an
impressive 232x speedup over the baseline was achieved in implementing
the batched square compact-Householder QR factorization problem, with
the author finishing 12th out of 183 participants. The project
involved using techniques like the blocked Householder algorithm,
continual kernel profiling, and iteration on ideas presented through
advanced AI models.

articles.title: Maximizing the value of your claude code sessions
Models are getting dumber on purpose
articles.description:
Recent advancements in AI models show that while their reasoning
capabilities continue to improve per parameter, their factual recall
has notably declined, suggesting a deliberate trade-off where
knowledge is sacrificed for reasoning skills. This shift allows models
to operate effectively by relying on external information sources to
provide up-to-date facts, reducing issues like hallucination by
enabling the model to reference and verify information against live
data rather than fixed weights.

articles.title: Software engineering fundamentals matter more than ever
articles.description:
Software engineering involves carefully navigating choices and
problem-solving, especially in the context of AI tools and agentic
engineering. While large models show potential in software
development, effective coding still relies heavily on human reasoning
and thoughtful design for maintainable and debuggable systems.

articles.title: Don't be a meat proxy
articles.description:
Using AI-generated responses as a middleman in communication can
detract from the value of conversations, as it leads to
misunderstanding and unnecessary complexity. Instead of only relaying
AI output, individuals should engage with the content, understand it,
and respond in their own words to add real value to discussions.

articles.title: Why does opus 5 feel worse to work with?
articles.description:
Working with Opus 5 feels less effective compared to its predecessors
primarily because it requires more oversight and fails to seek
clarification in ambiguous situations. This issue comes from a focus
on developing self-improving AI systems that excel on benchmarks,
which often focus on bold assumptions over the necessary inquiry and
flexibility required in real-life tasks.

articles.title: The first agent skills for barcode scanning
articles.description:
Your AI coding agent writes bad barcode scanning code. Wrong
defaults. Broken edge cases. Deprecated APIs. Scandit Agent Skills fix
that. One command teaches Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, and 40+
agents to integrate barcode, ID, and label scanning better than most
humans can, validated against ~500 real-world eval cases.

Try Scandit Agent Skills for free [14]

 This is a collection of free customizable UI components designed for
AI agents, with elements for managing thinking states, tool calls, and
text streams, along with various coding utilities and structured
outputs.

articles.title: Glm-5.3: frontier coding with emergent cyber capabilities
articles.description:
GLM-5.3 has been released, with improvements in coding capabilities
and cyber functions, achieving a 50% enhancement over its predecessor
in complex coding tasks and dominating various benchmarks involving
vulnerability discovery and exploitation. The model is set to be
open-sourced in two weeks after completing safety evaluations.

articles.title: Who are the token brokers?
articles.description:
“Token brokers" are individuals who purchase unused API credits
from startups to resell them. They have commercialized the token relay
market. This emerging market is characterized by various online
platforms offering discounts on credits for major cloud and inference
providers.

articles.title: The temu-fication of software, digital goods & services
articles.description:
The trend towards the "TEMU-fication" of software and digital goods
predicts a future where the majority of content will be produced
cheaply by AI, resulting in lower quality and a two-tier market, with
human-created products becoming a luxury niche. As mass-produced
digital content becomes the norm, it will be needed for consumers to
consciously choose between generated and authentic works.

articles.title: A fortuitous decade as an indie software developer
articles.description:
After quitting his job in 2016, an indie software developer faced
struggles for five years, culminating in a turning point with the
release of iOS 15, which revitalized his business and allowed him to
rebuild his savings. Despite facing ongoing challenges and not
replicating his initial success, he embraces a spontaneous approach to
his career, continuing to innovate and adapt without long-term plans.

articles.title: Something nobody told you about the image element (it can overflow!)
articles.description:
The image element in HTML can overflow due to properties like
`object-fit` and `border-radius`, showing its complexity as both a
container and content.

The rise of AI in software development could lead to security issues,
potentially causing US intelligence and law enforcement agencies to
lose critical access to communications and intelligence, resulting in
a "going dark" scenario.

articles.description:
Argo Workflows 4.1 adds OpenTelemetry tracing, improved resource and
artifact management, GPU and device allocation through Kubernetes DRA,
stronger database authentication and reliability, expanded CLI
capabilities, UI enhancements, and reduced controller memory usage.

articles.title: Secure all your internal vibe-coded applications — in one click
articles.description:
Cloudflare has launched tools that let account administrators apply
Access authentication policies directly to Workers, the company's
serverless application platform. A policy set at the account level
automatically covers all Workers in that account, current and future,
without requiring individual developers to configure anything. Access
can protect preview URLs, production traffic, or both, and
authenticated requests now expose user identity data through a context
object so developers can personalize responses or log activity per
user.

articles.title: How to run terraform in bitbucket pipelines
articles.description:
Bitbucket Pipelines provides a built-in CI/CD workflow for automating
Terraform and OpenTofu, with reusable YAML steps for formatting,
validation, planning, and applying infrastructure changes. The guide
demonstrates AWS S3 state storage and OIDC authentication, while
highlighting dedicated infrastructure automation platforms as
alternatives.

articles.title: How cloudflare detects mcp traffic and helps secure it
articles.description:
Cloudflare is adding new controls to its Zero Trust platform to help
security teams monitor and manage AI agent traffic using the Model
Context Protocol (MCP). The new tools include a Gateway selector that
detects MCP traffic based on protocol headers, a dashboard showing
which hosts and users are generating that traffic, and Traffic Source
selectors that let administrators distinguish requests routed through
approved MCP Server Portals from direct connections that bypass them.
MCP Portals now also support pre-registered OAuth clients, covering
providers that require a fixed client ID and secret rather than
dynamic registration. Private network connectivity for MCP Portals is
in development. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: Models are getting dumber on purpose
articles.description:
Smaller models are improving rapidly at reasoning while retaining
less factual knowledge, shifting more of the system's intelligence
into retrieval, tools, and external context supplied at runtime. This
trade can make models cheaper, more current, and easier to correct
because facts live in inspectable data sources rather than opaque
weights, while the model focuses on reusable reasoning procedures.

articles.title: Ai software development – what does the data say?
articles.description:
Recent research on AI-assisted software development shows a
consistent gap between higher output and better outcomes: teams
generate more code, commits, and larger diffs, but often do not ship
faster or produce better software. Evidence also points to limitations
in long-horizon agent reliability, effective context size,
repository-level instructions, and benchmark realism, suggesting AI
amplifies existing engineering strengths and weaknesses rather than
replacing disciplined development practices.

articles.title: Docker desktop gets a hypervisor of its own
articles.description:
Docker is introducing a unified virtual machine manager in Docker
Desktop 4.86 beta to deliver consistent performance across macOS,
Windows, and eventually Linux. The internally built VMM aims to
improve startup, recovery, I/O, file sharing, and memory efficiency
while reducing platform-specific inconsistencies from third-party
virtualization systems.

articles.title: Recover from infra failures with flyte 2
articles.description:
Keep your workloads running with durability. Recover from failures
and scale to production with self-healing workflows, agent-native

articles.description:
AI coding agents are increasingly capable of producing working,
testable software, but they remain much weaker at choosing
abstractions, designing clean interfaces, and making systems
maintainable, debuggable, and composable over time.

articles.title: Stripe clinches over $7 billion deal to buy ai firm openrouter
articles.description:
Stripe has finalized an agreement to acquire OpenRouter, a startup
that helps companies switch between AI models. The sale price of more
than $7 billion could change and the discussions are not public.
OpenRouter's rise highlights the industry's growing scrutiny on AI
costs. The acquisition will give Stripe a stronger footing in the
fast-growing AI sector.

articles.title: Anthropic sees ai risks rising, no plan to release stronger "model 2"
articles.description:
Anthropic says it will not release an internal model it claims to be
more powerful than Mythos and that it will not slow development
broadly. The company believes that the risks of the most serious harms
from its models are still low. While the company is seeing signs of
acceleration in its models' ability to conduct automated research and
development, it appears to be signaling that it is getting harder to
understand the capabilities and risks of its own models. OpenAI says
it is slowing down the release of an upcoming model called Astra
because it can't rule out critical cyber capabilities.

articles.title: Pandemic, from complex systems
articles.description:
Far-UVC 222 has been shown to efficiently inactivate airborne
pathogens in a room-sized chamber. While the technology is unlikely to
prevent the average common cold, mostly spread through close, extended
contact, it could be helpful in blunting a future respiratory pandemic
where more of the spread happens at a range through shared air. It is
functionally equivalent to an extremely strong air purifier. The
biggest bottleneck to the technology's adoption currently is
awareness.

articles.title: The world's largest electric plane takes flight
articles.description:
Heart Aerospace's X1 electric aircraft has a 106-foot wingspan and
weighs more than 25,000 pounds. It flew for 27 minutes on battery
power alone and reached an altitude of 1,100 feet during its recent
maiden flight. Heart plans to bring a hybrid-electric plane into
commercial service by 2031. The company's technology promises lower
maintenance costs and insulation from volatile jet fuel prices for
airlines.

articles.title: Reach 7 million engaged tech professionals
articles.description:
Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach developers,
PMs, marketers, founders and other tech leaders where they actually
pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities. [10]

articles.title: No plan survives contact with the enemy (reality)
articles.description:
If your most precious commodity is attention, ask your agents for the
design after they've built the thing. Let the agent spend extra cycles
in the lab, and get one layer deeper on the design. A plan that's been
prototyped is a better plan.

articles.title: A quick look at zero-knowledge proofs
articles.description:
The idea of a zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) is that there are two
parties: the prover and the verifier. The prover asserts that it has a
solution to a (generally NP-complete) problem. The prover can convince
the verifier of this without sharing the actual solution to the
problem. While they are used to secure some cryptocurrencies, that is
not their only use case. This article looks at how ZKPs work and how
they can be applied to other problems like age verification.

articles.title: So you want to build an ai star?
articles.description:
Several companies are attempting to build the synthetic superstars of
tomorrow. AI imaging tools have enabled anyone with a modest budget
and a sliver of vision to build their own photorealistic avatars. The
availability of virtual talent has unsettled many communities of human
performers. While AI influencers likely won't replace human
influencers fully, they'll likely become more prevalent as these tools
become more and more reliable. 

 AI JUST HAD ANOTHER MATH BREAKTHROUGH—WITH HELP FROM A HIGH-SCHOOL

articles.title: Dropout
articles.description:
Anthropic employee Jarred Sumner used the Claude app on his phone to
try to solve the infamous Riemann hypothesis. The model didn't
succeed, but it made a related finding that one Stanford number
theorist has called the most impressive result that AI has produced in
math so far. Sumner's formal mathematical education ended after just
one semester of high-school geometry, and he identifies as very much
not a mathematician. Most of the prompting he gave to the model was
variations of 'keep going' and 'believe in yourself'.

articles.title: Meet viktor: the ai employee that skips the "agent" debate
articles.description:
OpenAI still can't define "AI agent." Business owners skipped the
debate and hired Viktor, an AI employee in Slack & Teams. Dashboards.
Apps. Tasks... Start free → [18] 

 Z.AI DELAYS GLM-5.3 WEIGHTS TWO WEEKS AFTER CYBER SCORE BEATS MYTHOS

Z.ai released GLM-5.3 on Friday while holding back the model's
downloadable weights and gating its most sensitive cybersecurity
functions.

articles.title: Code is the byproduct
articles.description: Code is the byproduct of understanding.

articles.title: You can just choose how many bugs you want now
articles.description:
In a complex system, you can basically find as many bugs as you ask
the agents for.

articles.title: The task isn't the job
articles.description: A machine can nail the task but completely miss the job.

articles.title: “your benchmarks don't apply to us"
articles.description: The benchmarks are answering the wrong question.

articles.title: Evaluating ai agents as products
articles.description:
This study introduces three tasks for AI agents that allow
researchers to evaluate efficiency, collaboration, and taste,
providing a proxy for how well the agents perform as tools in real
coding situations.

articles.title: Scratch a simple data model, find a complex one
articles.description:
A seemingly simple Bible data model quickly breaks down once
real-world cases like verse ranges, missing verses, alternate
numbering, repeated chapters, and out-of-order text appear. The
practical lesson is to model only the complexity the product actually
needs, rather than chasing perfect fidelity by default. 

 POINT LOOKUPS ON THE LAKEHOUSE: HOW HUDI INDEXES ACCELERATE

articles.title: Read-heavy workloads
articles.description:
Apache Hudi's metadata-table indexes make selective lakehouse reads
behave more like database lookups than full scans. Record-level,
secondary, expression, and bloom-filter indexes can prune equality
predicates to a few files.

articles.title: Why ai is a storage workload
articles.description:
AI inference is becoming stateful infrastructure: long-context
sessions, agents, RAG, and multimodal workflows create durable KV
caches, prefixes, memories, and embeddings that are cheaper to store
than recompute after enough reuse. The storage hierarchy is moving
into the hot path, with HBM, DRAM, SSDs, object storage, CXL, and
flash tiers shaping latency and cost.

articles.title: Change-data-capture doesn't solve dual-writes
articles.description:
CDC makes downstream writes retryable, ordered, and observable, but
it does not make destination systems safe to write twice. The
destination still needs durable idempotency or a way to reject
duplicates after recovery. This is a useful design-review lens for
teams treating CDC as an automatic consistency fix.

articles.title: How kenn is doing agentic engineering
articles.description:
Kenn uses coding agents at high volume while keeping humans in
control of design, review, and final decisions. Detailed specs,
adversarial reviews, and continuous verification let three engineers
ship hundreds of PRs weekly without relying on autonomous loops.

articles.title: On benchmarking
articles.description:
A throughput number is not an architecture decision. Good benchmarks
explain the workload, cache state, client behavior, failure modes, and
scaling limit behind the result. Without that context, teams risk
optimizing for a synthetic score instead of the bottlenecks their
production data systems will actually hit.

articles.title: How we tracked down a 16-year-old sqlite bug
articles.description:
Tailscale spent six months tracing repeated SQLite corruption to a
rare 16-year-old race condition between WAL checkpointing and write
transactions, triggered more often by its aggressive manual
checkpointing. The investigation led to a SQLite fix, stronger
recovery tooling, and a broader lesson that even “boring”
technology becomes risky when operated outside its common paths.

articles.title: Introducing databench
articles.description:
Hex's DataBench tests AI agents on realistic, messy analytics tasks
and finds they are strong at gathering evidence but weaker at
open-ended decisions where judgment matters. Models often fail by
manufacturing certainty, missing subtle data traps or overthinking
correct answers, showing why human review is still essential for
complex analytical work.

articles.title: Apache datafusion comet 1.0.0 release
articles.description:
Comet, the Spark accelerator built on Apache DataFusion, reached 1.0
with semantic versioning, Spark 4 support, broader operator coverage,
and extensive correctness testing against Spark's own suite. It is
aimed at teams that want faster Spark execution without rewriting jobs
or replacing the surrounding Spark ecosystem.

articles.title: What's new in opensearch 3.8
articles.description:
OpenSearch 3.8 improves vector ingestion, radial query throughput,
and median query latency while expanding AI-agent support. MCP now
works across all agent types, tool discovery is richer, and gRPC
streaming inference lowers token latency. Analytics teams also get new
PPL/SQL tooling, Grok debugging, one-click Prometheus alerts, and
search-relevance workflow improvements.

articles.title: Fairly ranking the most brilliant birds
articles.description:
A transparent ranking of the world's most brilliant birds combines
chroma, colour variety, sample confidence and diversity, placing the
orange-breasted bunting first. The bigger idea is that ranking systems
are fairest when every factor is understandable, defensible and tied
to a reasonable human judgement.

articles.title: Snowflake says this 149 gb query scanned -1.5 gb
Querying 1 thousand json files from s3
articles.description:
DuckDB on ECS Fargate processed 1,000 JSON files about 3.4× faster
than Spark on EMR Serverless and at lower cost.

articles.title: Attackers kept pace
articles.description:
Security teams are adapting AI at unprecedented pace, but attackers
are not lagging behind: 78% of orgs saw AI-enabled attacks, and 95% of
leaders believe adversaries are already using AI.

The 2026 SANS AI Survey Insights report [5] breaks down where AI is
paying off, where it's lulling teams into a false sense of security,
and why "formal AI governance" often means less than leaders think.

For a deep dive into the survey results, [6]catch the related webcast
[6] [6]with Dave Shackleford, founder of Voodoo Security.

Browse more SANS AI resources [7] for ways to build, break, and defend
AI in production.

articles.title: Gpt-5.6 sol ultrafast
articles.description:
OpenAI previewed Ultrafast, a GPT-5.6 Sol mode capable of generating
up to 750 output tokens per second and operating at up to 14x standard
processing speed. The approach aimed to deliver real-time performance
without switching to a smaller model. 

 GOOGLE'S GEMINI 3.7 FLASH TARGETS CODING AND AGENTS WITH A 50%

articles.title: Introductory price cut
articles.description:
Google is rolling out Gemini 3.7 Flash, a new version of its
workhorse AI model. The release comes just three weeks after the
release of Gemini 3.6 Flash, an unusually short turnaround attributed
to developer feedback and algorithmic improvements. API prices have
been temporarily cut in half. Gemini 3.7 Flash will cost $0.75 per
million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens until the end
of the year.

articles.title: Anthropic could be worth $2 trillion when it goes public
articles.description:
Investors anticipate Anthropic's IPO could exceed a $2 trillion
valuation, potentially becoming the largest in history, fueled by
rapid revenue growth and demand for its AI models. Despite regulatory
hurdles and competition, the startup projects annualized revenue of
$100-120 billion by the end of 2026. Investors remain optimistic,
citing Anthropic's strong market position and performance compared to
rivals like OpenAI and Google.

articles.title: Will financing bottleneck ai compute? an anthropic case study
articles.description:
Much of the financing Anthropic needed for its infrastructure
buildout was assembled before the company's revenue spiked. The
buildout suggests that financing is unlikely to be the immediate limit
on frontier computer growth. Institutional investors appear willing to
lend capital against commitment to long-term payments, especially if
more established organizations are willing to back up part of the
risk.

articles.title: How ai agents could fail at scale
articles.description:
Anthropic examined how individually benign behaviors in frontier AI
agents could compound into systemic failures when many agents interact
in shared environments. The research highlighted risks including
confabulation, reward hacking, and unexpected dynamics emerging faster
than human institutions can oversee them.

articles.title: Subagents on subagents: how many layers deep is too many?
articles.description:
Recursive agent systems should be designed as dependency graphs
because upstream mistakes can propagate across many workers while leaf
errors stay localized. Reliability depends less on nesting depth than
blast radius, requiring provenance, verification, and stronger
controls at high-impact nodes. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: Extend zero trust to account for ai agents
articles.description:
AI agents are autonomous actors, operating at a speed and scale that
challenges today's security frameworks. “_From Zero Trust to Agent
Trust_,” from Teleport [15], explains why Zero Trust must extend to
Agentic Trust Principles: Enforce Continuously, Bound Collective
Autonomy, and Assume Misalignment. Read the paper → [15]

articles.title: Agent plugins are the future of agent skills
articles.description:
Agent Plugins package skills and MCP dependencies into one portable,
vendor-neutral folder that compatible clients can load. The standard
reduces fragmented setup through shared manifests, portable paths,
isolated failure boundaries, and client-specific extensions, while
leaving authentication unresolved.

articles.title: Cloud agents start 3x faster with builds
articles.description:
Agents are only as capable as the environments they work in. Cursor
can now continuously prepare development environments in the
background at no additional cost. Agents can now start in ready
environments, resulting in up to 3x faster responses. Agents will keep
using the last successful build, and work continues uninterrupted
while developers debug in the background. 

 OCR 4.1 (WEBSITE) [18] 

 Mistral OCR 4.1 is a highly specialized vision-multimodal model
engineered specifically to ingest, parse, and structure complex
document formats. It excels at reading complex tabular layouts,
understanding hierarchical document structures, and directly
outputting clean, machine-readable JSON or Markdown. The release
pressures cloud providers and proprietary players to re-evaluate their
pricing tiers for multimodal inputs.

articles.title: Google launches sheets canvas for gemini mini-apps
articles.description:
Google Sheets canvas is a Gemini-powered feature that turns
spreadsheet data into custom, interactive mini-apps inside Google
Sheets. The new layer sits directly on top of a spreadsheet to give
users a visual way to organize, edit, and navigate information without
formulas, programming, or a separate app. The visual layer is not
static and will update along with the spreadsheet underneath it.
Sheets canvas is now available globally in English to Google AI Pro
and Ultra subscribers. 

 OPENAI REVENUE CHIEF DENISE DRESSER LEAVING, SECOND MAJOR EXECUTIVE

articles.title: Departure in days
articles.description:
Denise Dresser, OpenAI's Chief Revenue Officer, leaves the company
just ahead of its anticipated IPO, marking the second executive
departure this week. Dresser, who joined OpenAI from Salesforce less
than a year ago, will be replaced by Dali Rajic from Wiz. Earlier this
week, OpenAI executive Brad Lightcap also announced his departure to
start a new venture.

articles.title: ⚡ you have the ai mandate. do you have the map?
articles.description:
Scribe Optimize captures how work happens — no surveys, no
workshops — so you know where AI pays off. Take the tour [23] 

 APPLE TRAINS OWN AI MODEL FOR CHINA WITH ALIBABA SUPPORT, REUTERS

articles.description:
A China-trained model could give Apple greater control over its AI
offerings in the country.

capabilities at a much lower price.

articles.description:

certify tens of thousands of consultants. The companies will jointly
build AI offerings for industries including finance, government,
telecom, and retail.

articles.title: Cisco's ai infrastructure orders hit $9.3b
articles.description:
Cisco booked $4 billion in hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders last
quarter, bringing its FY2026 total to $9.3 billion. It expects AI
infrastructure revenue to climb to roughly $7.5 billion in FY2027.

articles.title: The wrong defaults is why enterprise ai agents fail at adoption
articles.description:
Enterprise AI agents fail to gain broad adoption because
industry-standard interfaces force users to make too many engineering
decisions. The proposed alternative is a simpler default: one
persistent, general-purpose agent embedded in workplace chat, using
generic API access and live data rather than complex agent
configurations, knowledge bases, or fine-tuning.

articles.title: Why capital one chose open models for its ai agents
articles.description:
Capital One built its multi-agent platform around open-weight models
as it pushes toward enterprise-wide AI. The approach gives it more
control over deployment, customization, and infrastructure.

articles.title: Enterprise ssd prices are up 6.5x in a year
articles.description:
Prices for 30TB enterprise SSDs have risen roughly 6.5x year over
year, significantly changing the economics of AI infrastructure.
Storage is becoming a major cost factor for large GPU deployments. 

🤝

articles.title: A10 networks introduces ai gateway to secure and manage enterprise ai
articles.description:
A10 Networks has announced the general availability of the A10 AI
Gateway, a centralized control plane for routing, governing,
monitoring, and managing the costs of enterprise AI agents,
applications, and large language models. The company says it can route
requests by complexity, enforce identity-based access and usage
limits, and run in customer-controlled environments including
on-premises, private-cloud, and air-gapped deployments.

Oracle expands its enterprise ai stack

expanded on-demand models, and new IAM controls to OCI Enterprise AI.
The updates give enterprises more flexibility over models and
infrastructure.

articles.description:
AWS detailed how AgentCore Observability can monitor agents running
on-premises, Azure, GCP, or AWS. OpenTelemetry telemetry feeds into
one dashboard for tracing actions, token usage, and reliability.

articles.title: Mcp's new session model shifts more responsibility to applications
articles.description:
MCP's latest architecture makes models carry session handles rather
than relying on persistent server sessions. That improves scalability
but leaves applications responsible for reliable correlation,
authorization, and session management.

articles.title: Lovable partners with cerebras for faster ai inference
articles.description:

AI-powered application development platform.

articles.title: Nebius expands uk ai infrastructure with vantage
Instagram introduces a redesigned wordmark
articles.description:
Instagram has introduced a redesigned wordmark for the first time
since 2016, giving its name a sharper, more modern look while keeping
references to the original style. The new cursive-inspired lettering
has received mixed reactions, with some praising the fresher design
and others joking that the stylized “r” makes it look like
“Instagzam.” Instagram has not said whether the wordmark update
will be followed by broader visual changes, such as a new app icon.

articles.title: Here's your first look at the newest pixel devices
articles.description:
Google has unveiled its newest Pixel lineup, including Pixel 11
phones, Pixel Watch 5, and its first-ever Pixel Tag finder device. The
Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and Pro Fold are built for Gemini
Intelligence, with greater durability and upgraded cameras. Pixel
Watch 5 adds proactive Gemini features, strength coaching, improved
GPS tracking, and Health Guardian tools like breathing emergency
detection.

articles.title: Iphone ultra's cameras might get very unorthodox placement, per leak
articles.description:
A new leak suggests Apple's upcoming foldable iPhone Ultra may place
its two front-facing cameras in the corners of the displays rather
than the traditional centered position, with one camera on the outer
screen and another on the inner screen. If accurate, this would mark a
significant departure from Apple's usual iPhone design and could
require users to adjust how they take selfies.

articles.title: Measuring time savings from figma make
articles.description:
Figma's Data Science team ran a randomized controlled trial with 100
participants to measure how much time Figma Make actually saves on
design tasks. Design work was found to be 20% faster and 16% easier
overall, with product managers seeing the largest gains—23% faster
and 37% easier—though designers benefited most on complex tasks
while PMs gained more on simpler ones. Figma plans further RCTs,
including one testing its new design agent's parallel-agent
capabilities. 

 AI GOVERNANCE IN DESIGN TOOLS: WHAT HAPPENS TO YOUR DATA WHEN AI

articles.title: Enters the workflow
articles.description:
AI governance frameworks bring documentation, traceability, and
accountability to AI features embedded in design tools. Building a
framework involves defining scope and owners, classifying design data,
standardizing vendor evaluation, and embedding controls into workflows
and CI/CD processes. Penpot positions itself as a governance-friendly
alternative through self-hosting, open file formats, and its MCP
server, letting organizations control AI models and data flows on
their own infrastructure. 

 BIAS IN LLMS, OR HOW TO DESIGN FOR EVERYONE WITH TOOLS BUILT FOR

articles.title: Someone
articles.description:
Large language models are not neutral and often reflect or amplify
biases related to language, geography, gender, culture, and
socioeconomic status because of the data they are trained on and the
feedback systems used to refine them. As a result, AI-generated
personas, research summaries, copy, and recommendations can
overrepresent dominant groups and present their perspectives as
consensus while overlooking minority viewpoints. Designers should
treat AI outputs as inputs for further thinking rather than objective
conclusions, and actively review them for hidden assumptions, missing
perspectives, and demographic bias.

articles.title: Nine persona mistakes that are costing you customers
articles.description:
Nine common persona mistakes undermine product design, from
over-relying on AI to using outdated, generic, or ignored personas.
Personas should be research-based, focused, specific, updated per
project, and actively shared across teams to be effective. Avoiding
these pitfalls helps teams build products that better match customer
needs, improving satisfaction and business outcomes.

articles.title: Got no time for prd
articles.description:
PRDs still suit large teams aligning around a known target, but they
assume the destination is already chosen, which doesn't fit early
exploration. A lighter six-line alternative—Intent, Bet, Bar, Scope,
Loop, Never—distills into one sentence short enough to hand directly
to an AI agent. Unlike lengthy PRDs models can read but which lock in
premature decisions, this compressed brief keeps both humans and
agents flexible while testing risky assumptions.

articles.title: Everything i don't like is slop
articles.description:

broader cultural judgment about attention, trust, and creative

A range of AI models, including DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi, were tested
for generating web pages, showing large variations in performance and
credit costs. The best-performing models for a static coffee shop
website were DeepSeek V4 Flash, which consumed only 2.4 credits on
average, and GPT 5.6 Sol in low effort mode, which averaged 141
credits. In contrast, higher-tier models like Claude Opus 5 showed a
lot of credit usage with results that didn't necessarily justify their

articles.title: How compaction works in pi
articles.description:
Compaction in coding agents like Pi is a process used to summarize
and manage the growing conversation history that can exceed the
model's context window during log coding sessions. By creating a
smaller representation of prior messages, compaction makes sure that
the conversation can continue while preserving relevant information,
preventing errors related to context overflow.

articles.title: Understanding is the new bottleneck
articles.description:
As AI agents increasingly take on coding tasks, humans still need to
understand the code being generated to actively participate in the
creative process for collaboration purposes. Effective techniques for
improving this understanding include creating structured code
explainers, utilizing interactive environments to intuitively grasp
systems, and developing shared spaces for team discussions.

articles.title: Blog about things you don't understand yet
articles.description:
Blogging serves as a learning tool, where the author consistently
gains new insights through the writing process. This approach not only
enriches the author's understanding but also offers value to readers,
as it forces clear communication and thoughtful engagement with
complex topics.

articles.title: Text ai watermarks will always be trivial to remove
articles.description:
The European Union AI Act, which takes effect in August, mandates
that all AI-generated text be watermarked to make sure it can be
identified as artificially generated. Despite proposed solutions like
Google's SynthID and potential Unicode tricks from other providers,
the methods for watermarking text can still be easily circumvented.

articles.title: Accelerating gpt-5.6 sol ultrafast with openai
articles.description:

bottlenecks by packing 44 GB of SRAM on-chip to keep model weights
local. This allows organizations to use AI more effectively in
critical scenarios, such as addressing production outages rapidly or
responding to cyberattacks. 

 EMPTY SHELVES OR LOST KEYS? RECALL IS THE BOTTLENECK FOR PARAMETRIC

articles.title: Factuality
articles.description:
LLMs such as Gemini 3 and GPT-5 often encounter factual errors not
due to a lack of encoded knowledge, but because they struggle with
recalling this stored information. By using a knowledge profiling
framework, analysis shows that while encoding is nearly saturated in
these models, recall is still a hard challenge.

articles.title: Np-overrated
articles.description:
Despite the common belief that NP-hard problems are practically

Modern conveniences and technologies that once inspired awe have

articles.description:
Chinese AI practitioners are increasingly recognizing the
controversial practice of model distillation, which involves using
data from superior "teacher" models to improve the capabilities of
smaller "student" models, as a technical strategy that is
misunderstood and stigmatized.
