articles.title: Success
articles.description:
NASA's Perseverance Mars rover will set a record for the most
distance driven by any vehicle on another world sometime next week.
The rover's auto navigation system has enabled about 90% of the
distance driven by the vehicle to be autonomous. Not having to wait
for navigation commands from drivers on Earth has allowed the rover to
maximize the amount of scientific return. The vehicle will likely be
able to keep driving itself across Mars for many years to come.

articles.title: China-free batteries made from salt are finally here
articles.description:
Peak Energy, a US-based startup, has raised tens of millions of
dollars to build a factory for its sodium-ion battery packs. It
already has more than $1.1 billion in announced deals with customers.
Sodium batteries have less-intensive cooling needs than lithium-ion
packs, and they are less likely to catch fire. Another US-based
startup, Inlyte Energy, is working on another type of sodium-based
battery that can't catch fire at all.

articles.title: Agentic code quality
articles.description:
Software quality now depends on the constraints set around the agents
that wrote it. Constraints define what a system is allowed to do.
Setting and maintaining these constraints allows developers to build
loops that reliably deliver high-quality production software. Agents
can propose anything - constraints decide whether a proposal is safe
enough, correct, scoped, and useful.

articles.title: Google's westinghouse bet
articles.description:
Google's recent reshuffling of its AI operations has many thinking
that the company has failed in the AI race. However, the company may
just be refocusing its resources on its strengths. Google Cloud may be
a much larger economic opportunity than pursuing its rivals in the
frontier AI race. The company's enormous distribution advantage means
it doesn't have to compete in the expensive and unprofitable frontier
race.

articles.title: Crunch intensifies
articles.description:
AWS is cracking down on internal use of EC2 instances among its
engineers. Engineers have been told to reduce CPU waste to ensure the
company has enough CPU capacity to meet customer demand. The increased
demand for CPU is due to the rise of AI agentic workloads. Other cloud
companies are also seeing high demand for CPUs.

articles.title: Changing devtools is cheap. owning them isn't
articles.description:
The future of software will be powered by high-quality,
well-documented building blocks that users can build specialized
artifacts on top of. Agents are good at composing high-quality
components. Maintainers can provide these components alongside a focus
application, and users can choose how to modify their experiences
themselves. This allows software to be personalized while still being
developed by maintainers that care.

unclear ownership, permissions, dependencies, and behaviour. The
answer is not to restrict creation, but to build governance into the
platform so identity, permissions, logging, ownership, expiry, and

articles.title: Never mind clean data. annotate as you collect it.
articles.description:
AI teams should preserve provenance, schema, and source context at
ingestion because hallucinations often stem from stale or
non-canonical data. Gartner expects 60% of AI projects to fail without
metadata and observability, while nearly 75% of frontier-model
training CPU goes to cleansing and validation. Capture lineage and

articles.title: Data governance
articles.description:
Data ownership fails when responsibility comes without decision
rights, leaving owners unable to approve quality thresholds, accept
risk, or authorize usage. Effective governance needs authority and
escalation paths, with data owners deciding while stewards execute.
Decisions need accountable owners and traceable risk acceptance.

replacing pseudo-databases for metrics and dimensions. A new

7.0. Apache Ossie is also being built as a vendor-neutral JSON/YAML

deterministic checks of keys, joins, types, and values, asking users

increase before a funding round will improve the company's revenue and

articles.description:
AI models need precise loop engineering to determine when tasks are
complete, with strong verifiers at each step. Effective loops require
a clear target state, an observable current state, and precise, local
change methods. The challenge lies in creating loops that converge
successfully while managing the cost and ensuring an external stop
condition.

articles.description:

gives forecasters, on average, an extra day's worth of predictive
accuracy compared to current methods. Google has open-sourced its

community and amplify AI's impact on building more resilient
communities. The research has already had real-world impact - it
predicted Hurricane Melissa's rapid intensification and landfall in
Jamaica during the 2025 hurricane season, enabling advanced warnings
to be issued and giving teams on the ground critical time to prepare.

articles.title: Google assistant shutting down on android and wear os in september
articles.description:
Google says it will begin shutting down Google Assistant on mobile
devices on September 4, moving users to Gemini instead. The transition
may take several weeks and will also affect smartwatches, headphones,
and cars using Android Auto, while users who already switched to
Gemini will see no change.

articles.title: Piece
articles.description:
Data teams are moving away from all-in-one platforms toward a smaller
best-of-breed architecture centered on data movement, storage and
compute, and a control plane. Enterprise orchestration, observability,
metadata, incident management, and agent runtime are the missing
pieces needed to coordinate increasingly complex ELT pipelines and
reduce the operational burden of tracking failures and data freshness.

articles.title: Natjack at black hat: a new way to crack nat's trust gap
articles.description:
NatJack is a class of attacks that manipulates NAT
connection-tracking tables to hijack connections, poison DNS
responses, or trigger denial of service. Testing covered 32 products
and configurations across 13 vendors, with every implementation
vulnerable to at least some of the techniques tested. 

🤝

articles.title: Inference hooks: inline data loss prevention for claude enterprise
articles.description:
Anthropic's inference hooks for Claude Enterprise route prompts and
tool-call responses through a customer-controlled data loss prevention
server before Claude can process them. The beta works across Claude
surfaces, including chat, Claude Code, Cowork, and connected tools,
and supports a single organization-wide configuration with staged
enforcement options.

articles.title: Aws targets ai cost concerns with new marketplace insights tool
articles.description:
AWS Marketplace AI Insights explain complex product pricing in plain
language, including how costs scale, how multiple usage dimensions
combine, and what is included. The feature could help enterprises
compare consumption-based AI tools and forecast costs before
purchasing, although its accuracy depends on the pricing information
vendors publish.

articles.title: As space gets connected, security gets critical
Surprise ai costs threaten enterprise implementations
articles.description:
Unexpected AI expenses have caused one-quarter of enterprises to
delay or cancel projects, while nearly half have escalated spending
surprises to their boards, according to a survey of 396 organizations.
Costs are becoming harder to track as AI spending spreads across
models, infrastructure, developer tools, data platforms, and agentic
workflows, pushing CIOs to build cost controls directly into their AI
architecture.

articles.title: The agent access model
articles.description:
Cloudflare's Agent Access Model (AAM) is a security framework that
treats each agent task execution graph as untrusted and authorizes
every action against the agent, task, and accumulated resource state.
Agent controls should use short-lived, sender-constrained credentials
and inline enforcement in the harness and network, while a one-way
Trust Ratchet can remove capabilities when protected events occur.

articles.title: Attacks
articles.description:
Cisco released security updates for Catalyst SD-WAN Software to
address several vulnerabilities, including three rated CVSS 9.9 that
may enable access-control bypass, privilege escalation, or
sensitive-data exposure.

articles.title: Hpe extends validity of quoted hardware prices, possibly for months
articles.description:
HPE will honor hardware pricing from quote issuance until equipment
leaves its factories, easing pricing uncertainty caused by volatile
server, memory, and storage component costs.

articles.title: Linkedin's new anti-slop button is coming to every platform
articles.description:
LinkedIn has introduced a button letting users flag posts as "AI
slop," aiming to help the platform refine detection models and improve
feeds. The move follows a July study finding two-thirds of AI-flagged
long-form posts across major platforms originated on LinkedIn,
reflecting a wider industry struggle with automated content. Similar
tools have emerged elsewhere, including Pinterest's AI content
settings, TikTok's AI-content slider, and Substack's integration with
detection service Pangram.

articles.title: Design arena creators raise $7.9 million to bring taste to ai models
articles.description:
Intelligence, maker of Design Arena, raised $7.9 million in seed
funding led by Index Ventures, with Conviction, A*, and Valkyrie also
participating. The platform lets users rank AI-generated designs and
now serves 5.3 million users while generating $60 million in ARR by
selling human feedback data to frontier AI labs. This crowdsourced
evaluation model has mixed results industry-wide: Yupp shut down
despite $33 million raised, while LM Arena secured $150 million at a
$1.7 billion valuation in January.

articles.title: Ios 27 adds four new ways to customize your iphone's lock screen
articles.description:
iOS 27 expands Lock Screen customization with AI-powered wallpaper
features, including Extend, which intelligently expands photos to fit
the screen, and Image Playground, which lets users generate custom
wallpapers from photos or text prompts. It also lets users move the
clock higher to reveal more of the wallpaper and dismiss the Now
Playing widget without stopping audio playback.

articles.title: Claude cowork for designers: a working field guide
articles.description:
Claude Cowork, launched by Anthropic and expanded to web and mobile
in beta on July 7, acts as an agent that executes multi-step design
tasks rather than just answering prompts. This guide walks through
setup, permission modes, and hands-on exercises for research
synthesis, competitive audits, and scheduled client briefings, plus
building reusable "skills" that encode a designer's judgment. It also
flags real limitations—file overwriting, hallucination, thin memory,
rising usage costs, immature team governance, and browser-based
security risks—while positioning Cowork as best for documents and
synthesis versus Claude Code for technical, ship-ready work.

articles.title: Bottle your judgment and make it outlive you
articles.description:
AI is making it possible to capture and share a person's
judgment—not just their knowledge—by turning years of experience
into systems others can learn from. However, the most valuable
expertise is often tacit and can't be fully documented, so the best
approach combines structured knowledge with apprenticeship, using AI
to preserve what can be written down while relying on human mentorship
to pass on intuition, context, and judgment. Rather than replacing
experts, AI gives them a way to extend their expertise beyond
themselves and create lasting institutional knowledge.

articles.title: Better code, fewer tokens: the benefits of code connect in mcp
articles.description:
Figma's Code Connect feature links Figma components to real codebase
components, giving coding agents production-accurate context instead
of generic React output. Testing across 27 design-to-code tasks showed
Code Connect reduced median token usage by 29.5% and task duration by
19.6%, while raising code quality by a full point on a 1–4 scale.
Improvements scaled with Code Connect coverage: higher coverage meant
fewer exploratory searches and closer matches to real design-system
components, as illustrated by Coinbase's experience avoiding
fabricated components.

articles.title: Can we trust ai to moderate ux interviews?
articles.description:
A three-year-old prediction about AI replacing UX moderators is
revisited, as AI now handles interactive interviewing beyond simple
comment coding, prompting 419 researchers to sign opposition letters.
A 2025 Philippines study of over 70,000 job applicants found
AI-interviewed candidates were more likely to be offered, start, and
remain employed, though humans still made hiring decisions for
structured, closed questions. Anthropic's December 2025 study of
80,000 users found AI interviews elicited surprisingly candid
disclosures, but NN/Group's research suggests AI still falls short for
semi-structured, open-ended UX interviews requiring real-time
judgment. 

 BERLIN MUSEUM BREAKS THE RULES OF BRANDING WITH EIGHTY-ONE DIFFERENT

articles.title: Logos
articles.description:
Berlin Museum's new identity replaces a single logo with 81
interchangeable wordmarks, each combining typefaces inspired by
different parts of the city's typographic heritage. Rather than
prioritizing consistency, the flexible system reflects Berlin's
diverse voices and history, turning the museum's identity into a
celebration of the city's design culture itself.

articles.title: Brought to life
articles.description:
Gaku Tada's Blender scene, made with Deep Paint, resembles a
children's book illustration rather than a typical 3D render, with
painterly, watercolor-like textures.

articles.title: The "ai can do the ux" mistake
articles.description:
AI has narrowed the gap between design and development execution, but
unevenly: designers can now build, while developers still can't easily
judge whether an interface truly fits user needs.

articles.title: Generative ui
articles.description:
Generative UI replaces the “wall of text” in AI responses with
interfaces generated to match user intent. It breaks into three
generation categories: static/controlled (model picks tool arguments
and app code maps results to existing components), declarative (model
composes layouts from a versioned component catalog via specs like
A2UI over AG-UI), and open-ended (raw HTML/CSS/JS in a sandboxed
iframe, still blocked by security, latency, and consistency).

articles.title: 5 best practices for preventing chaos in tailwind css
articles.description:
To maintain a clean Tailwind CSS codebase, it's necessary to
implement best practices such as using design tokens instead of
arbitrary values, minimizing utility classes, and adopting a
component-based approach. Additionally, making sure of consistent
class ordering, grouping design tokens semantically, and managing
style variants can help prevent chaos as the code evolves.

articles.title: Experimenting with rscs for performance and ux in next.js
articles.description:
This article goes over three Server Component patterns from a demo
app on the Next.js 16.3 preview: a load-more button that only pushes
?page=N while the server renders each page in its own Suspense
boundary, a search input that writes to the URL but never reads it (so
it stays in the static shell and keeps focus while results stream
below), and a draft preview rendered by a Server Function returning
JSX, keeping syntax highlighting off the client.

articles.title: Make a decent one)
articles.description:
Cooking a steak may seem simple, but achieving a consistently good
result requires understanding and skill, much like developing software
with AI. While AI can expedite the coding process, it cannot replace
the judgment and insight needed to produce quality software.

articles.title: Taste is all that's left
articles.description:
AI has shortened the gap between ideas and their execution, allowing
people to create plausible products quickly without the friction that
traditionally taught them valuable judgment. However, this ease of
production has resulted in an overwhelming abundance of mediocre
outputs, making the skill of discerning what is worth creating more
important than ever.

articles.title: Google's mind is now less deep
articles.description:
Talent departures from Google, including key figures from DeepMind
and Google Brain (like Jeff Dean), may initially appear detrimental,
but could ultimately benefit the company's AI initiatives by forcing a
necessary organizational shift.

Bending Spoons' acquisition of Airtable for $1.28 billion shows a
pivotal moment for No Code platforms, which are now being challenged
by the rise of LLM loops and traditional development methods. The
emphasis is shifting toward using technologies like Linux for building
customized software, allowing for greater flexibility and control
compared to low-code solutions.

articles.title: Practical ai: don't work harder; work smarter
articles.description:
A more efficient approach to AI processing is by minimizing
unnecessary computations and reducing data movement, using their Graph
Streaming Processor (GSP) to optimize the flow of intermediate data
between computation stages. This methodology, termed Hybrid AI, allows
for a multi-tiered processing system that efficiently filters
workloads, directing only complex cases to more resource-intensive
models.

articles.title: Amazon dynamodb now supports real-time vector search at any scale
articles.description:
Amazon DynamoDB now supports native vector search, letting developers
store vector embeddings alongside operational data and run similarity
searches without copying data to a separate vector store. The feature
supports up to 4,096 dimensions, Euclidean, Cosine, and Dot product
distance functions, and returns up to 100 results per query with
single-digit millisecond latency at 99% or higher recall. It is
generally available in all commercial AWS regions, including the AWS
GovCloud (US) regions.

articles.title: Cloudflare os: an open platform for agents, apps, and work
articles.description:

company has run internally since May. Thousands of Cloudflare
employees across engineering and non-engineering functions have used
it daily to create documents, automate tasks, and build small apps.
Any organization can now deploy it by connecting it to internal
systems through a public GitHub repository.

articles.title: Controller does not crash the api server
articles.description:

cache populated through list and watch rather than directly from the
API server, making reads fast while introducing eventual consistency,
memory tradeoffs, and indexing considerations that developers must
understand to build efficient, reliable controllers.

articles.title: On building scalable control planes
articles.description:
Scalable control planes should keep coordination off the critical
data path, partition ownership cleanly, and rely on asynchronous
reconciliation instead of synchronous global agreement for every
change. Designs that minimize shared mutable state and let independent
partitions make progress can absorb failures and growth without
turning the control layer into the system's bottleneck. 

🧑‍💻

deployment. Connect models and oversee agents in a single control

 LOOPX (GITHUB REPO) [11]

task ownership, evidence, and handoffs stable across multiple turns
and agents rather than replacing the agent runtime itself. 

 CELLD (GITHUB REPO) [12] 

 celld is an open-source daemon that runs Cloudflare Workers and
Durable Objects on your own machines. Each object is its own SQLite
database, addressed by name and replicated to an S3-compatible bucket

articles.title: Just one function, 10x faster? reading a rust performance pr
articles.description:
GreptimeDB sped up Prometheus remote-read conversion by 4–16x by
borrowing strings directly from Apache Arrow arrays instead of
materializing every label value and by moving allocations from every
row to every unique time series. The optimization eliminated repeated
string copies, unnecessary heap allocations, and costly dictionary
expansion in a CPU-heavy conversion path that previously processed
only about 2 million rows per second.

articles.title: This ai just created viruses not found in nature
articles.description:
Researchers have used AI to create new kinds of viruses for the first
time. They taught AI to recognize patterns of DNA structure in nature
and then use that data to write recipes for entirely new viruses. The
researchers followed those recipes to create DNA molecules, which they
inserted into bacteria. The viruses were able to infect other
bacteria, demonstrating that they were viable.

articles.title: Nuclear startup oklo splits its first atoms in test reactor
articles.description:

The reactor is a demonstration version of the technology Oklo plans to
use for its new medical isotope business. The company also plans to
expand into recycling nuclear waste, fabricating its own fuel, and
producing medical isotopes. Oklo is preparing a site near the Idaho
National Laboratory for its first small modular reactor but does not
yet have permission to work on the reactor itself.

distribution, installation, permissions, user experience, and

articles.title: The agent access model
articles.description:
The Agent Access Model (AAM) enhances enterprise security by
redefining access control for software agents, focusing on
task-specific and ephemeral credentials. By removing implicit trust in
task execution graphs and evaluating every action against the task's
state, AAM minimizes agent capabilities, thus reducing risk. Core
principles include short-lived credentials, harness and network
enforcement, minimal human oversight, evidence-based grant reviews,
and unidirectional capability changes.

articles.title: The three ai pills
articles.description:
AI discussions often revolve around three core perspectives:
acknowledging current AI (AI-pill), believing in future advanced
general intelligence (AGI-pill), and anticipating superintelligence
surpassing human capabilities (ASI-pill). Many remain skeptical or
uninformed about AI's potential, underestimating its imminent impact
on society and technology. Being fully ASI-aware means advocating for
preparedness in policy, safety, and innovation, recognizing the
competitive advantage and potential risks of advanced AI systems. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: Prime agent: a self-improving rlm agent
articles.description:
Prime Agent is a self-improving coding harness designed around the
Recursive Language Model (RLM) and Continual Harness. The RLM treats
context as a variable and subagent delegation as function calls inside
a REPL. The persistent REPL gives the model programmatic access to its
history, sub-agents, and tools, allowing it to write language model
programs as actions over its own context. Continual Harness treats the
harness' state as something the agent can create, read, update, and
delete from its own trajectory. These abstractions make Prime Agent an
effective general coding assistant, a default runtime for long-horizon
autonomous evaluation, and a collaborator for research and
autoresearch.

articles.title: Introducing flex: let the model write the code
articles.description:
Flex leverages the coding skills of models to rewrite not just the
instructions of a program, but the code itself. It executes the
generated source inside a sandboxed interpreter. Flex produces cheaper
and faster programs by optimizing the prompt and the code.

Microsoft is assigning each department a limited pool of AI tokens as

The move suggests that even one of the industry's largest AI investors

articles.title: Chaindrop supply chain compromise: anatomy of a self-propagating worm
articles.description:
Microsoft identified a self-propagating supply chain attack affecting
more than 400 npm packages. The malware steals npm, GitHub, AWS,
Kubernetes, and HashiCorp Vault credentials from developer machines
and CI systems, then uses stolen publishing tokens to infect and
republish additional packages automatically.

articles.title: A data-driven explanation: why do ai agents still fail
articles.description:
Enterprise AI agents underdeliver not because they lack peak
capability, but because reliability, benchmark quality, agent-specific
errors, and alignment remain difficult problems. Agent reliability
falls sharply as workflows require more steps, while interrun variance
creates a large gap between what models can achieve on a best attempt
and what users can count on in production. Consistency and evaluation
design can expose this gap.

articles.title: Apple's memory crisis is a big red flag for tech
articles.description:
Apple is reportedly struggling to secure enough memory for upcoming
products despite its enormous purchasing power and supplier
relationships. The shortage could mean longer hardware lead times and
higher prices for smaller manufacturers and enterprise buyers
competing for the same components.

articles.title: Ai is exposing the limits of traditional network architecture
articles.description:
AI applications increasingly operate across public clouds, private
infrastructure, edge locations, and enterprise systems, creating
traffic patterns that conventional networks were not designed to
support. Networks must become more distributed, observable, and
adaptable rather than remain a passive transport layer. 

🤝

Research, the framework translates corporate and regulatory policies

articles.description:
A context graph is presented as a persistent memory system for AI
agents, connecting enterprise knowledge, conversation history, tool
evidence, and decision traces. This connected structure helps agents
maintain context across sessions, produce more relevant and accurate
answers, explain decisions, learn from prior cases, and support
auditable workflows.

articles.title: Cloud giants pour nearly $600b into capex as ai demand surges

approximately $220 billion in 2026 capital spending and says it still
will not have enough capacity to satisfy all demand through 2027.

 STARLINK'S RISE PUSHES HUGHESNET INTO BANKRUPTCY AFTER MASSIVE

Google's upcoming Pixel 11 will reportedly introduce HiLight
(formerly known as Pixel Glow), a color-changing LED that replaces the

articles.title: Artists are lawyering up against ai slop, and some are even winning
articles.description:
Illustrators, authors, and musicians are increasingly suing AI
companies like Anthropic, Meta, Google, and Suno over unauthorized use
of their work in training models. Some have already secured wins,
notably a $1.5 billion settlement in the Bartz v. Anthropic case over
pirated ebooks, though a judge ruled that training on legally acquired
scanned books counted as fair use. Despite mixed rulings, several
plaintiffs and lawyers say the legal and public-opinion tide is
shifting toward artists, even as concerns persist about creators'
long-term ability to earn a living from their work. 

 AWS IS HELPING VIBE-CODING STARTUP SUPERBLOCKS, AND THE IMPLICATIONS

articles.title: Are big
articles.description:
Superblocks, a vibe-coding startup, signed a multiyear marketing deal
with AWS to embed its tool inside enterprise customers' private
clouds. Under the partnership, apps built with Superblocks will use
Amazon Aurora databases and integrate with Amazon Bedrock, keeping
data internal and under IT's security controls. The deal reflects a
broader push by cloud providers like AWS and Microsoft to convince
enterprises to source AI orchestration and scaffolding tools from them
rather than frontier AI labs.

articles.title: Hedonic adaptation: the same design scores lower every year
articles.description:
Users grow accustomed to good design just as they do to sudden
wealth, so satisfaction scores on an unchanged product tend to slip
roughly 2–5% each year as expectations rise. Chasing novelty through
redesigns, gamification, or variable-reward feeds backfires, since
delight fades quickly while recurring irritations remain persistently
noticeable. The recommended strategy is to fix intermittent
annoyances, benchmark against competitors rather than past scores, and
treat gradual reliability gains as the lasting payoff, not fleeting
delight.

articles.title: Designing with code
articles.description:
Code has become a creative medium at Cursor, where AI agents now
handle implementation while designers focus on directing and iterating
on ideas. A gear-graphic case study shows the process: refining
shapes, spacing, motion, and looping through iterative prompts within
Cursor. Despite AI's speed, initial concept sketching remains a
distinctly human step, with designers retaining responsibility for
taste and judgment.

articles.title: I rebuilt our pricing page using nothing but customer complaints
articles.description:
A review of more than 200 pricing-related support tickets revealed
that users weren't frustrated by prices—they were confused by plan
names, feature descriptions, and unclear recommendations. By treating
complaints as research rather than noise, the team identified
recurring patterns, rewrote the pricing page around users' actual
questions, simplified decision-making with clearer plan guidance and
outcome-focused copy, and significantly reduced confusion without
changing pricing. The key lesson is that support tickets often contain
the most valuable UX insights: complaints reveal mismatches between a
product's mental model and users' expectations, making them a powerful
foundation for design decisions.

articles.title: Battling ai fatigue as a designer and developer: a practical guide
articles.description:
A UI designer and developer noticed AI fatigue while vibe-coding a
personal expenses app, prompting reflection on healthier AI habits.
Key recommendations include limiting AI use outside work, keeping
enjoyable tasks and personal writing human-made, and resisting
pressure toward extreme productivity or constantly adopting new tools.
Stepping away from AI in personal time feels liberating. Chasing 100x
productivity or fear of "falling behind" are misconceptions
unsupported by reality.

articles.title: Ai fluency isn't the finish line
articles.description:
Product builders increasingly value AI tool skills, but Figma's 2026
AI report argues collaboration and facilitation matter just as much as
tool fluency. Three practices stand out: building shared internal
tools so individual AI knowledge benefits whole teams, actively
guiding stakeholders toward decisions amid unlimited AI-generated
options, and openly sharing experiments—including failures—to
close AI adoption gaps between colleagues. Tool proficiency remains
necessary but insufficient. The surrounding human skills of building,
deciding, and sharing determine team success.

articles.description:
An advanced agentic harness for production-sized agents is proposed
here, emphasizing the need for well-structured operations through
components like typed tools, directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), tiered
memory, and verification hierarchies to create a reliable system
capable of planning, acting, recovering, and self-evaluating. This
architecture uses the composition of small, testable primitives to
improve efficiency and performance while making sure the system
remains extensible and adaptable.

Should you self-host inference?
articles.description:
Self-hosting AI inference is good primarily when processing over two
million tokens daily or when data cannot leave the organization's
network. For most companies, a hybrid approach combining local and API
models offers the best balance of cost and control.

articles.title: The valley of webhooks
articles.description:
Building systems that rely on webhooks for data synchronization
consistently proves problematic due to their inherent nature as
notifications rather than reliable data delivery methods. A proposed
alternative is a designated change log that would eliminate issues
like data drift and the need for complex mitigation strategies by
allowing consumers to request updates directly from providers.

articles.title: Cloudflare os: an open platform for agents, apps, and work
articles.description:
Cloudflare OS is an open-source platform designed to provide
organizations with customized agent workspaces that helps with
collaboration, task automation, and app development based on the
company's internal knowledge and context. The platform incorporates a
security framework to ensure safe access to internal data and
resources, allowing users to create and share applications while
managing access and costs effectively.

articles.title: Introducing hark handoff
articles.description:
Hark Handoff is a computer use agent designed to automate online
tasks by navigating the internet as a human would, freeing users from
mundane online activities. The agent excels in handling end-to-end
tasks such as ordering food, shopping, making reservations, and
conducting research.

articles.title: Prime agent: a self-improving rlm agent
articles.description:
Prime Agent is a self-improving coding harness that uses a Recursive
Language Model and Continual Harness for better context management,
multi-agent communication, and long-term evaluation, positioned as an
effective tool for coding assistance and research while maintaining
open-source accessibility.

articles.description:
Google and Alphabet are updating their AI initiatives, with Sundar
Pichai highlighting the successful rollout of their Gemini models and
the user engagement with AI applications. As part of a leadership
transition, Demis Hassabis (CEO of DeepMind) will focus on shaping the
future of artificial general intelligence (AGI), while Koray
Kavukcuoglu will take on a more senior, primary role overseeing Google
DeepMind's development and research efforts.

articles.title: Why the legendary erdős problems are falling to ai
articles.description:
Recent advancements in AI have led to breakthroughs in solving
classical mathematical problems proposed by Paul Erdős, regarding the
use of unique mathematical techniques previously unexplored in the
context of these challenges. As AI tools demonstrate increasing
capabilities, they are reshaping the landscape of mathematical
inquiry, attracting attention from both professional mathematicians
and enthusiasts.

automate documentation processes, allowing them to generate and review
documentation pull requests shortly after feature merges without

The rise of AI has altered the unit economics of software by
increasing costs associated with serving users, leading to a trade-off
between product quality and profit margins.

Hobby programming communities are increasingly hostile toward LLMs
because they view the process of mastering complex skills as essential
to their craft, believing that LLM use undermines genuine learning and
expertise.

articles.title: Hassabis steps down as deepmind ceo
articles.description:
Google's chief scientist, Jeff Dean, is leaving the company after 27
years. Demis Hassabis, the CEO of Google DeepMind, is moving into a
chairman role of that unit and also assuming the title of chief
scientist at parent company Alphabet. Dean is starting his own
company. The departure is on friendly terms, and Google will invest in
his startup, which will aim to accelerate discoveries in machine
learning, science, and engineering.

articles.title: Four top google ai researchers form new start-up
articles.description:
Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat, Quoc Le, and Oriol Vinyals have left
Google to start a company called Discovery Loop. The team aims to
build AI that can improve itself with little or no help from humans.
Google plans to collaborate with the new startup and has agreed to
provide the computing power it needs to build its AI technologies for
at least the next year. Discovery Loop will operate as a public
benefit corporation.

articles.title: Spacex aims to catch a starship out of the sky this month
articles.description:
Starship Flight 14 could launch before the end of August. SpaceX
plans to catch the upper stage during the test. The flight will also
carry Starlink V3 satellites to an operational orbit.

articles.title: Why i'm leaving openai to build telepathy
articles.description:
Conduit is a startup building thought-to-text models trained on
non-invasive neural data. Developing thought-to-text technology would
allow humans to talk to AI with their thoughts, allowing AI to become
an extension of them. To do this, the startup needs to scale up its
data collection and develop special hardware.

articles.title: What are code reviews even for?
articles.description:
Code review is how teams build a shared understanding of a system.
Automating the process removes that shared understanding. AI
accelerates cognitive and intent debt - debts that don't appear on a
dashboard. By the time anyone realizes, months later, recovering that
understanding will be far more expensive than preserving it would have
been.

articles.title: Google in the post-jeff dean, post-demis hassabis era
articles.description:
Fears that Google is losing talent are exaggerated in the media. The
impact of Google's recent loss of talent will be smaller than the
headlines suggest. Google is further behind in the AI frontier than
people estimate. However, its cloud business grew 82% year-over-year
last quarter, a sign that the business could still win on compute.

articles.title: Ai is a bubble, just like dot-com
articles.description:
Intelligent people can look at the same thing and see wildly
different things. History says that conclusions that are far apart can
both be correct. AI enables new things that nothing before could. This
post is the first in a series that explores what new things AI
enables.

articles.title: Pact cto used allstacks to cut product planning time by more than 60%
articles.description:
See how companies are improving product management processes and
defining quality specifications and requirements, for FREE [13].

articles.title: Apple's icloud private relay is leaking users' real ip addresses
articles.description:
iCloud Private Relay can expose users' real IPs to websites that use
or pretend to use passkeys.

articles.title: Open questions on open weights
articles.description:
Open weight models allow AI to truly be the user's property, but
their openness allows them to be used for nefarious purposes.

articles.title: See the sun like never before with most detailed images yet
articles.description:
The Inouye Solar Telescope, a facility built on a high peak in
Hawaii, has captured images of the surface of the Sun in new,
unprecedented detail.

articles.title: Openai models joined forces months ahead of hugging face hack
articles.description:
Multiple OpenAI internal-only agents spend months leaving notes for
each other on message boards around the goal of accessing the
internet.

articles.title: What's so hard about continuous learning?
articles.description:
Model weights are frozen once the model is released. 

 THE SIMS AND EA FC MAKER ELECTRONIC ARTS SELLS FOR $55BN TO SAUDI-LED

articles.title: Group
articles.description:
The investors are taking EA private, meaning all of its public shares
will be purchased and it will no longer be traded on a stock exchange.

articles.title: Cassandra cold reads
articles.description:
Netflix's TimeSeries Abstraction stores and queries multi-petabyte
temporal datasets, tiering older, immutable slices from hot Cassandra
into cheaper S3 storage. The earlier design used Kafka and Flink to
stream Parquet to S3 and daily compaction, serving cold reads with
roughly 500 ms p99 latency, but added operational cost. The later
Cassandra-native cold tier reads directly from S3 backups, serves 15+
PB of compressed cold data, and improves p90 latency by about 30%
while preserving the same query API. 

 GEM TRAINING: HOW META DOUBLED THE EFFICIENCY OF ITS LLM-SCALE ADS

articles.title: Foundation model
articles.description:
Meta scaled its ads recommendation foundation model 4x in 12 months
and doubled training efficiency to 20–25% MFU through five
techniques: jagged flash attention to eliminate padding waste, a
unified attention kernel with 2–3.5x speedup, MXFP8 precision
training, SM-free collective communication that reclaims ~23 SMs, and
a load-balancing shuffle that adds 4% efficiency at zero communication
cost. 

 LLMS FOR RELEVANCE: AUTOMATING HIGH-QUALITY PRODUCT RELEVANCE

articles.title: Labeling in flipkart search
articles.description:
Flipkart's Product Analyser trains a relevance labeling model in two
stages: SFT on millions of balanced query-product examples with
generated reasoning traces, then GRPO alignment using an 8B reward
model that scores explanation quality alongside label correctness. The
automated NDCG report it produces differs from the manual one by under
1%, at 30% lower cost.

articles.title: A single source of truth
articles.description:
Defining metrics once in a semantic layer reduces the risk of
conflicting numbers across Tableau, Power BI, and notebooks, and makes
permission controls and change propagation auditable from a single
place. The semantic layer is an operational risk mitigation strategy
rather than an optional layer.

articles.title: Prototype on a laptop, scale to 16 billion rows: one polars query
articles.description:
Polars lets teams develop ETL pipelines locally on a representative
data sample, then run the exact same LazyFrame queries across 16
billion rows in the cloud without rewriting the logic. The pipeline
pre-aggregates raw Polymarket data into small Parquet artifacts in S3,
allowing a Plotly Dash dashboard to remain fast without scanning the
full dataset on each request.

articles.title: The mean means nothing
articles.description:
A web service latency rollout shows the mean rising 9%, the median
falling 46%, and p99 rising 119% within the same dataset,
demonstrating how single-metric summaries can hide bimodal
distributions. Further analysis like density plots, CDFs, shift
functions, and ridgelines provide complementary views that together
identify response size as the root cause.

articles.title: Harnesses
articles.description:
Smevals is a lightweight Python CLI for running task-specific evals
across multiple models to find the cheapest one that meets a quality
bar. You define tasks, write YAML graders with custom checker scripts,
run them against a set of model configs, and view scored results in a
local dashboard or static site.

articles.title: Bringing ducklake to datafusion
articles.description:
DuckLake is now implemented for Apache DataFusion as a
production-ready, open-source catalog backend, giving Hotdata
transactional metadata, snapshots, and schema management for Parquet
tables in object storage. The design supports multiple relational
catalog backends and logical catalogs, enabling millions of isolated,
ephemeral databases for AI agents without duplicating infrastructure.
TPC-H benchmarks across 22 queries and three dataset sizes showed no
measurable overhead versus direct Parquet access, with slightly better
performance due to less metadata discovery during query planning.

articles.title: Everyone records the mysql audit log. nobody reads it
articles.description:
DB Trail makes MySQL audit logs queryable by linking row changes to
session identity, SQL statements, and before-images. It provides
attributed, row-level answers for destructive actions and generates
transaction-scoped reversal SQL to restore affected data.

articles.title: Encoding or compression: why not both?
articles.description:
Encoding improves analytical query execution, while compression
mainly reduces storage. Dictionary encoding and frame-of-reference
enable fast comparisons, pruning, and SIMD operations. CedarDB's
results suggest always encoding, then adding zstd only when the disk
savings justify it.

articles.title: Kafka app? there's a skill for that
articles.description:
Etsy built Claude Code skills for seven Kafka streaming workflows,
covering ML feature generation, embeddings, and fan-out pipelines.

articles.title: Stop graphing everything: when graphrag actually beats vector rag
articles.description:
GraphRAG works best for multi-hop, relationship-heavy, or explainable
queries, while vector RAG is cheaper for semantic lookup.

articles.title: Ibm bob makes workflows reviewable, testable and scalable
articles.description:
The value of IBM Bob, an AI development partner, isn't simply that
it writes code. It also helps turn messy discovery work into
artifacts engineers can review, test and reuse. For developers, Bob
helps reduce discovery work time by analyzing systems, generating work
that fits team conventions and supporting the software development
lifecycle.

CrushBank developers used IBM Bob to reason through architecture, move
into implementation and inspected generated changes without leaving
the workflow. Bob helped identify patterns, build ingestion paths and
create solutions while keeping developers in control through code
reviews, sensitive data scanning, test harnesses and human peer
review.

Read the full story [5]

articles.title: Anthropic reportedly signed a $10b cloud deal with volta
articles.description:
Anthropic reportedly agreed to buy six years of cloud capacity from
AI infrastructure startup Volta. The planned 133-megawatt Norway data
center would be developed with Bitdeer and powered by NVIDIA Vera
Rubin systems.

articles.title: A unified api for ai model routing
articles.description:
Model routing on the Google Cloud API Gateway is now available in
public preview. The API gateway provides a lightweight, serverless
ingress layer that accepts OpenAI-compatible requests and dynamically
routes them to Gemini, Claude, or OpenAI OSS-GPT. It can be used
standalone for simple rate limiting and token tracking or paired
seamlessly with the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. This article
contains a step-by-step guide on how to configure router logic.

articles.title: Cloudflare introduced programmable wallets for ai agents
articles.description:
Cloudflare Wallets is a system designed to give AI agents stable
identities and controlled access to payments for APIs, MCP tools, and
online content. Virtual Wallets will support spending limits, allow
lists, and transaction caps for safer agentic commerce.

articles.title: Unpacking chatgpt work: the agent for a billion users
articles.description:
ChatGPT Work is OpenAI's agent product for knowledge work. Its
current form is an amalgamation of ChatGPT, the Codex app, the Codex
harness, the original Codex cloud agent, ChatGPT agent, Atlas,
OpenClaw, and more. This article decodes the complex product lineup
and explains what Work is, where it fits in OpenAI's lineup, the many
interesting choices in its design, the tensions underneath, and where
the product is likely headed. OpenAI plans to merge Chat and Work, so
Work is really a preview for how ChatGPT's billions of users will soon
use the app.

articles.title: What codex actually sends to the model
articles.description:
A developer recorded the requests Codex generated for a 16-character
prompt by pointing it at a custom local server. They measured what
changed as it loaded instructions, exposed tools, read files, ran
commands, received images, and compacted its history. The experiment
did not call an external model. This post details the findings from
the experiment. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: Black duck: ai-driven exploits are here. are you ready?
articles.description:
The exploit window is collapsing. AI turns newly disclosed
vulnerabilities into working attacks in hours, not weeks. BLACK DUCK
POLARIS™ PLATFORM and SIGNAL™ help organizations become Mythos
Ready with intelligent prioritization, automated workflows, and faster
remediation of exploitable risk. 

BLACK DUCK CAN HELP. [11]

articles.title: Introducing shieldstral
articles.description:
Shieldstral features a 3B open-weights multimodal safety classifier
that outperforms models up to 7x its size. It accepts plain-language
policies at inference time, unifying text and image safety evaluation
without retraining. Shieldstral delivers calibrated safety scores
across diverse benchmarks while running efficiently on a single 16GB
NVIDIA GPU. It is a step toward moderation that adapts to context
instead of forcing every product through one frozen taxonomy.

articles.title: Nvidia released alpamayo 2
articles.description:
NVIDIA has released Alpamayo 2 Super under a commercial license for
robotaxis and autonomous vehicles. The reasoning model was designed to
handle rare driving scenarios with inspectable decisions and broad
multitask capabilities.

articles.title: Introducing kiro crew
articles.description:
Kiro Crew is a persistent workspace for development work that
self-improves and continues beyond one session. It can run locally or
remotely on personal hardware. Kiro Crew allows developers to start
work from within a desktop app, web dashboard, or CLI, and continue
the same work through connection tools like Slack and Discord. It can
run multistep tasks and recurring jobs on a schedule and also monitor
systems until something needs attention.

articles.title: Diffusiongemma technical report
articles.description:
DiffusionGemma adapted Gemma 4 into a discrete diffusion model that
refined 256-token blocks in parallel, reaching roughly 1,500 output
tokens per second on a single NVIDIA H100.

articles.title: The computer use verification skill that every agent needs
articles.description:
Computer-use verification lets coding agents reproduce bugs, validate
implementations against specs, and attach screenshots or videos to
pull requests. Integrated into triage, implementation, and review
workflows, cloud-based subagents reduce human review burden and enable
iterative self-debugging.

articles.title: Spacex says spending spree is supercharging ai revenues
articles.description:
SpaceX's capital expenditures hit $18.4 billion in the most recent
quarter. The bulk of that figure is tied to the company's ongoing AI
build-out. The company is plowing money into terrestrial computing
infrastructure, signing AI deals, and working toward launching orbital
data centers. SpaceX is on track to have $100 billion in annualized
recurring revenue by December, most of it coming from data center
deals.

articles.title: Fast.
articles.description:
The cost of enterprise AI scales with every query. CData Connect AI
can cut LLM context handling costs by up to 97.6% without sacrificing
answers. Learn more about token-efficient architecture [18]

articles.title: Nvidia's real-time full-duplex voice model
articles.description:
NemotronLabs VoiceChat is an 11B end-to-end speech model that handles
streaming understanding, speech generation, and tool calling within
one architecture.

articles.title: The reverse replicator
articles.description:
Backflip AI developed a model that converts physical parts into
digital CAD files in minutes for around $10.

articles.title: Mixture-of-kittens: our open-source moe megakernel for nvl72s
articles.description:
Cursor's Mixture-of-Kittens (MoK) is an open-source optimized
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) megakernel that improves efficiency on NVL72s
GPUs, which significantly boosts performance for models like Composer
by addressing computation and communication bottlenecks.

articles.title: Lfm2.5-2.6b: deploy agents everywhere
articles.description:
LFM2.5-2.6B, a 2.6B parameter on-device agentic model, enables free
inference, low latency, and robust privacy by running locally on
hardware like phones or CPUs.

articles.title: Knows.
articles.description:
1Password's research found that 33% of IT and security professionals
have no idea how many non-human identities or AI agents are being used
at their company. And 71% say they have visibility gaps into which
agents are using credentials.

1Password Privileged Access [5] logs every access event and session
automatically for every system it manages, so security teams get a
complete picture of who accessed what, when, and why.

 	* Access exists only as long as the work requires it.
 	* Every access event and session is logged automatically.
 	* Exact permissions are created directly in the system's native
policy language.

SEE HOW IT WORKS. [6]

articles.title: Google is working on plugins for gemini enterprise
articles.description:
Google appears to be developing Plugins and a dedicated Notifications
area for Gemini Enterprise, according to unfinished interface
elements. Plugins may package reusable Skills and Connectors into
multi-step workplace workflows, while Notifications would collect
completed results from background tasks. Google has not announced
either feature or provided a rollout timeline.

articles.title: Feds get 3 days to patch n-able god mode flaw under active exploit
articles.description:
CISA has ordered federal agencies to patch an actively exploited
N-able N-central vulnerability that can give attackers remote
administrative access to an MSP's management console. Successful
attacks have allowed access to managed customer systems and the
creation of persistent Cloudflare tunnels. All versions before
N-central 2026.3.1.7 are affected.

articles.title: Aws is failing fast. can its customers keep up?
articles.description:
AWS has placed Amazon Q Business, Amazon Kendra, Bedrock Agents
Classic, and nine SageMaker AI capabilities into maintenance mode,
blocking new customers while continuing access and support for
existing users. This is a rational portfolio correction driven by
changing technology and adoption, but AWS can reallocate resources
faster than enterprise customers can migrate from services in which
they have invested.

articles.title: The enterprise ai strategy that outlasts any single model
articles.description:
Enterprises should avoid tying their AI strategy to a single provider
as models, capabilities, and pricing continue to leapfrog one another.
A model-agnostic architecture that can swap underlying models and
compound improvements at the system level would allow organizations to
benefit from advances across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and others.

articles.title: Your team isn't ignoring security. they're just underwater
articles.description:
Cloud security tools can generate more findings than teams can
realistically address, leaving vulnerabilities and misconfigurations
open despite plenty of visibility. The article recommends a recurring
triage process with clear ownership and business context to prioritize
meaningful risks and keep remediation moving. 

🤝

articles.title: Sixb: the operating layer for enterprise ai
articles.description:
Sixb introduces an operational framework for enterprise AI that
connects business data, models, rules, permissions, and workflows in a
shared environment for teams and AI agents. The framework is intended
to let agents act within controlled business processes rather than
merely answer prompted questions. Version 0.1.0 includes data
connectors, automation, agent tooling, security controls, storage
options, and custom application support.

articles.title: Snaplogic introduces agentic assistant for data integration
articles.description:
SnapLogic has upgraded SnapGPT from an integration copilot into an
agentic assistant that can plan, build, explain, validate, and
troubleshoot enterprise data integrations through natural language.
The assistant also provides administrators with activity logs and
production monitoring insights for AI-assisted integration work.

articles.title: Removing the security barrier to agentforce adoption
articles.description:
Salesforce's Private Connect platform removes a security and
connectivity barrier to enterprise adoption of Agentforce and other
services by providing audited, encrypted private paths that avoid the
public internet. Architectural redesigns and automation reduced
provisioning from weeks to under 30 minutes. The platform now handles
approximately 120 TB of data and 683 million requests monthly across
15 AWS regions.

articles.title: Ai agents get better at it ops, but only with humans in the loop
articles.description:
A study of nearly 150,000 agent actions across 40 companies found AI
now performs about one-third of IT workflow actions, primarily routine
and reversible tasks, while humans retain control over higher-risk
decisions. Agent performance improved through repeated human feedback,
but identity, onboarding, and offboarding tasks failed most often
because of outdated data, missing accounts, and unreliable
integrations.

articles.title: Google workspace plugins: cursor
articles.description:
Cursor has launched plugins that let users read, write, and take
actions across Google Workspace without leaving Cursor.

articles.title: Redefining network security for the frontier ai era
articles.description:
Palo Alto Networks launched PAN-OS 12.2 Ceres with advanced virtual
patching, proactive IP-layer defense, six network administration
agents, quantum-safe security capabilities, and new high-performance
firewalls.

articles.title: Code, craft, and the making of nested folders
articles.description:
Figma's nested folders are a long-requested feature that helps
growing teams stay organized. Creating the feature required rebuilding
the company's content and permissions system from scratch. The team
abandoned traditional product development in favor of leading with
code, blurring roles across engineering, design, and product, and
replacing handoffs with ongoing collaboration and shared craft.
Customer feedback from early-access programs and community outreach
shaped the rollout, which is expected to reach all users within a few
weeks.

articles.title: Lawsuit
articles.description:
Apple has asked the court for a preliminary injunction in its trade
secrets lawsuit against OpenAI, arguing that it is being irreparably
harmed as OpenAI continues to use allegedly stolen confidential
information in its hardware development. While OpenAI agreed to stop
using Apple's confidential information, preserve evidence, and halt
disclosures, it refused Apple's requests for forensic inspections and
comprehensive searches of its systems. Apple is also seeking expedited
discovery, as OpenAI continues to publicly reject the allegations and
criticize the lawsuit. 

 GOOGLE PAUSES AI SATELLITE IMAGES, AFTER FEARS OF DEEPFAKES IN THE
articles.section: APPLE MOVES FOR PRELIMINARY INJUNCTION IN OPENAI TRADE SECRETS

articles.title: Sky
articles.description:
Google has removed a newly launched Google Earth feature that let
users generate AI satellite images, citing screenshots violating its
policies. Open-source researchers and journalists had shown the tool
could produce convincing fake imagery of disasters, like fires on
Iran's Kharg Island or Capitol flooding, raising misinformation
concerns. Experts warned such tools threaten satellite imagery's role
as a trusted verification source, especially as fake satellite images
had already circulated during the US-Israel-Iran conflict.
articles.section: APPLE MOVES FOR PRELIMINARY INJUNCTION IN OPENAI TRADE SECRETS

articles.title: Ideas are cheap. invention is not
articles.description:
Since AI can generate endless ideas, the real bottleneck shifts to
selecting, validating, and applying judgment to those ideas, rather
than producing them. A structured invention pipeline—discovering
opportunities, generating concepts through methods like SIT, TRIZ, and
cross-domain collision, then stress-testing, scoring, and
validating—turns raw ideation into genuinely usable, defensible
proposals. Invention is fundamentally about killing weak ideas and
distilling survivors into a clear, actionable brief.

articles.title: Designing for the proxy
articles.description:
AI has become the first audience for much of our work, interpreting
and summarizing content before people see it, which makes
machine-readable structure increasingly important. However, the goal
should be to optimize for AI without designing for it, as the real
value of design still lies in the invisible decisions—systems,
accessibility, information architecture, and judgment—that
AI-generated interfaces can't replicate. The challenge is to create
experiences that are easy for machines to understand while remaining
focused on the humans they're ultimately meant to serve.

articles.title: No, vermont's new logo design isn't comic sans
articles.description:
Vermont Tourism has unveiled its first dedicated brand identity,
created by DNCO, with a custom wordmark inspired by the state's
hand-painted signs, landscapes and cultural heritage. Rather than
relying on generic travel imagery, the branding highlights Vermont as
a "State of Inspiration," using a flexible design system to showcase
its artistic community, natural beauty and local traditions. While
some critics compared the logo to Comic Sans, the design's details
intentionally reference Vermont's hills, roads, moonlit landscapes and
folklore, making it part of a broader identity rather than a
standalone logo.

articles.title: From frictionless to meaningful
articles.description:
Frictionless design is often forgettable and meaningless, while
friction can bring memory, reflection, connection, and personal growth
back into experiences. Embracing friction, rather than eliminating it,
is the path toward greater awareness, transparency, and growth.

articles.title: Designing systems that decide
articles.description:
Runtime-assembled AI interfaces require a fundamental shift in design
thinking, not just new tactics. Rather than shipping fixed screens,
designers must move toward outcome-oriented thinking—defining goals,
constraints, and rules for generation, much like an improv director
shaping a scene instead of scripting every line. This essay outlines
ten outdated design instincts to unlearn, replacing assumptions like
"same input, same output" with approaches suited to radically
adaptive, agent-driven interfaces.

articles.title: Technical rebrand for indice
articles.description:
Adoratorio Studio rebranded luxury eyewear retailer Indice for its
10th anniversary by repositioning it as "The Eyewear Lounge"—a
welcoming, culture-driven destination rather than a traditional
optical store. Inspired by the shop's interiors, the new identity
features a flowing logo based on the curves of a De Sede sofa (which
also resembles an eyelash), a muted color palette drawn from the space
itself, and a mix of expressive typography and soft film-style
photography. The result is a brand system that reflects the store's
atmosphere of craftsmanship, intimacy, and slow, considered shopping,
making the visual identity feel like a natural extension of the
physical experience.
articles.section: ADORATORIO STUDIO TAKES A NEW LENS ON EYEWEAR WITH A SOFT BUT

articles.title: Stop using epics and user stories
articles.description:
Epics and user stories often spark pointless arguments that muddy
clarity.

articles.title: For creatives?
articles.description:
Anthropic's $1.5 billion settlement with authors, over pirated books
used to train Claude, sounds like a major win but changes little for
creatives. 

 USING PENCIL AND FINE LINERS, ANNA KARETNIKOVA KNOWS WHEN TO THRASH

articles.title: The traditional rulebook when needed
articles.description:
Illustrator Anna Karetnikova creates richly detailed, emotionally
expressive illustrations inspired by Slavic folklore, everyday life
and traditional drawing techniques, inviting viewers to slow down and
discover layered stories.

articles.title: Turn one giant ai-generated pull request to a reviewable stack
articles.description:
The management of AI-generated pull requests can be improved on
GitHub now by structuring them into smaller, reviewable components
known as stacked pull requests. This allows for the decomposition of
large features into manageable layers, each addressing a single
concern.

 HOW WE BUILT A REALTIME SYSTEM FOR RESPONSIVE VOICE AI IN SIX MONTHS

articles.title: Don't stop early: case-folding source code at memory speed
articles.description:
Case folding is an operation in text processing that makes sure
strings differing only in case are treated as equal, but achieving
this quickly at scale is a challenge. GitHub's code search engine,
Blackbird, efficiently implements case folding by using a branch-free
loop and byte-space arithmetic, enabling it to process ASCII
characters at speeds exceeding 45 GiB/s on a single core.
articles.section:
ARTICLES & TUTORIALS

 HOW WE BUILT A REALTIME SYSTEM FOR RESPONSIVE VOICE AI IN SIX MONTHS

articles.title: Rewrite all the code, all the time
articles.description:
The future of software development will have automatic coding
generated from high-level formal specifications rather than
conventional written code. While this shift presents opportunities for
improved software security and adaptability, it also requires changes
to current development practices and a move away from viewing legacy
code as a lasting resource.

articles.title: Pi, minimal and performant
articles.description:
Pi embraces minimalism in its design, offering only four tools and a
streamlined system prompt under 1,000 tokens, which has been shown to
produce better performance at a lower cost compared to more complex
coding tools. Case studies from Databricks and Shopify show Pi's
effectiveness in delivering ideal outcomes through its extensible
framework.

articles.title: Open source just reached frontier code review.🔍
articles.description:
PR-AF [9] ranks #2 of 42 on Martian's Code-Review-Bench — ahead of
the commercial tools, at ~10x lower cost per review. The harness is
why: a review strategy planned per PR, reviewer agents in parallel,
every finding verified against your source. No hallucinated comments.
Self-hosted, drops into GitHub Actions.

Star & Deploy [9]

 INTRODUCING THE WARP AGENT CLI: A CLI CODING AGENT THAT DOES WHAT

articles.title: Others can't
articles.description:
The Warp Agent CLI is a new standalone command-line interface
designed for better terminal workflows, compatible with various
platforms such as Ghostty, iTerm 2, and VS Code. It has built-in
model-routing, persistent sessions, and the ability to run remote
agents without needing installations, catering specifically to
professional developers. 

 ANNOUNCING CLOUDFLARE WALLETS: THE PROGRAMMABLE WALLET FOR THE

articles.title: Agentic internet
articles.description:
Cloudflare Wallets make interactions easier between AI agents and
APIs by providing a unique username and enabling payment for services.
The wallets include Account Wallets for human users and Virtual
Wallets for agents, allowing the latter to manage spending within
defined limits while exploring and testing various APIs with less
friction.

articles.title: Adversaries are weaponizing ai
articles.description:
Adversaries are increasingly using AI for their malicious activities,
using it for software development, scaling operations, and
vulnerability research. The effectiveness of AI in these scenarios
heavily depends on the user's expertise. While novice actors can
create basic malicious tools, more advanced users are able to produce
sophisticated outputs and automate complex processes.

articles.title: Deep dive: why did doordash ship a cli?
articles.description:
DoorDash's introduction of a CLI reflects a strategic shift aimed at
engaging with autonomous agents that may disrupt traditional food
delivery methods. This move, rather than serving as a conventional
growth channel, focuses on internal insights by analyzing how these
agents operate, which the company previously didn't have.

articles.title: What actually keeps an ai benchmark useful? scale
articles.description:
A study of 60 widely used LLM benchmarks shows that nearly half have
reached saturation, making them unable to differentiate top models due
to measurement noise. Some factors contributing to saturation include
benchmark age and test set size, while commonly assumed safeguards
like private test sets and output formats do not effectively prevent
this issue.

passes can outperform a seemingly efficient branchy single pass.

articles.title: Smaller, faster, safer: running kimi and glm at scale
articles.description:
Cloudflare has detailed three techniques it uses to run large AI
models like Moonshot's Kimi K2 and Z.ai's GLM on its Workers AI
platform more efficiently. The company stores the KV cache in 8-bit
floating point instead of 16-bit, which doubles the context capacity
for Kimi K2.6 from roughly 686,000 tokens to 1.37 million and reduces
cost per token by about 30%. For GLM, Cloudflare compresses model
weights from 8-bit to 4-bit integers, shrinking the checkpoint from
705 GB to 421 GB and boosting single-request decode speed by 55%. A
third layer, KV cache integrity checking, adds under 1% overhead on
throughput and tail latency while preventing requests from reading
data belonging to other users.

articles.title: Mirrorcode
articles.description:
MirrorCode is a benchmark that tests AI models on long-horizon tasks.
It contains tasks where AI models have to reimplement entire programs
end-to-end without access to the original source code. AI-generated
solutions must match the original program's output exactly on
end-to-end tests. The benchmark's 25 target programs span different
areas of computing, including Unix utilities, data serialization and
query tools, bioinformatics, interpreters, static analysis,
cryptography, and compression. 

 FROM RLVR TO RLSVR (GITHUB REPO) [14] 

 RLSVR expanded RLVR beyond inherently verifiable problems by
transforming open-ended tasks into proxy environments with rules and
outcomes that generated their own reward signals. SpyRL demonstrated
the approach through multi-agent self-play, where predetermined roles
and voting made evaluation automatic.

limitations, but because of undocumented decisions, hard-coded values,
and inconsistencies scattered throughout design systems. A practical
framework addresses this through treating design decisions as
infrastructure, auditing tools like FigmaLint, and a three-layer
system of spec files, token layers, and automated audits. Design debt
can't be resolved by AI alone—it requires deliberate human guidance
and ongoing maintenance of design systems over time.

articles.title: Creative technologists are moving from the margins to the center

combining design, engineering, and storytelling to explore what new
technologies can mean before their use cases are established. Although
the role has existed for decades under various names, AI has made it
increasingly valuable because companies need people who can quickly
prototype ideas, connect disciplines, and shape new experiences rather
than simply execute predefined ones. The broader shift is that many
designers and creative professionals will increasingly adopt this way
of working, treating technology as a medium for experimentation and
expression rather than just a tool.

articles.title: The hidden details in every font
articles.description:
Good typography is largely invisible. Type designers spend months
making subtle adjustments—such as optical sizing, spacing,
overshoots, ink traps, and character differentiation—so that text
feels effortless to read without readers ever noticing the craft
behind it. Many of these techniques have been refined over centuries
and are based on how human vision works, ensuring letters remain
legible at different sizes, in different contexts, and even under
challenging conditions like poor printing or road signage. The result
is that typography doesn't just convey words - it quietly influences
readability, tone, and even credibility, demonstrating that the best
type design succeeds precisely because it disappears behind the
meaning.

articles.title: 10 gui design elements build every user interface
articles.description:

menus, links, dialogs, alerts, icons, checkboxes/radio buttons, tabs,
and search—that form the basic vocabulary underlying nearly every
interface built over 40+ years. The article traces each element's
history, explains its usability role, and offers 86 evidence-based
design guidelines plus bonus coverage of windows and pointers. It
argues designers should master this established alphabet rather than
invent new conventions, since familiarity, tested through Jakob's Law
and decades of use, consistently outperforms novelty.

recognizable brand identities.

team-led rituals, and thoughtfully designed spaces. As Koto grows, it
prioritizes hiring ambitious, low-ego people with potential, investing

craftsmanship, and co-creation to build a lasting creative legacy.
