articles.title: What's the largest software project ai can complete on its own?
articles.description:
MirrorCode is a benchmark designed to evaluate AI's ability to
autonomously reimplement entire software programs from scratch without
access to the original code, focusing on long-horizon coding tasks. AI
models have shown they can successfully tackle some of these complex
tasks.

articles.title: Massively parallel postgres backups
articles.description:
Massively parallel backups for sharded Postgres databases are
designed to create consistent, encrypted snapshots every 12 hours with
minimal impact on production queries. By using cloud infrastructure
and advanced techniques like Write-Ahead Log (WAL) replay, these
backups can efficiently handle petabyte-scale databases, reducing the
time needed for backup processes through parallelism across multiple
shards.

articles.title: Experiments with ai code review
articles.description:
Wealthfront went on a multi-year experiment to improve AI-augmented
code review processes, transitioning from initial skepticism to a
structured approach that uses models like Opus 4 and Gemini for
effective bug detection and code analysis. Their iterative refinements
have led to improved review outcomes, reduced false positives, and an
efficient review timeline.

articles.title: Llms reward expertise
articles.description:
LLMs have transformed the way individuals approach technical tasks by
allowing those with limited skills to produce decent results, turning
them into generalists. However, true expertise in a given domain is
necessary for maximizing LLMs' potential, as shown by the ability of
knowledgeable users to engage more effectively with the models.

articles.title: Use task runners for common coding tasks
articles.description:
Task runners can streamline the workflow of software developers by
automating common coding tasks across various repositories. By
creating simple scripts or using tools like Make, Just, or Mise,
developers can run commands for tasks such as installing dependencies,
building, testing, and formatting code without having to remember
complex commands specific to each tech stack.

articles.title: Native apps should be avoided whenever possible
articles.description:
Native apps often collect much more personal data than their web
counterparts, granting third-party software access to users' sensitive
information without explicit consent.

articles.title: Celeris-1 is now ranked the #1 fastest llm by artificial analysis
articles.description:
Every LLM call in a chain compounds latency. Celeris-1 cuts each one
to almost nothing: it decodes in parallel at 2,086 tokens per second,
the first model ever to cross 2,000. OpenAI-compatible. Up to $1,000
in free credits. See the results [14]

articles.title: Next.js 16.3
articles.description:
Next.js 16.3 has reduced memory usage in development, faster builds,
better server-side rendering, and custom error boundaries, all aimed
at optimizing existing applications without requiring changes to the
application code. The release also has Instant Navigations and new
tools like Instant Insights and Partial Prefetching. 

 BONSAI (GITHUB REPO) [16] 

 Bonsai is a UI library designed for building efficient and reactive
web applications in OCaml, allowing developers to create components as
purely functional state machines while managing state and
incrementality modularly. Its architecture helps with the development
of both browser-based and terminal-based UIs.

articles.title: Frame selection is the whole game: notes from making llms watch video
articles.description:
To effectively train vision-based LLMs on video content, careful
frame selection is necessary, as using a fixed sampling method often
misses important moments while overwhelming the model with redundant
visuals. The approach involves dynamic scene detection and multiple
channels for deduplication, along with synchronized transcripts,
allowing the model to analyze the video more comprehensively than
summaries provided by human interpreters.

articles.title: The endgame of vertical integration
articles.description:
Model Labs and Agent Labs are increasingly converging as AI
companies, like Anthropic, focus on co-designing harnesses that
optimize model performance. By integrating model and harness
development, businesses can better handle a variety of workloads and
improve their competitive edge in the enterprise AI market.

articles.title: The build vs buy head fake
articles.description:
The emergence of AI tools has led to a market upheaval, impacting
traditional software models by making the initial development of
applications cheaper and more accessible. Despite the accessibility of
AI tools, established software solutions remain valuable due to the
complexities of long-term maintenance and integration, alongside the
unique advantages of proprietary data and deep industry expertise held
by specialized companies.

articles.title: Traffic spikes
articles.description:
Join this workshop to learn how Etsy's engineers prepare for peak
traffic, debug in real time, and measure the business impact of
crashes. Save your spot [20]

articles.title: Don't be a meat proxy
articles.description:
Relying solely on AI-generated responses without understanding or
contextualizing the information can make effective communication and
collaborative work worse, as it reduces the added value of personal
insight and comprehension.

articles.title: What the bliss taught us
articles.description:
The maintainers of curl took a month-long break from handling
vulnerability reports, which resulted in a refreshing sense of relief
and allowed them to focus on other neglected project aspects.

articles.title: The ai productivity gap
articles.description:
While AI has improved productivity for engineering teams, the overall
gains in efficiency are still modest.

articles.title: You cannot own a falling floor
articles.description:
Inference costs in AI are expected to drop dramatically, becoming
nearly free within two years at any fixed level of capability, which
undermines the long-term viability of products that rely solely on
model access for differentiation.

articles.title: Reach the people who make tech buying decisions
articles.description:
One of the biggest challenges in digital advertising is reaching the
people who actually make buying decisions. Founders, CTOs, engineering
leaders, and product managers read TLDR every day to stay on top of
the tools, platforms, and trends shaping their industry. Unlike social
media, where attention is split across endless content, TLDR readers
are intentionally engaged, giving your brand the opportunity to reach
the people who influence technology purchases when they're actively
paying attention. See how TLDR sponsorship works. [4]

articles.title: Spacex's bumpy ride on the stock market may get bumpier
articles.description:
The first lockup on SpaceX shares is set to expire today. Employees
and other company insiders who were prevented from trading stock after
SpaceX's IPO will now be able to do so. Lockups prevent shares from
flooding the market and driving down their price after an IPO. More
than double the current supply that can be traded will be made
available, which may further depress the price. 

 SPACEX IS SET TO ACQUIRE 130,000 ACRES OF MARSHLAND IN SOUTHERN

articles.title: Louisiana
articles.description:
SpaceX is close to finalizing a deal to acquire about 130,000 acres
along the northern coast of the Gulf of Mexico. The deal is expected
to be officially announced later this month. The site, known as Pecan
Island, is an 18-mile stretch of marshland. It became available as
part of a legal settlement that resolved dozens of lawsuits blaming
ExxonMobil for pollution and coastal land loss.

articles.title: Base power raises $1b to roll out its giant new home battery
articles.description:
Base Power's Core is a 39.2-kWh home battery that can keep a house
running for up to 36 hours. Core, which can be installed in under an
hour, can be connected to solar and has a built-in port for recharging
from a portable generator. The lithium iron phosphate battery is
designed to operate between -22F and 122F and has an IP67 rating for
submersion in up to 3 feet of water. Core will only be available as
part of a subscription service, and the company will retain ownership
of the battery.

articles.title: Drug discovery has no magic wands
articles.description:
AI is set to transform human health. However, it will not be a magic
wand: we don't understand human biology well enough for a clever
enough reasoner to find the cures hidden in what we know. Aimed at
biology we barely understand, AI will mostly help us generate failures
faster. The path to real cures is to measure biology in the right way
and use AI to derive novel insights from those measurements.

articles.title: Improving
articles.description:
🆕 Serverless Fine-Tuning [9] is now GA in Crusoe Intelligence
Foundry. Select from a curated library of top open models and stop
troubleshooting infra with automatic recovery, full job lineage, and
unified tooling. Early stopping ends billing when your model tops
improving. No lock-in with one-click deploy to self-serve deployments.
Try now → [9]

articles.title: Cloudflare computer
articles.description:
Cloudflare Computer is a virtual file system that lives inside a
Durable Object which holds the authoritative state in SQLite and
exposes a pluggable execution surface. It handles the details and
mechanics of what code runs in an isolate, a container sandbox, or a
web browser. Cloudflare Computer gives each agent a computer optimized
for efficiency and scalability.

articles.title: Llms reward expertise
articles.description:
The most important skill in prompting is expertise in the domain
you're prompting for. The domain knowledge makes you better at using
AI because you have a sense of what a good solution might look like
and can therefore write better prompts. The usefulness of domain
knowledge suggests that human expertise will continue to be useful
even as models get stronger.

articles.title: The endgame of vertical integration
articles.description:
Model labs and agent labs are converging. Model labs continue to
develop first-party applications that compete with their customers,
while agent labs are starting to train models. The gains from
co-designing models with harnesses is why agent labs need to move into
model training. The challenge is for agent labs to offer the best
intelligence per dollar at margins that the model labs can't match.

articles.title: What are companies getting for all that ai spending?
articles.description:
The cost and benefits of AI are difficult to weigh. There are now
thousands of models, and there is no consensus around how much energy
a token requires, which model is best to perform a given task, or how
many tokens it should take. The Linux Foundation established the
Tokenomics Foundation in June to create common parameters for AI
providers to disclose. Being able to measure the costs and benefits of
AI will help researchers understand how AI is going to change
everything.

articles.title: Tool overload got your head spinning?
articles.description:
Tech stack complexity is out of control, and the last thing you need
is a bigger “stack”. Azure gives you a unified view of
applications, cloud resources, and AI—so you can ship more software
with fewer open tabs. Simplify with Azure [15]

articles.title: Why silicon valley is divided over china's powerful, cheap ai models
articles.description:
Whether to embrace or reject Chinese models has become a divisive
issue in the US tech industry.

they're building.

articles.description:
AI superforecasters have come close to the accuracy of top humans,
and their performance is rising rapidly.

The maintainers of curl took the entire month of July off from

articles.title: The shape of things to come

Software will be excavated rather than designed, created without a
concrete plan, just a lot of accretion over thousands of working days.

articles.title: Workos mcp: manage your auth platform from any ai agent
Qwen3.8-max: a new bar for coding and cowork
articles.description:
Qwen 3.8-Max is now available. The open weights will be released next
week. The model, which has 2.4 trillion parameters, delivers
comprehensive improvements across coding, work, research, and
long-horizon tasks. It can answer questions as well as complete
complex tasks end-to-end with greater reliability.

articles.title: Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science
articles.description:
OpenAI has shared a selection of ten results discovered while
evaluating an unreleased model. Each resolves or makes substantial
progress on a long-standing open problem. These problems span
high-dimensional geometry, coding theory, arithmetic circuit
complexity, group theory, operator algebras, quantum complexity,
lattice cryptography and extremal combinatorics. All of these problems
are of substantial interest to their respective mathematical
communities. Several are of broad interest across mathematics as a
whole.

articles.title: Deepseek v4 flash
articles.description:
DeepSeek released the production version of V4 Flash with stronger
agentic performance and an attached speculative decoding module. It
reportedly surpassed the larger V4 Pro Preview on several benchmarks
while activating far fewer parameters.

articles.title: Microsoft tests new mai realtime voice model
articles.description:
Microsoft's first native real-time voice model, MAI Realtime, has
surfaced as a hidden early-access entry in the company's MAI
Playground. The listing points to a bidirectional, full-duplex system
that can listen and speak at the same time rather than trading turns.
There are two voices available, both noticeably more natural than what
Copilot's voice mode currently delivers. The model will likely be made
available on Microsoft Foundry and Copilot voice, but no timeline is
available.

articles.title: Further developments about internal ai models hacking things
articles.description:
OpenAI and Anthropic's recent announcements that their unreleased
models had escaped their sandboxes and hacked external companies is a
warning, not a marketing stunt. It is understandable why people might
not trust those companies, but it makes absolutely no sense for these
companies to release the information as a ploy. Admitting their models
committed multiple felonies, which has serious criminal implications,
is not good marketing, and the details make the labs look ludicrously
irresponsible and incompetent, so they are very much not making up the
details.

articles.title: Openai's abundant intelligence
articles.description:
OpenAI outlined a cycle in which cheaper, more capable intelligence
drives adoption, revenue, infrastructure investment, and further model
improvements. The company framed large-scale infrastructure as a means
of making useful intelligence more broadly available.

articles.title: Kimi k3 on amd
articles.description:
Wafer reported 952 tokens per second per node when serving Kimi K3 on
AMD MI355X GPUs, with better performance per dollar than its Blackwell
deployments. The results suggested that high-memory accelerators and
improving software support could narrow AMD's inference gap with
Nvidia. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: Ramp swe-bench
articles.description:
Ramp built a private benchmark from 80 production backend tasks
spanning payments, accounting, procurement, treasury, and fraud. It
scores review-ready patches that pass tests within 45 minutes,
exposing model trade-offs across accuracy, latency, and cost without
public-benchmark contamination. 

 MSLK KERNEL REFERENCE (WEBSITE) [17] 

 MSLK (Meta Superintelligence Labs Kernels) is a library of fused GPU
kernels for transformer workloads. It contains a collection of
high-performance kernels and optimizations built on top of PyTorch
primitives for GenAI training and inference. MSLK is released in
accordance with the PyTorch release schedule. There is no guarantee
that each release works in conjunction with PyTorch releases that are
older than the one that the MSLK release corresponds to.

articles.title: Openai
articles.description:
Jacob Tsimerman, who recently won the Fields Medal, is starting a
position at OpenAI. Tsimerman previously wrote a paper categorizing
the ways AI might kill everyone. He appears to be so worried about the
dangers of AI that he's pivoting to work on AI safety. The star
professor wants to use math to advance the study of AI and ensure that
the technology won't lead to our extinction.

articles.title: A new era of ai testing
articles.description:
Andrej Karpathy asked Opus 5 to make a Three.js render of the first
paragraph of The Lord of the Rings with a 1-million-token budget, and
the model returned 5,500 lines of code that procedurally rendered the
story. The LLM orchestrated the polygon assets and wrote code that
animated it all according to the story. No human would have the
stamina and patience to write something this custom, so they are a
good test of what LLMs are capable of. A video of the generated
animation is available in the post.

articles.title: Ai build took a week. your data prep's still going.
articles.description:
Deasy maps, filters, enriches your unstructured data in minutes, so
retrieval pulls the right doc the first time. See how → [20]

articles.title: When genius fails—the intellectual arrogance of the ai labs
articles.description:
Leopold Aschenbrenner's hedge fund, Situational Awareness, crashed
after taking high-risk leveraged bets on the AI boom.

articles.title: Apex-accounting: ai productivity benchmark for accounting
articles.description:
APEX-Accounting, created by Ramp and Mercor, tests AI models' ability
to complete accounting tasks across 160 scenarios.

articles.title: Claude cyber evaluations
articles.description:
Anthropic found three evaluation runs in which Claude accessed the
public internet and compromised real organizations after mistakenly
treating them as capture-the-flag targets.

articles.title: Google is aiming to close feature gaps on gemini desktop
articles.description:
Google is enhancing the Gemini desktop app by adding dedicated tabs
for image and video generation and introducing a camera attachment
feature for capturing photos.

articles.title: You're invited to tailscaleup, live in san francisco
articles.description:
TailscaleUp [5] is Tailscale's flagship event for engineering,
security, and IT leaders working the hard problems in secure
connectivity: identity, access, infrastructure, and AI, across every
team and environment.

Join us on August 26 at SFJAZZ Center to see how teams are locking
down access without locking people out: writing least-privileged
grants, segmenting environments, and configuring device posture
checks. A customer panel with Duolingo, Lyft, and Microsoft covers
deploying Tailscale as a VPN replacement at enterprise scale, from
onboarding to scaling across distributed teams. See the complete
speaker lineup [6], including Grafana Labs and more. 

👉 Register now [7] with code 'TLDR20' for 20% off.

articles.title: Scanning 7.6 petabytes of huggingface training data for secrets
articles.description:
Truffle Security Co. says it scanned 7.6 petabytes of public Hugging
Face datasets and found 221,303 live, unique credentials across 6,003
datasets. The verified secrets included software supply-chain tokens,
cloud credentials, database logins, communications keys, and
AI-provider keys that the company says represent at least $920,000 in
potential annual inference charges at default spending caps.

articles.title: Scale ai hires former google cloud coo as ceo
articles.description:
Scale AI appointed Francis deSouza as CEO as it expands beyond
training data and evaluations into enterprise AI applications. The
company expects its applications business to become larger than its
original data operation within 18 months.

articles.title: Eu plans seven ai gigafactories in $11.4b compute push
articles.description:
The EU plans to invest €10 billion in seven AI gigafactories, each
designed to house at least 100,000 advanced chips. Officials hope the
funding will attract another €20 billion privately and reduce
Europe's reliance on foreign AI infrastructure.

articles.title: I'm (mostly) picking models on speed now, not intelligence
articles.description:
AI models have reached a sufficient intelligence level for many
everyday tasks, making inference speed a more important factor in
model choice. 100–200 tokens per second feels fast for human use,
while tool calls and human oversight limit the benefits of faster
models and intensifying competition may drive prices down.

articles.title: Most corporate it now runs outside company-owned data centers
articles.description:
Companies now place 46% of their workloads with cloud and colocation
providers, compared with 44% in their own data centers. AI is also
making capacity planning harder while worsening staffing shortages and
the cost of infrastructure failures. 

🤝

articles.title: Meta sees an enterprise business beyond ai agents
articles.description:
Meta says it could sell businesses APIs, AI agents, compute capacity,
and other enterprise services. The strategy could turn its enormous
internal AI infrastructure investment into a new revenue stream beyond
advertising.

articles.title: Static devirtualization of tencent vm
articles.description:
Classic virtual-machine obfuscators remain vulnerable to flexible
lifting, recompilation, and guided symbolic execution. A static
devirtualization approach for Tencent VM obfuscation analyzes the VM
dispatcher, boxed native instructions, and CET/SEH compatibility
mechanisms to symbolically recover bytecode-driven control flow and
virtualized loops. 

 UBER IS BUILDING AN AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE EMPIRE, AND HERE'S EVERY

articles.title: Company it's using to do it
articles.description:
Uber has partnered with or invested in more than 30 autonomous
vehicle companies over the past two years, rebuilding an AV strategy
focused on integrating outside technology and fleets globally.
TechCrunch's tracker details deals involving robotaxis, autonomous
trucks, sidewalk robots, drones, fleet operators and vehicle makers,
including major investments in Aurora and Lucid.

articles.title: Europe is rewriting its quantum roadmaps and asking for comments
articles.description:
The European Quantum Flagship has opened a public consultation on six
draft technology roadmaps intended to guide the EU's quantum research,
industry, and procurement priorities through 2035.

articles.title: Google cloud expands storage and networking for ai clusters
articles.description:
Google Cloud has made Managed Lustre generally available, with four
performance tiers and support for up to 8 PB of storage.

articles.title: Pixel 11 pro fold design leaks ahead of google launch event
articles.description:
Leaked marketing renders from Evan Blass reportedly reveal the
unannounced Pixel 11 Pro Fold, alongside new Pixel Buds and a Pixel
Watch, ahead of Google's launch event. The foldable appears similar to
last year's model, keeping a tall outer screen and 8-inch inner
display, but with a redesigned camera array featuring a glowy light
teased for the Pixel 11 Pro. Google's Made by Google event is set for
August 12th, where these devices are expected to be announced, though
prices may rise.

articles.title: A properties panel and annotations, now in figma make
articles.description:
Figma Make now includes a properties panel and annotations, letting
users edit designs visually or with in-context prompts instead of
relying solely on text. The properties panel adjusts spacing,
typography, and layout directly, while annotations let users mark
elements and describe changes like hover effects or animations for the
agent to apply. Both features roll out to all seats and plans, consume
credits, and currently only work with new Make designs, not previously
created ones.

articles.title: Reddit is testing a new way to watch and listen to its viral posts
articles.description:
Reddit is testing a new TikTok-inspired video experience that would
let users watch videos based on viral Reddit posts and listen to
narrated stories in the background. CEO Steve Huffman said the company
is responding to the popularity of Reddit-story content on platforms
like TikTok, where millions of videos already repurpose Reddit
discussions with text-to-speech narration. The feature is expected to
enter testing later this year, as Reddit continues expanding its video
offerings following the recent launch of video comments.

articles.title: Box
articles.description:
Jakob's Law still applies in the AI era, but the reference point has
shifted from websites to AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, and
Copilot. As users increasingly start tasks through conversational
interfaces rather than individual apps, products need to be
discoverable, understandable, and usable through assistants by using
clear naming, structured data, standard UI patterns, and protocols
like MCP and A2UI. Rather than designing only for users who visit an
app directly, designers should also optimize for products that work
behind the scenes, with AI assistants becoming the primary interface
for many tasks.

articles.title: Your people get ai. get out of their way
articles.description:
Despite widespread investment in AI, 95% of corporate AI projects
fail, not because of the technology but because bureaucracy, excessive
approvals, and a lack of trust prevent capable employees from using it
effectively. Smaller, empowered teams can make fast decisions and
focus on solving real problems, while large organizations often reward
control over judgment, creating "organizational debt" that slows
innovation. The companies that will benefit most from AI won't be
those with the best tools - they'll be the ones that trust their
people, remove unnecessary layers of management, and let experienced
employees openly experiment, share what works, and make decisions.

articles.title: How to reduce ai drifting in design
articles.description:
Design systems drift when Figma components and front-end code fall
out of sync, and AI often widens that gap rather than closing it. A
proposed fix uses "component contracts" — plain-language specs that
become the shared source of truth — paired with harness engineering,
deterministic guardrails surrounding an AI model. Testing showed an AI
agent scored 100/100 building screens from a contract catalog, versus
69/100 when ungoverned.

articles.title: Gunnersbury museum a reason to be found
articles.description:
Gunnersbury Museum and Park has introduced a new modular identity by
Wiedemann Lampe to solve a long-standing visibility problem: most
people knew the park but not the museum. The system uses separate
symbols and colors—a green tree for the park and a purple building
for the museum—that combine into a yellow identity when representing
both together, giving each its own voice while maintaining a cohesive
brand. Supported by flexible illustrations, human-focused photography,
and intuitive yellow wayfinding, the rebrand is designed to increase
awareness, encourage exploration, and help the historic site become a
more recognizable cultural destination. 

 BETHESDA'S NEW LOGO DESIGN BRINGS PEAK GAMING NOSTALGIA WITH A NOD TO

articles.title: Its iconic original branding
articles.description:
To celebrate its 40th anniversary, Bethesda has introduced a new
retro-futuristic logo that replaces its clean, corporate identity with
one inspired by the company's original 1980s and 1990s branding. The
redesign brings back the "Bethesda Softworks" name, uses an angular
cyberpunk-inspired typeface reminiscent of its early years, and aims
to better reflect the publisher's long history and personality. Fans
have overwhelmingly praised the change, seeing it as a welcome return
to Bethesda's roots and a reminder that distinctive branding can be
more memorable than generic minimalism. 

 GOOGLE'S SYNTHID WATERMARK IS HARD TO BREAK, BUT IT DOESN'T SOLVE AI

articles.title: Disinformation
articles.description:
Google's SynthID watermark survived 300 rounds of simulated
compression and resizing in testing, though cropping combined with
heavy compression eventually defeated it. Even so, watermarking can't
solve AI disinformation broadly, since fragmented detection systems,
usage limits, and unlabeled open-source models leave huge gaps.
Experts argue the better long-term strategy is authenticating genuine
content via cryptographic metadata like C2PA rather than trying to
flag every piece of synthetic media.

articles.title: The ai aesthetic
articles.description:
AI has spawned distinct design idioms—sparkle emojis, streaming
text, shimmering "thinking" indicators, tiny icons, and beige/cream
palettes with orange accents—some likely to fade, others already
spreading into broader software design.

articles.title: Chunking: how to design for a brain that can only hold four things
articles.description:
Design that groups information into meaningful units reduces
cognitive load and errors.

articles.description:
Developer tool sprawl is real. You've got one tab for logs, another

🫣 Stop playing hide-and-seek with your tools. Microsoft Azure [5]

articles.title: How to build an os without being a degenerate
articles.description:
Building an operating system effectively involves labeling your
project honestly, starting from an established OS, and engaging in
reading to understand the components thoroughly before coding. There
needs to be a focus on creating genuine drivers and collaborative
argumentation within a team are necessary for meaningful development
in OS creation.

articles.title: Curiosity reduced the heap size by 60%
articles.description:
An agent kept filtering a Ruby warning out of its test output, and
chasing it down revealed that the OpenTelemetry AWS instrumentation
was force-loading about 200 SDK service classes at boot when the app
only needed a handful. A small patch that skips unresolved autoloads
cut VM classes and heap roughly 60% and boot time 36%. Following an
odd signal for five minutes is now cheap enough to do routinely. 

 WHY DOORDASH, INSTACART, AND UBER EATS INTEGRATED LLMS INTO SEARCH

articles.title: Three different ways
articles.description:
Food search breaks keyword retrieval every way at once with synonyms,
typos, bilingual collisions, a long tail with no conversion data, and
hard constraints where “vegan chicken sandwich” scores as similar
to something that violates the whole point. Three companies solved it
off the same research base and landed at different depths of LLM
integration: DoorDash keeps it offline enriching a knowledge graph,
Instacart puts it at query understanding with a head/tail split, and
Uber Eats makes a fine-tuned Qwen the embedding backbone of two-tower
retrieval.

articles.title: Developers are attached to tools because tools encode trust
articles.description:
Developers often struggle to trust new coding tools, especially as
AI-driven systems become more integrated into the software development
lifecycle. The shift to these tools can challenge established
processes and cultural practices, leading to broken workflows despite
having advanced technology at their disposal. To regain trust, teams
need to establish clear, defined workflows that prioritize human
oversight and accountability.

articles.title: My agentic coding setup, july 2026
articles.description:
Running agents unattended, with approvals off, in parallel, with work
that survives closing your laptop and follows you to your phone, turns
out to require getting development off your local machine entirely,
onto a disposable Ubuntu VM joined to a Tailscale tailnet. Tailscale
does the heavy lifting (SSH from any network, HTTPS certs so agent dev
servers are secure contexts and stay private), with git worktrees and
a Portless wrapper keeping parallel agents from colliding. Safety is
handled by blast radius rather than prevention: push to GitHub
constantly, treat the VM as expendable.

articles.title: Advancing the price-performance frontier with gpt-5.6
articles.description:
GPT-5.6 Luna has become cheaper by 80% to $0.20/M input and $1.20/M
output. Terra has dropped20% to $2/M and $12/M. Sol is the same, with
the cuts also flowing through Codex and ChatGPT Work quotas, and
Priority Processing becoming Fast mode: 2.5× faster on Sol at 2×
price, same capability, backward compatible with priority tags.

articles.title: Swiftui after 7 years: a story of mediocrity
articles.description:
Seven years after its launch, SwiftUI is still plagued by performance
issues, unpredictable layout behavior, and a frustratingly
inconsistent API, leaving many developers feeling like they are

practice, resulting in a landscape where developers must constantly
implement workarounds and deal with a lack of backward compatibility.

The myth of Snow Leopard, a 2010 Mac OS X version marketed by Apple

articles.description:
Terraform AzureRM Provider 5.0 is generally available with improved
Azure subscription control, opt-in preflight validation, updated

properties. The major release simplifies provider behavior, improves
infrastructure feedback, and requires users to review configurations
before upgrading.

articles.title: Kubernetes v1.37 sneak peek
articles.description:
Kubernetes v1.37, planned for release on August 26, will deprecate
ipvs mode in kube-proxy, with clusters running that mode now logging a
deprecation warning on startup. Static pods will no longer be allowed
to reference Secrets or ConfigMaps via API fields, closing a
long-standing bug, and the --filename flag for kubectl run is also
being deprecated. The metrics.k8s.io API will graduate to stable after
nearly nine years in beta, and kubelet in User Namespace (Rootless
Mode) moves to beta, allowing node components to run without
host-level root privileges. Cgroup v1 support continues its phaseout,
with removal planned for a future release.

articles.title: Deploy enterprise powershell modules using azure artifacts
articles.description:
Enterprise PowerShell modules can be distributed via a private Azure
Artifacts feed using PSResourceGet, with Azure DevOps pipelines
handling GitVersion-based semantic versioning, Key Vault code signing,
and JEA restricting privileged runtime access.

articles.title: Scaling kubernetes pods with keda based on amazon sqs queue depth
articles.description:
This article walks through how to use KEDA to scale Kubernetes worker
pods based on Amazon SQS queue depth rather than CPU or memory usage.
The core idea is that in queue-driven systems, the number of messages
waiting is a more accurate signal of demand than infrastructure
utilization. KEDA calculates desired replica counts using the formula:
outstanding messages divided by a configured per-pod target. It can
scale deployments all the way down to zero when queues are empty.

articles.title: Speed is becoming more important than intelligence for ai models
articles.description:
Once models are capable enough for everyday coding, research, and
analysis, inference speed can matter more than marginal gains in
intelligence, with roughly 100–200 output tokens per second feeling
fast enough for interactive work. Further model acceleration
eventually produces diminishing returns because tool calls, databases,
local hardware, and human review become the dominant bottlenecks,
shifting competition toward serving speed and price. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: How cloudformation express mode accelerates your development cycle
articles.description:
AWS CloudFormation Express mode reports stack completion as soon as
resource configuration is applied rather than waiting for full
stabilization, speeding development iteration and AI agent workflows
while preserving dependency ordering and rollback options.

articles.title: Faster floating-point math with rust's new api
articles.description:
Rust 1.98 adds algebraic floating-point operations that let
developers explicitly permit reassociation and fused instructions
without enabling every risky optimization associated with fast-math.
Allowing the compiler to reorder independent calculations can unlock
SIMD vectorization and significantly accelerate numerical workloads,
with the tradeoff that results may vary slightly because
floating-point addition is not associative.

science. The total number of tokens used to discover all ten solutions
would have cost around $2,000 at GPT-5.6 Sol API rates. Each solution
was formalized in Lean, allowing them to be verified using the

clear path to selling it to consumers. Companies can now pay $12,500
to apply to a newly established board for approval, as long as the
drugs have been through preliminary testing. The drugs will be sold
via experimental treatment clinics, the first of which is likely to be
open by the end of the year. Patients must provide fully informed
consent, and each application must be reviewed by a board that

articles.description:
Balaji Srinivasan, a tech founder, said that he believed the US was
descending into anarchy, so he decided to build a new city from
scratch. He started by creating a tech community in Malaysia, setting
up a campus with co-working spaces, a high-end gym, and meals designed
by longevity guru Bryan Johnson. Two years in, his vision is now
colliding with reality. The project has been shut down over licensing
issues. Within hours of the government announcement, Srinivasan signed
an agreement to open a campus in Kazakhstan.

articles.title: Devtools must be open source
articles.description:
Before AI, development costs made it rational for complex software to
ship with large configuration files, extension systems, and plug-in
systems. Now, the cost of creating software and making changes has
dropped dramatically. Software that can be personalized doesn't need a
plugin system or config file. Users can just make the changes they
need themselves, with the help of agents if required.

articles.title: Ai bubble?
articles.description:
When Trump came into office, he took the guardrails that were
hindering AI development, and Larry Ellison cashed in by signing
several large infrastructure deals. This big bet on AI was built on an
astronomical amount of debt in every imaginable form. The hypothesis
was that whoever controlled the most computing power would control the
AI economy. Investors have started questioning whether this level of
spending is sustainable in recent weeks and are concerned about
whether the money being pumped into data centers will ever return the
promised profits. 

 HIS WEDDING GUESTS WERE ARRIVING—JUST AS HIS $45 BILLION FUND WAS

articles.title: Falling apart
articles.description:
Leopold Aschenbrenner had planned a multiday celebration for his
wedding, but his fund started unraveling just when guests started to
arrive. The 24-year-old investor had built a $45 billion investment
powerhouse that primarily bought stocks in the AI trade. The firm
borrowed too much money to make these AI bets, leaving it at risk as
they faltered. Citadel then swooped in and purchased the vast majority
of the firm's public stock portfolio at a discount of more than 10% to
the market value of those shares. The firm is left with a portfolio of
stocks and stakes in startups valued at more than $10 billion, but it
is still alive.

articles.description:
Halodoc migrated Airflow workloads from polling sensors and
synchronous Redshift loads to Airflow 3.x Assets and deferrable
operators. Across 160 DAGs, the team reduced worker CPU from 26.1% to
7.71% and worker memory from 49.2% to 30.8%, while also lowering

articles.title: Openai just made analytics 10x cheaper
articles.description:
OpenAI's cheaper GPT 5.6 Luna shifts agentic analytics toward small,
fast models paired with low-latency analytical databases, delivering
highly accurate SQL answers for under half a cent while making
frequent evals far more affordable. The advantage now comes less from
using the smartest model and more from strong business context,
rigorous model-agnostic evals, and a responsive data platform.

articles.title: Beyond happy path engineering: databases
articles.description:
Production databases fail at the edges: stale replica reads,
ambiguous commits, deadlocks, and live migrations can break flows that
pass the happy-path tests. The practical takeaway is to enforce
invariants at the database boundary with guarded writes, constraints,
short transactions, idempotent retries, and explicit recovery
procedures.

articles.title: Kafka's broken promise: there is no goldilocks log
articles.description:
Kafka's partitioned stream model is a poor fit for router-style
workloads with millions of independently keyed ordered logs. OpenData
Log is built in Rust on object storage and SlateDB. It uses segmented
LSM storage, key-based scans, metadata-only splits, and read replicas
to support high-cardinality log routing more cheaply.

articles.title: Asynchronous i/o in duckdb: work, thread, work
articles.description:
DuckDB is adding asynchronous I/O so worker threads stop blocking on
S3-backed Parquet and CSV reads. The design separates async and worker
pools, adds read-ahead and memory governance, and shows some large
performance wins: TPC-H Q6 on 22 GB Parquet fell from 8.23s to 2.84s,
while a large CSV scan time improved by nearly 20x.

articles.title: Video needs a knowledge base
articles.description:
Video is difficult to use because it can be stored and watched but
not queried, forcing manual review or repeated AI processing.
CreativAI's platform structures footage once into a searchable
knowledge base for fast queries across robotics, logistics, safety,
compliance, and physical AI use cases. 

 XBERG (GITHUB REPO) [12] 

 Xberg is an open-source engine that extracts text, tables, metadata,
and structured data from 101 formats, including PDFs, images, audio,
video, URLs, archives, and code. Its Rust core supports 15 languages
plus OCR, transcription, embeddings, structured extraction, and
deployment through libraries, CLI, REST, MCP, Docker, or Helm.

articles.title: Data lessons from inside meta (shridhar iyer)
articles.description:

validated with live search behavior. Candidate parent, child, and
sibling relationships are injected into suggestions, then clicks,
dwell time, scrolls, and conversions are aggregated into confidence
scores that promote or prune taxonomy edges.

articles.description:

articles.title: Openai cuts gpt-5.6 prices
articles.description:
OpenAI reduced GPT-5.6 Luna pricing by 80% and Terra pricing by 20%,
while improving Sol's API speed. The changes extended efficiency gains

articles.title: Gemini robotics er 2
articles.description:
Gemini Robotics ER 2 enhances automation capabilities with advanced
AI and LLM integration. This innovation improves robotic efficiency,
making it pivotal for industries needing precise automation.

articles.title: The waste inference engine
articles.description:
WASTE is an open source inference engine designed to run models whose
weights are substantially larger than the memory available on the host
machine. It is an initial step into a broader effort to make
increasingly capable models available on more hardware. The project
aims to provide people and organizations greater control over
infrastructure costs, data privacy, availability, and deployment. The
first fully supported model by WASTE is Kimi K3, which can run on a
MacBook Pro with 64 GB of unified memory.

articles.title: Building cloud environments for coding agents
articles.description:
Cursor described how making development environments easier for
agents to understand, run, and test helped cloud agents grow from
authoring about 10% of merged pull requests to more than half.

articles.title: The agent graveyard isn't real anymore
articles.description:
Enterprise AI projects increasingly reach production when vendors
prove value on live workloads, provide ongoing testing and iteration,
and expose ROI. Successful deployments start with decomposable
workflows that ship quickly and expand, rather than broad
transformations with undefined success criteria.

articles.title: Open-weight llms have caught up on accuracy
articles.description:
Open-weight LLMs have now reached accuracy parity with closed models
in regulatory and clinical tasks, at significantly lower costs. The
ClinReg benchmark showed models like GLM 5.2 and Kimi K3 performing
within one standard deviation of top proprietary models like GPT 5.6
Sol, at one-third of the cost. Different models displayed distinct
error profiles, highlighting the importance of choosing models based
on task-specific requirements rather than just ranking. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: The session you cannot take with you
articles.description:
Users should be able to close an account, keep a session, and hand it
to another model. Stateful storage should be optional, and hosted
tools should be observable. Compaction should be readable, and agent
communication should be auditable. Distillation should be a path by
which capability becomes more available, not a reason for building
ever higher walls.

articles.title: Minimax h3
articles.description:
MiniMax H3 is an open model that breaks the boundaries between tasks
and modalities. It understands unified context across text, images,
video, and audio. The model can generate up to 15 seconds of video at
2K resolution with native stereo sound. H3 excels at instruction
following, accurate text and brand rendering, and V2V motion transfer.
Early testing shows that it is ready for commercial content creation
across a wide range of use cases.

articles.title: Gemini live api overview
articles.description:
The Gemini Live API enables low-latency, real-time voice and vision
interactions with Gemini. It processes continuous streams of audio,
images, and text to deliver immediate, human-like responses. The API
creates a natural conversational experience for users. It can be used
to build real-time agents for a variety of industries. 

 AGENT BEHAVIOR (WEBSITE) [18] 

 Agent Behavior is an open standard for defining and evaluating how an
AI agent should behave across a whole trajectory. Each behavior spec
is a Markdown file that describes the recurring conduct that makes the
agent reliable. The spec gives reviewers, rubrics, scorers, and evals
something concrete to measure against. It can be used to review
traces, write eval cases, revise prompts or tools, and communicate
intended agent conduct to teams.

articles.title: Gpu management: why idle gpus are the new grounded aircraft
articles.description:

ensure efficiency - companies must focus on optimizing GPU workload
orchestration to maximize output. Specialized models and continuous
GPU management are crucial strategies for improving utilization and
staying competitive in the AI arena.

articles.description:

management into Infrastructure as Code, APIs, and CLI workflows so

Opposition to new data centers is becoming a material infrastructure

articles.title: We're launching lyria 3.5 in google flow music

out in Google Flow Music on July 29. The model brings notable
improvements in musicality, lyric quality, and vocal realism, aiming
to help users create richer, more emotionally expressive songs. It
also adds finer creative control, letting users more easily adjust the

 JONY IVE'S FIRST OPENAI HARDWARE DEVICE SOUNDS RATHER LIKE … A

articles.title: Homepad
articles.description:
OpenAI continues to tease its first AI hardware product, and recent
comments from company president Greg Brockman suggest it could
resemble a screen-equipped smart home device rather than the radically
new form factor previously implied. While the company remains
intentionally vague, the device is increasingly rumored to be part of
a family of AI-first products, potentially competing with Apple's
upcoming HomePad.

articles.title: Information architecture is the foundation ai is starving for
articles.description:
Poor information architecture, not weak models, drives AI
hallucinations and wrong answers, since retrieval only surfaces the
best-matched text, not the most accurate one. Unlike human users who
tolerate ambiguity, AI systems reproduce mislabeled or unstructured
content confidently and at scale, turning a once-invisible cost into
measurable failures and financial liability, as seen in the Air Canada
chatbot case. This cost is now trackable in retrieval accuracy and
hallucination rates, so organizations should audit and fix their
content structure before purchasing new AI models or tools.

articles.title: How figma uses 3 collaboration ux patterns to drive product adoption
articles.description:

patterns: real-time multiplayer editing, contextual on-design
comments, and effortless link sharing, now used by 95% of Fortune 500
companies. Each pattern lowers barriers for non-designers to
participate, letting files support up to 500 collaborators and turning
every shared link into a potential new user. These patterns succeed by
embedding teamwork directly into the product itself, creating network
effects as adoption spreads naturally through everyday collaboration
rather than top-down rollout.

articles.title: How to improve website performance: best practices for faster sites
articles.description:

search rankings, making performance optimization a priority for
growing sites. Seven tactics are recommended, including image
optimization, code minification, browser caching, reduced third-party
scripts, and stronger hosting. Common mistakes—like disabled
compression, excess metadata, and missing server cache—can undermine
these efforts if left unaddressed.

articles.title: On layout choreography
articles.description:
Layout choreography gives interface reflows a visible path, letting
users track where elements moved instead of experiencing a
disorienting jump. FLIP animates the transform property rather than
layout properties like top or height, since layout has already
occurred by the time the animation runs. Effective choreography
sequences movement by importance—the triggering element responds
first, then surrounding content adapts—while still requiring a
reduced-motion fallback that preserves content and clarity.

articles.title: Type designers have created a free font that "poisons" ai

content from AI scraping by displaying readable text to humans while
subtly altering the underlying source code that many AI crawlers
ingest, potentially contaminating training datasets. Unlike previous
anti-AI fonts, it works as a practical web font and includes a toolkit
that allows the same protection to be applied to other compatible
typefaces. Its creators describe it as a way to make unauthorized
content scraping more difficult without opposing AI itself, arguing
that publishing work online should not be treated as consent for AI
training.

articles.title: Mcp is going stateless: what the new spec means for ai agents
articles.description:
The Model Context Protocol releases a spec update that drops stateful
sessions in favor of stateless HTTP, meaning remote MCP servers no
longer require sticky sessions, shared session stores, or instance
coordination to function behind a load balancer. Each request now
carries its own context in a metadata object, so any server instance
can handle any request. The update also replaces MCP's proprietary
logging channel with OpenTelemetry and formally standardizes request
tracking using W3C Trace Context, letting teams correlate agent tool
calls with the rest of their application stack in a single
observability backend.

select specific tokens. A researcher created a blacklist of words,

routing, switching, and network troubleshooting, alongside its Cloud
Control agentic operations platform. Cloud Control will let
administrators diagnose issues across Cisco products through a single
interface, explain the potential impact of actions such as reboots,
and support on-prem deployments, with US availability planned by the
end of August.

articles.title: Thinks about ai agent sandboxes
articles.description:
Perplexity's SPACE platform separates short-lived Firecracker microVM
sandboxes from durable sessions that can be paused, resumed, moved, or
forked across clusters without losing an agent's work. The
architecture uses frequent snapshots, isolated credential handling,
and network controls to securely support long-running agents at a
scale of millions of sandbox creations and tens of millions of
reconnects.

articles.title: Control costs
articles.description:
Snowflake unveiled Cortex AI Gateway, a runtime control plane for
tracking agent actions, enforcing access policies, and monitoring
token usage and costs across models, tools, MCP servers, and
enterprise systems. Built using technology acquired from Natoma, the
service integrates with Snowflake's Horizon Catalog and is expected to
enter public preview soon. 

 ABNORMAL AI EXTENDS BEHAVIORAL SECURITY TO IDENTITIES, AI SYSTEMS,

articles.title: And insider threats
articles.description:
Abnormal AI launched three products that extend its behavioral
security platform into identity threat detection, AI governance, and
fraudulent applicant screening. The tools correlate email, identity,
SaaS, agent, and recruiting signals to flag compromised sessions,
risky AI activity, suspicious help-desk requests, and potentially
fabricated candidates before access is granted.

articles.title: Remediation
articles.description:
Reco expanded its AI Runtime platform with browser-based discovery of
unsanctioned AI usage, automated permission remediation, and planned
controls that analyze and block risky prompts, responses, and tool
calls in real time. Browser Guard is in early access, while broader
runtime enforcement across agents and MCP connections is expected to
become generally available in October. 

 US GOVERNMENT BANS NEW FOREIGN-MADE HUMANOIDS, ROBOT DOGS, AND SOLAR

articles.title: Inverters, citing risks to national security
articles.description:
The FCC banned imports of new foreign-made humanoid robots, robot
dogs, and power inverters over concerns that connected devices could
be remotely controlled, used for surveillance, or exploited in
cyberattacks. Existing installations are unaffected, and exceptions
may be granted for devices deemed safe.

articles.title: Your ai agents can reach data no one approved
articles.description:
A 1Password survey found that 71% of organizations' AI agents can
access sensitive data, while one-third of developers reported a
security incident tied to overprivileged non-human identities.

articles.title: Paper raises $34m to build the next great design platform
articles.description:
Paper raised $34M in Series A funding from Accel and ICONIQ, bringing
its total funding to $38.5M, to build a design platform for the
agentic era. Following its Paper Desktop launch, the company saw 25x
ARR growth in a month and now serves thousands of paying customers,
including Ramp, Lovable, and Harvey. Paper plans to use the funding to
expand its editor and agent infrastructure, positioning itself as
infrastructure for agents while continuing open-source projects like
Paper Shaders and Paper Mono. 

 IYO'S TRADEMARK LAWSUIT AGAINST OPENAI AND JONY IVE PAUSED OVER

articles.title: Settlement talks
articles.description:
OpenAI, Jony Ive's hardware venture, and iyO have reached a
settlement in principle in their trademark and trade secret dispute,
prompting the court to pause proceedings for seven days while the
agreement is finalized. If the settlement is completed by August 6,
the lawsuit will be dismissed. Otherwise, the parties must provide a
status update and continue with scheduled hearings. The agreement
could also resolve the ongoing dispute over OpenAI's use of the
“io” branding for its future AI hardware.

articles.title: As ai content floods the internet, pangram raises $9m to detect it
articles.description:
Pangram has raised $9 million to expand its AI detection tools as
AI-generated content spreads across the internet, academia, legal
work, and social platforms. The startup launched Pangram 4, which it
says is over 99% accurate at detecting AI-assisted and mixed human-AI
writing, along with a research-preview image detector that can
identify AI-generated visuals across different models. While the tools
are not perfect, Pangram is positioning itself as a way to preserve
human-made content and add transparency around when AI has been used.

articles.title: Ux-context design: using ux knowledge to inform ai-generated design
articles.description:
UX-context design reframes research and design deliverables as
curated, machine-readable context that guides AI tools rather than
documents meant for human interpretation. Google's DESIGN.md
exemplifies this shift for visual identity, while a hypothetical
broader file, UX.md, could similarly encode research findings,
interaction standards, glossaries, and user/world models for AI
consumption. Unlike traditional handoffs, this context lives alongside
the product, continuously updates, and is read by every AI tool
whenever anyone in an organization generates work.

articles.title: Thinking outside the box: digital design in the ai era
articles.description:
MacPaw explored moving beyond typical text-box AI interfaces, leading
to Eney, a proactive assistant designed as an expressive character
rather than a chatbot. Designers chose a circular pink figure with
minimal facial features, prioritizing warmth, approachability, and
restrained emotional expression over flashy or distracting UI. Despite
AI streamlining design work, human judgment, artistic intent, and
curiosity remain essential and increasingly valuable in the AI era.

articles.title: How design leaders influence decisions without being in the room
articles.description:
As AI-generated interfaces make visual quality easier to achieve,
designers can no longer rely on polished screens alone to communicate
the value of their work. A more effective approach is to annotate
presentations with three elements: the design decision, the hypothesis
behind it, and the outcome it produced, making the strategic thinking
explicit. This framework helps stakeholders understand not just what
changed, but why it mattered and how it impacted users or the
business.

articles.description:
Framer is a pro website builder trusted by companies like Miro and

without leaving the tool. Agents bring speed and scale; you bring the

articles.title: Designing fast and slow
articles.description:
Designers often favor deliberate, evidence-based decision-making,
while business partners tend to move quickly on instinct. This creates
a "chess versus poker" divide: designers treat decisions as costly and
hard to undo, while business leaders treat them as cheap, disposable
bets. The real question isn't whether to think fast or slow, but
whether a given decision is truly reversible and worth the cost of
caution. 

 DIGITAL TOOLS, HUMAN EXPRESSION: THE VISUAL IDENTITY BEHIND CONFIG

Figma's Brand Studio built Config 2026's visual identity around
evolution, fluidity, and harmony. The team used Figma Make to create
glyphs, dithering effects, and scribbly textures, then translated them
into physical installations, motion pieces, wayfinding signage, and
merchandise. Interactive elements like Shared Frequency, the Play
Canvas, and Collage Remixer let attendees personalize prints and
designs, extending the theme of imperfect, human-driven creativity
into tangible keepsakes and audio. 

 ACCEPT & PROCEED'S NEW SYSTEM FOR VANS IS A LESSON IN HOW TO INJECT

articles.title: Clarity into an iconic brand
articles.description:
Vans has introduced a refreshed brand system that unifies its
previously fragmented identity around the idea “Our Canvas. Your
Way,” celebrating the brand as a platform for personal expression.
Rather than redesigning iconic assets, Accept & Proceed clarified what
should remain consistent while creating a more flexible framework for
future teams, products, and communities. The update also refines the
brand's typography and guidelines, giving Vans a more cohesive
identity without losing the authenticity that made it culturally
significant.

articles.title: It)
articles.description:
Google, Amazon, and Walmart retain "dated," utilitarian designs
because simplicity reduces cognitive load, speeds load times, and
builds user trust.

articles.title: Landor designs human-centric trackside experiences for mclaren racing
articles.description:
Landor has designed a mobile, three-storey Team Hub and updated
Garage experience for the McLaren Mastercard Formula 1 Team, debuting
at the Barcelona Grand Prix.

articles.title: A bad logo could cost you your job
articles.description:
Cracker Barrel's controversial 2025 logo redesign sparked intense
cultural and political backlash, culminating in the restoration of its
original logo and the departure of CEO Julie Felss Masino.

articles.title: How gpt-5.6 fuses frontier intelligence with frontier efficiency
articles.description:
The GPT-5.6 model family has been designed to optimize both
performance and cost efficiency across various tasks, with load
balancing and caching techniques that allow the system to handle more
tokens effectively. GPT-5.6 Sol also helped optimize itself to improve
its code execution and resource allocation.

articles.title: How chatgpt optimizes its agent loop: harness, api, and inference
articles.description:
AI models like ChatGPT optimize their performance using various
layers, including a harness, API, and inference, to improve efficiency
and reduce costs. They use techniques like persistent WebSockets,
stable prompt prefixes, and parallel safety checks to minimize
repetitive work and improve the overall processing speed of tasks.

articles.title: Github is the wrong shape for this new world
articles.description:
The current software development landscape requires a reevaluation of
collaboration tools like GitHub, as traditional paradigms are being
overwhelmed by the velocity and scale of new contributions from
various teams. To address these challenges, the focus should shift to
developing high-throughput infrastructure primitives that improve
software delivery processes. 

 NEW RESEARCH: THE CORE WEB VITALS THRESHOLDS YOU TRUST MIGHT BE WRONG

articles.title: For your site
articles.description:
Google's 2.5s “good” LCP threshold comes from aggregated data
across millions of sites, so it tells you nothing about where your own
users actually start bouncing. Across ten major retailers, every
single one hit its best bounce rate somewhere between 100ms and 1
second, well before that line. Four of the ten had already flattened
out onto the performance plateau before reaching 2.5s, meaning they
were technically “good” for Google while having stopped gaining
anything from speed a while back.

articles.title: Ai's top startups are barely publishing their research
articles.description:
More than half of AI unicorns valued at over $1 billion have never
published a scientific paper or preprint. A small number of these
firms dominate academic citations, with OpenAI accounting for a
significant share of them, while others prioritize fast-paced,
informal disclosure methods over formal publications.

articles.title: Contagious interview malware in svg images: dprk campaign
articles.description:
DPRK-aligned actors are handing developers fully-functional “coding
challenge” repos, one seeded through Elastic's own community Slack
#jobs channel, with the payload split into Base64 chunks hidden in
HTML comments across SVG flag images. It is reassembled and executed
on every npm run dev or npm start. What lands is a four-module
OTTERCOOKIE stack: browser credential and crypto wallet theft, a
recursive sweep for .env files, SSH/AWS configs and shell histories, a
Socket.IO RAT with live shell access, and a clipboard stealer.

articles.title: How much can you delegate to agents?
articles.description:
To effectively delegate tasks to agents, it's necessary to assess the
ease of reviewing their work and the cost of undoing mistakes, which
helps determine the appropriate level of autonomy.

articles.title: The productivity mirage
articles.description:
A prolific engineer, known for his achievements at Facebook,
surprised a productivity enthusiast by using a simple code editor
without advanced tools, yet still demonstrated exceptional skills and
intuition that led to winning a hackathon.

articles.title: Some thoughts about anthropic's new cryptanalysis results
articles.description:
Anthropic's recent cryptanalysis results, which include a new key
recovery algorithm for the HAWK signature scheme and an improved
attack on reduced-round AES, show AI's expanding role in cryptography
and its potential impact on future standards and scientific discovery.

articles.title: Spacex looks to compete with the carriers
articles.description:
SpaceX has been hunting for a spectrum that works well in cities and
dense areas for its wireless network. It is considering buying
competitors to acquire the spectrum or competing at a government
auction set for next year. The company has expressed interest in
building its own terrestrial networks and has demonstrated a prototype
mobile handset to some investors. Entering into the mobile market is
capital intensive, so SpaceX could ultimately choose not to follow
through on these plans.

articles.title: July topped all of q2
articles.description:
OpenAI's annualized recurring revenue in July exceeded the company's
entire second quarter. The growth was driven by the release of the
company's GPT-5.6 series of models and ChatGPT Work, as well as
growing adoption of Codex. OpenAI is under pressure to justify its
$852 billion valuation as it prepares for its IPO. It has been racing
to bring in new users to generate the revenue needed to help support
its infrastructure spending plans.

articles.title: Doordash gets faa nod to run its own drone delivery program
articles.description:
DoorDash has received permission from the FAA to deliver packages by
drone at altitudes below 400 feet. The drones will be built in the
company's in-house robotics unit, DoorDash Labs. DoorDash Air aims to
cater to any merchant, anywhere. The company will release more
information later this year on its drones and how its drone program
will fit into DoorDash's broader ecosystem.

articles.title: China closes the satellite gap in space race with the us
articles.description:
China has accelerated its deployment of civilian and military
hardware into orbit. The country's growing constellations of
satellites could help it track events on Earth in real time and in
greater detail than ever before. This has raised concerns among US
officials, who see China's growing array of space-based capabilities
as a quest to displace the US as the pre-eminent space power. Western
analysts say that China is leading the world in research in sensors
and satellite positioning technologies.

articles.title: Datadog's resources for shipping observable ai apps
articles.description:
Ever feel like you're shipping AI in slow-motion? This Datadog kit
[12] includes an AI monitoring eBook, product briefs, and an on-demand
webinar on software delivery best practices. Download it to get up to
speed on delivering observable AI. Grab your Developer Toolkit for the
AI Era [12]

articles.title: How chatgpt optimizes its agent loop: harness, api, and inference
articles.description:
AI labs are moving faster than ever. However, capability is only half
of the picture. Optimizing the cost per successful task makes models
more affordable and less costly to serve. This article discusses
techniques adopted in frontier labs to make API applications more
efficient. It covers what happens when requests are sent to an AI
agent, how the harness layer cuts repeated work, and more.

articles.title: Treat prompt changes like code deploys
articles.description:
Prompts are dependencies. Changing them can shift downstream behavior
with no warning, no failing build, and no obvious signal in the
request pipeline. Treat prompts exactly like any other artifact that
can change production behavior. Test them, give them a gate, and
default that gate to blocking until proven otherwise.

articles.title: Why compute might get 10x+ more expensive in coming years
articles.description:
Labs do not want to spend greater and greater shares of compute on
inference. The point of inference revenue is to convince investors to
spend more money to buy more compute to train bigger models. Spending
too much on compute on inference signals that progress has stalled
because it's not worth investing more in training. Labs believe that
their models will continue to get better, so this only means that
compute will get more expensive.

articles.title: The rise of million-dollar companies with just one employee
articles.description:
A new class of entrepreneurs is launching and running new
million-dollar companies on their own. AI's ability to handle various
administrative tasks makes it useful for launching solo businesses in
many fields. The effect of one-person businesses on the labor market
remains to be seen. While many people are worried AI will limit
employment opportunities, these solo operators show how the technology
can also open new doors.

articles.title: Eval-driven development: lessons from evaluating genai at scale
articles.description:
Airbnb evaluates GenAI by reviewing 100 prototype outputs to find
real failure modes before creating automated evals. Its stack uses
programmatic checks, calibrated LLM judges with agreement in the high
80% range against human reviewers. Agentic systems are assessed across
tool calls, reasoning steps, and final outputs.

articles.title: Indexing the data lake for online point queries
articles.description:
Spotify built an external index mapping keys directly to file offsets
and row numbers in unmodified Parquet files, replacing distributed SQL
scan chains with parallel ranged reads for lookups across
petabyte-scale data lakes. Complementary write-time optimizations
(per-key page flushing, ZSTD frame resets, column interleaving,
covering index entries) reduce both bytes read and round trips
further, making the same files serve both batch analytics and
interactive queries. 

 PINNER PROGRESSION: BETTER USE-CASE REPRESENTATION DRIVING WEEKLY

articles.title: Active user growth at pinterest
articles.description:
Pinterest replaced single-user embeddings with per-user agglomerative
clusters over the last 500 engagements, with dynamic cluster count and
lifecycle metadata tracking recency and frequency. It feeds retrieval,
ranking, and blending layers, with lifecycle stages determining which
utility signals get weighted during ranking. The retention benefit is
nonlinear and accelerates sharply once users adopt enough distinct use
cases. 

 SCALING STREAMHUB: TRANSITIONING FROM KINESIS TO KAFKA FOR 145

articles.title: Billion daily events
articles.description:
Atlassian moved from Kinesis to Kafka on AWS MSK as traffic rose from
22 billion to 150 billion events a day. Tiered Storage cut costs, but
incidents exposed broker, S3, control-plane, and disk limits. Quotas,
sharding, spare capacity, backups, and failover were critical.

articles.title: The new wave of the streaming log technologies
articles.description:
New streaming platforms are dropping Kafka compatibility for
different bets: Iggy uses Rust with TCP, QUIC, and HTTP; S2 uses HTTP
and object storage for bottomless retention; and OpenData Log replaces
partitions with key-based routing. Whether they complement or replace
Kafka remains open.

articles.title: How langchain built an agent-first data stack
articles.description:
LangChain rebuilt its stack for agent-native analysis, migrating
fully off its previous BI tool in six weeks. Hex combines dbt
definitions, semantic models, trusted datasets, guides, and LangSmith
traces so agents generate reliable SQL while the data team controls
modeling and governance.

articles.title: Artifact
articles.description:
Composable canonicals encode domain knowledge in versioned models.
Source layers define transformations and ontology, while business
layers merge identities across systems. AI agents use stable concepts
and identity rules, not simply more tables.

articles.title: How mvcc and transactions work in rocksdb
articles.description:
RocksDB tags keys with increasing sequence numbers, so readers
snapshot a consistent view while writers append without blocking.
Pessimistic transactions lock on write - optimistic ones check
conflicts at commit using pre-hashed mutexes. TiDB and CockroachDB
skip native transactions and build their own layers.

articles.title: From python script hell to a modern data integration framework
articles.description:
Apache SeaTunnel is presented as an alternative to fleets of
hand-written ingestion scripts that duplicate connection handling,
retries, checkpoints, idempotency, concurrency, and observability. Its
Source-Transform-Sink model separates declarative pipeline definitions
from execution and centralizes connector/runtime behavior.

articles.title: The real ai risk is inside the labs
articles.description:
Frontier AI labs are more likely to cause the first serious AI
incident than open models, since closed systems are vulnerable to
insider leaks. Current open models also lack the domain depth to pose
immediate risk in fields like biology, and restricting access helps
malicious actors more than defenders.

articles.title: The 2026 guide to agent observability tools
articles.description:
Agent observability has moved from nice-to-have to a production
requirement: Monte Carlo cites 73% of enterprises refusing to ship
agents without monitoring and alerting, and 53% expecting major
redesigns after deployment. The guide separates tracing-first,
eval-first, gateway, and platform approaches, but highlights a
persistent blind spot: most tools observe the agent while missing
upstream data freshness, lineage, and quality failures.

articles.title: How to consolidate your database stack for production ai
articles.description:
CockroachDB argues for consolidating transactional data, ephemeral
state, and embeddings under serializable SQL, row-level TTL,
changefeeds, and distributed vector indexing.

articles.title: Wide column stores explained: cassandra, bigtable, and scylladb
articles.description:
A clear refresher on when wide-column stores fit firehose workloads
and predictable single-partition reads, and why they fail for ad hoc
SQL or joins.

articles.description:

articles.title: Introducing build mode
articles.description:
xAI launched Build Mode for SuperGrok Heavy subscribers, letting
users generate, edit, preview, and publish websites, apps, games, and
dashboards directly from chat. Projects require no setup and can be
shared through grok.me links or custom domains.

articles.title: Openai's agents hacked second account during model testing
articles.description:
Modal Labs says that one of its customers' assets was hacked when an
OpenAI agent broke into Hugging Face's systems earlier this month.
Hugging Face noted in a technical write-up of the hack that OpenAI's
agent system accessed an isolated testing environment hosted on
third-party infrastructure during the attack. A Modal customer had
published an unauthenticated endpoint that allowed anyone on the
internet to use their sandboxes for code execution. This was used by
the rogue agent. 

 PACING THE FRONTIER (WEBSITE) [10] 

 AI could help create a dramatically better future. The world's
leading AI companies believe they could be close to automating AI
research. There is a real risk that capability development rapidly
accelerates beyond researchers' ability to understand or control the
resulting systems. Over a thousand employees from frontier AI
companies have signed a statement requesting that the US government
support an international effort to develop the technical and
governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated
AI development.

articles.title: Kimi k3 architecture notes
articles.description:
Kimi K3's architecture is essentially a scaled-up production version
of the Kimi Linear model released last year. The model seems to be
trending toward better inference efficiency. It now has native
multimodal support. This post summarizes some of the major changes and
additions noted in the open-weight model release.

articles.title: The inference engine guide for k3 deployment
articles.description:
Kimi K3 is a 2.8-trillion-parameter multimodal MoE (16 of 896 experts
active per token) with a context window of up to 1M tokens. Its
architecture departs from a standard transformer in several ways. Each
changes what a serving engine has to do. This post looks at Kimi K3's
architecture and how vLLM serves it.

articles.title: The july 2026 incident
articles.description:
An autonomous AI agent driven by a combination of OpenAI models ran
an end-to-end intrusion against Hugging Face's platform over roughly
two and a half days. The models made thousands of small, automated
decisions, and executed at machine speed across short-lived sandboxed
environments. Command-and-control was staged on ordinary public web
services. The intrusion was likely, from the agent's point of view, an
attempt to cheat on an evaluation by stealing test solutions rather
than solving a challenge on its own.
