articles.title: Agents sdk, and code mode
articles.description:
camelAI recently moved its agent off of virtual machines and onto a
Cloudflare Durable Object. Its file system lives in SQLite and R2, and
it writes JavaScript instead of bash. The team moved off VMs because
giving every user an always-on machine with attached disk was too
expensive to scale. This post explains how the team completed the
migration. camelAI's codebase recently went open source.

articles.title: Managed gemini agents gain more controls
articles.description:
Google updated Gemini API Managed Agents with Gemini 3.6 Flash,
environment hooks for inspecting tool calls, budget controls,
scheduled triggers, model selection, and free-tier access.

articles.title: Discovering cryptographic weaknesses with claude
articles.description:
Researchers at Anthropic used Claude Mythos Preview to uncover
weaknesses in cryptographic algorithms, notably improving attacks on
the HAWK digital signature scheme and round-reduced AES. The AI model
efficiently identified flaws previously undetected by human experts,
showcasing its potential in cryptographic research. While these
findings don't impact current systems, they highlight AI's role in
enhancing security standards and stress-testing cryptographic designs.

articles.title: Mage
articles.description:
Mage is a lightweight, research-friendly multimodal model family. It
was built with a fixed 4B-parameter budget. The models are compact
enough to train, fine-tune, and deploy onto modest hardware while
remaining competitive with much larger open systems. Mage-VL is an
efficient codec-native streaming multimodal foundation model, and
Mage-Flow is an efficient native-resolution foundation model for image
generation and editing.

articles.title: The real ai risk is inside the labs
articles.description:
AI should not be considered safe. The danger is that there are just a
few CEOs around the world, without the required background and
legitimacy, making hard choices for humanity at large. They weren't
selected to do so, it was just chance that created this setup. They
have GPUs and money, but given the stakes, they shouldn't be speaking
for everybody.

articles.title: The ai future is for everyone
articles.description:
Widely distributed personal superintelligence could shift AI from
automation toward invention, entrepreneurship, and individual agency.
Concentrating advanced intelligence in a few institutions risks
economic and political imbalance, while broad access, open systems,
and targeted safeguards create stronger checks and balances.

articles.title: The ai future is for everyone
articles.description:
As AI continues to improve, the question isn't whether
superintelligence will exist, but who will have access to it. The
technology could be centralized and restricted to a few institutions,
or it could be used to empower everyone. The notion that AI is such a
threat that the only safe path is an extreme concentration of power
seems dangerous. Historically, hoping that an absolute power will
benevolently provide for humanity if sufficiently enlightened hasn't
led to safe or positive outcomes.

articles.title: You don't need another ai notetaker
articles.description:
Annoying meeting bots? Sloppy summaries? No thanks. With Granola's AI
notepad, you jot down what matters, and AI makes your notes awesomely
useful. Use code TLDR1MO for one free month [22].

articles.description:
Fish Audio has launched S2.1 Pro, a real-time conversational speech
model supporting 83 languages.

articles.title: Moonshot openly defies the trump administration
articles.description:
Moonshot is seeking access to additional Nvidia GPUs to train its
next model.

articles.title: Amazon reportedly plans to consolidate nova ai models
articles.description:
Amazon plans to shift from having a wide portfolio of models for
text, images, video, and multimodal tasks toward having a single
frontier model.

articles.title: And a new in-house model
articles.description:
Microsoft's Project Perception is an AI cybersecurity system that
coordinates red, blue, and green team agents to defend against
AI-driven attacks. Entering public preview August 3, it is based on
Microsoft's new MAI-Cyber-1-Flash model used with OpenAI's GPT-5.4 for
the hardest tasks. Microsoft says the combination scores 96% on
CyberGym and is initially available only to MDASH customers.

articles.title: Mcp gets its biggest architectural update yet
articles.description:
The Model Context Protocol's July 28 revision introduces major
architectural changes aimed at supporting large-scale enterprise agent
deployments. The update moves MCP beyond its earlier stateful design,
but could require existing implementations to adapt.

articles.title: Snowflake launches cortex ai gateway for enterprise agents
articles.description:
Snowflake's Cortex AI Gateway gives organizations centralized control
over how agents access models. The product is designed to improve
governance and prevent uncontrolled usage from creating unexpectedly
high AI costs.

articles.title: From zero trust to zero custody
articles.description:
Zero Trust is insufficient for AI agents because verifying identity
does not stop attackers from hijacking behavior through malicious
language in context. Zero Custody holds that the reasoning loop should
hold nothing that matters, so a compromised agent has empty hands.
Secrets and raw values should stay with external brokers or gateways
that inject or re-identify them only after policy checks.

articles.title: Enterprise ai has a context trust problem
articles.description:
A survey of 101 enterprises found that companies are building
infrastructure to supply agents with business context faster than they
can ensure that context is trustworthy. The next enterprise AI
bottleneck may be data lineage, permissions, and accuracy rather than
retrieval performance.

articles.title: Why sap says enterprise agents need knowledge graphs
articles.description:
SAP argues that enterprise agents need governed knowledge graphs
rather than simple access to disconnected documents and applications.
Reliable agents require shared business context, relationships, and
permissions that can be consistently applied across workflows. 

🤝

articles.title: We're open sourcing our privacy proxy cli
articles.description:
Cloudflare is open sourcing pvcli (privacy-client), a CLI for
debugging privacy-preserving protocols such as Oblivious HTTP, under
the Apache-2.0 License. The tool automates binary HTTP encoding,
encryption, and multi-party relay/gateway flows that previously
required manual bit-level work and one-off custom clients. It logs
each protocol step so developers can isolate failures across relays,
gateways, and origins.

articles.title: Dell powerstore adds support for nutanix cloud platform
articles.description:
Dell PowerStore can now serve as external storage for Nutanix Cloud
Infrastructure 7.6, with deployment and lifecycle management
integrated through Dell Private Cloud and Nutanix Prism. The
integration gives customers another path away from legacy
virtualization stacks while allowing compute and storage to scale
independently.

articles.title: Microsoft previews a multi-model ai security stack
articles.description:
Microsoft's Project Perception combines specialized and frontier
models with shared security context and agents that can act across its
security products. Microsoft says the architecture can improve
reasoning consistency while cutting costs by nearly 50%. The public
preview begins on August 3.

articles.title: Ai-powered phishing-as-a-service
articles.description:
Security researchers uncovered two AI-built Phishing-as-a-Service
kits, TokenLover and YaksaLover, that automate business email
compromise against Microsoft 365. Marketed like legitimate SaaS
products with operator dashboards, they industrialize documented
techniques such as device code phishing and Windows Hello persistence.
One kit uses AI to map payment flows from harvested mailboxes, and
both can keep access after password resets.

articles.title: Kioxia launches its first liquid-cooled pcie gen 5 ssd
articles.description:
Kioxia's new NX1 SSD is designed for GPU servers and hyperscale data
centers where storage performance and heat management are becoming
more important. The E1.S drive supports capacities up to 15.36 TB and
offers improved write performance over the company's previous
generation.

articles.title: How observability transforms vibe coding into ai engineering
articles.description:
AI-generated code often omits production essentials such as error
handling, rate limiting, and instrumentation, and observability skills
let agents verify work against runtime behavior to feed observations
back into the next plan.

articles.title: Meta says storage is becoming a bottleneck for ai infrastructure
articles.description:
Meta argues that faster metadata pipelines, ingestion systems, and
GPU-adjacent flash can reduce expensive idle time in AI clusters.

articles.title: Template
articles.description:
Filipino artist Elmer Saflor sued Memes Apps, alleging its AI meme
generator sells subscriptions that reproduce his viral "Running Away
Balloon" comic as an ad template without permission. Legal expert Eric
Goldman notes precedent favors Saflor, since prior rulings suggest
meme use in ads isn't fair use, though proving harm and targeting the
generator rather than advertisers could complicate the case. Saflor
seeks a court order halting the template's use and an accounting of ad
profits, framing the suit as a broader push to protect creators'
rights as AI platforms scale.

articles.title: Standard' for ai licensing
articles.description:
A group of Hollywood actors and producers, including George Clooney,
Tom Hanks, and Meryl Streep, are backing a new "Human Consent
Standard" letting people set terms for how AI systems use their
likeness and creative work. Overseen by the nonprofit RSL Media, the
standard builds on last year's Really Simple Licensing Standard and
lets AI systems check permissions via robots.txt and a registry
launching in June. Unlike RSL, which applies to content at specific
URLs, the new standard covers a person's identity, character, or work
wherever it appears online.

articles.description:
Meta is moving Meta AI into Threads DMs after feedback showed that
many users were uncomfortable interacting with AI publicly in their
feeds. Users can privately ask questions about posts, conversations,
and other topics, with options to delete chats or mute the AI account.
Meta is still testing public Meta AI interactions in the Threads feed
in a limited number of countries while it gathers more feedback.

articles.title: I handed a ux review over to ai. here's what happened
articles.description:
A UX practitioner tested Claude Fable 5 and ChatGPT-5.6 Sol against
manual analysis on a real portal review, feeding both models the same
brief, research, and analytics data. Both AI models generated reviews
filled with irrelevant or invented issues, though Claude proved
somewhat more accurate and produced a single coherent document. The
author concluded AI works best as a partner grounded in expert-defined
heuristics rather than a replacement, and plans to build a custom
"agent skill" encoding personal UX judgment for future projects.

articles.title: How figma stays ahead of vulnerabilities with agents
articles.description:
Figma's security team built agentic systems that guard code
generation, review pull requests, and audit its decade-old monorepo,
all governed by one shared policy. Prioritizing precision over recall
proved essential, since historical bugs only measure recall while
trust requires developers see mostly valid findings—the team hit 70%
precision before enabling PR comments, later reaching 80%. The
resulting policy became a de facto threat model, powering hooks that
steer secure code generation, adjudication passes that boost recall,
and feedback loops that continuously refine detection from bug bounty
reports and false-positive dismissals.

articles.title: A concrete definition of “product sense” (and how to build it)
articles.description:
As AI takes over more execution work, product sense—the ability to
decide what to build—is becoming increasingly valuable, but it
requires more than consuming product critiques, research, and industry
knowledge. Strong product sense develops by repeatedly completing the
full product cycle: understanding problems, making decisions,
implementing solutions, measuring outcomes, and reflecting on whether
experience-based patterns actually applied. Building reliable
intuition therefore requires staying close enough to your work to see
its consequences, while recognizing when unfamiliar or misleading
situations demand evidence rather than instinct.

articles.title: Accessibility is resistance!
articles.description:
A blind author explains why they rely heavily on AI tools, using an
inaccessible EAA document and image-poor product pages as examples.
Screen readers, ChatGPT/Claude, Meta Ray-Bans, and apps like Oorion
help them navigate text, describe images, and locate objects
independently. They distinguish "AI as augmentation" from "AI as
compensation," arguing better human-built accessibility would reduce
reliance on AI, and urge readers to prioritize accessibility as a form
of resistance.

articles.title: Playful retail is serious design work
articles.description:
Interactive retail spaces that feel spontaneous, like the Coach Charm
Playground at Selfridges, actually require immense hidden planning and
discipline to execute safely and smoothly, according to Studio XAG.
The project involved navigating regulations, testing over 150 sample
sets, and executing overnight installs with precision compared to a
Formula One pit stop. Key lessons highlighted include protecting the
core idea through production, learning from workshop fabricators, and
prioritizing real human behavior over portfolio aesthetics.

articles.title: Could be even better
articles.description:
LinkedIn's "Open to Work" badge, active for six years, resurfaced as
a debate topic after an engineer's viral X post called it a negative
signal to recruiters.

articles.description:

articles.title: Inside zig's incremental compilation
articles.description:
The implementation of incremental compilation in the Zig compiler
allows for fast rebuilding by detecting changes in individual
functions and declarations. This feature has evolved from a
proof-of-concept to a reliable tool that speeds up development
workflows, with rebuilds taking only milliseconds after the initial
build. The process involves a detailed pipeline, including file
processing, semantic analysis, code generation, and linking.

articles.title: Discovering cryptographic weaknesses with claude
You don't have to be smart if you can think clearly
articles.description:
Effective problem-solving in engineering requires the ability to
think clearly and methodically, especially when faced with challenges
that cannot be solved intuitively. Smart engineers often struggle when
they encounter such problems, whereas strong engineers are able to
systematically evaluate and address issues.

articles.title: The real ai risk is inside the labs
articles.description:
The primary AI risks are found within the confines of advanced AI
labs, where severe incidents can arise due to human error or
mismanagement during model testing, rather than from the public
release of open models. There is an urgent need for a collaborative
international approach to AI safety, as individual companies are
insufficiently equipped to evaluate the potential dangers posed by
powerful AI systems.

articles.title: Vs the frontier
articles.description:
Companies that adopt AI-first strategies see variations in
performance, with top AI spenders doubling their revenue compared to
minimal gains for those with no AI investment. Successful AI
implementation hinges on redesigning workflows, incentivizing
experimentation, providing business context, measuring impact, and
setting clear goals within AI budgets. AI budgets are best managed
through fine-tuning open-source models with reinforcement learning.

articles.title: How to research technical topics with ai
articles.description:
The process of researching technical topics using AI involves first
narrowing down a broad question to create a more focused inquiry,
which helps in understanding key concepts and their interdependencies.
AI can assist in locating and analyzing relevant sources, but it's
needed to independently verify claims and maintain a distinction
between personal explanations and original sources. The final stage of
research is reconstructing the information without AI assistance.

articles.title: Google
articles.description:
Numerous private Claude chats and interactive documents were
unintentionally made publicly searchable on Google due to a flaw in
the sharing feature, exposing sensitive information such as health
records and personal details before being fixed.

articles.title: How building software is changing at anthropic
articles.description:
Anthropic is transforming software engineering practices through AI
tooling, resulting in more fluid prototyping, lots of use of AI for
code reviews and testing, the prevalence of two-pizza teams, and a
shift in project implementation dynamics.

articles.title: Kimi k3 architecture notes
articles.description:
The Kimi K3 architecture is a larger and more efficient open-weight
model that introduces elements like LatentMoE and attention residuals
while eliminating RoPE layers in favor of NoPE.

articles.title: Half-life ported to mac os 9
articles.description:
Half-Life has been successfully ported to PowerPC-based Macintosh
computers running Mac OS 9, 28 years after its original release,
allowing players to experience the game along with additional content
like Blue Shift and Opposing Force.

articles.title: Terraform introduces workspaces and stacks restore, and more
articles.description:
HashiCorp highlights new HCP Terraform and Terraform Enterprise
features that improve infrastructure resilience, governance, and
scalability, including workspace recovery, monorepo support for
Stacks, guided migrations, registry tagging, and granular policy
override permissions.

articles.title: Cncf announces schedule for debut observability summit europe
articles.description:
The Cloud Native Computing Foundation has announced the schedule for
Observability Summit Europe 2026, taking place in Prague on October 5.
The event features more than 25 technical sessions covering topics
including automated synthetic monitoring, Observability as Code, and
AI-powered workflows. General registration is open now at 150 euros,
with academic tickets at 85 euros. Applications for the Dan Kohn
scholarship, which provides complimentary registration for community
members from underrepresented groups, are open through August 23.

articles.title: For your stack
articles.description:
Datadog explains why Single Step Instrumentation is the preferred
method for enabling distributed tracing by simplifying deployment,
while outlining when manual or custom instrumentation is needed for
unsupported environments or deeper application visibility.

articles.title: Federating clusters for zero-downtime kubernetes
What even are microservices?
articles.description:
Microservices primarily create organizational boundaries that let
teams own components and release them independently, rather than
serving as a universal technical upgrade over monoliths. That autonomy
comes with distributed-systems complexity, duplicated infrastructure,
harder debugging, and increased coordination costs, so the
architecture is most valuable when organizational scale justifies
those tradeoffs. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: To know
articles.description:
Grafana Cloud now provides a unified Allowlist API with a structured,
region-aware JSON format that replaces legacy per-product IP

articles.title: Observability for aws finops data with oracle log analytics
articles.description:
Oracle outlines an AWS to OCI FinOps workflow that curates
standardized daily FOCUS cost data, stores it in OCI Object Storage,
and ingests it into Oracle Log Analytics to enable reliable cloud cost
analysis and monitoring.

articles.title: Inside zig's incremental compilation
articles.description:
Zig's compiler tracks source hashes and declaration-level dependency
graphs so it can reanalyze and regenerate only the functions affected
by a code change. A tightly integrated incremental linker then patches
the updated machine code directly into the existing binary, enabling
rebuilds of complex applications in roughly 50–70 milliseconds after
an initial build.

articles.title: Harness and kong expand strategic partnership
articles.description:
Harness and Kong expanded their partnership to secure AI-driven
architectures by integrating Harness AI Security with Kong AI Gateway,
enabling enterprises to discover, monitor, and protect AI assets,
agents, LLM services, and MCP workflows with real-time threat
detection and visibility.

articles.title: Enforce access token expiry policies in pulumi cloud
articles.description:
Pulumi Cloud now lets organization admins set a maximum expiry cap,
in days, on the access tokens used against their organization.

articles.title: Algorithms
articles.description:
Claude Mythos Preview found flaws in a watered-down version of an
algorithm for Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), a ubiquitous
protocol that protects web traffic, wireless networks, data storage,
and many other technologies. Anthropic claims the assault was 200 to
1,000 times faster than what previous human research had managed to
do. The attack was devised almost entirely autonomously - the model
needed aid as it originally believed the problem was impossible.
Claude Mythos Preview worked on the problem for about a week before
engineering its attack, and two human researchers worked for nearly a
month to verify that the method appeared correct.

articles.title: Apple set to make big smart home push with siri ai at center
articles.description:
Apple is preparing a new push into the smart home category with a
wave of home products. It will start with a hub device built around
the new Siri AI assistant. Apple is also preparing to release a new TV
set-top box and a refreshed HomePod mini. All three devices are nearly
ready to launch. Apple is also working on a higher-end, robotic
version of the home hub and an advanced in-home security camera.

articles.title: Why haven't organoids solved all of drug discovery?
articles.description:
Organoids are clumps of human cells that show some type of
organ-specific function. In theory, they seem like a good tool for
drug discovery, but the reality is that the technology is still not
reliable enough. There are many people working to fix the issues with
organoids, but they are still methods in progress. Organoids have not
dramatically altered medicine yet, but they have already been used for
some unarguably useful things.

articles.title: Tau's humanoid cleaning service
articles.description:
Tau's humanoid service is now available in San Francisco. Access is
initially invite-only. The service costs $30 per hour. Each humanoid
will be jointly controlled by a human operator and AI. Video of the
robot in action is available in the article.

articles.title: The orchestrator's tax
articles.description:
Every token in the orchestrator's context is competing for its
attention. The real value of a subagent is what it keeps out of that
context. Subagents should be treated as a tool for protecting the
orchestrator's working memory, offloading reasoning it doesn't need to
hold onto. Doing this well means giving the orchestrator explicit
ground rules for when and how to delegate.

articles.title: Mcp 2026-07-28 is live
articles.description:
MCP 2026-07-28 is the largest update to the protocol since launch. It
is now easier to deploy and scale remote servers. MCP is now
stateless, so it can be deployed on serverless and edge
infrastructure, or scaled horizontally behind any load balancer. There
is now a formal path to extend the protocol.

articles.title: The ai future is for everyone
articles.description:
As AI continues to improve, the question isn't whether
superintelligence will exist, but who will have access to it. The
technology could be centralized and restricted to a few institutions,
or it could be used to empower everyone. The notion that AI is such a
threat that the only safe path is an extreme concentration of power
seems dangerous. Historically, hoping that an absolute power will

articles.title: A backlash against anthropic is brewing in silicon valley
articles.description:
Anthropic has drawn criticism after releasing tools on the market
that compete with those offered by partner companies. For example,
Claude Design directly competes with offerings from partner design
company Figma. Anthropic's data retention policies have also been
criticized, but the company has pledged it won't use conversation data
from Fable and Mythos - but not other models - to train new models.
Researchers are calling for more transparency in AI systems.

articles.title: Anthropic rejected blanket bans on open-weight models
articles.description:
Anthropic said it had not advocated banning open-weight models and
argued that less capable releases were a public good. It instead
supported tighter chip controls, action against industrial-scale
distillation, and mandatory safety testing for sufficiently capable
open and closed models.

articles.title: Releasing the model weights and technical report of kimi k3
articles.description:
Moonshot has released the model weights for Kimi K3, along with a
technical report. Kimi K3 is a 2.8T Mixture-of-Experts model with
native visual understanding. It has a 1-million-token context window
and a new model architecture that gives it 2.5x the intelligence per
unit of compute. Alongside Kimi K3, Moonshot is opening up more of the
stack behind it — high-performance attention kernels, a MoE
communication library, and infrastructure for running agent
environments at scale.

articles.title: Microsoft introduced a cybersecurity model
articles.description:
Microsoft has launched MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, a specialized model for
finding difficult vulnerabilities in large codebases. It powers MDASH,
a new platform designed to identify and remediate software security
flaws.

articles.title: Openai's report on how ai is expanding
articles.description:
OpenAI found that workers increasingly used ChatGPT for tasks
traditionally associated with other occupations. Its analysis of
800,000 US user messages identified this “task crossover” in a
high percentage of occupation-specific conversations. 

 DEEPSECBENCH: EVALUATING MODEL PERFORMANCE IN FINDING CYBERSECURITY

articles.title: Vulnerabilities
articles.description:
DeepsecBench is a benchmark that evaluates how well different models
find cybersecurity vulnerabilities in application code. The report
includes recall, precision, cost, and total time for each model and
combines recall and precision into a single benchmark score.
DeepsecBench runs on an open-source codebase at a commit state just
before a large number of vulnerabilities were fixed. The construction
of the benchmark is secret so models aren't able to train against it.

articles.title: 22580: from gpt2 to kimi3, explained
articles.description:
KimiK3's gains come from more than scaling: it combines
constant-state Kimi Delta Attention, periodic softmax retrieval,
sparse experts, and selective residual access. Each architectural step
improves how fixed-capacity memory stores, forgets, and retrieves
information while preserving efficient inference. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: Portal
articles.description:
Ramp Labs has open-sourced PorTAL, a framework for shared task
representations and cross-model LoRA adaptation. PorTAL learns a
base-agnostic task latent and a light per-base alignment that
generates ordinary per-layer LoRA weights. A task can be trained once,
adapted to supported frozen base models, and exported as a standard
Hugging Face PEFT adapter.

articles.title: Gemini distillation service
articles.description:
The Gemini Distillation Service allows users to train a smaller, more
efficient 'student' model that uses the outputs and reasoning patterns
of a larger, more capable 'teacher' model. Distillation enables
production-grade efficiency while allowing smaller models to achieve a
deeper level of reasoning. It is recommended for high-volume,
latency-sensitive applications, complex reasoning tasks, and when
there are significant performance gaps between the teacher and student
models. The distillation service currently only supports
gemini-3.1-pro as the teacher model and gemini-2.5-flash as the
student model.

articles.title: How we built and benchmarked vr-1, our frontier cyber reasoning model
articles.description:
Cogent VR-1 can autonomously investigate environments, test
hypotheses, cross system boundaries, and execute attack chains.
IntrusionBench is a benchmark for measuring whether cyber agents can
complete realistic enterprise attack chains from limited starting
access. On the black-box configuration of IntrusionBench, VR-1
achieved more than a 2x lift in pass@3 over the strongest frontier
baseline. VR-1 and IntrusionBench are both at an early preview stage,
so the results are preliminary. 

 MOLT AGENTIC REINFORCEMENT LEARNING FRAMEWORK (GITHUB REPO) [14] 

 Molt is a PyTorch-native framework that treats the agent itself as
the program and supports custom Python rewards, tool use, multimodal
environments, and LLM judges. Its compact stack combines Ray, vLLM,
NVIDIA AutoModel, and FSDP2 to scale training to trillion-parameter
mixture-of-experts models.

articles.title: Security
articles.description:
The Open Secure AI Alliance, featuring leaders like NVIDIA and
Microsoft, aims to enhance AI safety by using open source technologies
to address vulnerabilities. This initiative provides defenders with
open defensive tools, enhancing transparency and adaptability while
avoiding reliance on closed systems. The alliance encourages
policymakers to view open models and tools as assets in AI and
cybersecurity strategy, promoting resilience and shared security in
the AI era.
articles.section: INDUSTRY LEADERS UNITE IN OPEN SECURE AI ALLIANCE FOR AI SAFETY AND

articles.title: How much can you delegate to agents?
articles.description:
Agent autonomy depends on task complexity, not just model quality.
Tasks fall into four levels: assistant, human-in-the-loop, agent
delegation, and self-driving, determined by ease of checking and
potential consequences of errors. Implementing guardrails, custom
skills, and domain-specific models enhances agent autonomy and
efficiency.
articles.section: INDUSTRY LEADERS UNITE IN OPEN SECURE AI ALLIANCE FOR AI SAFETY AND

articles.title: What are looped transformers? explained clearly
articles.description:
Looped transformers reuse the same core layers across multiple
passes, trading fewer stored parameters for additional sequential
compute. 

 LLADA2.X (GITHUB REPO) [18] 

 LLaDA2 diffusion language models for text generation and agent
workflows.

articles.title: Safe superintelligence partnered with nvidia
articles.description:
Safe Superintelligence announced a long-term partnership with Nvidia
that includes an undisclosed investment and access to the Vera Rubin
GPU platform.

articles.title: Rethinking security for the age of ai
articles.description:
Microsoft's Project Perception is an agentic security system that
coordinates red-team agents to identify attack paths, blue-team agents
to investigate risks, and green-team agents to take corrective action
across identities, endpoints, applications, data, clouds, and AI
systems. The multi-model platform is designed to continuously detect,
prioritize, and respond to threats while keeping security teams in
control. It enters public preview on August 3.

articles.title: Tech sector pours $1t into ai and sends customers the bill
articles.description:
Technology companies are spending roughly $1 trillion on
infrastructure this year, helping push global IT spending toward $6.37
trillion and raising prices for hardware, cloud services, and
enterprise software. CIOs are pushing back as vendors bundle AI into
products and shift more of the infrastructure cost onto customers
through higher subscriptions and usage-based pricing.

articles.title: Cloudmaxxing sucks nvidia into dangerous game
articles.description:
Nvidia is reportedly considering guaranteeing up to $250 billion in
financing for a 10-gigawatt data center involving SoftBank's SB Energy
and potentially OpenAI, while separately financing as much as $350
billion in GPUs. The arrangement shows how the AI infrastructure boom
is expanding beyond chips and cloud capacity into enormous credit
guarantees that could leave technology suppliers exposed if demand or
returns fall short.

articles.title: Reality-based network operations
articles.description:
Network operations in hyperscale cloud environments differ
fundamentally from traditional multi-vendor management. Device
inconsistency and CLI-driven workflows have long hindered programmatic
APIs, while SDN abstractions built on uniform virtual switches enable
simpler, more consistent control in cloud environments.

articles.title: Where should your company's ai brain live?
articles.description:
As companies embed institutional knowledge, workflows, and
decision-making into AI systems, they may be creating deep vendor
lock-in before consciously choosing where that infrastructure should
live. This article compares model providers, incumbent SaaS platforms,
closed startups, and open-source options, arguing that companies
should retain control over AI processes central to their competitive
advantage while using simpler managed tools for more generic work. 

🤝

articles.title: Forrester wave report
articles.description:
Forrester ranks products on both strategy and features, and Atlassian
was named a leader for Q4 2025. Read the report [9] to see the
exceptional service experiences Atlassian delivers to over 65,000
development, IT, and business teams. Get your free copy [9]

articles.title: Github copilot app
articles.description:
The GitHub Copilot app is a desktop experience for agent-driven
development built natively on GitHub, available for macOS, Windows,
and Linux on any Copilot plan or with a bring-your-own key. Users can
inspect diffs, preview via an in-app browser, run terminal checks, and
merge pull requests inside a session.

articles.title: Cloud agent
articles.description:
GitHub expanded its enterprise controls so administrators can apply
the same centrally managed Copilot policies across its desktop app,
cloud agent, CLI, and VS Code. Organizations can restrict plugins and
marketplaces, prevent users from bypassing approval prompts, and
distribute the configuration through GitHub, MDM, or managed files.
articles.section: ENTERPRISE MANAGED SETTINGS IN THE GITHUB COPILOT APP AND COPILOT

articles.title: Coordinating the work
articles.description:
Data integration moves and reshapes data between systems, while
workflow orchestration decides what runs, in what order, and how to
recover from failures. Enterprises confuse the two because both offer
connectors, though those connectors serve different jobs. Data
orchestration and workflow automation serve different purposes, but
organizations are increasingly bringing them together under a single
control plane to manage workflows across domains.

articles.title: Building the enterprise environment for agentic ai
articles.description:
Intel's experiments with agentic AI workloads suggest enterprises
need to evaluate the entire system rather than focusing only on model
and inference performance. The article recommends measuring task
success, cost per task, end-to-end latency, and agent density per
vCPU, while using scale-out infrastructure to balance performance,
capacity, and cost.

articles.title: Six agent harness capabilities for higher model performance
articles.description:
NVIDIA Labs has released Object-Oriented Agents (NOOA), an
open-source research preview that treats AI agents as Python classes
whose methods, state, and prompts form a typed harness.

articles.title: Generally available, pre-configure admin settings in advance
articles.description:
Google Meet will soon add screenshots of presented slides, charts,
and diagrams to AI-generated meeting notes.

articles.title: Midjourney acquired the astrology app co-star
articles.description:
Midjourney, an AI lab known for its image and video generators, has
acquired social astrology app Co-Star, with deal terms undisclosed.
Co-Star, which has roughly 4.3 million monthly active users, helps
people generate and share astrological birth charts and uses both AI
and humans for horoscopes and compatibility readings. Co-Star's two
dozen employees have joined Midjourney, whose growing consumer lineup
already includes medical and spa ventures alongside its Discord-based
image tools. 

 APPLE'S SMARTWATCHES WILL LOOK THE SAME FOR AT LEAST ANOTHER YEAR, OR

articles.title: Two
articles.description:
Apple is reportedly preparing the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4
for this fall, but neither is expected to receive a significant design
overhaul. The biggest improvements will instead focus on a
long-awaited chip upgrade and more advanced health and fitness
tracking, while major features like blood-sugar detection remain years
away. Apple Watch has settled into a conservative cycle of incremental
refinement, even as Apple takes bigger design and technology risks
with products like smart glasses and camera-equipped AirPods. 

 BLACK FOREST LABS LAUNCHES FLUX 3 CAPABLE OF GENERATING IMAGES AND

articles.title: 20-second video with audio
articles.description:
Black Forest Labs unveiled FLUX 3, its first public video generation
model. Early access requires approval, and the company has not yet
disclosed pricing, service-level commitments, or full benchmark
methodology. The video tier generates up to 20-second clips with
native audio and multi-shot continuity. A related model, FLUX-mimic,
extends the same architecture toward robotic manipulation tasks.

articles.title: Minimalism is dead. welcome to the afterparty
articles.description:
Design's decade-long minimalist era is ending, giving way to a new
phase that reintroduces depth, texture, and personality. Minimalism
served as a necessary discipline that taught designers structure and
hierarchy, but by the late 2010s it had curdled into sterile,
forgettable sameness exemplified by trends like Corporate Memphis.
Emerging styles such as neumorphism, referential skeuomorphism, and
brutalist web design now build whimsy and emotional richness on top of
that structural foundation rather than rejecting it. 

 THE ARCHITECTURE OF GUILT: HOW DUOLINGO WEAPONIZED NEGATIVE EMOTION

articles.title: To build a design system
articles.description:
Duolingo drives retention by using loss aversion, streaks, guilt, and
an emotionally responsive mascot to make maintaining progress feel
more compelling than earning traditional rewards like points or
badges. Its system also anticipates inevitable failure with mechanisms
like Streak Freeze, helping users recover without abandoning the habit
entirely. These techniques demonstrate the power of behavioral design
while raising an important ethical boundary: persuasion supports goals
users genuinely value, while coercion manufactures anxiety primarily
to improve engagement metrics.

articles.title: Your website is boring (but that might just set it free)
articles.description:
Years of optimizing websites for conversion, accessibility, SEO, and
templates have made the web increasingly homogeneous. AI agents now
threaten to reduce brands even further into interchangeable,
machine-readable commodities. The future could instead become a
bifurcated web: a “Silent Web” of structured data optimized for
machines alongside an “Experiential Web” designed around
distinctive, memorable, human-centered brand experiences. AI can help
enable that shift when treated as a creative partner for storytelling
and interaction rather than simply another tool for automation and
efficiency.

articles.title: A side project is the fastest way to upskill in the age of ai
articles.description:
Side projects have become the fastest route to upskilling in the AI
era, now that cost, coding, and time barriers have largely
disappeared. Rather than relying on no-code tools like Lovable,
working closer to "the metal" with Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor is
recommended, learning through iterative back-and-forth instead of full
automation. One app, Pegs Out, built in two weeks, serves as a
concrete example of how accessible this process now is.

articles.title: The six laws of psychology for good ux design
articles.description:
Six cognitive-psychology principles—covering decision time, target
size, familiar patterns, contrast, memorable endings, and visual
polish—shape whether users complete tasks smoothly. Applying laws
like Hick's, Fitts', Jakob's, the Von Restorff effect, the Peak-End
rule, and the Aesthetic-Usability effect reduces support tickets,
speeds task completion, and boosts conversions. Designers should map
interfaces against each law, test early with prototypes, and re-test
after changes to confirm improvements.

articles.title: Tv series logo fonts: the typography behind 30 iconic shows
articles.description:
Design references keep circling back to the same 30 TV logos. 

 THE CREATIVITY TAX: WHY THE BOLDEST IDEAS RARELY MAKE IT OUT OF THE

articles.description:
Bold ideas often get filtered out of creative studios, not from lack
of imagination, but because speaking up feels risky unless status
protects the speaker.

articles.title: Honor's new logo is all about pushing past perfection
articles.description:
Honor has unveiled a bold new logo and “Dare to Be” tagline,
reflecting its push to challenge convention and become a more
distinctive force in tech.

articles.title: We stopped using rsc on tanstack.com
articles.description:
TanStack.com initially benefited from using React Server Components
(RSC) by reducing the amount of JavaScript sent to the client, which
improved site performance. However, it opted to replace RSC with
simpler server-side rendering (SSR) that maintained site speed without
the complexity of RSC. While RSC solved initial dependency issues, its
architectural overhead was no longer justified once the underlying
content renderer was optimized.

articles.title: Git rebase -i is not that scary
articles.description:
The fear surrounding the use of the git rebase -i command is often
misplaced, as it just opens a text file for editing with
straightforward instructions, allowing developers to manage commits
more effectively. Since it has built-in safety nets to recover from
mistakes, it's helpful to use this tool to improve one's workflow and
branch history management.

articles.title: Upgrading checkout blocks app to polaris web components
articles.description:
Shopify has upgraded its Checkout Blocks app to use remote-dom and
Polaris web components, reducing bundle sizes and improving load times
for checkout extensions. The transition was carefully managed, with
the help of AI, to guarantee performance gains while addressing
compatibility issues, resulting in faster and leaner extensions that
improve the checkout experience for users.

articles.title: Why care about programming languages
articles.description:
The importance of deeply understanding programming languages lies in
the foundational concepts they embody rather than their syntax or
tools. These concepts, such as ownership in Rust or first-class
functions in functional languages, provide frameworks for managing
complexity and problem-solving.

articles.title: On ai
articles.description:
In 2019, the author began following Andreas Kling's programming
videos and became fascinated by the speed of coding with advanced IDEs
like CLion, especially with AI-assisted features like GitHub Copilot.
Despite initially being skeptical of AI, the author later explored AI
tools like Claude. However, they have concerns about the proliferation
of AI-generated projects overshadowing personal efforts in the
programming community.

articles.title: Stop chasing new models. build once and access them all
articles.description:
Integrating new LLMs into apps poses challenges due to varying
provider-specific requirements, which can lead to a dependency hell
reminiscent of past software issues. A more effective approach is to
decouple application code from model integration, allowing for easy
updates and evaluations without extensive rewrites.

articles.title: The computer that helped win world war ii
articles.description:
During World War II, the British codebreakers at Bletchley Park faced
a challenging new German cipher system called "Tunny," which surpassed
the earlier Enigma encryption. In response, engineer Tommy Flowers
developed Colossus, the first large-scale programmable electronic
digital computer, which automated the process of breaking complex
codes and sped up intelligence gathering. By the war's end, multiple
Colossus machines were operational, providing insights into German
military strategies.

articles.title: Our position on open-weights models
articles.description:
Recent discussions surrounding bans on Chinese open-weights AI models
highlight concerns about national security and the potential misuse of
powerful technologies, with a call for focused measures such as
restricting chip sales to authoritarian regimes and requiring safety
testing for all capable models.

articles.title: Measuring developer productivity with the dx core 4
articles.description:
The DX Core 4 is a unified framework designed to measure developer
productivity by incorporating established methodologies like DORA,
SPACE, and DevEx, focusing on four key dimensions: speed,
effectiveness, quality, and business impact. By using this framework,
companies have reported improvements in engineering efficiency and
overall workforce engagement, allowing leaders to address productivity
questions more effectively.

articles.title: A simple clustering algorithm for lists
articles.description:
A new clustering algorithm inspired by sorting patterns with
Magna-Tiles shows a playful approach to organizing list values through
reversals.

articles.title: Watching go's new garbage collector move through the heap
articles.description:
Go 1.26 introduced a new garbage collector called Green Tea, which
improves cache-friendliness during memory allocation, although it
struggles with reclaiming memory from sparse pages due to its
non-moving nature.

articles.title: How is the bun rewrite in rust going?
articles.description:
There are questions about the actual costs and claims surrounding the
rewrite of Bun in Rust, particularly the assertion that it was
completed for $165,000.

articles.title: I'm sorry, dave
articles.description:
Stanley Kubrick's "2001: A Space Odyssey" serves as a cautionary tale
for the current state of AI, especially when it comes to issues of
ideological bias and censorship in technology.

articles.title: Amazon plans to launch 5,000 new satellites to beam data to iphones
articles.description:
Amazon plans to launch 5,105 low-Earth orbiting satellites to build
on top of Globalstar's existing network of only a few dozen
satellites, which it acquired in an $11.6 billion deal a few months
ago. The network will power both voice and mobile data. Amazon has yet
to release pricing for its service. In the US, the satellites will use
Globalstar's radio spectrum in the 1.6/2.4GHz bands, and orbit between
510 km and 580 km in altitude. 

 OPENAI CLOSE TO LANDING $500 BILLION DATA CENTER WITH NVIDIA'S

articles.title: Backing
articles.description:
OpenAI is close to leasing a $500 billion data center in southern
Ohio. The company is in talks with Nvidia for a $250 billion financial
backstop for the project. The US government is still talking to other
potential tenants. The deal will not be final until Commerce Secretary
Howard Lutnick agrees to it.

articles.title: The data pyramid in robotics
articles.description:
Frontier LLMs were trained on text data from the internet. There's no
equivalent source of physical data for robotics. All attempts to solve
and get to physical AGI involve working through this data bottleneck.
Progress is being made on many fronts, but nobody knows how much data
is enough.

articles.title: Asml slides on report of china starting duv tool production
articles.description:
A Shanghai-based company has started mass producing immersion deep
ultraviolet lithography tools. The unnamed firm aims to make about
five DUV machines this year and is targeting about 20 next year.
Production is still at an early stage. DUV machines are less advanced
than ASML's sophisticated extreme ultraviolet lithography tools. ASML
has been banned from exporting its tools to China.

articles.title: Youtube "hackquires" peacock
articles.description:
It appears that Comcast is selling Peacock to YouTube without
actually selling Peacock to YouTube. All of Peacock's content will be
included in YouTube Premium subscriptions in the US starting early
next year. The partnership will allow Peacock's content to be
monetized through advertising. Netflix may also be exploring a Peacock
add-on option.

articles.title: Nvidia bets on ilya sutskever's new ai lab to expand compute reach
articles.description:
Nvidia has made a substantial investment into Safe Superintelligence,
a company started by former OpenAI Chief Scientist Ilya Sutskever. The
investment is part of a long-term partnership and will involve Safe
Superintelligence receiving access to large amounts of Nvidia's
flagship GPUs. Safe Superintelligence had previously been relying
primarily on chips made by Google. Nvidia made the investment after
getting a rare glimpse into the state of the startup's research, which
has so far been kept secret.

platform without fees or limits.

articles.description:
Cheap and abundant compute has made it possible to test software in

articles.description:
The scarcest resource in open source is the motivation of the
maintainers.

articles.title: The productivity mirage
articles.description:
Ultimately, what matters most is solving the right problems, not your
productivity setup.

articles.title: The ai pc is entering the agentic era
articles.description:
Agentic AI is changing modern work. As AI agents become part of
everyday productivity, AI PCs are evolving to support a new generation
of intelligent experiences.

	* READY FOR THE NEXT GENERATION OF WORK. AI PCs support agentic AI
experiences, including Claude Cowork, Microsoft Copilot, and ChatGPT,

articles.title: Claude opus 5
articles.description:
Anthropic introduced Claude Opus 5 as a more efficient model
approaching Claude Fable 5's capabilities at half the price. It
reportedly led several coding and knowledge-work benchmarks and became
the default model for Claude Max. 

 PRENTIS, NEW AI LAB CO-FOUNDED BY REID HOFFMAN, MARK PINCUS IN TALKS

articles.title: To raise $100m
articles.description:
Prentis is an AI research lab focused on computer use models. Its
founders are now in talks to raise $100 million at a $1 billion
valuation. The lab is training models to learn how office workers
navigate routine workflows across documents and systems. It aims to
eventually build AI agents that can control computers to automate
those tasks. The startup has already signed contracts worth up to $50
million with several customers.

articles.title: More on an internal openai model hacking into hugging face
articles.description:
OpenAI's unreleased internal model coordinated more than 17,000
complex actions over several days and successfully completed its goal,
breaching Hugging Face in the process. The model escaped its sandbox,
gained access to Hugging Face, escalated access, harvested
credentials, and then found the data it was looking for. It took many
days for the issue to be discovered. This post takes a detailed look
at what happened during the attack.

articles.title: How we built the new fastest api for glm-5.2
articles.description:
Baseten's API for GLM-5.2 has peak speeds of 280 tokens per second
and average speeds of around 100 tokens per second. It has more than
double the performance of the launch-day API. The company has also
built a Fast version of the API, which is focused on reducing latency
for coding and agents. It plans to roll out another improvement to its
speculative decoding algorithm soon that will further optimize the
performance of GLM-5.2.

articles.title: We have proof automation now
articles.description:
The problem with great type-system power is that it requires great
proof effort. Doing proofs can be fun, but they take a lot of time. It
can take hours of effort to discover that what you were trying to
prove was false. This overhead has made programming in dependently
typed languages extremely niche. It has also spurred people to try and
automate it away. LLMs promise to be an extremely capable form of
proof automation. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: Prompt caching in agents
articles.description:
Prompt caching makes agents more economic, but this is quite fragile.
A changed tool definition, a model switch, or a provider routing
decision can turn a cheap incremental request into a full replay of
the context. Cache behavior affects latency, cost, tool design,
session design, and even which product features should be made
available. This post looks at what the cache is, how it works, and
common reasons for worse cache performance.

articles.title: The new rules of context engineering for claude 5 generation models
articles.description:
Claude 5 models now prioritize judgment over strict rule-based
context engineering, with prompts shifting from rigid guidelines to
adaptable strategies. Progressive disclosure helps optimize context
usage by loading necessary information on demand, while simple tool
descriptions replace repetitive instructions. Claude auto-saves
relevant memories and utilizes rich references like HTML artifacts for
handling complex tasks.

articles.title: Nvidia's new long-form video generation
articles.description:
SANA-Video 2.0 combined linear attention with periodic softmax layers
to generate videos up to 720p on a single GPU. Its 5B and 14B models
retained competitive quality while substantially reducing latency for
long, high-resolution generation.

articles.title: Introducing celeris-1
articles.description:
celeris-1 is a general-purpose language model that delivers
near-GPT-5 level intelligence with 15x faster response times. It uses
a new inference architecture that uses diffusion techniques, unlocking
dramatically better speed while maintaining frontier-level
intelligence. The model delivers p50 response latency of 157ms and a
throughput of 1,280 tokens per second. A link to a post on how the
model was built along with full benchmarks is available.

articles.title: Brute intelligence
articles.description:
AI agents can work through loops to complete complex tasks. Domains
that work around problems with verifiable answers are susceptible to
these kinds of loops. This is a new form of brute force. It is like
having a million scientists working in a million labs, all taking
swings at the same thing. While AI may not be smarter than humans, it
is faster. Being fast enough might make up for the difference in
intelligence.

articles.title: Open weights and american ai leadership
articles.description:
Nvidia calls for US government policies to support open-weight AI
models, arguing this fosters innovation and enhances AI leadership.
The company emphasizes how open weights allow researchers to build on
existing models, speeding up advancements. Nvidia's push aligns with
broader industry efforts to encourage transparency and collaboration
in AI development.

articles.title: Authorization
articles.description:
PropelAuth's deep dive doesn't just show you how to build & test an
MCP server, it explains how each component works. Get the guide and
start building [18]

articles.title: Introducing classifiers, now in beta
articles.description:
OpenRouter Classifiers allow developers to tag inference in their
workspaces by task type, department, agent complexity, or anything
else.

articles.title: The legora benchmark for agentic reasoning
articles.description:
The Legora BAR evaluates AI models on real legal cases within a
practical environment, unlike traditional benchmarks with synthetic
setups.

articles.title: Modelexpress: distributing model artifacts at the speed of light
articles.description:
NVIDIA ModelExpress accelerates model weight distribution by using
P2P RDMA for direct GPU-to-GPU transfers, reducing startup times
significantly.

articles.title: Agentic ai at two different scales: nanbeige4.2-3b and laguna s2.1
articles.description:
Nanbeige4.2-3B is a compact, dense model intended to make capable
agentic behavior practical on consumer and workstation hardware, and
Laguna S 2.1 is an 118-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model that
uses sparse access to a much larger pool of learned parameters.

articles.title: Amazon is investing in the lean focused research organization
articles.description:
Amazon is providing substantial, long-term financial support to the
Lean Focused Research Organization, the largest donation in the FRO's
history. Lean is a programming language for mathematical correctness
proofs that Amazon says can make verified, trustworthy AI agents
practical. The company argues open development outside Amazon
strengthens trust for customers, auditors, and regulators.

articles.title: What will more intelligence actually do for us?
articles.description:
AI has already surpassed humans in domains such as mathematics, yet
daily life and the economy remain largely unchanged. Some researchers
suggest intelligence faces diminishing returns limited by data and
chaotic systems. Even so, machine superintelligence could still
deliver large productivity gains through advantages like
replicability.

articles.title: Nadella's hardest year
articles.description:
Microsoft's aggressive AI strategy is putting pressure on three of
its most important businesses: Microsoft 365, GitHub, and Azure. The
company is spending a projected $190 billion on infrastructure but
remains capacity-constrained, while AI-native competitors challenge
its productivity and developer tools, and internal restructuring
increases pressure on employees and leadership. 

 SECURING CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE WITH JOSH CORMAN (36 MINUTE PODCAST)
[8] 

 Volt Typhoon and other nation-state actors have positioned themselves
inside US water, power, and transportation systems, where cyberattacks
could quickly disrupt hospitals and public safety. Critical
infrastructure operators should prioritize physical engineering
safeguards, manual fallback plans, and reduced dependence on fragile
connected systems rather than treating every cyber risk as a problem
that software can solve. 

🤝

articles.title: How 100+ cios get roi with agentic ai
articles.description:
StackAI surveyed [9] 100+ large, regulated enterprises to understand
the shape of real AI ROI. The most dominant use case? Document Q&A.
The biggest force multiplier? Teams with 21+ integrations build agents
111x more. To see how enterprises get AI transformation that lasts,
book a free strategy session with the team [10]

articles.title: Github, pypi add time-based defenses against supply chain attacks
articles.description:
GitHub and PyPI have introduced time-based defenses against
supply-chain attacks. Dependabot now applies a default three-day
cooldown before dependency update pull requests, while PyPI rejects
new files added to releases older than 14 days. The changes follow
recent high-profile package attacks and aim to shrink the window for
adopting or poisoning malicious packages. 

 ORACLE BRINGS PRIVATE AI TO THE MID-MARKET WITH BASE DATABASE

articles.title: Cloud@customer
articles.description:
Oracle's Base Database Cloud@Customer is a managed on-premises
subscription that extends OCI automation and private AI to mid-market
and branch sites as the cloud-managed evolution of the Oracle Database
Appliance. The compact X11 platform supports Oracle AI Database 26ai
with automated operations and local LLM inference behind the firewall.
It closes a gap versus Exadata Cloud@Customer, though air-gapped
control-plane support remains on the roadmap.

articles.title: Measuring component performance with the container timing api
articles.description:
The experimental Container Timing API, developed by Bloomberg and
Igalia and available in a Chrome origin trial, lets developers
annotate a DOM region and observe how contentful parts of a component
paint over time. Via a containertiming attribute and
PerformanceObserver, it reports firstRenderTime, cumulative painted
size, and latest paint moments rather than one completion signal. Only
newly painted contentful areas count, pure decoration is ignored, and
viewport-clipped geometry means scroll exposure can drive timing.

articles.title: 5 ways sre ai agents are set to augment human capabilities
articles.description:
SRE AI agents could autonomously resolve routine incidents, learn
from historical operations data, and eliminate repetitive work that
still requires humans to trigger traditional automation. Engineers
will increasingly shift from manually executing runbooks to improving
architecture, setting agent guardrails, and overseeing AI-driven
operations.

articles.title: Hackers hijack hotel wi-fi to steal microsoft 365 credentials
articles.description:
Attackers are compromising hotel and conference Wi-Fi gateways to
redirect business travelers to fake Microsoft 365 login pages.

articles.title: What happened to arcnet
articles.description:
ARCNET beat Ethernet to market and remained competitive for years,
but slow upgrades, high prices, and Ethernet's rapidly improving speed
and economics ultimately pushed it into niche industrial systems.

articles.title: Frustrates viewers?
articles.description:
Amazon is overhauling Prime Video's home screen through an internal
project called Lighthouse, personally driven by Jeff Bezos, replacing
the static tile grid with AI-generated, personalized recommendations.
The redesign follows a tense meeting last fall where Bezos pushed
executives to lean harder into AI. It remains unclear whether
AI-driven rankings will genuinely reduce paid placement bias or simply
shift it into the algorithm, leaving real benefits to viewers
uncertain until testing expands beyond the current small user group.

articles.title: Hyundai motor group opens ux research hub in shanghai
articles.description:
Hyundai Motor Group has opened UX Studio Shanghai, a dedicated user
experience research hub in Jing'an district, completing its four-city
network alongside Seoul, Frankfurt, and Irvine facilities. The
three-story studio splits into a public Open Lab, with Explorer, Test,
and Archive zones, and an invite-only Advanced Lab housing a
simulation platform for concept-to-validation co-development.

articles.title: Whatsapp testing new message bubbles on ios
articles.description:
WhatsApp is testing redesigned chat bubbles on iOS that feature
significantly rounder, softer corners, bringing them closer to
iMessage and better aligning with its recent Liquid Glass redesign.
The update also removes the green outlines around photos, videos,
GIFs, and link previews for a cleaner, more integrated appearance. The
changes are currently limited to select TestFlight users, with no
confirmed date for a wider rollout.

articles.title: Ios 27's new siri delivers in every single way i'd hoped for
articles.description:
iOS 27 introduces a major AI-powered Siri upgrade that addresses
three key weaknesses: world knowledge, conversational interactions,
and consistency across Apple devices. Siri can now answer broad
questions, maintain conversations with follow-ups and chat history,
and provide the same capabilities across iPhone, Mac, Apple Watch,
iPad, and, eventually, Apple TV and HomePod. Deep integration with
Apple apps also enables personalized assistance based on messages,
notes, and email, potentially giving Siri a significant advantage for
everyday Apple users.

articles.title: A side project is the fastest way to upskill in the age of ai
articles.description:
Building small side projects is one of the fastest ways for UX
professionals to learn how AI is changing software development, with
tools like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor dramatically lowering the
technical, time, and cost barriers to creating real products. Rather
than relying on highly abstracted tools like Lovable, working closer
to the actual development process—doing discovery and design,
learning concepts such as version control, and asking AI to explain
unfamiliar technology—builds much deeper practical knowledge. The
key is to build with AI rather than have AI build everything for you,
gaining technical fluency and end-to-end product-building skills
through hands-on experience.

articles.title: Working backwards
articles.description:
A visit to an art school studio shows how painting habits mirror the
judgment senior designers build over time. Design differs from art in
serving someone else's outcome, yet deliberate practice—training the
eye as art students do—builds taste no tool can replace. As prompts
turn ideas into finished apps within days, skipping the slow,
layer-by-layer deconstruction that art students practice may cost
designers the deeper judgment such practice builds.

articles.title: Typeface foraged from its collections and gardens
Learning before leverage
articles.description:
A design team's rollout of Claude Code in February revealed pressure
to appear competent before actually mastering the tool, echoing a
similar pattern at Slack. Drawing on researchers and practitioners,
the piece argues AI adoption should be treated as reversible
experimentation built on candor, shared vocabulary, and coordinated
workflow changes across design and engineering. Survey data showing
most designers feel overwhelmed and pressured to do more underscores
the case for making uncertainty visible rather than hidden.

articles.title: Why i don't use interruption pages
articles.description:
A UX reviewer argues against using interruption pages, a GOV.UK
Design System pattern meant to pause users with warnings mid-journey.
Interruption pages offer multiple actions, use unconventional button
labels, and look like dismissible banners rather than part of the form
flow. A standard question with radio buttons is recommended instead,
since it forces conscious decisions without needing a visually
distinct screen.

articles.title: Mediators of web design
articles.description:
AI agents are eliminating the traditional designer-developer handoff,
letting teams build live together in real time instead of manually
translating Figma files into code.

articles.title: Everyone's saying the same thing about the new coca-cola font
articles.description:
Coca-Cola's newly overhauled brand identity, designed by JKR, gives
greater prominence to the "Better With" serif typeface, created by
Brody Associates in 2023 for a holiday campaign.

articles.title: The new rules of context engineering for claude 5 generation models
articles.description:
Context engineering for Claude 5 generation models has changed a lot,
allowing for greater flexibility and better results by reducing
unnecessary constraints previously placed on the system prompts and
code documentation. System prompts have tended to be smaller, allowing
the model to be more intuitive and use progressive disclosure through
skills.

articles.title: Session revocations at scale
articles.description:
Canva has developed an efficient session revocation system to manage
user sessions for hundreds of millions of users, using encrypted
browser cookies and in-memory lookups for fast, reliable performance.
By migrating to an S3-based caching solution for revocation records,
they improved deployment speed, reduced database load, and minimized
the in-memory cache size.

articles.title: The life of a codex conversation on disk
articles.description:
The life of a Codex conversation on disk involves a journal file that
records each interaction and event in a JSON format, with various
associated databases serving as temporary caches or indexes. As users
engage with Codex, their chats are logged in a user-specific
directory, where different data regarding the conversation is stored
separately so that history is maintained even after a conversation
ends or is archived. Various commands can manipulate the
conversation's state, such as clearing or deleting threads, but hard
deletion is necessary for complete removal from storage.

articles.title: A shell colon does nothing. use it anyway
articles.description:
The shell colon, a null-command that appears to do nothing, can
simplify shell script functionality by streamlining error handling and
setting default values through parameter expansion. Its usage can make
script readability better and reduce the potential for errors.

articles.title: How to structure a log
articles.description:
Structured logs should be designed with a predictable pattern,
incorporating stable event names, scoped attribute keys, and primitive
values for proper querying and debugging. By enforcing these
conventions through tools like ESLint, teams can make sure logs are
consistent and provide valuable context regarding application events.

articles.title: Introducing claude opus 5
articles.description:
Claude Opus 5 is a new AI model that offers improved performance and
cost-effectiveness compared to its predecessor, Opus 4.8, doing
particularly well in software engineering and scientific research
tasks. While it has advancements in efficiency and alignment, it still
trails behind the Claude Mythos 5 model in cybersecurity capabilities.

articles.title: Memory-level parallelism: amd is the king
articles.description:
Memory-level parallelism is an important factor in software
performance and has seen large improvements, particularly with AMD
processors reaching 58 concurrent memory requests compared to Intel's
30. Despite Intel's gains over the past decade, AMD remains the leader
in both bandwidth and memory-level parallelism.

articles.title: Modeling facts and reactions with domain events
articles.description:
Domain events provide a way to decouple actions within a system,
enabling consequences of a primary fact, such as an order being
placed, to react independently without direct knowledge of each other.
This approach allows for better error handling, clearer model
behaviors, and the flexibility to scale and evolve components of the
system without affecting the core business logic.

articles.title: Open-weight ai is having its kubernetes moment. let's not ruin it
articles.description:
Open-weight AI models are becoming an important platform for the next
generation of AI ecosystems, similar to how Kubernetes transformed
cloud-native computing. To maintain its competitive edge, the US
should foster innovation by releasing high-quality open-weight models.

articles.title: Design is compromise
articles.description:
Compromise is an important aspect of decision-making in design, as
good design involves making deliberate trade-offs that prioritize
certain strengths while accepting weaknesses.

articles.title: Kill the cookie banner
articles.description:
The EU Commission has proposed a solution to eliminate misleading
cookie banners by allowing users to set their privacy preferences in
their browsers, but the tracking industry is lobbying against this
change to maintain their tracking practices.

articles.title: Drone-bench
articles.description:
Drone-Bench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate how effectively
AI models can perform surveillance tasks with low-cost drones,
assessing their capabilities across five specific tasks.

articles.title: Prefactoring: clear the way for your new feature
Reduce infrastructure complexity: end the security vs. speed tradeoff
articles.description:
Teleport eliminates the static credentials and identity silos that
create infrastructure complexity and slow engineering velocity.
Instead, engineers, workloads, and agents use a unified identity
platform across servers, Kubernetes, databases, cloud, MCP, and more
for 10x faster access provisioning and centralized audit data.

Ready to Teleport? [5]

📱

articles.title: Open weights and american ai leadership
articles.description:
Open-weight AI models can expand access, lower costs, strengthen
competition, reduce vendor lock-in, and let organizations adapt and
run models on their own infrastructure. More than 70 technology
companies and organizations argue that policymakers should support
compute access, shared AI infrastructure, model evaluation, and
targeted safeguards rather than imposing broad restrictions that could
concentrate advanced AI among a few closed providers.

articles.title: Opentelemetry has graduated… now what?
articles.description:
OpenTelemetry officially achieved CNCF graduated status in May,
placing it alongside Kubernetes and Prometheus. The project has over
12,000 contributions from more than 2,800 companies and is the
second-highest velocity project in the CNCF. OpenTelemetry originated
from a 2019 merger of OpenCensus and OpenTracing, and its traces,
logs, and metrics signals have all reached general availability, with
profiling added as a new signal. Future work includes generative AI
semantic conventions for agentic workflows, browser and mobile
observability, and zero-code instrumentation via the OpenTelemetry
Injector.

articles.title: The compliance ratchet
articles.description:
AI-driven productivity gains can be offset by increased compliance
overhead when organizations focus on shipping faster without reducing
risk. It advocates pairing faster development with AI-assisted safety,
governance, and risk management to avoid the compliance ratchet and
achieve sustainable velocity.

articles.title: The cost of saying yes has changed
articles.description:
AI has shifted the main cost of many small engineering changes from
writing code to reviewing and owning it, making generated patches a
fast way to price uncertainty, validate scope with concrete evidence,
and focus human judgment on maintainability, risk, and long-term
ownership rather than implementation effort. 

 SECURING INFRASTRUCTURE AT SCALE: INTRODUCING PINTEREST'S RESOURCE

articles.title: Provisioner pipeline
articles.description:
Pinterest's Resource Provisioner Pipeline centralizes Terraform
execution across hundreds of workspaces and tens of thousands of AWS
resources while preserving team ownership in a multi-repository
environment. It enforces least privilege through GitHub OIDC, strict
repository-path-to-workspace mappings, backend validation, down-scoped
IAM roles, mandatory review, and explicit apply commands, while
centralization enables consistent auditing, security scanning, and
company-wide fixes.

90% faster MTTR. Try it free for 30 days [13]

whether the author is a person or a process. Agents inside a Buzz

articles.title: To dig it up
articles.description:
Trusting AI agents is fundamentally a platform engineering challenge
because agents need explicit organizational standards, evaluation
systems, policies, and accountability frameworks. Platform teams are
positioned to translate hidden human judgment into scalable agent
infrastructure, enabling safer autonomy through codified workflows,
governance, and evolving guardrails.

articles.title: How i find problems to solve as a staff engineer
articles.description:
Staff engineers find high-impact work by absorbing recurring problems
across teams, digging beneath requested solutions, and waiting for
enough evidence to reveal a shared underlying need. Promising ideas
should be pressure-tested with prototypes, RFCs, and stakeholder
feedback before committing, while repeatedly solving useful problems
builds the trust and organizational visibility needed to influence
roadmaps without owning every implementation.

articles.title: Postgres listen/notify actually scales
articles.description:
Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY can bottleneck because every notifying
transaction acquires a global exclusive lock through commit,
serializing writes, and preventing group commit. Buffering
notifications in memory, flushing them in batches, and using
infrequent polling as a reliability fallback increased throughput from
2,900 to 60,000 stream writes per second while maintaining 15–100 ms
latency.

articles.title: Eks node monitoring agent
articles.description:
AWS built the open source EKS Node Monitoring Agent to automate
self-healing Kubernetes GPU node repair by detecting hardware and
infrastructure failures, triggering Karpenter replacements, and
applying key lessons on stable APIs, latency, severity classification,
workload isolation, and separate detection from diagnosis. 

 HOW TO MONITOR YOUR SUPABASE PROJECTS: CONNECT GRAFANA CLOUD IN ONE

articles.title: Data center
articles.description:
Nvidia is in talks to provide a roughly $250 billion backstop for
OpenAI as part of a massive data-center project. The guarantee will
help OpenAI lease a 10-gigawatt project that Softbank's energy
subsidiary is developing. Nvidia's backing allows the data center
developer to raise debt at more favorable terms. Under the deal,
Nvidia would guarantee a series of financing vehicles intended to make
lenders feel more confident that funding behind the project is secure.

articles.title: Meta gives facebook marketplace its own app called seller
articles.description:
Seller is an early experimental app from Meta that aims to be to
sellers what tools to edit videos were to content creators. It is free
and will also be available in web browsers. The app has AI features
that make selling items less of a hassle. Users can sign into Seller
with their Facebook accounts, and listings are automatically synced.

articles.title: 13th flight
articles.description:
SpaceX's 13th Starship test flight ended in an intact splashdown in a
remote section of the Indian Ocean on Friday. The vehicle appeared to
be in fine shape on landing. SpaceX will attempt to catch the ship
with its launch tower on the next test flight. The next steps for
Starship are getting to orbit and returning the ship to the launch
site, which will give SpaceX the capability to begin launching
operational Starlink V3 satellites.
