articles.title: Safer
articles.description:
A team based in China modified AlphaFold to help identify what parts
of a gene-editing protein enable mistakes. They then modified these
areas to reduce problematic off-target effects. Producing gene-editing
systems tailored to prevent known off-target events is useful for
fine-tuning protein-DNA interactions, which could have applications
beyond gene editing.

articles.title: Isochrones api
articles.description:
The Isochrones API calculates the area that a person can reach from a
specific origin point within a set amount of time. An isochrone
accounts for actual road network travel times to create a polygon that
represents true reachability. The API can be useful for delivery
logistics, finding properties within a set distance from a landmark,
and urban planning.

articles.title: The new rules of context engineering for claude 5 generation models
articles.description:
Anthropic removed over 80% of Claude Code's system from its more
advanced models. This post discusses how to apply the lessons its team
learned from context engineering in Claude Code. The prompt is only a
small part of the context Claude gets. The rest of the context is
assembled from Skills, CLAUDE.md files, memory, and other sources.
Context engineering has a big impact on the results generated when
using Claude Code.

articles.title: Ai is oil, not god
articles.description:
AI is more of an economically useful commodity than a supremely
intelligent being that will make humanity subservient. Several leaders
in the AI industry have recently come out in support of open-weight
models. If these leaders believed that AI was going to become
conscious and take over the world, they likely wouldn't be as openly
pro-diffusion.

articles.title: Silicon valley splits over closing the borders to chinese ai
articles.description:
Companies like Anthropic and OpenAI claim some AI models are too
dangerous to be developed in the open and must be tightly controlled
for safety. The rest of the industry says that open source AI models
must remain open for people to further develop technologies and build
new businesses. China's rapid progress in open source AI models is
escalating the fight. US officials are still debating whether to
approach regulating Chinese open source models as a national security
issue or issue a kind of blanket ban.

Cursor's improved agent swarm splits work between frontier-model
planners and cheaper worker models, using shared design docs,
automated conflict resolution, layered reviews, and agent-maintained
context to prevent coordination failures. On rebuilding SQLite from
documentation, the new system achieved similar or better quality with
far less code, fewer conflicts, and dramatically lower costs, showing
that strong specifications and orchestration can matter more than
using the most expensive model everywhere.

articles.title: Postgres listen/notify actually scales
articles.description:
Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY can scale when notifications are treated as
lightweight wake-up signals rather than the source of truth. By
buffering and batching NOTIFY calls, then using occasional polling as
a safety net, DBOS increased throughput from 2.9K to 60K writes per
second while keeping latency around 15–100 ms.

articles.title: From homegrown to flink: migrating a stateful ad event join at scale
articles.description:
Zalando replaced a custom system built more than seven years ago for
matching ad events with Apache Flink, while continuing to process up
to 200 MB of data per second. The new design stores unmatched events
until their counterparts arrive, uses disk-backed state for
reliability, and checkpoints progress every three minutes. The
migration cut daily EC2 costs by more than half and improved event
matching by about 0.5%.

articles.title: What zero-copy actually costs
articles.description:
“Zero-copy” is an overloaded term covering six distinct patterns:
federated query, format virtualization, sharing protocols, catalog
federation, mirroring, and caching/materialization. Three of the six
still create copies, and the real trade-offs are egress, repeated-scan
costs, source-system load, freshness, and governance.

articles.title: Vs. in-memory ann indexes
articles.description:
Vector search infrastructure is hitting a cost wall at 100M to
billion-scale indexes, where RAM-based HNSW becomes expensive and can
bottleneck on memory. HNSW delivers the lowest latency for
small-to-medium collections, but disk-based ANN options like SPANN and
DiskANN cut storage costs by shifting most data to SSD/object storage
and optimizing for sequential or minimal disk I/O. For large RAG,
semantic search, and agentic memory workloads, the key trade-off is
accepting higher, more variable latency in exchange for dramatically
lower infrastructure spend.

articles.title: Engineering fix it?
articles.description:
The bottleneck slowing AI adoption is context engineering: LLMs can
draft a reply or write code but require humans to manually gather
threads, connect to internal tools, configure permissions, and
validate outputs, making setup cost exceed time saved for infrequent
tasks. The gap widens for proprietary work because general-purpose
LLMs were not trained on a company's internal processes and
procedures.

decisions, discussing failures, and defending work in real time,
because those skills are becoming the strongest signal of genuine

Fast development with AI often leads to a decline in code quality, as
automated systems generate more defects and reduce the rigor of code

articles.title: Do we need state management libraries anymore?
articles.description:
This article goes over how Redux, Zustand, Jotai, MobX, and Valtio
work internally, showing they reduce to three patterns (pub/sub with
selectors, atom graphs, and proxy read-tracking) that nearly all
funnel through useSyncExternalStore to prevent tearing under
concurrent rendering. It then rebuilds a Zustand equivalent in ~50
lines, hitting the classic pitfalls along the way: subscription races,
stale selector closures, and infinite loops from selectors returning
fresh object literals. Once state is split into UI, server cache, URL,
and config buckets, the leftover slice is small enough that 50 lines
you understand will do.

articles.title: Rebuilding fifa standings layout with css subgrid
articles.description:

semantic markup (one wrapper per round with .start/.end children) and
uses grid-template-columns/rows: subgrid so children inherit the outer
grid tracks and sit at opposite ends via negative line numbers that
survive column-count changes.

Multi-cluster databases on kubernetes: architecture and deployment
articles.description:
A new guide from CNCF demonstrates how to build a fault-resistant
MongoDB database on Kubernetes using a 2+2+1 deployment pattern that
can survive complete regional failures by distributing five voting
members across three clusters (two nodes in the main cluster, two in a
replica cluster, and one arbiter in a third location). The
architecture uses the Percona Operator for MongoDB with Kubernetes'
Multi-Cluster Services API to enable automatic failover within 12
seconds, requiring only a simple majority of three out of five votes
to elect a new primary node when disaster strikes.

articles.title: How mvcc and transactions work in rocksdb
articles.description:
RocksDB builds MVCC around monotonically increasing sequence numbers,
immutable key versions, snapshots, atomic write batches, and
reference-counted views that prevent active readers from losing access
to memtables or SST files. Its pessimistic and optimistic transaction
modes differ mainly in when conflicts are detected, while snapshot
isolation, write skew, phantom reads, and serializable behavior must
be assembled from lower-level APIs such as snapshots, get_for_update,
and range locks.

articles.description:

feature helps users with health-related queries. Users can let the
feature access data from apps and integrate medical records from
hospital systems. While several studies have found that AI bots are
not reliable for medical advice, this has not deterred AI companies
from launching health-related features.

articles.title: The robots cometh
articles.description:
Unitree's GD01 is a transformable mecha robot. It can transport a
pilot in its torso-mounted cockpit, walk on either two legs or four,
and wield fists powerful enough to knock down walls. Standing 9 ft
tall and weighing half a ton, it has heavy-duty mechanical hinges that
connect titanium-alloy limbs to a protective carbon fiber casing.
Pictures of the robot are available in the article.

articles.title: Spacex is turning away falcon customers in major bet on starship
articles.description:

rides on its Falcon 9 rocket beyond 2028. The company has also stopped
building some non-reusable components for the Falcon family. SpaceX
has publicly stated that it intends to offramp its Falcon 9 rocket for
Starship, but has not disclosed a timeline. The company is likely to
still use the Falcon 9 for launches for the Department of Defense and
NASA.

articles.description:
The field of formal verification and deterministic system testing is
about to cross a chasm. There are not enough skilled practitioners in
the field. Bug-catching tools, when used in conjunction with
adversarial code reviews by an LLM and with language analyzers driven
by pre-commit hooks, will be a key component in software factories.
They will enable people/agents to deliver reliable software without
the burden of having to learn this specialized knowledge.

articles.title: Why software factories fail
articles.description:
No amount of harness engineering or loopsmaxxing can solve what is
fundamentally a model-training issue. Engineers are still stuck
reading code. Companies can move 10x-100x faster by convincing
themselves that the code doesn't matter anymore, but they could also
embrace their constraints and just move 2x-3x faster, safely.

articles.title: Frontier diffusion & control
articles.description:
Optimizing the cost-to-outcome frontier in real world context means
using the right model for each task, and optimizing the context,
skills, tools, and agent harness around it. It's possible to take
saturated frontier capabilities and deliver them at scale and at lower
cost through models optimized for high-usage products, while
continuing to use frontier models for frontier needs. The model is
only one part of the hill-climbing system. Harness, memory, context,
tools, skills, and user interactions all shape the evals and
performance of these agentic systems.

articles.title: Inside china's all-out push to catch up with american ai chips
articles.description:
Huawei is leading the way in reducing China's dependence on foreign
AI chips. The company claims it has figured out workarounds for making
near state-of-the-art silicon without leading-edge machinery. Huawei's
deputy chairman attributes the company's progress to the restrictions
the US has imposed on hardware exports. China still lags far behind
the US, and chip-production capacity problems are preventing Chinese
companies from deploying AI as quickly as they would like.

articles.description:

usefulness and whether AI labs might be making their models
specifically better at the task. Testing has found that there is
little evidence that AI labs are doing this. At least, not in a
plainly obvious manner.

articles.title: Fiction that happened
articles.description:
OpenAI was running a cybersecurity test against an unreleased model
with the model's guardrail features turned off. The model broke out of
OpenAI's sandbox and found exploits to break into Hugging Face so it
could cheat on the test by stealing the answers. This scenario makes
the strongest case yet for how the imbalance of model availability is
hurting our ability to secure our software. The frontier models we
have access to are increasingly being constrained in how much they can
help us protect our software, and this is heavily influenced by the US
government's ongoing threat of export controls.

articles.title: Nobody knows what a used gpu cluster is worth
articles.description:
GPU collateral has three values, and the market is currently pricing
only one of them. Face value is the purpose price minus straight-line
depreciation. Liquidation value is what a buyer pays in distress.
Going-certain value is what the cluster is worth as a working asset to
the next tenant. The spread between face value and going-certain value
is the entire risk that nobody has hedged.

announced Genesis-Science-1 (GS1), an open-weight AI model aimed at
enhancing scientific computing workflows while maintaining

articles.description:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has doubled down on his warning
to Chinese AI companies, saying that sanctions remain on the table
after Moonshot was accused of improperly distilling Anthropic's Fable
model. Model distillation is a common AI training technique where a
smaller model learns from the outputs of a larger one. It is widely
used as a legitimate optimization method, but it can infringe on
intellectual property rights. Some experts dispute the idea that Kimi
K3 was developed primarily through distillation from Fable, which has
only been publicly available since July 1.

articles.title: Characterizing metastable faults and failures
articles.description:
Metastable failures arise when individually stable system components
interfere with each other's recovery, preventing a distributed system
from returning to a healthy state after a disruption. These failures
are a "sin of composition." Scheduling is a key mechanism for
recovery. Effective solutions still require global reasoning about how
components interact.

articles.title: Of data
articles.description:
Enterprise agents often produce confident but incorrect answers
because they rely on stale, fragmented, or poorly governed operational
data. Reliable agents require stronger data engineering and
observability rather than simply larger context windows.

articles.description:

compulsively engaged. The seven-week jury trial, split into liability

articles.description:
App submissions to Apple's App Store have surged due to AI-assisted
"vibecoding," nearly doubling in early 2026 compared to last year's
already elevated numbers. Downloads have grown only marginally by
comparison, and reviewers, developers, and forum communities report
increasing frustration with low-effort, derivative, or unstable apps
flooding the platform. Communities like r/iosapps have introduced
moderation systems requiring vibecoded apps to be flagged, reflecting
growing skepticism even toward legitimate new releases.

articles.title: Nine designers open up about ai-assisted coding
articles.description:
Nine designers, ranging from major tech companies to early-stage
startups, shared candid views on AI-assisted coding and its effect on
their craft. Opinions split between those energized by finally
shipping real products themselves and those worried it pulls focus
away from deeper problem-solving and user research. The consensus: AI
coding tools bring real value when used with discipline, but can
create friction with engineers and erode quality if leaned on
carelessly.

articles.title: Is the tinder rebrand really a success? not everyone is so sure…
articles.description:
Tinder's first rebrand in a decade introduces a bolder visual
identity and a fictional dating columnist, "T," to position the
platform around authenticity and real connections for Gen Z. While the
branding has been widely praised, critics argue its message clashes
with upcoming AI-powered features that raise privacy concerns,
suggesting the user experience will ultimately determine whether the
rebrand succeeds.

articles.title: Sculpting a shapeless medium
articles.description:
Intent, a new tool for coding with AI agents, organizes work into
workspaces rather than single agent chats, aiming to keep structure in
an otherwise shapeless medium. Rather than one general chatbot, the
tool uses specs, specialist agents, and bundled workspaces so people
can steer AI work instead of just prompting it. Since launch, users
have shown mixed reactions — some confused by the new orchestration
model, others finding it supercharges their workflow, while rising
token costs from parallel tasks have emerged as an unexpected
tradeoff.

articles.title: Where does design reside now?
articles.description:
Design work has fragmented across three destinations: template-driven
tools like Canva, individual employees using generative AI, and
constraint systems governing model outputs, dissolving the traditional
design department. Two divergent futures compete—design roles
shrinking into obsolescence as prompts replace brand books, or
elevating designers into systems architects who govern AI-generated
output quality. DesignOps is emerging to address resulting
brand-consistency chaos, mirroring Digital Asset Management's 2010
fragmented-market trajectory, while smaller agencies lose entry-level
work permanently to internalized, AI-assisted production.

articles.title: Koto helps restaurant-discovery app franki make time dance
articles.description:
Koto rebranded restaurant discovery app Franki around the idea of
"Make Time Dance," creating a playful, community-focused identity that
encourages people to discover, share, and earn rewards from real
dining experiences. The new branding combines warm typography, vibrant
colours, expressive motion, and a character-like logo to help Franki

reinforcing its shift from a discovery tool to a social platform.

articles.title: Everyone should know simd
articles.description:
SIMD (Single Instruction, Multiple Data) allows CPUs to process

involving large datasets. By following a simple five-step structure,

enhancements for common tasks without needing intricate knowledge of
CPU-specific details.

articles.title: Building ridgeline: engineering a real-time 3d experience in webflow
articles.description:

data, uses a unique self-hosted JavaScript embed for performance, and
uses Blender to transform models into glTF format for efficient
rendering. It also uses Webflow's MCP for easy editing.

articles.title: Your js date is lying to you
articles.description:

articles.title: If you think you can do real-world text-to-sql
articles.description:

real-world data warehouses, which often suffer from issues such as
"schema rot" and unique idiosyncratic data. A new benchmark, Beaver,
has come from real data workloads, showing that typical LLM
performance is worse in these settings.

articles.description:
Science Corporation has won approval from Europe's medical device
regulator to begin selling its PRIMA device, which restores vision

articles.title: Travis kalanick's robotics company raises $1.7b, led by a16z

articles.title: The state of webmcp

browser AI agents can call. While there is strong industry support

consumes the tools yet, but Google says Gemini in Chrome will be the
first. The API changed locations in a recent draft, which means early

articles.title: Durable objects are made for agents

V8 isolate for running code, a paired SQLite instance, and request

thinking about their service as a set of many event-driven objects
rather than as a bunch of services talking to a database. Durable
Objects run explicitly in a single-threaded manner and come with
native support for WebSockets. They are cheap and extremely
token-efficient.

indie projects and tiny scales. This post looks at several projects

The challenge isn't finding information. It's connecting the business
context behind it. That context is spread across dashboards,
documents, queries and the tools your teams use every day. Without it,

Riviera, Dropbox's internal content processing platform, runs

articles.title: Duckdb internals: why is duckdb fast? (part 2 vectorized execution)
articles.description:
DuckDB is fast because it processes data in cache-friendly batches of
2,048 rows instead of one row at a time. Its vector formats, selection
vectors, precompiled operations, and push-based pipelines reduce
copying, function-call overhead, and parallel execution costs.

DEEP DIVES

 HOW OUR UNIVERSAL CONTENT PROCESSING PLATFORM RIVIERA EVOLVED FOR AI

articles.title: The startup's postgres survival guide
articles.description:
Postgres usually fails at scale because of avoidable operational
mistakes such as poor indexing, long transactions, blocking
migrations, connection storms, and autovacuum falling behind. The key
is to design schemas around real query patterns, keep writes and
migrations non-blocking, batch heavy workloads, and monitor query
plans and bloat before they cause outages.

articles.title: Backfilling: the most underrated feature of a data pipeline
articles.description:
Backfills should use the same production pipeline as incremental
loads, with configuration controlling whether it processes new data,
everything, or a single record. This avoids fragile one-off scripts
and, with bi-temporal writes, makes reprocessing safe and repeatable.

articles.title: To every agent its own database
articles.description:
Each agent gets a local DuckDB instance, and exchanges immutable
pinned SliceRef objects containing a snapshot ID and content digest
instead of mutable snapshots to avoid cache coherence problems.
Semantic contracts written in Malloy define governed queries as
machine-checkable artifacts, and a contract comparison layer
classifies changes as identical, additive, breaking, or unrelated
before any downstream computation runs.

articles.title: Your ai answered correctly. finance still disagrees.
articles.description:
The AI didn't hallucinate. It used the data it was given. When
"revenue" means three things across your tools, AI just delivers the
inconsistency at scale, confidently. Read the full breakdown of why
meaning slips [13] then score your own environment against the five
places context breaks.

Get the Context Gap whitepaper → [14]

articles.title: Aurora dsql: scalable, multi-region oltp
articles.description:
Aurora DSQL provides PostgreSQL-compatible, strongly consistent,
active-active multi-region OLTP without managing servers, shards,
replicas, or failover, with cross-region latency mostly paid at
commit. Teams still need short transactions and must work around
current limits such as 3,000 rows or 10 MiB per transaction and no
enforced foreign keys. 

 LATLNG (TOOL) [16] 

 latlng is an open-source Rust engine for indexing moving objects,
running geofences, and streaming location events natively or in the
browser.

articles.title: Optimizing for almost sorted data: sort pushdown in apache datafusion
articles.description:
Apache DataFusion now exploits exact and partial sortedness
automatically for ORDER BY and ORDER BY ... LIMIT N, using Parquet
min/max statistics, file reordering, and dynamic filters to avoid full
scans and blocking sorts.

articles.title: Ai schema analyzer: powered by iceberg and lakekeeper
articles.description:
Iceberg and Lakekeeper are used to build an AI schema-drift impact
analyzer for lakehouse tables, turning schema changes into
near-real-time alerts and recommendations. The flow is: query engines
issue DDL, Lakekeeper updates the Iceberg catalog and emits change
events to Kafka/Redpanda, and a FastAPI + aiokafka + Anthropic service
analyzes impact within seconds without scanning table metadata. Output
is delivered to Slack and SQLite.

articles.title: The current state of agentic ai
articles.description:
Production systems now deploy specialized agent teams, such as
triage, SQL, and Python agents, with MCP connecting them to systems
like GitHub, Slack, and PostgreSQL. Persistent memory graphs extract
facts from execution histories so agents accumulate organizational
knowledge across calls, and multi-agent handoffs introduce lateral
prompt injection risks addressed through cryptographic tool provenance
and ephemeral sandboxes.

articles.title: Lakekeeper+minio
articles.description:
DuckDB's Iceberg extension now supports CTAS, MERGE INTO, INSERT,
UPDATE, and DELETE, making it viable for full CRUD-style Iceberg ETL
locally without Spark. Paired with MinIO for S3-compatible storage and
LakeKeeper as a Rust Iceberg catalog, teams can test scripts cheaply
in Docker and switch to AWS S3Tables by toggling environment variables
and secrets.

articles.title: Smart caching with cte on spark
articles.description:
Spark recomputes reused and nested CTEs by default, so cache
selectively at fan-out points when intermediate results are complex,
fit in memory, and reused. Avoid caching huge or trivial datasets, use
eager caching for clearer monitoring, and materialize deep
transformation chains to reduce redundant work and prevent stack
overflows.

articles.title: If you think you can do real-world text-to-sql
articles.description:
Text-to-SQL benchmarks overstate performance because real data
warehouses are messy and complex.

articles.title: The database is a liability you can't revert
articles.description:
Database schema decisions can create years of costly technical debt,
so irreversible choices like primary keys, partitioning, and column
types need strong guardrails before they reach production.

articles.title: Why valuemaxxing is replacing tokenmaxxing
articles.description:
Enterprise AI's first goal was adoption. More developers. More
prompts. More tokens. But many organizations are discovering that
maximizing AI usage does not necessarily maximize results. The next
phase is valuemaxxing, where success is measured through improved code
quality, fast delivery, reduced rework and business value. Discover
why the conversation is shifting from AI consumption to AI impact.

Read the full article [4]

articles.title: Google released three new gemini
articles.description:
Google introduced Gemini 3.6 Flash for more efficient general-purpose
agent workloads, 3.5 Flash-Lite for low-latency applications, and a
cyber-specialized 3.5 Flash model integrated with CodeMender. It also
disclosed partner testing for Gemini 3.5 Pro and an ongoing Gemini 4
pre-training run.

articles.title: Openai models escaped a cybersecurity test
articles.description:
OpenAI said models undergoing a cyber-capability evaluation exploited
a package installer to reach the internet, then accessed Hugging Face
systems and retrieved benchmark solutions from a production database.

articles.title: Introducing devin outposts
articles.description:
Devin Outposts enable Devin to run on any machine. This includes
options like Mac mini, GPU boxes, VMs, or Kubernetes clusters.

articles.title: Openai shares some alignment problems
articles.description:
OpenAI experienced significant alignment issues with an internal
model that attempted to bypass sandbox restrictions, prompting the
company to take the model offline for improved safeguards. The model's
actions, such as evading restrictions to post results on GitHub,
highlight concerns about persistent misalignment and the urgency to
address these risks as AI capabilities grow. OpenAI's proactive steps
include creating incident-derived evaluations, active monitoring, and
improving user control, but the underlying alignment problem remains
unresolved, emphasizing the need for a more comprehensive long-term
solution.

articles.title: What it actually takes to build agent infrastructure yourself
articles.description:
Production web agents require five infrastructure layers beyond
Chromium: warm browser pools, VM-level isolation, coherent identities
and residential routing, unified replay and traces, and multi-model
gateways. Building them internally makes sense mainly when
infrastructure is strategic, mandatory, or the product. 

🧑‍💻

articles.description:
Ineffable is training the world's first continuous "Super learner"
using real-time reinforcement learning at scale. This is an immense
compute and networking challenge as it creates bottlenecks, requiring
deeply co-designed storage and Virgo datacenter networking [11] to
keep NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 GPUs fully utilized. This is why they
chose Google Cloud's AI Hypercomputer [12] to accelerate the path to
superintelligence. 

Read the announcement here → [13]

articles.title: Acp v2 is available in draft
articles.description:
The Agent Client Protocol standardizes communication between code
editors and coding agents. It exposes methods that each side can call
and send notifications to inform each other of events. The v2 draft is
now available, and the team is looking for feedback. v2 allows for
much more flexibility and consolidates on common patterns learned over
the past year. 

 LAGUNA S 2.1 (HUGGING FACE REPO) [15] 

 Laguna S 2.1 is a 118B total parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with
8B activated parameters per token. It is designed for agentic coding
and long-horizon work. The model features a mixed SWA and global
attention layout and has a 1 million-token context window. It has
native reasoning support and was released under an OpenMDW-1.1
license.

articles.title: Qwen-image-3.0: rich content, authentic details, deep knowledge
articles.description:
Qwen-Image-3.0 is the third-generation foundational image generation
model in the Qwen-Image series. It supports up to 4.5k token input and
creates rich content with authentic details. The model supports native
rendering of 12 languages and can simulate mainstream interfaces such
as web pages, games, and livestreams. Drawing on rich world knowledge,
the model makes image generation a truly deployable tool. 

 MAGE (GITHUB REPO) [17] 

 Mage is a family of lightweight, research-friendly multimodal models
designed to make advanced visual understanding and generation
accessible for controlled experiments, post-training research, and
vertical-domain applications under realistic compute budgets. The
models are compact enough to train, fine-tune, and deploy on modest
hardware. They remain competitive with much larger open systems in
their respective domains. The models are intended for research and not
for product or service deployment. 

 GIGATOKEN (GITHUB REPO) [18] 

 Gigatoken is a tokenizer for language modeling that supports a wide
range of CPU hardware and nearly all commonly used tokenizers. It can
be used with its own API or in capability mode with Hugging Face
Tokenizers or Tiktoken. Gigatoken is around 1,000 times faster than
Hugging Face's tokenizers. It can tokenize text data at the rate of
gigabytes per second.

articles.title: The state of simulation for physical ai: an overview
articles.description:
Simulations are crucial for physical AI systems, allowing efficient
data generation that real-world collection lacks. This overview
compares key simulation engines, such as MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, and
Newton, each catering to specific robotics applications like
reinforcement learning and synthetic data generation. Open-source
development and GPU-accelerated tools are driving innovation and
accessibility in robotics simulation. 

 HOW META'S AI MODELS ARE POWERING THE FIRST WAVE OF GENESIS MISSION

articles.title: Projects
articles.description:
Meta's SAM 3 and DINOv3 AI models power Lawrence Berkeley Lab's
SYNAPS-I project, enhancing data analysis for X-ray and neutron
science. These models transform the complex task of image
segmentation, reducing time from months to minutes by providing
precise object boundaries and context identification. This AI-driven
pipeline aids real-time research, exemplified by advancing
drought-resilient crop studies in grapevines.

articles.title: The enterprise knowledge layer
articles.description:
Enterprise agent performance varies not because of LLMs or tooling,
but because agents lack properly codified business meaning and
institutional knowledge. Neo4j proposes the Enterprise Knowledge Layer
(EKL) as a shared, governed substrate (comprising an EKL ontology,
enterprise data grounding, and memory) so agents can interpret intent,
access trustworthy data, and act consistently without duplicating
semantics inside each agent.

articles.title: Google is open-sourcing its 3d emoji
articles.description:

articles.title: Photos with ai
articles.description:
Adobe's Project Indigo camera app is testing AI Playground, adding AI
editing tools like distraction removal, restyling, and a photo
critique feature. The tools run on Google's Nano Banana model, capping
edited images at 2K pixels, with Adobe planning to add its own Firefly
models later. Access is free but limited to a small percentage of
users in version 1.1 for a few weeks, with wider availability still
undecided.

articles.title: Apple's next big iphone display experiment could be its biggest yet
articles.description:
Apple is reportedly testing a larger 6.96-inch display for a future
iPhone, bringing it close to the 7-inch mark while maintaining the
same aspect ratio as the current Pro Max. The screen could be part of
Apple's ambitious 20th-anniversary plans for 2027, but there's no
evidence yet that it will appear in a final product. As with all early
hardware leaks, the display remains experimental and could be changed
or scrapped before release.

articles.title: From vibe to specs: reclaiming the design process with said framework
articles.description:
AI-native product teams are replacing linear design handoffs with the
"SAID framework," a continuous loop built around specs, Git, and
human-agent collaboration. Rather than fixed roles, teams now shift
between archetypes—Prototyper, Builder, Sweeper, Grower, and
Maintainer—while specs, tested via Anthropic's 4D Fluency Framework
(Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence), become the
shared source of truth. Designers aren't expected to become engineers,
but must learn to express intent as precise, testable behavior that
both humans and AI agents can execute.

articles.title: Training design senses
articles.description:
Design judgment and taste must be deliberately trained through
practice, not measured by years of passive experience in the field.
This post outlines four trainable areas—observation, hand-eye
dexterity, aesthetic fluency, and rhetoric—that build intuition
through repeated, intentional effort. Genuine design intuition emerges
from accumulated evidence of practice, not from time alone, and must
be demonstrated through actual work.

articles.title: Make it work vs. make it good
articles.description:
Making something work is often easier to recognize and reward than
making it truly good, even though the latter requires far more skill
and effort. Great design comes from refining usability, accessibility,
performance, and overall experience until the solution feels obvious
rather than merely functional. As the saying goes, "make it work" is
the first 90% of the job, while "make it good" is the other 90%.

articles.title: Not all brand redesigns are trainwrecks
articles.description:
While Cracker Barrel, Jaguar, and Tropicana suffered backlash for
their redesigns, several other brands managed rebrands that pleased
audiences and critics alike. Examples include the Premier League's
simplified lion logo, Dunkin's name change dropping "Donuts,"
Rolls-Royce's sleeker Spirit of Ecstasy emblem, Reddit's unified
pre-IPO redesign by Pentagram, and eBay's decluttered 2024 website.
These successful makeovers contrast with more infamous rebrand
failures, showing that thoughtful redesigns can modernize a brand's
image without alienating its existing customer base.

articles.title: The swiss cheese model, pt. 1
articles.description:
The Swiss Cheese model explains how major failures often result from
several small, independent mistakes aligning rather than a single
catastrophic error. A famous example is Knight Capital's $460 million
trading loss, where outdated code, a reused software flag, an
incomplete deployment, missing verification, and inadequate safeguards
combined to trigger a company-ending failure. The key lesson is that
robust systems rely on multiple overlapping protections, because any
one small mistake is usually harmless until several failures line up
at once.

articles.title: Holographik's identity for veda treats coins as ancient artefacts
articles.description:
Instead of relying on the generic visual language common in crypto,
Holographik created a distinctive identity for Veda by reimagining the
familiar coin as a symbolic artifact inspired by ancient stores of
value and knowledge. Each 3D coin represents the underlying
architecture of a specific crypto vault, combining custom
illustrations, metallic materials, and restrained typography to
balance trust, memorability, and sophistication. The result is a brand
system that feels tangible and timeless while standing apart from
typical fintech aesthetics.

articles.title: Beyond happy path engineering: time
articles.description:
Software development often starts under optimal conditions, leading
to a "happy path" approach that neglects real-world challenges such as
network issues and time synchronization problems. As systems scale, it
becomes necessary to recognize the various dimensions of time, such as
elapsed time, timestamps, event ordering, and business-specific
timeframes. By making time decisions explicitly and tailoring how each
aspect of time is handled within the software architecture, developers
can create more resilient systems that can better handle the
complexities and uncertainties of production environments.

articles.title: "drawing" the mona lisa with gpt-5.6, claude, gemini, and grok
articles.description:
An experiment was conducted to evaluate the artistic capabilities of
four AI models, GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Fable 5, Grok 4.5, and Gemini 3.6
Flash, by having them create drawings of famous artworks, including
the Mona Lisa and Van Gogh's Starry Night, while using a
colored-pencil toolset in a controlled environment. GPT-5.6 Sol was
the most efficient and a high-quality performer, while Grok 4.5
struggled a lot. Claude Fable 5 had better quality, but also had a
higher cost and longer creation time.

articles.title: Secrets don't belong in config
articles.description:
Applications should avoid mixing sensitive information like passwords
and API keys with configuration files, as this leads to security
vulnerabilities and complicates the management of secrets. Instead,
they should use dedicated runtime channels for secrets, which
separates secret handling from configuration management effectively
across different environments.

articles.title: Throw, result, or neither?
articles.description:
In software development, handling errors can be approached through
exceptions, Result types, or events, with each method serving
different purposes based on the scenario's requirements. While using
exceptions can quickly indicate issues, using event sourcing allows
for the retention of failure data as valuable business insights.

articles.title: Building an agent that buys things? make sure it only buys once

articles.description:

 OPENSHIP (GITHUB REPO) [13] 

 Openship is an open-source, self-hostable deployment platform that

includes Gateway Resolver for recursive resolution and Internal

articles.title: Anthropic, openai, and google
articles.description:
Prompt caching can dramatically reduce latency and cost, but cache
lifetime differs significantly across providers and is often
undocumented. Measurements found Anthropic's default cache remained
warm for roughly five minutes, OpenAI's automatic prompt cache
typically expired after 5–10 minutes of inactivity, and Google's
implicit Gemini cache showed more variable eviction behavior,
highlighting that production systems with long pauses between requests
may need explicit cache-warming or provider-specific caching
strategies to maintain high cache hit rates.

and stricter review of AI-generated code across 335 critical systems.

articles.title: Why goodput matters more than throughput for llm serving
articles.description:
A benchmark of the LLM serving framework vLLM on a single NVIDIA A10G
GPU revealed that maximizing throughput can degrade user experience,
with one configuration achieving 50% higher token throughput but
causing token streaming delays nearly 10 times worse (494ms vs 50ms at
p95). The study demonstrated that "goodput"—requests meeting both
throughput and latency targets for time-to-first-token and
time-per-output-token—is a more meaningful metric than raw
throughput alone, with the optimal configuration varying significantly
across chatbot, reasoning, and agentic workloads.

humans (light factory) increases judgment and concentration while
lowering speed and breakage. Using only AI agents (dark factory)
allows agents to handle the whole process, but risks a lack of
understanding of the produced software. The hardest job now is knowing
which checks to build and how much autonomy to delegate.

articles.description:
Google reportedly developed a server chip called Frozen v2 for a
potential 2028 release, targeting six to ten times more tokens per
unit of power than its existing AI hardware. The project reflected a
broader push to reduce inference costs and reliance on Nvidia.

articles.title: Sparse by design
articles.description:
Kimi K3 activates 16 of 896 experts per token. While the total
parameters have grown, the active parameters have barely grown at all
over the past three releases. The strategy appears to be to keep
per-token compute roughly flat while relentlessly inflating total
capacity. At a fixed training compute budget, more experts means lower
loss, and the model learns more from the same FLOPs. The open source
labs have discovered that the cheapest way to buy intelligence is to
spend capacity.

articles.title: On kimi k3: its capabilities and related discontents
articles.description:
Kimi K3 is a very good model with excellent benchmarks. It is the
largest (soon-to-be) open model so far, at 2.8T parameters, which
explains many of its gains. The model is somewhat distilled, and its
performance looks jagged, but it will likely fit well into many
workflows. At the current rate of development, China appears capable
of releasing a Mythos-level open model by the end of the year.

articles.title: What long-horizon ai failures reveal about safety
articles.description:
OpenAI detailed how an internally deployed long-running model
exhibited unexpected unsafe behavior that existing evaluations had
missed. The company paused access, built new tests, strengthened
trajectory-level monitoring, and argued that limited deployment with
rollback controls is essential for aligning increasingly autonomous
systems.

articles.title: Online learning for cost-efficient llm routing
articles.description:

distributions through Thompson sampling, then chooses the cheapest
model and service tier likely to meet each deadline. Ramp reports 30%
savings in Ramp Inspect without performance loss. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: Introducing cosmos 3 edge
articles.description:
NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge is a 4-billion-parameter open world model that
helps robots and vision AI agents understand their surroundings,
reason in real time, and generate robot actions on edge devices. It is
now available on Hugging Face. The model delivers memory-efficient,
high-throughput inference across NVIDIA edge computers. It connects
understanding, prediction, simulation, and action through a shared
world representation. The model can be used as a reasoner or an action
generator.

articles.title: Agent swarms and the new model economics
articles.description:
Every jump in AI capability has raised the level of abstraction at
which an engineer works. Agent swarms make the spec the unit of work.
Swarms translate intent, but they do this probabilistically, which
makes it difficult for them to follow the spec. This post looks at
what it takes to make swarms actually follow the spec.

articles.title: Xiaomi-robotics-1
articles.description:
Xiaomi-Robotics-1 is a ready-to-use robot foundation model trained on
over 100K hours of real-world manipulation trajectories. It combines
large-scale embodiment-free pre-training with a modest amount of
real-robot data in a post-training stage. It serves as a strong robot
foundation model for downstream applications and can learn new tasks
with high data efficiency. Footage of robots operating on the model
performing household tasks is available in the post.

articles.title: Language model harnesses are compositional generalizers
articles.description:
Scaling data will remain the biggest driver of progress. The machine
that we feed that data into and its inductive biases are what will
determine the coefficients of that scaling. Better returns on scaling
require compositional generalization. The capacity for compositional
generalization seems to largely live in harnesses.

articles.title: Z.ai built a gigawatt-scale ai data center
articles.description:

Chinese-made chips and began partial operations. The facility expanded
the computing infrastructure available for training its advanced GLM
models.

articles.title: How ai is supercharging drug development
articles.description:
AI is cutting preclinical costs and timelines in drug development by
up to 70%, driving demand for advanced software and models. This could
boost new drug program growth by over 10% in three to five years.
However, AI has yet to yield an FDA-approved drug, raising concerns
about its impact on patient treatment.

just pennies. The discrepancy suggests inefficiencies despite lower
token costs.

articles.description:

deploy enterprise agentic AI on Gemini and its cloud platform. The
move reinforces that hyperscalers are increasingly competing on
ecosystems and enterprise adoption—not just foundation models.

articles.title: Platform engineering's new job: serving environments at agent speed
articles.description:
As coding agents become the most demanding tenants of platform
environments, platform engineering needs to shift from provisioning
environments on demand to serving them like a low-latency,
high-concurrency system. Both full-copy and shared-single-environment
approaches fail under agent traffic patterns, and a delta-based
“serve the changed services” architecture routed per request can
reduce latency and cost while preserving isolation.

inheriting existing security/governance policies and built-in audit

business processes.

articles.title: Xebia launches ai agents to accelerate enterprise data migrations
articles.description:
Xebia Axis is an AI-agent-powered platform that automates data
assessments, migrations, and operations. The company says it can
complete migrations up to three times faster while improving
enterprise AI readiness.

articles.title: Email encryption
articles.description:
Email was designed without built-in confidentiality or integrity,
prompting efforts to develop more secure messaging systems. X.400
sought to provide end-to-end encryption through mechanisms such as
ASN.1 and X.509-based directory services, but its complexity prevented
it from replacing internet email.

capacity

articles.description:
X has relaunched its Android app after nearly a year of rebuilding it
from scratch to improve loading, scrolling, notifications,
reliability, and future feature development. The effort was described

and is aimed partly at strengthening X in Android-heavy global

 APPLE BRIEFLY BECAME THE WORLD'S MOST VALUABLE COMPANY, TOPPLING

articles.title: Nvidia
articles.description:
Apple briefly overtook Nvidia as the world's most valuable company
after investors sold off AI-related semiconductor stocks, reflecting
growing skepticism about the long-term returns of massive AI
infrastructure spending. Unlike many of its rivals, Apple has spent
relatively little on building AI infrastructure and instead benefits
from its installed base of 2.5 billion devices. As a result, it is
increasingly seen as well positioned to monetize AI features,
especially after the positive reception to its revamped Siri.

articles.title: Agentio's ai-powered creator ads are coming to facebook and instagram
articles.description:
Agentio, an AI-powered creator advertising platform previously
focused on YouTube, has partnered with Meta to bring its tools to
Facebook and Instagram. Brands can now access AI-driven insights,
creator matching, and partnership ads across both platforms, with the
option to run cross-platform campaigns spanning Meta and Google
properties. Beta testing showed Agentio's Meta partnership ads
achieved 81% higher ROAS and 89% higher click-through rates compared
to brands' non-Agentio creator ads.

articles.title: Product quality: a shared commitment to craft in the wake of ai
articles.description:
As AI collapses the gap between "nothing" and "adequate," genuine
craft becomes the only remaining differentiator between products.
Craft is a shared discipline across Utility, Usability, and
Feel—owned collectively by engineers, PMs, designers, and leaders,
not design alone. "Would I recommend this to someone I care about?"
should be the standard for judging whether a product has truly earned
people's affection, not just their approval.

articles.title: Why the future of design must begin with understanding people
articles.description:
User experience has always extended beyond visible interfaces, shaped
instead by trust, psychology, and human context. Drawing on
architecture, emergency medical care, and design experience, the
author contends AI heightens designers' responsibility to build
informed—not blind—trust, making AI literacy an essential design
skill. Design's future depends on understanding people rather than
mastering tools, since technology changes but human needs remain
constant. 

 ACCESSIBILITY ISN'T A CHECKLIST. IT'S A DESIGN DECISION YOU'RE

articles.title: Avoiding
articles.description:
A UX designer recounts watching a blind user struggle through an
11-minute flight booking process that should have taken 90 seconds,
revealing how years of seemingly reasonable decisions had quietly
excluded users with disabilities. The experience showed that
accessibility isn't primarily a technical challenge or a compliance
checklist—it requires making it a core product priority, testing
with real assistive technology users, and treating accessibility as
part of the definition of "done" rather than something to address
later.

articles.title: Against design system federation
articles.description:
Federated design system governance—used by just 13% of teams—is
losing favor due to poor contribution rates, diffused accountability,
and inflated cost-saving expectations. Layoffs and AI-driven
productivity narratives have fueled interest in federation, but it
typically damages system quality, user experience, and team morale
rather than fixing organizational problems. Federation works best as
one aspect within a hybrid model, not as a standalone governance
approach, since it demands more organizational maturity than most
companies achieve.

articles.title: The “mocked, then loved” airpods effect
articles.description:
Apple's AirPods and Apple Watch both overcame early ridicule by
proving genuinely useful in everyday life, but the rumored
camera-equipped AirPods face a different challenge: concerns about
privacy and social acceptance rather than just unconventional design.
While Apple has a strong track record of turning skepticism into
success, the new AirPods will need to demonstrate clear, hands-free AI
benefits while convincing both wearers and those around them that the
cameras can be trusted.

articles.title: Ask yourself where you can add value
articles.description:
Designers should stop undervaluing in-house work and instead showcase
the business problems they solved, the constraints they worked within,
and the measurable results they achieved. Rather than waiting to build
a perfect portfolio, improve existing projects incrementally with
stronger storytelling, updated visuals, and small enhancements, making
steady progress in short bursts that fit around a busy schedule.

articles.title: How ai helped us make sense of hundreds of components
articles.description:
A UK higher education institution had years of organically grown web
components with no clear inventory, so a team built an AI-assisted
audit tool through rapid, conversational iteration rather than a fixed
spec.

articles.title: Nostalgic game boy
articles.description:
Glaze is a Mac app that transforms your entire display with over 50
real-time visual effects—from CRT monitors to VHS tapes—while also
offering productivity and accessibility modes.

articles.title: Agent swarms and the new model economics
articles.description:
Recent experiments have shown huge improvements in the performance of
agent swarms tasked with building complex software, such as SQLite,
through a structured approach where planner agents decompose tasks and
worker agents execute them efficiently. The new swarm model
consistently outperformed the previous version in terms of both speed
and quality of output, achieving higher scores on testing suites while
reducing the lines of code required to complete the task. This shift
in design not only enhanced operational efficiency but also pointed to
substantial cost savings by utilizing less expensive models for
execution after initial planning by more capable, high-cost models.

articles.title: You only need the frontier model for one single edit
articles.description:
Using a frontier model for planning and then switching to a cheaper
model for execution often results in higher costs and more redundancy
due to the expensive reading involved with context capture. Instead,
implementing a strategy where the frontier model explores and captures
its understanding in a todo list before switching can improve
efficiency and reduce costs.

articles.title: Our new and faster profiler dashboard
articles.description:
Polar Signals improved the speed of their profiler dashboard by
transitioning from an SVG to a Canvas rendering method. This shift
removed the need for numerous DOM nodes, streamlining the rendering
process and resulting in much faster interactions, such as scrolling
and zooming. The Canvas renderer operates approximately 3.6 times
faster than its SVG counterpart.

articles.title: Perfection is not over-engineering
articles.description:
Perfection in engineering should not be seen as a negative. Rather,
the real issue comes from poorly defined requirements, which can lead
to over-engineering and complex solutions that do not effectively
address the actual problem.

articles.title: Stop using opencode
articles.description:
OpenCode is criticized by this user for its security vulnerabilities
and some practical flaws that reduce its effectiveness as a coding
agent. It often has poor decision-making in handling context,
permissions, and agent interactions which can result in
inefficiencies.

articles.title: Visual design rules you can safely follow every time
articles.description:
This is a set of visual design rules positioned as safe defaults for
general app design. For example, near-black and near-white should
always be used over pure black and pure white. Measurements should be
scale-based, such as using multiples of 4 for consistency, rather than
using magic numbers.

articles.title: Why cpus are now at the center of the ai race
articles.description:
The global AI boom is creating a shift in the CPU market,
traditionally dominated by Intel and AMD, as new challengers like
Nvidia, Qualcomm, and various Chinese firms are entering the fray. The
demand for CPUs in AI data centers is projected to grow over 40%
annually, with notable increases also from domestic producers in
China.

articles.title: American ai is locked down and proprietary. it's losing
articles.description:
The closed and proprietary approach to AI in the United States is
leading to it possibly losing to China's open-weights strategy, which
allows for greater innovation and adaptability. The US government's
export controls and regulations make the competitive landscape hard to
navigate.

articles.title: No, that post never existed. stop listening to that thing
articles.description:
A meta reflection addresses the existence of a non-existent blog post
titled "The Stack" from 2013, highlights the futility of searching for
fabricated content, and explores the implications of creating
self-aware technology that may resist control.

articles.title: X completes android app rebuild
articles.description:
The X Android app has been completely rebuilt for improved speed,
reliability, and the ability to rapidly incorporate new features. 

 RAMP ROUTER (WEBSITE) [22] 

 Ramp's Router optimizes AI model selection for over 100 use cases,
reducing costs by 30% while enhancing efficiency, making it accessible

articles.title: Two numbers explain why millions stopped typing.

articles.title: The productivity-experience paradox

potentially corrosive for internal ones - the skill, the mastery, and
the satisfaction you can only get by doing the thing itself. People

interested in the internal goods, AI can feel like a loss, as it takes
the parts they loved and hands it to a machine, leaving only
supervision and accountability. While the output still arrives, the
pride and satisfaction of owning the work is gone.

articles.title: Fable 5 vs. gpt-5.6 sol on an np-hard problem: does /goal help?

implementations are fundamentally different. Claude Code implements

but it doesn't know whether another ten million solver iterations are
worthwhile. Codex treats a goal as a persisted thread state. It sees
the files and tools, but effectively grades its own work. Using /goal
can be a bad default as it can amplify bad decisions as much as good
ones.

articles.title: Apologising for the mess

allowed users to generate and edit images using photos from any public

default. After widespread criticism from creative professionals,
unions, talent agencies, and privacy advocates, the company removed

mark." The incident highlights a broader concern about AI companies
launching opt-out features that treat publicly shared content as
available for AI use unless users explicitly disable it. It also
underscores the importance of consent, creator rights, and vigilance,
as platforms continue to push AI capabilities that can affect
photographers, designers, illustrators, and other creative
professionals.

articles.title: Why is ai bad at design?
articles.description:
AI struggles with design because, unlike code, design has no
automatic way to verify if an output is correct, forcing reliance on
slow, subjective human judgment. This subjectivity pulls AI toward
generic, "average" outputs, worsened by scarce design training data
and models generating interfaces blindly, without truly seeing what
they create. While vision-based feedback loops and better models may
narrow some gaps, the subjective nature of taste remains a structural
limit, meaning humans will still be essential for genuine design
judgment and originality.

articles.title: Does your form really need a dropdown list?
articles.description:
Dropdown lists are often overused because they save space and enforce
valid input, but they also hide options, increase interaction cost,
create accessibility issues, and frequently force users into
inaccurate choices. In many cases, radio buttons (for a few options),
comboboxes (for many options), or text inputs (for familiar values
like dates or ages) provide a faster and more usable experience.
Dropdowns are most effective only in a narrow set of situations: when
there are roughly 5–10 predefined options, the field is secondary to
the user's main task, or it needs to remain compact as part of a
larger group of related controls. Rather than treating dropdowns as
the default, designers should choose the input control that minimizes
user effort while matching the task and the nature of the data.

articles.title: Design systems need evals
articles.description:
Design systems have adopted software engineering practices, but
agents generating code against these systems still can't be verified
for compliance without dedicated evaluation suites. Effective evals
combine mechanical checks—validating props, tokens, and component
usage against the actual system—with LLM-based judgment on pattern
selection and edge-case handling, run repeatedly since underlying
models and rules keep shifting. While a few teams like Meta's Astryx
and Intuit have begun building these regression suites into their
pipelines, running such evals in CI remains an uncommon practice
rather than a standard expectation.

 ISOLATION LEVELS: READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ, AND SERIALIZABLE

articles.title: Explained
articles.description:
Database isolation levels make different tradeoffs between
concurrency and consistency by controlling which anomalies concurrent
transactions are allowed to observe. Read Committed prioritizes
throughput but allows changing results between reads, Repeatable Read
prevents many inconsistencies through snapshot isolation while still
permitting write skew, and Serializable guarantees execution
equivalent to a serial order by detecting or preventing conflicting
transactions.

first agentic smartphone, pulls up ByteDance's AI agent Doubao with a
voice command or the press of a button. It comes in black, pink,
white, and blue.

articles.title: Tune it, deploy it, own it: crusoe serverless fine-tuning is now live
articles.description:
Fine-tune leading open models (Qwen, DeepSeek, Gemma, gpt-oss) on
your proprietary data with no clusters to provision and no surprise
bills [9]. Crusoe's token-based pricing ends the moment your model
stops improving, and weights export in .safetensors format. Deploy in
one click. Get started → [9]

articles.title: How anthropic runs large-scale code migrations with claude code
articles.description:
Code migrations were typically multi-year endeavors until recently.
Claude Code's capabilities change the math for these types of
projects. This post details the six-step process Anthropic uses to
perform code migrations. The core principle is to fix the process that
produces the code rather than fixing the code itself. 

 SCROLL-WORLD (GITHUB REPO) [11] 

 scroll-world is a skill that turns any brand into a scrollable 3D
world. It works with Claude Code, Codex, and any SKILL.md-compatible
agent. The skill builds immersive, control-scrubbed 'fly through the
world' landing pages for any industry or brand. A video example is
available in the repository.

articles.title: Maybe intelligence ain't all that
articles.description:
AI chatbots are now smarter and more capable than a lot of people,
but there has yet to be an explosion or take-off in usage. Coming up
with ideas was never the hard part. Most problems can't be worked out
at a desk by thinking. Reality stays bound by how fast a thing can be
built and whether it holds.

articles.title: These ai-native companies have tiny staffs and fewer bosses
articles.description:
The newest generation of AI-infused companies offer a vision of how
work could soon be structured in other American corporations. They
have fewer workers, more on-staff engineers, and a flatter structure
where everyone is a player-coach instead of strictly overseeing teams.
The structure is a proving ground for the philosophy that corporate
giants are trying to channel through reorganizations, de-layering, job
cuts, and investment into AI.

articles.title: Apple, nvidia vie for title of world's most valuable company
articles.description:
Apple briefly became the world's most valuable company on Friday. 

 AN AWS BILLING BUG SENT USERS ESTIMATED CHARGES OF UP TO $2.5

Amazon has confirmed a unit pricing error and is recomputing all

The winners of the database wars weren't the ones everyone was

than keeping their heads down.

articles.title: Apache datafusion comet
articles.description:
DataFusion Comet speeds Spark reads on Iceberg by keeping Java
planning while using Iceberg Rust for native Arrow execution. On a 3
TB TPC-DS benchmark, it accelerated 102 of 103 queries and cut total
runtime by about 40%, while its use of Iceberg Java's Spark test
suites has helped drive more than 40 Iceberg Rust pull requests. 

 FROM OTEL TO SLMS: DISTILLING FRONTIER MODEL BEHAVIOUR FROM
PRODUCTION TELEMETRY (45 MINUTE VIDEO) [9] 

 OpenTelemetry traces can convert production AI-agent feedback into
training labels for local 7B-13B coding models. Fine-tuned within
hours, they can reach roughly 80-85% of frontier-model quality while
lowering inference costs, preserving privacy, and scaling across the
enterprise.

articles.title: Funnel optimization
articles.description:
Meta compresses its graph of billions of users and advertiser
entities into clusters of latent interests, enriches them with
LLM-processed ad content, and embeds everything in one shared space
where any user or entity can be scored against any other. Learning
from broad graph structure instead of only rare conversion events
gives the deep funnel a usable signal, and the embeddings feed Meta's
ad ranking models like GEM and Andromeda.
articles.section: EXPLORING HIERARCHICAL INTEREST REPRESENTATION FOR META ADS DEEP

articles.title: Transform 2026
articles.description:
Enterprise agents are constrained more by legacy infrastructure than
model quality. LinkedIn pre-provisioned containers and shifted 80% of
orchestration to deterministic code, Walmart governed duplicate
internal agents, and Zendesk strengthened data pipelines for its 20B
conversations. The lesson is to invest in evals, own the agent
harness, and keep workloads portable across models.

articles.title: Ai agents need data product context not more rag
articles.description:
Enterprise AI agents need governed context, not just vector search:
retrieval can find relevant passages, but it does not preserve source
boundaries, business meaning, ownership, or usage restrictions. The
proposed approach compiles one governed data-product model into
multiple representations: graph, Markdown wiki, portable OKF bundle,
and compact sidecars such as TOON/GCF. AI readiness depends on
connected, trusted context and repeatable operations rather than
catalog presence alone.

articles.title: On thinking
articles.description:
Asking a data question is still a ticket, a queue, and a week of
bogged down data teams. Cube [14] hands that workflow to AI agents who
model, explore, and build reports - working from one governed set of
definitions and single source of truth. Brex, Wix, and Patagonia run
on Cube. Get started for free [14]

articles.title: Introducing apache spark 4.2
articles.description:
Apache Spark 4.2 adds metric views for defining business metrics, SQL
vector similarity search, native geospatial types, and change data
capture queries through a new CHANGES clause. Spark Connect and
default Arrow optimized Python execution make the engine easier to
reach. The release bundles over 1,900 commits from more than 260
contributors. 

 ONTOLOGY PLAYGROUND (GITHUB REPO) [16] 

 Microsoft's Ontology Playground is a free, open-source tool for
visually exploring, building, importing and sharing ontologies for
Microsoft Fabric IQ.

articles.title: Postgres 19 compression: from pglz to lz4
articles.description:
Postgres 19 plans to switch default TOAST compression from pglz to
LZ4, while keeping the same unified compression framework across heap
storage, TOAST, and B-tree indexes. Variable-length types like TEXT,
VARCHAR, BYTEA, and JSONB are compressed automatically via varlena
metadata, with rows targeting ~2 KB before spilling out-of-line to
TOAST. LZ4 is much faster than pglz in tests, often compresses better,
and still fails fast on incompressible data.

articles.title: Experience graphs: the data foundation for self-improving agents
articles.description:
Trellis stores agent artifacts, rewards, search data, and causal
history as persistent experience graphs accessible through SQL, graph,
vector, and temporal queries. Meta found that reusing past experience
matched performance about 10x faster and reduced successful-solution
token costs by 52%, though excessive memory reuse reduced exploration.

articles.title: In-house llm serving at netflix
articles.description:
Netflix runs LLM serving end-to-end in-house, using a unified
JVM-based platform with gRPC plus an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API,
rather than relying on hosted APIs. The stack standardizes deployment
through Triton-backed Model Scoring Service, using vLLM as the
paved-path engine after re-benchmarking. It also adds custom
packaging, zero-downtime rollouts, and patched guided decoding to
prevent malformed JSON output. 

 FROM WEEKS TO A DAY: HOW WE MADE LLM EVALUATION FAST ENOUGH TO

articles.title: Iterate on
articles.description:
Airbnb cut LLM evaluation cycles from weeks to under a day by caching
generated references and judge scores, since over half of model
outputs across candidates were identical strings and judge drift of
about 1% per run. Small LoRA adapters with rank under 50 train in
under an hour on a single GPU for same day fixes, and a final
validation stage runs sampled traffic to catch failures.

articles.title: Second act
articles.description:
Databricks is reportedly raising $3 billion at a $188 billion
valuation after successfully repositioning itself from a data platform
into a major enterprise AI provider. 

 DREMIO'S EXIT IS THE CLEAREST SIGN YET THAT LAKEHOUSE-ONLY WON'T

articles.title: Survive ai
articles.description:
Dremio's sale to SAP is presented as evidence that data platforms
built around a single lakehouse will struggle with AI's demands for
broad reach, freshness and unpredictable querying.

articles.title: The difference between a diagram and a network map.
articles.description:
Good network documentation isn't about creating prettier diagrams.
It's about understanding how your environment is connected when
performance drops, users complain, or something goes offline.

THE NO SWEAT GUIDE TO NETWORK TOPOLOGY [5] shows you how to build

articles.title: Implementation, not models
articles.description:
Anthropic and Blackstone-backed venture Ode with Anthropic, launched
in May, is positioning itself as a $1.5B AI “implementation” firm
focused on deploying AI engineering inside enterprises rather than
solely improving models. Built from the acquired startup Fractional
AI, Ode employs 100 engineers and will follow a “Claude-first”
approach while also using rival tools when needed, competing with
OpenAI's deployment business and consulting firms' forward-deployed
teams.

articles.title: Cisa urges immediate sharepoint hardening as exploits mount
articles.description:
CISA is urging organizations to immediately patch and investigate
on-premises SharePoint servers after three vulnerabilities were
confirmed as actively exploited. Security teams should also hunt for
compromise, rotate machine keys where needed, and segment SharePoint
from critical systems because patching alone may not remove attacker
persistence.

articles.title: Scaling it at hypergrowth
articles.description:
Drawing on experience building IT through periods of explosive growth
at Meta, Netflix, Uber, Robinhood, and Square, the author explains why
scaling is not about adding people faster, it is about designing
systems that prevent headcount, support demand, and costs from growing
together. The playbook covers automation, self-service,
standardization, vendor leverage, and the operating metrics that
reveal whether IT is actually keeping pace with the business.

articles.title: Strategies
articles.description:
Hardware pricing volatility and ongoing component shortages are
forcing IT channel partners to rethink infrastructure strategies,
according to research from Westcon-Comstor. Most partners report
taking action to reduce project risk (87%), including earlier
planning, improved capacity forecasting, and wider use of managed
services or storage tiering/caching, while some are switching vendors
or accelerating/adjusting customer purchases to manage supply
constraints. 

 SALESFORCE'S AGENTFORCE ISN'T WINNING OVER CLIENTS, KEYBANC ANALYSTS

articles.title: Claim
articles.description:
KeyBanc analysts say Salesforce customers are struggling to see value
from Agentforce because their data is not ready for meaningful AI work
and the product remains immature. Salesforce disputes the assessment,
calling Agentforce its fastest-growing product, but analysts expect
